Guards L37, L47, L50 constrain emptiness/length only, never idx's value; the missing one-statement fix is a bounds check on idx before the write (or overflow-checked stride multiplication).

assumptions: shape_t dims are entry-point attacker-controlled int64 values with no shown upper bound (only non-negativity implied by the unshown TensorShape constructor).
allocate_output/reduced_shape.num_elements() uses an unchecked int64 product, so [2^32,2^32] yields 0 elements (standard TensorFlow behavior).
SparseTensorReduceHelper keeps the non-reduction dims in group_by_dims and reduced_shape (natural semantic of reduce-over-axes).
out_flat operator() performs no bounds checking on the index (standard flat-tensor access).
limitations: ValidateInputs at L8 has an unshown body; if it capped shape dim magnitudes it would block the witness, but no such bound is derivable from the shown fragment.

If TensorShape/num_elements used checked multiplication (newer TF), the allocation would fail closed; the wrap-to-zero capacity is assumed from standard library semantics, giving the witness one fragile boundary.
Out-of-range group_by_dims reaching the L41 shape_vec read is not demonstrated (helper contract assumed valid), so it is demoted rather than reported.
CHECK_EQ at L50 is a fail-closed diagnostic abort and is not reported as a finding.
The VLOG at L65-67 only renders numeric coordinates and an index; no log-injection vector is present.

verdict.summary: In dostor(), the FTPWHO block copies into shm_data_cur->filename from &name[sl - sizeof shm_data_cur->filename - 1U] (line 155). For an attacker-supplied STOR filename with sl == sizeof shm_data_cur->filename, the all-size_t arithmetic wraps (N - N - 1U == SIZE_MAX), so the N-byte memcpy reads out of bounds from &name[SIZE_MAX] (CWE-125), typically crashing the FTP process. The guard at line 150 (sl < N) routes exactly this failing value into the else branch rather than excluding it; the absent one-statement fix is the index correction + 1U so the copied tail starts at name[sl-N+1] and ends at the NUL.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): 'name' is the attacker-controlled STOR argument and line 142 derives 'const size_t sl = strlen(name)' with no shown length cap; line 150 'if (sl < sizeof shm_data_cur->filename)' admits every sl >= N to this else branch, including the failing boundary sl == N, at which the size_t expression 'sl - sizeof shm_data_cur->filename - 1U' wraps to SIZE_MAX, so the N-byte memcpy reads from &name[SIZE_MAX] (the string object has capacity sl+1). The guard constrains the same value at the same type immediately before the sink but does not exclude the failure (boundary insufficiency, no drift); the absent fix is the + 1U index shift making the source '&name[sl - sizeof shm_data_cur->filename + 1U]' so the copy starts at name[sl-N+1] and includes the terminating NUL.

assumptions: FTPWHO support is compiled in and shm_data_cur is non-NULL when the vulnerable block executes, as gated by '#ifdef FTPWHO' (line 140) and 'if (shm_data_cur != NULL)' (line 141).
N = sizeof shm_data_cur->filename is a fixed positive compile-time constant named in the fragment itself.
checknamesanity (line 33) is assumed passable with a plain filename of length N; its internals are not shown and it is not relied on to bound sl.
limitations: For every else-branch value (sl >= N) the copied filename is not NUL-terminated (copy ends at name[sl-2]); consumers of shm_data_cur->filename are outside the fragment, so this is not independently confirmed.
Impact is a crash/DoS if &name[SIZE_MAX] is unmapped; an information-disclosure variant would require the wrapped read to land in mapped memory.
FSTATFS(f, &statfsbuf) at line 180 runs after close(f) at line 174; the return status is checked and only an informational disk-space message is produced, so no security consequence is confirmed.

verdict.summary: The args-array construction is properly bounded: process->args is allocated with (argc + 1) elements (line 42), and every write — the loop body at indices 0..argc-first_arg-1 and the NULL terminator at index argc-first_arg — stays within that capacity for every reachable first_arg >= 0. argv[first_arg] is guarded fail-closed by crun_assert_n_args (line 17). No demonstrable failing value reaches a dangerous sink; remaining concerns (LISTEN_FDS unvalidated env value, xstrdup(argv[argc]) NULL-term copy) lack fragment-shown consumers or callee behavior.

assumptions: process->args capacity is argc + 1 elements per line 42, and elements are zero-initialized by xmalloc0.
first_arg is initialized to 0 (line 3) and set by argp_parse (line 16) to the index of the first non-option argument, i.e., in [0, argc], so argc - first_arg <= argc.
argv holds argc + 1 slots with argv[argc] == NULL per the C runtime contract, so the loop's final read at index argc is defined.
crun_assert_n_args (line 17) enforces a minimum of 1 (with -p) or 2 remaining positional arguments and aborts fail-closed otherwise, keeping argv[first_arg] (lines 19, 92) in bounds.
limitations: The loop at line 43 copies argc - first_arg entries, i.e., one more than the number of command arguments after the container name; the extra source is argv[argc] == NULL. Whether xstrdup(NULL) crashes or is NULL-tolerant is unshown callee behavior, so no CWE-476 finding is confirmable from the fragment.

LISTEN_FDS (lines 28-31) is parsed with strtoll without range/negativity validation and added to preserve_fds; its security impact depends on the unshown consumer libcrun_container_exec_with_options, so no overflow/truncation finding is demonstrable in-fragment.

process->args_len is set to argc while only argc - first_arg entries are populated; any downstream read of args_len entries stays within the argc + 1 allocation, so this is a semantic mismatch, not a memory error.
(argc + 1) * sizeof(*process->args) could theoretically overflow int only at argc == INT_MAX, which is not derivable from shown code; xmalloc0 aborts fail-closed.

verdict.summary: The u64 size parameter is bounded by the guard at lines 7-8 (size > RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ rejected) before the u64-to-u32 truncation at line 10 and the header store at line 33, and the reservation window is bounded by the capacity check at line 26 before the header placement at line 31. Every dangerous sink carries its own decisive protective statement, so no failing value reaches an out-of-bounds write.

assumptions: RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ (lines 7-8) is the module's compile-time record-size cap, small enough that round_up(RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ, 8) cannot exceed U32_MAX; its numeric value is not defined in the fragment.
rb->mask equals the ring buffer size minus one and rb->data has capacity mask+1, consistent with the inline comment at lines 23-25 and the & rb->mask access convention at line 31.
The BPF caller writes exactly `size` bytes to the pointer returned at line 41, honoring the reservation contract.
limitations: The numeric adequacy of the lines 7-8 guard rests on the unshown constant RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ; if that constant were itself >= 2^32 the truncation would not be excluded, but no fragment evidence supports such a value.
bpf_ringbuf_rec_pg_off internals (line 32) are not shown; no dangerous operation depends on its result.
Consumer-side behavior that reads hdr->len / hdr->pg_off is outside the fragment and was not analyzed.

verdict.summary: do_put() is the fixed member of the pair: every security-relevant size computation carries its own in-fragment guard. The MBLOCK path bounds count*(yanklen+spaces)+padding against INT_MAX before the alloc (lines 363-365, sink 371-372); the MCHAR y_size==1 path bounds count*yanklen (line 507, sink 512); the empty/NULL register is rejected before any y_array access (line 182); the '='-register y_array is allocated to the exact pass-1 line count (line 116) with identical pass-2 control flow; and every alloc/append/undo return is FAIL/NULL-checked before use. No demonstrated failing value reaches any sink.

assumptions: y_array from a yank register (lines 134-135) is a paired (size, array) unit; its empty case is explicitly rejected at line 182 before any access.
alloc()/ALLOC_MULT() return NULL on failure and every such result is NULL-checked before dereference (lines 117, 373, 532, 592, 603).
The '='-register array capacity equals the pass-1 y_size counted by the identical control flow used in pass 2 (lines 91-119).
limitations: 'alloc(totlen + oldlen + 1)' at lines 372/531 could in principle wrap if oldlen were near INT_MAX, but the fragment shows no producer of a line that long; treated as a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
Helper-internal contracts of ml_get/ml_append/lbr_chartabsize were not re-derived; the fragment's own guards independently cover the indexed accesses.
The MCHAR split path (lines 591, 602) uses single-line sums with no count multiplier; overflow would require near-INT_MAX line lengths not derivable from shown statements.

verdict.summary: The attacker-controlled catalog_size (line 32, from ph.catalog_entries) is capped by line 33 (`if (s->catalog_size > INT_MAX / 4)`) before the `catalog_size * 4` allocation (line 38), the identical-sized catalog read (line 40), and the index loop (lines 45-46). The admitted range [0, 536870911] makes the product at most 2147483644 (no 32-bit wrap, fits int), and the loop's max index 536870910 stays below the catalog_size-element capacity. All dangerous sinks carry verbatim protective statements; no failure value is derivable on any admitted path, so the fragment is the fixed counterpart.

assumptions: s->catalog_size is the 32-bit value produced by le32_to_cpu(ph.catalog_entries); the analysis also holds if it were signed, because negative values are rejected-or-fail-closed (huge gsize passed to g_malloc aborts) and never reach a memory-corrupting sink.
catalog_bitmap points to catalog_size 4-byte elements because the allocation (line 38) and the read count (line 40) are the identical expression `s->catalog_size * 4`.
bdrv_pread writes at most its count argument and returns < 0 on failure, per its name-implied standard semantics; the return is checked at lines 12 and 41.
limitations: catalog_size == 0 leads to g_malloc(0) and a zero-length bdrv_pread into a possibly NULL buffer, but no in-fragment dereference occurs (the loop at line 45 executes zero times), so no NULL-deref failure is demonstrated in the shown code.

The fail-path g_free(s->catalog_bitmap) (line 52) before line 38 is safe only if the caller zero-initialized bs->opaque; that invariant is not visible in the fragment and was not relied upon for any verdict.
bs->total_sectors (line 23) and s->tracks (line 25-30) have no in-fragment security-relevant consumer, so their guards/boundaries are not audited as sinks here.

verdict.summary: In rsi_send_beacon, skb->len is 0 (dev_alloc_skb at line 6 allocates an empty skb and the memset at line 10 does not change the length), yet when dword_align_bytes is nonzero the fragment executes skb_pull(skb, 64 - dword_align_bytes) for a pull of 1..63 bytes. Pulling more than the current length underflows the unsigned skb->len to a huge u32 value (CWE-191), and the corrupted buffer is subsequently queued for TX at line 19. The guard if (dword_align_bytes) only skips the zero-pull case and does not constrain the pull against the length, so the underflow is admitted. The fix (absent) is to substitute a length-preserving skb_reserve for skb_pull or to guard the pull against skb->len.

evidence.reason: Sink is the skb_pull call. dword_align_bytes is computed at line 12 as ((unsigned long)skb->data & 0x3f) with residual range 0..63; the guard at line 13 (if (dword_align_bytes)) admits 1..63, giving a pull of 1..63 bytes. skb->len is 0 at this point: dev_alloc_skb (line 6) allocates with len 0 and memset (line 10) does not alter skb->len, with no skb_put shown. Pull length 1..63 therefore exceeds the length 0 and subtracts into the unsigned length, wrapping skb->len to a huge u32 (0 - n), an integer underflow (CWE-191); the corrupted skb is then queued at line 19. The guard is wrong-target: it excludes only the zero-pull case and never bounds the pull by skb->len, and no length-preserving substitute (skb_reserve) or explicit skb->len >= (64 - dword_align_bytes) check exists anywhere in the fragment — the absent fix.

assumptions: dev_alloc_skb(MAX_MGMT_PKT_SIZE) returns an skb with skb->len == 0 and at least MAX_MGMT_PKT_SIZE writable tailroom at skb->data (standard skb semantics; capacity for line 10's memset derives from line 6).
skb_pull(n) advances data by n and subtracts n from the unsigned skb->len; a pull larger than the current length underflows the length.
MGMT_BEACON_Q is a valid constant index into common->tx_queue (capacity not shown).
limitations: The failing value dword_align_bytes in 1..63 requires the allocator to return skb->data not 64-byte aligned; that address is a runtime magnitude not shown in the fragment, so the witness is a range (1..63) resting on one assumed external fact, capping confidence.

The concrete downstream consumption of the underflowed skb->len (e.g., TX descriptor/DMA length) is in unshown code, so an out-of-bounds read/write (CWE-787/125) is not independently confirmed; only the in-fragment length underflow is demonstrated.

On the error path (lines 15-17) the skb is returned without dev_kfree_skb when rsi_prepare_beacon fails; this is a resource leak whose trigger (a nonzero return from rsi_prepare_beacon) is an unshown call result, so it is not a confirmed finding.
A NULL result from dev_alloc_skb is checked at line 7 before the memset, and allocation failure of the fixed-size MAX_MGMT_PKT_SIZE allocation is not attacker-reachable; no NULL-deref finding.
The NULL check (line 7) and the rsi_prepare_beacon return check (line 15) are present but do not constrain the skb_pull at line 14.

verdict.summary: string_scan_range can loop forever: for any min >= 3 (admitted by the only min check, line 28) and bytes forming a 2- or 3-rune printable ASCII string followed by NUL inside the scanned range, the backup at line 187 (needle -= 2) rewinds needle exactly to the previously scanned str_start and the outer while (needle < to) loop at line 72 re-parses identical bytes indefinitely, since runes < min prevents any reporting and the guard at line 185 imposes no forward-progress requirement.

evidence.reason: Non-termination sink: with attack-controlled bytes buf[0..2] = 'a','b','\0' (line 42 reads entry-point file data; to-from >= 5 passes line 23; min=4 is admitted by the line 28 check that excludes only min==0), the scan computes str_start=needle=0, runes=2, str_type=ASCII, needle=2. Line 185's guard (runes < min && runes >= 2 && str_type == R_STRING_TYPE_ASCII && needle < to) is true, so line 187 rewinds needle to 0; the line 72 loop then re-decodes the same bytes to the identical state, repeating forever. The guard at line 185 fails the Guard-Identity Audit for this sink: it bounds membership conditions but not progress, admitting the full failure set; the absent one-statement fix is a forward-progress bound on the backup (e.g., permitting the rewind only when it leaves needle strictly greater than the previous str_start, or equivalently a condition that guarantees the next iteration cannot rescan the identical position). Reachable hang on crafted input: CWE-835.

assumptions: min >= 3 is required for the witness; the fragment's only min guard at line 28 (if (!buf || !min)) rejects 0 and admits [1, INT_MAX], so 3..INT_MAX is admitted by the shown code; the actual caller value is not shown.
R_STRING_SCAN_BUFFER_SIZE is the declared capacity of tmp (line 4); the tmp-write sinks (lines 161, 166-167, 183) are bounded by lines 128 and 165 and were audited safe under that capacity.
buf capacity is len bytes (line 27), with len bounded to [1, ST32_MAX] by line 23.
limitations: Charset path (lines 47-50): int overflow in outlen = len * 4 with len up to ST32_MAX and calloc(len,4) over-allocation require RABIN2_CHARSET plus unshown r_charset_encode_str shrink/overflow semantics to corrupt memory; not confirmable from the fragment.
A possible r_utf8_encode error return for surrogate runes (would make i regress) depends on unshown callee contract; not confirmed.
If a console break hook is registered (line 70/73), it could eventually abort the loop, but the fragment shows it may be NULL and never guarantees termination.
The r_read_le32 sink (line 78) is protected by line 77 and the utf decode/w[0..8] reads (lines 84/95-109/131/136/141) by lines 72/93/128; no OOB read or write is confirmed in the shown fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched counterpart of Vim's eval7: the unbounded-recursion sink (recursive re-entries through eval1/eval_func at lines 181/225) is protected by the verbatim recursion guard `if (recurse == 1000)` at line 43, paired with `++recurse;` (line 48) and `--recurse;` (line 280), capping active evaluation depth at 1000 and excluding depth >= 1000 on every path. No remaining sink has a demonstrable in-fragment failure set: the ufunc dereference at line 168 has no shown NULL producer, all format strings are compile-time literals, and string reads are bounded by NUL-checked advances. Verdict: NOT vulnerable.

assumptions: *arg points into a NUL-terminated expression buffer (Vim's argument convention), which bounds the byte reads at lines 30, 99, 136-145.
get_lambda_tv returning OK (line 160) produces a partial with non-NULL pt_func per its standard semantics, so `rettv->vval.v_partial->pt_func` (line 163) has no in-fragment NULL producer.
`recurse` (static int, line 15) is mutated only by `++recurse;` (line 48) and `--recurse;` (line 280), making the `==` at line 43 equivalent to `>=` for exclusion of depth >= 1000.
limitations: A NULL-dereference candidate for `ufunc` at lines 163-171 (absent fix form `if (ufunc == NULL)`) is not confirmable: no shown branch, parse, or return status in the fragment admits a NULL pt_func/v_partial while ret == OK; per the NULL rules this is demoted rather than a finding.
Extreme recursion causes a controlled fail-closed error (lines 45-46), a robustness property, not a reachable DoS, since the depth cap excludes the crashing depth range.

If an enclosing caller could supply `*arg` without NUL termination, the line 149-150 advance would be unbounded; this relies on an unshown environmental fact and is recorded as an assumption rather than a confirmed failure.
An error-abort/longjmp skipping `--recurse` would only raise the counter and make the guard more restrictive (fail-closed); no failing value becomes admitted.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in OP_ARGARY/OP_BLKPUSH: the environment-stack guard `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1` does not account for the keyword-argument bit kd. With kd==1 and MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2 (the exact boundary the guard admits), `stack[m1+r+m2+1]` (OP_ARGARY line 672) and `stack[m1+r+m2+kd]` (OP_BLKPUSH line 1176), computed on `stack = e->stack + 1`, dereference e->stack[m1+r+m2+2], one element past the environment array. The missing one-statement fix is `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+kd+1`.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read (CWE-125). kd==1 (decoded from bytecode operand b at line 623) selects line 672 in the branch `if (kd)` at line 670. On the lv!=0 path, stack = e->stack + 1 (line 641), so line 672 reads e->stack[m1+r+m2+2]. The only guard, line 639 `if (MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1)`, admits MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2 (capacity established by the sibling guarded accesses `b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e)` at lines 252/267), i.e. the access index equals the array length — out of bounds by one. The guard is the same object/type and nothing mutates the values after it, but it is off by the kd term the sink consumes (bound off-by-one). Absent fix statement: `if (MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+kd+1)`.

Heap OOB read (CWE-125). kd is decoded at line 1158; with kd==1 the read `stack[m1+r+m2+kd]` (line 1176; the identical read is also made by the nil-probe at line 1172) equals e->stack[1+m1+r+m2+1] = e->stack[m1+r+m2+2] because stack = e->stack + 1 (line 1170). The guard at lines 1165-1166 (`MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1`) admits MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2, for which that index is one past the environment array (capacity from the access convention at lines 252/267). No later statement constrains len or kd before the sink; the guard fails the identity audit by the missing +kd term. Absent fix statement: `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+kd+1`.

assumptions: e->stack has MRB_ENV_LEN(e) elements — established by the fragment's own guarded sibling accesses `e->stack[b]` under `b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e)` (lines 252-253 and 267-268).
Instruction operands b (and thus m1, r, m2, kd, lv) are bytecode-supplied entry-point input with the masked residual ranges shown at lines 620-624 and 1155-1159.
Crafted bytecode (.mrb) is the threat model for interpreter-side entry-point analysis per category (a).
limitations: The failing boundary requires the runtime environment length to equal m1+r+m2+2, a value the shown guards explicitly admit but whose exact runtime production (environment capture depth/size) is not shown in this fragment; this caps confidence at the fragile-boundary band.

Unsized operand indexing (syms[b] line 120, pool[b] line 53, register writes regs[a]/regs[b], and the OP_JMPUW main-path target at line 322 without an irep->ilen check) follows the VM's load-time-validated/compiler-trusted bytecode convention shared by every jump/operand opcode (e.g., OP_JMP line 276); since the pair differs by exactly one statement, these are out of scope for this verdict and are demoted rather than reported.
Null-deref of uvenv results is properly guarded at lines 638 and 1165, and was not treated as a finding.

verdict.summary: Both dangerous operations carry their own protective statements: line 14 rejects size > r_size(op1) before count is computed (line 18), so the search loop at line 27 can only read indices within [0, r_size(op1)-1]; lines 20-21 divert size == 0 to found before ch = pat[0] at line 25. The backward empty-string placement is a semantic oddity with no memory or security consequence.

assumptions: r_size(op)/r_size(op1) return the true byte lengths of the two t_string operands, so a pattern with size >= 1 has valid bytes [0, size-1].

The operand stack has depth for push(2), and Ghostscript's push(2) semantics place a copy of op1 (rsize == r_size(op1)) at op[-3], making the line 47 subtraction `rsize -= count + size` safe because count + size <= r_size(op1) on every found path.
check_read_type at lines 12-13 enforces t_string for both operands before any bytes pointer is used.
limitations: For backward search with size == 0, the match is reported at the string start (ptr is not advanced to the end before goto found at line 21); this is a correctness/robustness oddity with no memory-safety or security-relevant consequence in the shown code.

Out-of-bounds or type violations that would require the operand refs to lie about r_size, or stack-depth exhaustion by push(2), depend on interpreter invariants not shown in the fragment and are not demonstrated findings.
A loop read past the end would require size > r_size(op1) with count = r_size(op1) - size underflowing; that state is excluded verbatim by the line 14 guard, so it cannot be used as a witness.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains the size-bound guard `if (unlikely(size > RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ)) return NULL;` before `len = round_up(size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ, 8)` and before storing `size | BPF_RINGBUF_BUSY_BIT` into the header length field. This guard constrains the same u64 `size` value, at the same type, on every path to those sinks, excluding all values above `RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ`, and no failing value is derivable from the shown code. The remaining dangerous operations (producer-position advance and masked data offset) are each protected by shown guards/capacity conventions. No confirmed vulnerability.

assumptions: Line 11 (`if (len > rb->mask + 1)`) establishes the fragment's access convention that the ring-buffer data capacity is `rb->mask + 1`, so any offset `prod_pos & rb->mask` at line 34 lies within capacity.

`RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ` is the module constant used precisely so that `size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ` and the u32 `len`/header-length fields remain representable; its numeric value is not displayed in the fragment.
`BPF_RINGBUF_BUSY_BIT` and `BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ` are fixed kernel constants; the recorded record-size domain fits the header length field after line 7's bound.
limitations: The numeric value of `RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ` is not visible, so the excluded bound of line 7 is stated symbolically (`size > RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ`); a concrete overflowing witness could not be enumerated without that constant.
A cumulative `u64` wraparound of `prod_pos` at line 24 would require ~`2^64/len` reservations and is not a single-call failure derivable from the shown statements.
The exact field width of `hdr->len` is inferred from the conventional header layout (u32 length + pg_off) rather than displayed in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The do-while body reads spans[1] even when num_spans == 1 because the guard at L9 only rejects num_spans == 0, so an admission of a single-span call produces an out-of-bounds read past a 1-element span array; the guard should reject num_spans <= 1.

evidence.reason: num_spans is an unsigned parameter whose residual range after the only guard (L9 "if (num_spans == 0)") is 1..UINT_MAX; the witness num_spans == 1 is admitted by that guard, and the do-while at L14-L94 executes its body at least once (condition --num_spans > 1 is evaluated after the body), so L15 dereferences spans[1] on a 1-element span array. The span-array capacity is established by the fragment's own access convention: the loop advances spans (L93) and indexes only 0..num_spans-1, with spans[1] valid only when num_spans >= 2. The guard-identity audit resolves no drift (same unsigned value, no interleaved mutation between L9 and L15), but the guard's boundary is wrong (== 0 instead of <= 1) and its admitted set {1..UINT_MAX} intersects the failure set at {1}; no other conditional (L16, L55, L88, L94) constrains num_spans before the read. The absent one-statement fix is "if (num_spans <= 1) return CAIRO_STATUS_SUCCESS;". The OOB-read result is then consumed as span geometry (len and composite width at L51), enabling crash or information disclosure; primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: The spans array contains exactly num_spans elements, per the pointer+count parameter contract, reinforced by the fragment's own iteration convention at L93-L94 which indexes only 0..num_spans-1.
r->_buf has a capacity related to r->u.composite.run_length (access convention at L16, where spans with len >= run_length are routed to direct compositing instead of the buffer).
limitations: S2: a heap overflow of r->_buf via the else branch (L87/L89) is not confirmable from the fragment alone: no allocation or declaration of _buf is shown, and a failing partial-coverage span width exceeding the buffer is not derivable from shown data.

With num_spans == 1, if the OOB len value happens to be > 1 and coverage is partial, L89 could pass a garbage length to memset (follow-on OOB write); the magnitude depends on unshown memory contents, so it is not confirmed.
Negative span widths or unsorted spans (which would make pixman composite sizes negative) require a span-ordering invariant not shown.
A NULL dereference of r is not demonstrated: no NULL producer is visible in the fragment.

verdict.summary: get_visual_text computes *lenp at lines 24/29 from the raw, unvalidated visual-selection byte columns (VIsual.col, curwin->w_cursor.col; only lnum equality is enforced at line 8) and then uses *lenp - 1 as a byte offset into the NUL-terminated line buffer at line 35. Because no shown statement bounds *lenp above by the line length, a selection ending at or past the end of the line makes (*mb_ptr2len)(*pp + (*lenp - 1)) read past the NUL terminator (heap out-of-bounds read, CWE-125). The guards at lines 8, 21, 31-32, and 33 cover only line equality, ordering, and the lower bound of *lenp; the absent one-statement fix is an upper-bound check such as 'if (*lenp > (int)STRLEN(*pp)) *lenp = (int)STRLEN(*pp);' placed before the mb_ptr2len call.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Witness: VIsual.lnum == w_cursor.lnum (line 8), w_cursor.col = 0, VIsual.col = STRLEN(*pp)+1; line 21's LT_POS branch admits it, line 31 sees a non-NUL first byte so line 32 does not fire, line 33 admits *lenp = STRLEN(*pp)+2 > 0, and line 35 then reads char bytes at *pp + STRLEN(*pp)+1, one past the NUL terminator, overflowing the line object inside mb_ptr2len. A negative *lenp (read before *pp) is not separately demonstrated: under LT_POS's standard same-line column ordering, lines 24/29 cannot produce a negative span; the confirmed failure is the oversize span on the upper side.
Downstream consumers of the returned *lenp/*pp (e.g., yank/delete operators) are not shown, so no separate claim is made about them.

verdict.summary: The fragment guards the only dangerous reuse point: the refill of a fragment packet is conditioned on ipf_handle_frag() returning false (`if (!ipf_handle_frag(ipf, pkt, dl_type, zone, now, hash_basis)) { dp_packet_batch_refill(pb, pkt, pb_idx); }`). verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. No attacker-controlled input, injection, crypto, path/URL, or authz sink is present in the shown fragment.

verdict.summary: In the non-process branch of crun_command_exec, the loop at line 43 (i < argc - first_arg) makes one extra iteration whose read at line 44 reaches argv[first_arg + i + 1] with index argc — one past the last live argument (argc-1) and the argv NULL terminator — and the length field at line 41 is set to the whole argc instead of the number of arguments actually copied (argc - first_arg - 1). The NULL terminator value is stored as a phantom array entry while args_len overcounts it, so any length-driven walk of process->args sees a NULL inside the string array. The decisive fix, process->args_len = argc - first_arg - 1 / i < argc - first_arg - 1, is absent.

evidence.reason: Off-by-one read: with the loop bound at line 43 ("for (i = 0; i < argc - first_arg; i++)") the last admitted i is argc - first_arg - 1 (line 17 guarantees argc - first_arg >= 2 on this branch, so that iteration always runs), making the index at this sink first_arg + i + 1 = argc, one past the last live argv entry (indices 0..argc-1; line 19 consumes argv[first_arg] as the container id, so the command args after it number only argc - first_arg - 1). The value read is the argv NULL terminator, which is stored into process->args[argc - first_arg - 1] while line 41 (args_len = argc) declares the whole span as strings. The guarding statements on the path (line 17 min-arg assert) fail the Guard-Identity Audit (wrong target: minimum count, no upper bound on i), and the decisive bound fix (argc - first_arg - 1) is absent at lines 41/43. Primary CWE-125.

Incorrect length calculation (CWE-682): args_len is set to the whole argc, but only argc - first_arg - 1 arguments follow the container id (argv[first_arg], line 19) and are copied at line 44. The array additionally contains a NULL entry copied from argv[argc] plus zero-filled tail entries from line 42, so any consumer that walks args_len entries of the exec process spec (passed at line 92) traverses NULL entries declared as strings. The absent fix is process->args_len = argc - first_arg - 1;.

assumptions: argv's live argument span is 0..argc-1, as used by the fragment itself (line 19 consumes argv[first_arg] as the container id; the loop intends to copy only the arguments that follow it).
The allocation at line 42 ((argc + 1) * sizeof(...)) plus the NULL write at line 45 keep the write side in bounds (index argc - first_arg <= argc), so no OOB write is claimed.
limitations: The LISTEN_FDS block (lines 28-31) is an unvalidated strtoll result feeding preserve_fds += listen_fds; it is demoted because the field types and the FD-duplicating consumer are inside unshown code, so no wrap/truncation or FD-leak failure is demonstrable within this fragment (it is also present in current upstream and outside this fix pair).

A downstream NULL dereference from the phantom NULL entry requires an unshown length-walking consumer; within the fragment the confirmed mechanism is the one-past read of argv[argc] and the overcounted args_len.

If one assumes the main()-style argv[argc] == NULL invariant (not shown in the fragment), the read at index argc lands on the terminator rather than raw out-of-bounds memory; either interpretation yields the same absent fix and verdict.

verdict.summary: bgp_capability_msg_parse performs an unconditional fixed-size memcpy of sizeof(struct capability_mp_data)=4 bytes from pnt+3 even when the attacker-chosen capability length hdr->length is less than 4 (e.g., 0), reading past the message boundary end defined at line 12 (heap OOB read, CWE-125). Additionally, the continue at line 66 for invalid attacker-supplied afi/safi skips the pnt advance at line 102, causing non-termination of the parse loop (CWE-835). The missing fix is a lower-bound check on hdr->length before the memcpy.

evidence.reason: CWE-125 heap out-of-bounds read. hdr->length (u_char at pnt+2) is attacker-controlled with residual range 0..255 and no shown minimum; the only size guard, line 41 "if ((pnt + hdr->length + 3) > end)", admits hdr->length in {0,1,2,3} and thus guarantees only hdr->length bytes at pnt+3, while this memcpy copies the fixed sizeof(struct capability_mp_data)=4 bytes. Witness: capabilities [SET][MP][len=0] with pnt+3 == end passes line 17 ("if (pnt + 3 > end)", equality admitted), line 27-28 action check, and line 41, then this memcpy reads bytes [end, end+4), 4 bytes past the message boundary end = pnt + length (line 12). Guard-Identity Audit: line 41 fails (wrong-magnitude/transformation drift — guard bound is hdr->length, sink consumes unconstrained 4 bytes). Absent fix: a check such as "if (hdr->length < sizeof(struct capability_mp_data))" before this copy.

CWE-835 reachable non-termination. afi/safi are attacker-supplied (lines 54-55 from packet bytes copied at line 49) with no shown constraint before the validator call at line 61; for an invalid value such as afi=0, bgp_afi_safi_valid_indices returns false and this continue jumps to the loop condition "while (pnt < end)" (line 14) without executing the sole advance "pnt += hdr->length + 3;" (line 102), which sits after the branch. pnt and end are unchanged, so pnt < end stays true forever. Absent fix: advancing pnt before the MP branch / before this continue.

assumptions: sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) == 4 bytes (afi uint16_t + reserved uint8_t + safi uint8_t); even without the exact value, any fixed size >= 1 overreads when hdr->length == 0.
The valid message region is [pnt, end) per "end = pnt + length" (line 12); every in-fragment read is guarded against end (lines 17, 41), establishing the access convention.
hdr->length is a single attacker-controlled byte read at pnt+2 (u_char, range 0..255).

bgp_afi_safi_valid_indices returns false for at least some attacker-chosen afi/safi (e.g., afi = AFI_UNSPEC or out-of-range), which is the purpose of the branch at lines 61-67; afi is 16-bit and valid AFIs are a small set.
limitations: The continuation path via PEER_FLAG_OVERRIDE_CAPABILITY (line 58-59) also loops forever but requires the operator-configured flag, so it is not attacker-controlled and is not the primary trigger.

The layout of the underlying buffer beyond `end` is not shown; the overread magnitude is bounded (up to 3 bytes past the message window in the common len=1..3 cases, 4 bytes for len=0) and severity is DoS/information disclosure rather than memory corruption.
No integer-overflow, injection, crypto, or authz sink exists in this fragment: format strings are literal, and the afi/safi array writes (lines 79/82/88/89) are gated by the validator at line 61.

verdict.summary: The only dangerous operation is the dereference of the map iterator at L6, whose failure set is it == idInfoMap.end(). STFATAL's non-returning behavior is established by the framework's fail-closed diagnostic-abort rule and the macro's name rather than by an in-fragment [[noreturn]] annotation; if one reads STFATAL as a non-terminating log, the iterator dereference at L6 would be UB, but that reading contradicts the diagnostic-abort treatment and is therefore not credited.

verdict.summary: The fragment is LuaJIT's fixed finderrfunc. Every dangerous sink carries its protective statement: the cframe-NULL dereference at line 6 is guarded on all paths by the verbatim check `if (cf == NULL)` / `return 0;` (lines 12-13) immediately after `cf = cframe_prev(cf)` (line 11), and all frame/frame-1 stack reads (including `(frame-1)->u32.lo` at line 28 and `savestack(L, frame-1)` at line 42) are bounded by the outer condition `while (frame > bot && cf)` (line 5), which admits only frame >= bot+1 so frame-1 >= bot. Negation `-cframe_nres(cf)` could wrap at INT32_MIN only if a cframe header were corrupted, which is not derivable from the shown code.
Any out-of-bounds scenario relying on attacker-forged frame-header fields (type tags, ftsz) is not derivable: bytecode execution cannot write those headers directly.
NVD-style weak-crypto, injection, and authorization checks are absent from this fragment by construction.

verdict.summary: In stl_remove_degenerate, when both neighbor1 and neighbor2 of a degenerate facet are the -1 'no neighbor' sentinel (a value the fragment itself produces and tests for at lines 48/51 and writes at line 74), the independent if-branches at lines 48-50 and 51-53 unconditionally call stl_update_connects_remove_1(stl, neighbor2) and stl_update_connects_remove_1(stl, neighbor1), passing -1 as the index. verdict.summary: A negative request length is admitted by the `remain >= len` branch (line 11), copied unchecked into `rlen` (line 12), and reaches `memcpy` (line 20), where the int-to-size_t conversion wraps -1 into SIZE_MAX and drives an effectively unbounded copy that corrupts `buf`. `dp` is non-NULL when dynamicGetbuf is invoked (no NULL producer is shown in the fragment).
`len` is a length/count parameter whose full declared int domain is analyzed because the fragment shows no minimum and no call site.

`buf` capacity and `dp->data` allocation size are not shown, so an independently bounded OOB (CWE-787) cannot be confirmed; the finding rests on the SIZE_MAX copy generated by the signed-to-unsigned conversion.

verdict.summary: ex_retab is the patched (fixed) form after Vim patch 8.2.4359. The decisive protective statement `if (vcol >= MAXCOL) { emsg(_(e_resulting_text_too_long)); break; }` (lines 156-160) bounds the virtual column and therefore the retab whitespace length used at lines 91/128/130, stopping the unbounded line-growth crash loop. Every other dangerous sink carries its own guard: `alloc` NULL is checked at lines 131-132 and 166-167, the allocation capacity at line 130 is byte-exact for the memmoves at 134-136 and fill loop at 138-139, `new_ts` is range-validated at 50-61, `tabstop_set`/`u_save`/`ml_replace` returns are checked, and `new_ts_str` is NULL-guarded at line 195. No failing value derivable from the shown code reaches any sink.

assumptions: object capacity for the retab write is established by the allocation itself, line 130: `new_line = alloc(old_len - col + start_col + len + 1);`, which is exactly prefix(start_col) + whitespace(len) + suffix(old_len - col + 1), so the memmoves at 134-136 and the fill loop at 138-139 stay inside it
start_col <= col <= old_len: start_col is set from the current col at line 77, col only advances via mb_ptr2len/++col (162/164) and the scan stops at NUL (153-154), so col never exceeds STRLEN(ptr)
vcol < MAXCOL at the retab block is established entirely in-fragment: line 155 is the only assignment `vcol += chartabsize(...)`, immediately checked by lines 156-160 before any retab use at 91/98
new_ts >= 1 at the divisions (103/109): negative rejected at 50-59, zero replaced by curbuf->b_p_ts at 60-61
limitations: the same function text is the pre-image of the follow-up hardening patch 8.2.4362, which adds `new_len = old_len - col + start_col + len + 1; if (new_len >= MAXCOL) ...` before the alloc; that cap is absent here, but an oversized alloc returns NULL and is handled by lines 131-132 and 166-167, so no attacker-reachable memory-safety failure is demonstrable in-fragment - it is a residual allocation-size hardening concern

verdict.summary: NULL-pointer dereference in call_qftf_func: the list pointer returned by the user-supplied 'quickfixtextfunc' callback is stored from rettv.vval.v_list (line 42) and dereferenced at line 43 after only checking rettv.v_type == VAR_LIST (line 40). A VAR_LIST return with a NULL v_list (Vim null-list value) reaches the dereference because the missing guard `rettv.vval.v_list != NULL` is absent, causing a crash.

evidence.reason: qftf_list is assigned rettv.vval.v_list (line 42), the return value of the user-configured callback invoked at line 38 (call_callback(cb, 0, &rettv, 1, args)). The only guard before the dereference, `if (rettv.v_type == VAR_LIST)` at line 40, constrains the type discriminator, not v_list itself - wrong-target drift (Guard-Identity Audit class 3) - and admits a VAR_LIST whose vval.v_list is NULL (Vim null-list representation), which no shown statement excludes. The dereference at line 43 then accesses NULL, a CWE-476 NULL-pointer dereference. The absent fix statement is a check on `rettv.vval.v_list != NULL` before the dereference; the line 23 dict_alloc_lock NULL check protects a different object and does not cover this path.

assumptions: call_callback invokes the user-configured 'quickfixtextfunc' function and stores its return typval in rettv (standard Vim semantics of the shown call).

A Vim VAR_LIST typval may carry vval.v_list == NULL (null-list value representation); this invariant is library semantics, not quoted in the fragment, so the witness rests on one external semantic link.
limitations: The NULL-producing case depends on the Vim null-list representation of a VARCHAR/VAR_LIST-byte return, which is not literally defined inside the fragment; under a reading where VAR_LIST always carries a non-NULL list, the dereference cannot be shown to fail, hence confidence is calibrated at 0.74.
Whether the attacker can set 'quickfixtextfunc' depends on the surrounding configuration/scripting context not shown here; the sink analysis assumes that demonstrated threat model.

verdict.summary: QPaintEngineEx::stroke is the fixed member of the pair: the empty-path guard `if (path.isEmpty()) return;` (lines 9-10) is present and excludes elementCount == 0 from every sink that unconditionally reads `points[0]/points[1]` (lines 139, 145-146, 197-199, 203, 211-212) or dereferences `types` (lines 112, 168), passing the Guard-Identity Audit (const `path`, no interleaved mutation, points/pointCount read from the same path after the guard). For non-empty paths, all reads are bounded by the fragment's own arithmetic `lastPoint = points + (pointCount<<1)` (line 88) and the strict loop conditions `while (points < lastPoint)` (lines 111, 141, 167, 206), with the type-advance lock-step (++types with points+=2; types+=3 with points+=6) keeping `types` inside [0, pointCount). The only residual failure (a caller-constructed malformed path whose trailing CurveToElement is not backed by 6 points, or a curve-data type hitting `default:` without advancement) requires unshown caller data and is not derivable from the shown fragment.

assumptions: QVectorPath::isEmpty() has its standard documented semantics: true exactly when elementCount() == 0.

The fragment establishes by its own arithmetic (line 88 `lastPoint = points + (pointCount<<1)`, and paired reads `points[0], points[1]`) that `points` spans 2*elementCount qreals and `types` spans elementCount entries; this is the in-fragment access convention used for all bounds.
`if (types)` (lines 110, 166) guarantees the `switch (*types)` dereference is non-NULL on the branch that executes it.
`new StrokeHandler(...)` (line 13) failure is not attacker-controllable; Qt `new` throws/aborts rather than returning NULL.
limitations: A malformed caller-supplied QVectorPath holding a trailing lone CurveToElement not backed by six qreals (or a CurveToElementData at a position the loop lands on, hitting `default:` with no pointer advance) could cause an out-of-bounds points read (CWE-125) or non-termination (CWE-835). No shown statement in the fragment produces such a types array, so per the derivability rule this cannot be confirmed from the shown code.
Integer overflow of `pointCount<<1` (line 88) would require elementCount > 2^30 with a corresponding backing allocation, which is not derivable from the fragment.
The debug-only qDebug() log write (line 4) is a Qt streamed operator<< with no format directives; log-injection into an unshown backend is out of scope.
StrokeHandler's internal storage behavior (fixed-capacity versus auto-growing) for the `elementCount()+4` constructor argument is not shown, so output-side overflow cannot be confirmed.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in drill_parse_T_code carries its own protective statement: the aperture index (L73/L127/L185) is bounded by `if (tool_num < TOOL_MIN || tool_num >= TOOL_MAX)` at L63; the file-cursor rewind at L25 is reachable only when `(fd->ptr + 2) < fd->datalen` at L22 guarantees both probe reads succeed, so the rewind lands at entry-1 >= 0 under the documented post-'T' calling convention; `apert->parameter[0]` (L115/L136/L214) is guarded by `if (apert != NULL)` (L110) and by allocation-plus-NULL-check (L129/L186); all printf-family calls use literal format strings. No sink has a shown-derivable failing value.

assumptions: The fragment's own guard at L63 defines the aperture-indexing convention: image->aperture is indexed over [0, TOOL_MAX-1]; TOOL_MIN/TOOL_MAX are program constants not defined in the fragment, with TOOL_MIN >= 1 implied by the T00-unload special case at L60-L61.
gerbv_aperture_t.parameter is a fixed array containing at least index 0 (only constant index 0 is used: L115, L136, L214).
gerb_fgetc returns EOF without advancing when at the end of the buffer, so the probe reads at L23/L24 cannot read out of bounds even without the L22 guard.
The file cursor on entry is past a consumed 'T' (function name 'drill_parse_T_code' and the L15 comment 'after the T'), so the L22-guarded rewind at L25 lands at entry-1 >= 0.
limitations: If a caller invoked drill_parse_T_code with the cursor at position 0 (no preceding 'T' consumed), `fd->ptr -= 4` at L25 could drive the cursor negative and `get_line` at L26 would read out of bounds; that entry state is not derivable from any shown statement and would require a caller-contract violation outside the fragment.
image->drill_stats / stats NULL deref (L27, L147, L220, L223): no in-fragment NULL producer; allocation occurs outside the fragment.
NaN drill sizes from read_double (L83) bypass `size <= 0. || size >= 10000.` (L104) and reach a double field and the stats list — robustness only, no memory-safety consequence.
Integer overflow of `8 * tool_num` at L196 is not derivable because TOOL_MAX's magnitude is not shown in the fragment.
CWE-117-style log-content injection via tmps at L30/L48 is not confirmed: the target is the application's in-process message store with no security decision depending on its content.
A 'TxxC' at the exact EOF boundary fails the L22 guard and is mis-classified as junk text (L40 path) — a parsing-robustness behavior, not a memory-safety issue.
The `'\n'/\r'` restore branch at L175-L176 is unreachable dead code (temp == EOF inside that block).

verdict.summary: The capability-header reads (`action = *pnt` at L23 and `memcpy(&cap, pnt + 1, sizeof(struct capability))` at L26) are protected by the verbatim bound check `if (pnt + 3 > end)` (L16), which excludes the only failing input state (1-2 bytes remaining, where the 2-byte struct copy would over-read). Capability bodies are bounded by L43, and the afc array indices are equality-whitelisted to {1,2}x{1,2,4} by L61-L65 before use. No attacker-derivable witness reaches any security-relevant sink, so this is the fixed member of the pair.

assumptions: struct capability is the Quagga layout {u_char code; u_char length; u_char mpc[];} so sizeof(struct capability) == 2; the fragment's later use of cap.mpc.afi/cap.mpc.safi (L53-L54) as data at offset 2 is consistent with mpc being the byte-stream tail, making the L16 `pnt + 3 > end` check exactly cover the L26 memcpy extent.

The afc arrays (peer->afc_recv, peer->afc, peer->afc_nego) are sized [AFI_MAX][SAFI_MAX] with AFI_MAX = 3 and SAFI_MAX >= 6 in the parent codebase, so every index in the whitelisted set {1,2} x {1,2,4} is in bounds.
`length` describes a valid buffer of `length` bytes beginning at `pnt` (caller-supplied message section); `end = pnt + length` (L11) delimits it.
limitations: The `continue` at L58 skips `pnt += cap.length + 3` (L104), so an MP capability received while PEER_FLAG_OVERRIDE_CAPABILITY is set would loop forever (CWE-835-style non-termination); this is demoted because peer->flags is operator configuration with no in-fragment producer, so the failing witness is not derivable from the shown code.

L53-L54 read cap.mpc.afi/cap.mpc.safi from the uninitialized tail of the 2-byte local struct (only code+length were copied at L26); the values are not attacker-controlled and are equality-validated at L61-L65 before any array indexing, so there is no security-relevant consumption.
If a different struct capability layout with sizeof(struct capability) > 2 were in use, the L16 check would not cover the full memcpy extent; that layout is not shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Fail-open status-handling flaw: the checks at lines 217 and 235 abort only when seccomp_rule_add returns -EFAULT (the benign 'unknown syscall' case per the comment), so every other negative return (e.g., -EINVAL, -ENOMEM, -EEXIST) is treated as success and the failed blocklist rule is silently omitted from the exported seccomp filter, weakening sandbox enforcement. The absent one-statement fix is 'if (r < 0 && r != -EFAULT /* unknown syscall */)'.

evidence.reason: r from seccomp_rule_add at lines 214/216 is consumed at this decision with no intervening assignment (no drift class). The guard's own 'r < 0' term classifies negative returns as failure, but the operator '==' admits every negative errno except -EFAULT onto the success path, so a failed rule add (e.g., -EINVAL/-ENOMEM/-EEXIST) proceeds to export (line 266) and install (lines 271-272) a filter missing that block — fail-open seccomp enforcement (CWE-754). The absent fix form is the fail-closed check 'if (r < 0 && r != -EFAULT /* unknown syscall */)'.

Identical inverted status check for the nondevel list: r from seccomp_rule_add at lines 231/233 is treated as success for every negative value except -EFAULT, silently dropping rules such as ptrace/perf_event_open/personality from the installed filter when the add fails (CWE-754). The absent fix form is 'if (r < 0 && r != -EFAULT /* unknown syscall */)'.

assumptions: Loops at 206, 223, 244 are bounded by G_N_ELEMENTS over static tables defined in-fragment (lines 50-111, 118-126, 132-141).
Loop at 191 is bounded by the sentinel terminator of the static extra_arches arrays assigned at lines 162/172.
seccomp_rule_add returns negative errno on failure; the fragment's own 'r < 0' probe at line 217 encodes that convention.
limitations: A concrete non-EFAULT failure of seccomp_rule_add (e.g., -ENOMEM or an arch-invalid rule) is not produced inside the fragment; it requires libseccomp/OS state, which is the fragile boundary of this witness, hence confidence 0.7.
seccomp_rule_add_exact return values at lines 256/261 are deliberately ignored per the in-fragment comment at lines 240-242; treated as an intentional limitation, not the finding.
Unchecked lseek at line 269 has no security-relevant consumer and is demoted.
All format strings in the fragment are literals with matching argument types; no format-string injection sink exists.

verdict.summary: In mrb_vm_exec, the send path declares `mrb_value recv, blk;` (line 413) without initializing `blk`, and no entry path into L_SENDB_SYM (OP_SEND/OP_SENDB/OP_SSEND/OP_SSENDB/L_SEND_SYM) ever assigns it. `blk` is then read uninitialized: `if (mrb_proc_p(blk))` (446), `struct RProc *p = mrb_proc_ptr(blk);` (447) with `p->flags |= MRB_PROC_ORPHAN;` (449) on every ordinary C-function method-call return, and it is passed to `prepare_missing` on the missing-method path (421) and in OP_SUPER (570). An indeterminate tag equal to MRB_TT_PROC yields a garbage RProc pointer that is dereferenced and written through, enabling memory corruption. The absent one-statement fix is an initialization of `blk` (e.g., `blk = mrb_nil_value();`) before these uses.

evidence.reason: Uninitialized read of `blk`: declared without initializer at line 413 (`mrb_value recv, blk;`); all entry paths into the L_SENDB_SYM block (OP_SSEND 385-388, OP_SSENDB 391-393, OP_SEND 396-397, L_SEND_SYM 399-403, OP_SENDB 405-407) assign only regs[a], insn, c, mid, never blk. This read executes whenever a C-function method is dispatched (branch at 430) and returns without exception (guard at 444 `if (mrb->exc) goto L_RAISE;` does not fire), i.e., an ordinary method call. The indeterminate value is type-dispatched by mrb_proc_p; if its tag equals MRB_TT_PROC, line 447 `struct RProc *p = mrb_proc_ptr(blk);` casts the indeterminate payload to a struct RProc* and line 449 `p->flags |= MRB_PROC_ORPHAN;` writes through that garbage pointer. Primary CWE-457 (uninitialized use); the absent one-statement fix is an initialization of `blk` before use.

evidence.snippet: m = prepare_missing(mrb, recv, mid, &cls, a, &c, blk, 0);
evidence.reason: The same uninitialized `blk` (declared line 413, never assigned on any shown path) is passed as the block argument to prepare_missing on the missing-method path (branch at 420), so the indeterminate value is consumed by the method_missing machinery. Guard-Identity Audit: no initialization, NULL probe, or any protective statement exists between the declaration at 413 and this use. Absent fix: `blk = mrb_nil_value();` (or an OP_SENDB-aware initialization) before this call. CWE-457.

evidence.snippet: m = prepare_missing(mrb, recv, mid, &cls, a, &b, blk, 1);
evidence.reason: OP_SUPER declares `mrb_value recv, blk;` at line 533 without initialization, and no statement between 533 and 570 assigns `blk`; the indeterminate value is passed to prepare_missing when the superclass method is undefined (branch at 569). Same absence of any protective statement (CWE-457); the absent fix is the initialization of `blk` before this use.

assumptions: mrb_proc_p reads the value-type tag of an mrb_value and mrb_proc_ptr extracts its pointer payload as struct RProc*, per their name-implied standard semantics.
The VM-stack slot backing `blk` at the declaration point holds indeterminate bytes (it is never written between declaration and use).
limitations: The concrete corruption magnitude (address written by `p->flags |= MRB_PROC_ORPHAN;`) depends on the indeterminate stack contents, i.e., the specific failing tag value MRB_TT_PROC is memory-state dependent; the uninitialized read itself is guaranteed on the ordinary C-method-call path.

Operations indexed by decoded bytecode operands (regs[a], pool[b], syms[b], irep->reps[b], pc-relative jumps, pool-string lengths) have no in-fragment capacity or size evidence, so out-of-bounds there is not demonstrable from this fragment alone and is left as a limitation rather than a finding.
OP_ENTER/OP_HASH/OP_APOST argument-packing behaviors depend on the unshown ci->n/bidx conventions and nregs guarantees; no confirmed in-fragment failing value was derivable for them.

verdict.summary: In parse_die, the loop bound `i < abbrev->count - 1` underflows when `abbrev->count == 0` (an unsigned count with no shown minimum), making the bound SIZE_MAX and admitting i = 0, 1, ... The body then writes/reads `die->attr_values[i]` and `abbrev->defs[i]` out of bounds on every iteration. The absent one-statement fix is an underflow-proof bound such as `i + 1 < abbrev->count`.

evidence.reason: Index i comes from the L6 loop bound `i < abbrev->count - 1`. `abbrev->count` is unsigned with no shown minimum, so count == 0 is admitted and `abbrev->count - 1` wraps to SIZE_MAX (CWE-191), admitting i = 0, 1, ... . The paired accesses `abbrev->defs[i]`/`die->attr_values[i]` inside a loop bounded by count establish the parallel-array convention (index space [0, count)), so at count == 0 the arrays hold 0 slots and this memset writes at `die->attr_values[0]` out of bounds, continuing for arbitrarily large i (CWE-787). The guard L6 fails the Guard-Identity Audit by transformation drift (the -1 is applied before the comparison), and the absent fix is `i + 1 < abbrev->count`, which yields `0 + 1 < 0` = false and skips the loop.

evidence.snippet:
buf = parse_attr_value(buf, buf_end - buf, &abbrev->defs[i],
			&die->attr_values[i], hdr, debug_str, debug_str_len, big_endian);
evidence.reason: Same underflowed loop index i (count == 0 admitted by L6 with no shown minimum) reaches `&abbrev->defs[i]` (out-of-bounds read of a def in a convention-derived 0-slot array, CWE-125) and `&die->attr_values[i]` (out-of-bounds write target, CWE-787). No guard between L6 and this call re-validates i; the absent fix is the underflow-proof bound `i + 1 < abbrev->count` (or an explicit `abbrev->count > 0` check before the loop).

assumptions: abbrev->count is an unsigned size-like count (it is subtracted by 1 and compared against size_t i), so count - 1 wraps to SIZE_MAX when count == 0; if signed, the comparison with size_t i converts -1 to SIZE_MAX, giving the same degenerate bound.

die->attr_values and abbrev->defs are parallel arrays whose intended index space is bounded by abbrev->count, established by the in-fragment paired accesses `&abbrev->defs[i]` and `&die->attr_values[i]` inside a loop bounded by count.
limitations: The actual allocations of die->attr_values and abbrev->defs are not shown in this fragment; their 0-slot capacity at count == 0 is inferred from the access convention, not from a visible allocation.
The producer of abbrev (i.e., whether count == 0 is attacker-reachable in practice) is not shown; count == 0 is admitted solely because no shown constraint excludes it from the unsigned value domain.

parse_attr_value's return value is used without a NULL check (if it returned NULL, `buf_end - buf` would be invalid), but no NULL producer is demonstrated in-fragment, so this is demoted to a limitation.

Whether parse_attr_value advances buf correctly on all inputs is not verifiable in-fragment; `buf_end - buf` underflow on over-advance would depend on unshown callee behavior and is not reported as a finding.

verdict.summary: In getInfoForId, an arbitrary id that is absent from idInfoMap makes find() (line 3) return end(); the guard at line 4 admits exactly that failing value, line 5 only streams to STFATAL with no shown return/abort/throw, and control falls through to `return it->second;` (line 7), dereferencing a past-the-end map iterator (undefined behavior). The absent one-statement fix is an early return (e.g., `return TerminalUserInfo();`) on the not-found path.

evidence.reason: S1 (line 7) dereferences the map iterator returned by `idInfoMap.find(id)` (line 3). `id` (line 1) is never validated or restricted, so any id absent from `idInfoMap` yields `it == idInfoMap.end()` — an outcome the fragment itself admits by branching on it at line 4. When the condition is true, the branch body only executes `STFATAL << ...` (line 5), which has no shown return, throw, or abort, so execution falls through to line 7 and dereferences the end() iterator (invalid/past-the-end dereference, undefined behavior). The guard-identity audit passes on same-value/same-type/no-mutation (there is no drift class), but the guard admits the sink's entire failure set and therefore protects nothing; the missing one-statement fix is an early `return TerminalUserInfo();` (or equivalent terminating statement) after line 5. Primary mechanism: unchecked not-found result dereferenced (CWE-476).

assumptions: `idInfoMap` is a std::map-like associative container whose `find` returns `end()` for an absent key — evidenced in-fragment by the `it == idInfoMap.end()` comparison at line 4.
The not-found state is reachable/expected: the fragment itself handles it at lines 4–6 and its diagnostic text ('no longer exists', line 5) contemplates an id that was previously present.
limitations: The definition of the `STFATAL` macro is not shown; if it internally aborts, the miss path would be fail-closed and this would not be vulnerable. Per the Verifiability Rule, that abort contract cannot be credited from the shown fragment.
Whether any caller can supply an id missing from `idInfoMap` is not shown here; reachability rests on the fragment's own handling of the miss case (lines 4–6).
Impact is undefined behavior from a past-the-end iterator dereference (typically a crash/garbage read); no write or corruption primitive is demonstrated, so severity is capped at medium.

verdict.summary: ReadTGAImage contains protective statements for every dangerous sink: the colormap write loops are guarded by the allocation-sizing clamp `if (image->colors < tga_info.colormap_index) image->colors=tga_info.colormap_index;` followed by `AcquireImageColormap(image,image->colors,...)`; the row index into the pixel cache is kept in [0, rows-1] by the offset clamp `if (offset >= image->rows) { base++; offset=base; }`; blob reads for RLE and pixel data are count-checked; colormap lookups are clamped via ConstrainColormapIndex; and the comment terminator writes are within the length+MagickPathExtent allocation. No demonstrated failing value reaches any sink.

assumptions: TGAInfo header fields read by ReadBlobLSBShort are unsigned short; `colormap_index + colormap_length` thus promotes to int with a maximum of 131070 and cannot wrap (line 122).

`AcquireImageColormap(image, image->colors, ...)` (lines 130/188) either allocates exactly `image->colors` entries (so `image->colors` is the colormap capacity) or returns MagickFalse and the reader aborts fail-closed via ThrowReaderException.

verdict.summary: ex_retab sizes a line allocation from vcol-derived len (alloc(old_len - col + start_col + len + 1)) with no bound on vcol, len, or the allocation size. A buffer line of many tabs with a large 'tabstop' (or repeated :retab) drives vcol and len arbitrarily large, causing uncontrolled memory allocation and, once vcol exceeds colnr_T range at the (colnr_T)vcol cast, corrupting size arithmetic (crash/out-of-memory, fixed upstream by MAXCOL bail-outs in patches 8.2.4359/8.2.4362 that are absent here).

evidence.reason: Allocation-size sink: len is set at line 128 (len = num_spaces + num_tabs) from len = vcol - start_vcol (line 91), and vcol accumulates unboundedly at line 155 (vcol += chartabsize(ptr + col, (colnr_T)vcol)) with no shown cap on vcol, len, or the computed size. new_ts is admitted in [1, TABSTOP_MAX] by lines 50/55/60-61 (the divisor guard is wrong-target drift: it does not bound num_spaces/len), and the only check after alloc is the NULL check at line 131, which does not constrain size. Entry-point line content plus a large 'tabstop' config (len ≈ k*9999 for k tabs) yields arbitrary allocation sizes; the absent one-statement fix is a MAXCOL bound on the computed length before alloc (upstream: if (new_len >= MAXCOL) { emsg(_(e_resulting_text_too_long)); break; }) — CWE-400, with the unbounded vcol arithmetic feeding the size (CWE-190).

Unbounded accumulator sink: vcol is a long that grows by chartabsize per character with no limit; its value is consumed at line 91 (len = num_spaces = vcol - start_vcol) and line 128, then at the allocation sink line 130. The (colnr_T)vcol narrowing cast can wrap once vcol >= 2^31 (reachable with k*9999 for ~215k tabs), corrupting the size computation. No guard constrains vcol between accumulation and use; the absent fix is the upstream if (vcol >= MAXCOL) { emsg(_(e_resulting_text_too_long)); break; } (patch 8.2.4359).

assumptions: Buffer line content read at line 65 (ml_get) and the 'tabstop'/'vartabstop' user-config values read at lines 61 and 42 are treated as entry-point/user-config inputs per Phase 1 rule (a).
TABSTOP_MAX at line 55 confines the :retab argument new_ts to [1, TABSTOP_MAX]; this constrains only the divisor, not vcol/len (Guard-Identity drift class 3).

The fragment corresponds to the pre-8.2.4359/pre-8.2.4362 Vim state: it includes 8.2.3402's tabstop_set status handling (line 32) and 8.2.4245's TABSTOP_MAX use (line 55), but lacks both upstream MAXCOL bail-outs.

The crash/illegal-memory-access consequence after the allocation (line-too-long state consumed by ml_replace/redraw) occurs outside the fragment; in-fragment the confirmed mechanism is the unbounded allocation size.

verdict.summary: copy_page_to_iter_pipe reuses a slot of pipe->bufs (selected at lines 21/30, wrap via p_mask at line 7) and re-initializes only ops/page/offset/len (lines 35-39) without clearing buf->flags. A stale PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE from a prior producer survives on a page-cache-backed pipe buffer, so the downstream pipe-write merge path can append into the page cache of a read-only file (CVE-2022-0847, Dirty Pipe class). The fail-closed guards at lines 11, 14, 17 and 32-33 constrain bytes/iter state only and never touch flags, so a stale CAN_MERGE bit reaches the downstream pipe-write merge decision on a page-cache-backed buffer, enabling page-cache writes to read-only files (CWE-457: use of a field not re-initialized on reuse, consumed by a security-relevant decision).

assumptions: pipe->ring_size is a power-of-two invariant so p_mask = ring_size - 1 (line 7) bounds 'i_head & p_mask' to [0, ring_size-1]; the mask alone bounds the index regardless.

Merge-path growth 'buf->len += bytes;' (line 25) has no shown cap versus PAGE_SIZE; its security consumer is unshown, so it is demoted rather than reported.
'pipe->ring_size - 1' (line 7) with ring_size == 0 is not handled, but the non-zero power-of-two ring invariant is kernel-internal and not attacker-derivable from the shown code.

verdict.summary: On the uECC_VLI_NATIVE_LITTLE_ENDIAN build path, the bcopy at line 52 receives its source and destination arguments reversed (standard bcopy(src, dst, len) semantics). The function writes tmp (the RNG blinding value, or constant 1) over the caller's const private_key buffer and never loads d into tmp, so the later uECC_vli_modMult at line 59 computes s = r*tmp instead of s = r*d, and the function still returns 1 with an invalid signature. The same argument-order flaw appears in the s-store bcopy at line 68, which never writes the computed s into the signature. The one-statement fix, a correct-direction load (bcopy(private_key, (uint8_t *) tmp, BITS_TO_BYTES(curve->num_n_bits))), is absent.

evidence.reason: Under the standard semantics implied by the bcopy name, bcopy(src, dst, len) copies from tmp into private_key. The sink's required operation is the reverse load (the #else branch at line 54, `uECC_vli_bytesToNative(tmp, private_key, BITS_TO_BYTES(curve->num_n_bits)); /* tmp = d */`, demonstrates the intent). Starting from private_key (caller-supplied secret, full domain, Phase 1) and tmp (RNG value or 1 from lines 34-36), the guards at lines 22, 28 and 37 all pass for valid inputs and none constrains the copy operands (line 22 tests the nonce k, drift class 3 wrong-target). After line 52 the caller's const private-key buffer is overwritten and d is not loaded; line 59 `uECC_vli_modMult(s, tmp, s, curve->n, num_n_words)` then computes s = r*tmp instead of s = r*d and line 72 returns 1. The absent one-statement fix is the correct-direction load `bcopy(private_key, (uint8_t *) tmp, BITS_TO_BYTES(curve->num_n_bits));`. Primary CWE-685: wrong argument order in the copy call, causing secret-buffer corruption and a signature that does not commit to the private key, on the little-endian build path.

Same argument-order flaw class, same standard bcopy(src, dst, len) semantics: the shown statement copies from (signature + curve->num_bytes) into s, so the computed ECDSA s value is never stored into the output signature; the #else branch at line 70 (`uECC_vli_nativeToBytes(signature + curve->num_bytes, curve->num_bytes, s)`) demonstrates the required direction. The s-half of the signature remains caller-provided garbage while line 72 returns 1. The absent fix is the correct-direction store `bcopy((uint8_t *) s, (uint8_t *) signature + curve->num_bytes, curve->num_bytes);`. CWE-685 on the little-endian build path.

assumptions: The uECC_VLI_NATIVE_LITTLE_ENDIAN preprocessor branch (lines 11, 51, 67) denotes a real build configuration in which the little-endian statements execute.
bcopy is analyzed by the standard semantics its name implies: bcopy(src, dst, len) copies from the first argument to the second.

verdict.summary: PipeSocketHandler::listen copies the endpoint path into sun_path with strncpy bounded by sizeof(local.sun_path) but never verifies the source length or forces a terminator. When pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path), sun_path is not NUL-terminated, and the C-string sinks unlink(local.sun_path) (line 16) and chmod(local.sun_path, ...) (line 21) read past the 108-byte terminal array member — a stack out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The duplicate-path check at lines 5-7 constrains only value equality (Guard-Identity wrong-target drift) and admits the 108-byte witness. No pre-copy length guard and no explicit terminator store exist; the absent fix is 'if (pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path)) throw ...' or 'local.sun_path[sizeof(local.sun_path)-1] = '\0';'.

CWE-125 out-of-bounds read, same root cause as the line 16 sink. With a pipePath of length >= sizeof(local.sun_path), line 15 leaves sun_path without a NUL terminator, and ::chmod reads the unterminated array past its capacity (established by 'strncpy(local.sun_path, pipePath.c_str(), sizeof(local.sun_path));' at line 15) until it finds a NUL on adjacent stack memory. The failure is admitted by every shown branch (lines 5-7 check duplicates only; line 15 bounds the write count, not termination), and the decisive protective statement (a length check before the copy or an explicit terminator after it) is absent, so the terminating array remains unterminated on this second C-string sink.

assumptions: sockaddr_un::sun_path is a char array of size sizeof(local.sun_path) (108 on Linux) and is the final member of the struct, so a scan past index sizeof-1 reads beyond the local object on the stack.
strncpy standard semantics: copies at most n bytes and zero-pads only when the source is shorter than n; if the source length is >= n, no NUL terminator is written.
unlink and chmod consume their path argument as a NUL-terminated C string (libc contract).
limitations: The exact extent of the over-read beyond byte index sizeof(local.sun_path) depends on adjacent stack contents (where the next NUL lies), an unshown environmental fact; the crossing of the array boundary itself is guaranteed once a length-108 path is admitted.
The magnitude (a path of length >= sizeof(local.sun_path)) is produced by the unshown caller of listen; a caller that always supplies shorter paths would not trigger the failure.

::bind at line 18 uses an explicit addrlen (sizeof(sockaddr_un)), so the kernel reads within the struct; an unterminated path only causes binding to a truncated 108-byte prefix, a logic/robustness concern, not a memory-safety finding.
The discarded return of ::listen(fd, 5) at line 19 is a status-handling robustness concern (the failed state is not consumed by any security decision), not a confirmed finding.
The precise sun_path capacity differs by platform (e.g., 104 on macOS), but in every case it equals sizeof(local.sun_path) as used at line 15.

verdict.summary: Stack-based buffer overflow in the BMP V4/V5 header path: at line 194, ReadOK(fd, buffer, Bitmap_File_Head.biSize - 4) writes 104 or 120 bytes into the 64-byte stack array 'buffer' (line 4) when the file-controlled biSize (line 75) equals 108 or 124 (admitted by lines 189-190). No statement bounds the read length to sizeof(buffer), so a crafted BMP of at least 138 bytes overflows the stack by 40 or 56 bytes (CWE-121).

evidence.reason: Stack buffer overflow at the read sink: buffer is declared 'unsigned char buffer[64];' (line 4, capacity 64). Bitmap_File_Head.biSize is read from 4 file bytes at line 75 (entry-point input, unconstrained 32-bit range). The only guard on this path is the branch condition at lines 189-190 ('Bitmap_File_Head.biSize == 108 || Bitmap_File_Head.biSize == 124'), which admits exactly the overflowing sizes: for biSize=124 the length argument biSize-4 = 120 (> 64) and for biSize=108 it is 104 (> 64). The '!ReadOK(...)' check is a read-success test, not a length bound, and is satisfied by a file containing at least biSize-4 bytes. The overflow guards at lines 302-303 and 314-315 constrain biWidth*biBitCnt for rowbytes (line 321), not the read length (drift class 3, wrong-target), and execute after this sink anyway. The absent fix form is a bound on the read length (e.g., rejecting 'biSize - 4 > sizeof(buffer)' or reading only sizeof(buffer)); its absence lets an attacker-controlled length of 104/120 bytes reach a write into the 64-byte object, overflowing the stack by 40/56 bytes and enabling CWE-121.

assumptions: buffer capacity is 64 bytes per line 4: 'unsigned char buffer[64];'
Bitmap_File_Head.biSize is attacker-controlled via the 4-byte file read at lines 68/75 ('ToL(&buffer[0x00])'), with no shown cap

ReadOK performs a direct copy (fread semantics) of the requested byte count into the destination and returns success only when that many bytes were read, so a 120-byte read writes 120 bytes into buffer
ColorMap has 256 rows (line 7) and masks has 4 entries (line 12); ColormapSize is capped at 256 (lines 261-262)
limitations: The unsigned-short truncation of biWidth/biHeight at line 350 ('at_bitmap_init(...)') is noted but cannot be confirmed as a failing memory operation because at_bitmap_init's consumption is not shown in the fragment
ReadImage's internal allocation behavior (lines 341-348) is not shown; heap overflow inside it is not independently confirmable from this fragment
The 'BA' magick loop (lines 37-52) cannot be shown to non-terminate from within the fragment (depends on unshown stream semantics)
Exploitability beyond the confirmed stack overwrite (e.g., code execution) is not assessed; only the overflow is confirmed

verdict.summary: parse_command_modifiers rewrites the command buffer after a Visual-area range. Both write paths are bounded by shown code: STRCPY(orig_cmd + len, " *+") writes a fixed 4 bytes at offset len where the buffer provably holds at least len+6 bytes (STRNCMP matched the 5-byte prefix at line 17 and STRLEN(cmd_start) at line 336 with cmd_start = orig_cmd+5), so no attacker-controlled len can overflow; the other branch's 6-byte write at eap->cmd-1 is protected by the guard at line 328 (eap->cmd > cmd_start), which forces the destination to be at or past orig_cmd. All helper results (vim_regcomp, skip_vimgrep_pat_ext, get_address, *nulp) are NULL- or range-checked before use. This is the fixed member of the pair: the vulnerable sibling writes the 8-byte literal "'<,'>+" into the same len+6 buffer.

assumptions: Line 17 (STRNCMP(eap->cmd, "'<,'>", 5) == 0) plus line 24 (eap->cmd += 5) and line 25 (cmd_start = eap->cmd) establish cmd_start = orig_cmd + 5.

Line 336 (size_t len = STRLEN(cmd_start)) establishes a NUL at offset 5+len, so the command buffer holds at least len+6 writable bytes; the 4-byte write at line 343 (offsets len..len+3) is in bounds for every len >= 0.
Lines 24-25 also make cmd_start - 5 == orig_cmd at line 347, so that memmove's destination is the buffer start.
limitations: The one-byte-past-NUL read p[1] at line 164 (when *p == NUL and vim9script is true) is not a confirmed finding: whether the caller-owned buffer has no slack beyond strlen+1 is not shown in the fragment, so the OOB capacity requirement is unconfirmable.

atoi((char *)eap->cmd) + 1 at line 316 can overflow int on hostile digit strings, but cmod_verbose is not consumed by any size/index/security decision inside this fragment, so it is a robustness concern only.
Caller-side invariants (e.g., that eap->cmd may be read-only memory when reassigned to string literals at lines 356/361) are outside the fragment and were not assessed.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed member of the pair: every JUMP/GOTO verdict path resolves its target chain through IS_ERR, base-chain, already-bound-chain, and SETELEM/binding guards, all evaluated on the same `chain` value before any dereference or `chain->use++`. The historically decisive statement `if (nft_chain_is_bound(chain)) return -EINVAL;` (lines 52-53) is present verbatim, so no demonstrable failing value reaches a sink.

The `tb` array (line 5) has capacity NFTA_VERDICT_MAX + 1, and all attribute indices used at lines 14/16/35/39/40 are within the range enforced by the parser argument at line 9.
