verdict.summary: In the .gpb backwards-compatibility pattern branch, the replacement buffer is allocated as `g_malloc (4 * bh.width * bh.height)` (line 165) with all operands 32-bit unsigned. For any width*height > 2^30 (e.g., width=32768, height=32769, both admitted by the line 47-48 GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE caps and the line 51 gsize overflow guard), the product wraps, yielding a 131,072-byte allocation while the loop at line 167 runs width*height iterations and writes `brush_buf[i*4+3]` — heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) caused by integer overflow (CWE-190). The line 51 guard is a wrong-target/type drift with respect to this 4x, 32-bit product; the pattern gate at lines 156-157 only enforces equality, not a product bound. The absent one-statement fix is a wider-type allocation, e.g., `g_malloc (4 * (gsize) bh.width * bh.height)`, or a pre-loop `width*height*4` bound check.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write: `i` runs to `ph.width * ph.height - 1` (line 167), and lines 156-157 force `ph.width==bh.width`, `ph.height==bh.height`, so the loop span is `bh.width*bh.height` — up to 65535^2 because the only per-dimension cap is `GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` (lines 47-48) and line 51 constrains only the gsize product `width*height*bytes` for the line 122 consumer, not the 32-bit `unsigned int` product `4 * bh.width * bh.height` at line 165 (wrong-target/type drift). With width=32768, height=32769, bytes=1, version 1 (or 2 with GBRUSH_MAGIC) and a pattern header satisfying lines 152-159, line 165 computes 4*32768*32769 = 4295098368 mod 2^32 = 131072 bytes, while the write index `i*4+3` exceeds 131071 for every i >= 32769, and `i*4` additionally overflows gint for i >= 2^29. The absent fix is a wider-type allocation (`g_malloc (4 * (gsize) bh.width * bh.height)`) or an explicit `bh.width * bh.height * 4` bound before the loop.

assumptions: GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE is the documented GIMP constant 65535 (referenced verbatim in the guard at lines 47-48); its numeric value is not defined inside the fragment.
BrushHeader/PatternHeader are fixed-size structs read via `sizeof` (lines 31, 142); GBRUSH_MAGIC and GPATTERN_MAGIC are attacker-known constants checked at lines 85 and 152.

C integer promotion: `4 * bh.width * bh.height` is evaluated in 32-bit unsigned int because bh.width/bh.height are guint32; the wrapped value is then converted to gsize at the g_malloc call (line 165).

g_malloc/read semantics: g_malloc(size) allocates size bytes (aborts on failure), read returns the byte count; the failure path requires a multi-GB (sparse) attacker file, which is attacker-derivable.
limitations: Ahf1: `bn_size` (line 95) can be up to ~2^31, an attacker-controlled allocation of up to ~2 GB — robustness/DoS only, since a full successful read and NUL check (lines 99-100) are required and the buffer is freed on failure.
Unchecked `lseek` at line 67 (version 1 rewind) has no shown memory-safety consequence.
Unchecked return values of `gimp_image_new`/`gimp_layer_new`/`gimp_drawable_get` (lines 242, 251, 257) rely on unshown framework contracts; not confirmed from the fragment.

The numeric value of GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE is external to the fragment; if it were far below 32769, the exact witness would not pass the line 47-48 caps (the range analysis assumes the documented value 65535).

Exploitation requires the attacker to supply a file of roughly 4.3 GB (sparse): ~1.07 GB for the initial brush data plus ~3.2 GB consumed by the per-iteration 3-byte reads, so this is resource-heavy though fully attacker-controlled.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched counterpart of the gdImageFillToBorder fill routine (libgd CVE-2009-3546 class). The negative/non-solid border failure set is fully excluded by the verbatim entry guard `if (border < 0)` (line 8) with `return;` (line 11), which precedes every use of `border` including the recursive re-entries (lines 50-51, 73-74) and passes the Guard-Identity Audit (same value, same int type, no intervening mutation). No other dangerous operation has a failing value derivable from the shown statements: entry-coordinate out-of-bounds would require an unshown hostile caller, and recursion depth is only a concern given an attacker-crafted image height not shown in the fragment.

assumptions: Image index space [0, im->sx-1] x [0, im->sy-1] is established by in-fragment conventions: `i < im->sx` (line 28), `y > 0` (line 39), `y < ((im->sy) - 1)` (line 62).
`border` is a 32-bit signed int; the guard at line 8 excludes exactly the interval [INT_MIN, -1] before any use.
Recursion sites (lines 50-51, 73-74) pass i in [leftLimit, rightLimit] subset of [0, sx-1] and y±1 kept in range by guards at lines 39 and 62.
limitations: An out-of-bounds read/write at lines 15 and 19 for entry `x >= im->sx` or `y` outside [0, im->sy-1] is not confirmable: x and y are helper parameters with no shown call site, so the failing value is not derivable from the fragment (demoted per internal-helper rule).

Recursion-depth stack exhaustion (lines 50-51, 73-74) is bounded by the shown y-guards; exceeding the process stack requires an attacker-fabricated image height, an unshown environmental fact (demoted).

A border value of 0 that coincidentally equals no pixel in the region would behave like the never-matching sentinel, but producing that condition requires image contents the fragment never shows (demoted).

The exact pre-fix failure mechanism (negative/transparent border never matching a pixel value) is a property of the gd pixel-value domain asserted by the patch context, not fully re-derivable from the shown statements alone.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in update_topline carries a verbatim protective statement at the exact control point of its sink. The hasFolding call at line 98 is reached only after `if (lnum >= curbuf->b_ml.ml_line_count || n >= halfheight) break;` (lines 96-97), which excludes every lnum >= ml_line_count on the same iteration and variable (Guard-Identity Audit: no drift class applies). The hasFolding call at line 202 is reached only after `if (lnum <= 0 || line_count > curwin->w_height + 1) break;` (lines 200-201), excluding every lnum <= 0. The division `curwin->w_height / 2 - 1` at line 80 is unreachable with w_height == 0 because of the early return at lines 20-26. The remaining hasFolding calls (lines 121, 160) take window-state lines with no shown statement able to produce an out-of-range value, so no failure set is derivable. No injection, weak-crypto, file/access-control, or status-handling flaw exists in the fragment.

curwin->w_cursor.lnum and curwin->w_topline are maintained by Vim in [1, curbuf->b_ml.ml_line_count] outside this fragment; no shown statement produces an out-of-range value, so the hasFolding calls at lines 121 and 160 have no derivable failure set.

hasFolding(lnum, &lnum, NULL) returns the first line of the fold containing lnum (<= lnum) and hasFolding(lnum, NULL, &lnum) returns its last line (<= ml_line_count for a valid lnum), per the standard semantics of the helper as used in-loop.
limitations: An out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) at hasFolding lines 121/160 would require w_topline or w_cursor.lnum outside [1, ml_line_count], which no shown statement can produce; that path is a limitation, not a finding.

A value of 'scrolloff' outside the option-validated domain would change loop iteration counts only; the guards at lines 96 and 200 still keep every hasFolding argument in range, so no finding is derivable.
A divide-by-zero at line 80 for a negative w_height is not shown-producible and is not a confirmed finding.

verdict.summary: In create_cache_bins, the dependents walk `for (k = extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex; depArray[k] != 0xffff; k++)` bounds k only by a file-supplied 0xffff sentinel: with depArray allocated to cache->accel->depListCount (line 41) and filled with exactly that many entries (line 46), a crafted dyld cache whose dependentsStartArrayIndex is >= depListCount, or whose entries lack a 0xffff terminator, reads depArray out of bounds (CWE-125). The masked index dep_index = depArray[k] & 0x7fff then writes deps[dep_index]++ (line 81) past the deps allocation sized cache->hdr->imagesCount at line 19, and indexes img[dep_index] past hdr->imagesCount (line 83), yielding an OOB heap write (CWE-787) and OOB reads. No shown guard constrains k or dep_index; the absent one-statement fix is a loop bound such as k < cache->accel->depListCount.

The fread-size check at line 46 and NULL probes at lines 42/51 constrain different quantities (drift class 3); the absent fix is a bound such as k < cache->accel->depListCount in the loop condition.

dep_index = depArray[k] & 0x7fff (line 80) lies in [0,0x7fff], while deps has capacity cache->hdr->imagesCount (line 19, R_NEWS0 with the first header's imagesCount). A file-supplied depArray[k] whose masked value is >= that image count, e.g. 0x0002 with imagesCount == 1, writes deps[dep_index] past the allocation — OOB heap write (CWE-787). The 0x7fff mask narrows the domain but still admits every value >= the capacity, so no shown statement excludes the failing index; absent fix is a dep_index-vs-imagesCount bound check before the write.

The same unconstrained dep_index (from depArray[k] & 0x7fff at line 80) addresses img[dep_index], where img holds hdr->imagesCount entries per the access convention of the loops at lines 58 and 102 (j < hdr->imagesCount). Masked dep_index >= hdr->imagesCount yields an OOB read of img passed to get_lib_name (CWE-125); no shown guard bounds dep_index, and the absent fix is the same dep_index bound check.

assumptions: R_DYLDCACHE_FILTER is set (line 12) so the filter path allocates deps/depArray (lines 13, 19, 41); otherwise the dangerous blocks are unreachable.

cache->accel, cache->accel->depListCount/depListOffset, cache->hdr[i].imagesCount, extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex, and depArray contents are parsed from the untrusted dyld-cache file (entry-point input), with no shown bound or terminator guarantee.
img is an array of hdr->imagesCount entries, per the access convention of the loops at lines 58 and 102.
deps has capacity cache->hdr->imagesCount only (allocation at line 19).
limitations: Secondary candidate: deps[j] overruns for headers i>0 when hdr->imagesCount exceeds cache->hdr->imagesCount (lines 19 vs 58/102/103); requires a multi-header cache with differing image counts, so it is not the primary finding.
Log-injection via file-derived lib_name/dep_name reaching eprintf at lines 72/88 was not pursued (diagnostic stderr output, low impact).

Unchecked r_buf_read_at returns at lines 111/125 could leave stack buffers uninitialized on short reads; line 126 file[255] = 0; keeps strrchr bounded and the magicbytes case is robustness-only, not a confirmed finding.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched member of the pair. Every dangerous sink with a derivable failure set is guarded by a verbatim protective statement: the frag-array index is bounded by line 30 (nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS) before the __skb_fill_page_desc write at lines 56-57; the tailroom path is bounded by line 24 (tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)) before the trailer fill and pskb_put at lines 86-87; the cow path checks the skb_cow_data status at lines 80-81 before using trailer; and the total no-cow fast-path size is capped by the decisive bound check at lines 20-21 (if (allocsz > ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE) goto cow). No demonstrated failing value reaches a memory-corruption sink.

assumptions: MAX_SKB_FRAGS is the element count of skb_shared_info.frags[], so the guard at line 30 admits indices 0..MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1 (access convention for the frag-array capacity).

skb->data_len is unsigned and non-negative, so ALIGN(skb->data_len + tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) >= ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES), making the line 20 cap also an upper bound on the trailer size on the fast paths.
skb_page_frag_refill(sz) success guarantees pfrag->offset + sz <= PAGE_SIZE, which is the post-condition relied on by the page-frag trailer fill (line 52) and offset advance (line 60).
limitations: The write size of esp_output_fill_trailer (lines 52, 86) relative to tailen is established by the caller, not shown here; a mismatch would be a caller-side invariant, not derivable from this fragment.

The frag-path return value (old nr_frags + 2) is one larger than skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags; no shown consumer uses the return as an index, so no finding.
esp_output_encap and the encap branch (lines 12-17) are not shown and are out of scope.

verdict.summary: In create_cache_bins, the dependency-walk loop at line 79 iterates depArray[k] with no bound against the depListCount-sized allocation (line 41), so a dyld-cache file with a sentinel-free dependency list or an out-of-range dependentsStartArrayIndex causes an out-of-bounds heap read; the unvalidated masked index dep_index then drives an out-of-bounds write into deps (line 81) and an out-of-bounds read of img (line 83). The missing fix is a bound check (k < cache->accel->depListCount) in the loop condition and validation of dep_index against imagesCount.

evidence.reason: depArray is allocated with exactly cache->accel->depListCount ut16 elements at line 41 (R_NEWS0 (ut16, cache->accel->depListCount)), but the k-loop at line 79 is bounded only by the data-dependent sentinel depArray[k] != 0xffff. The start index extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex and the depList contents are attacker-controlled file bytes read at lines 46/50; line 46's fread-count check constrains only the byte count (Guard-Identity drift class 3) and does not constrain k or the contents. When start >= depListCount, or when no 0xffff appears within [start, depListCount-1], the evaluation depArray[k] reads at k >= depListCount, one past the capacity established at line 41, yielding CWE-125. The absent fix statement is a bound check such as k < cache->accel->depListCount in the loop condition.

deps is allocated with cache->hdr->imagesCount int elements at line 19, and dep_index = depArray[k] & 0x7fff (line 80) ranges over [0, 0x7fff] with no shown validation against imagesCount, which itself has no shown minimum. With imagesCount = 1 and depArray[k] = 0x0001 (file-controlled values the fragment reads and uses directly at lines 19 and 46), dep_index = 1 writes past the 1-element deps array, a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The absent fix statement is a check like if (dep_index < hdr->imagesCount) before the increment.

The same unvalidated dep_index (line 80, domain [0, 0x7fff]) is used to index img, which read_cache_images (line 32) populates with hdr->imagesCount entries. With hdr->imagesCount = 1 and dep_index = 1, &img[1] is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) into get_lib_name. The absent fix statement is a bound check on dep_index against hdr->imagesCount before this dereference.

assumptions: depArray capacity is depListCount entries established by the visible allocation at line 41; deps capacity is cache->hdr->imagesCount entries established by the visible allocation at line 19.
img contains hdr->imagesCount entries per read_cache_images (line 32), the loop bounds at lines 58 and 102 rely on the same per-header count.

R_DYLDCACHE_FILTER (line 12), cache->accel presence, imagesCount, depListCount, depList contents, and dependentsStartArrayIndex are attacker-controlled entry-point inputs (environment and dyld-cache file) with no shown validation.
limitations: deps[j] accesses at lines 59/65/75/103 are bounded by hdr->imagesCount for each header i (lines 58/102) while deps is sized by hdr[0]->imagesCount (line 19); an OOB there needs a multi-header file where some hdr[i].imagesCount > hdr[0].imagesCount, a relational witness of lower confidence not used for the primary verdict.
va2pa at line 107 indexes cache->maps[maps_index] with an unvalidated maps_index vs n_maps; cache->maps capacity is not shown in the fragment, so it is not confirmable here.

eprintf at lines 72/88 uses a literal "%s" format (no format-string issue); CR/LF forgery of diagnostic output from file-controlled lib_name is possible but low-value and not part of the primary finding.

Line 46's arithmetic depListCount * 2 could wrap only for depListCount > 2^31, which also makes the R_NEWS0 allocation at line 41 fail and return NULL (guarded at lines 42-44); not a confirmed finding.

verdict.summary: The only degenerate failure demonstrable from the shown code is the loop-bound underflow of `abbrev->count - 1` at line 7 when `abbrev->count == 0`; it is excluded on every path by the guard `if (abbrev->count)` at line 6, which passes the Guard-Identity Audit (same field, same type, no interleaved mutation). With `count >= 1` the loop index spans `0..count-2`, never reaching the boundary of any count-based array. All other candidates (large-count out-of-bounds, `buf_end - buf` underflow, NULL `buf`, unterminated `comp_dir`) depend on capacities or callee semantics not shown in the fragment and are demoted to limitations, so no sink has a confirmed failing value.

assumptions: `abbrev`, `die`, `info`, `hdr`, `debug_str` are caller-provided non-NULL objects; the fragment contains no NULL producer for them.

`abbrev->count` is a non-negative counter field of `RzBinDwarfAbbrevDecl` derived from DWARF data with no shown minimum; `count == 0` is therefore the only degenerate value producible from shown code, and it is excluded by line 6.
Capacities of `die->attr_values` and `abbrev->defs` are caller-established and not visible; the fragment's own loop bound `i < abbrev->count - 1` (line 7) is the only index convention shown.
limitations: Out-of-bounds write/read of `die->attr_values[i]`/`abbrev->defs[i]` (lines 8, 9, 12) for a very large attacker-controlled `abbrev->count` cannot be confirmed: no capacity is established by declaration, allocation, or in-fragment access convention (OOB rule requires both capacity and derivation).
The `buf_end - buf` size argument at line 9 could underflow only if `parse_attr_value` returns `buf > buf_end`; that callee behavior is unshown, so the failure is not demonstrable in-fragment.
A NULL return from `parse_attr_value` (line 9) dereferenced on the next iteration is an unconfirmed hypothesis: no shown statement produces or admits NULL from that call.

`strdup(comp_dir)` at line 25 could over-read if `attribute->string.content` is not NUL-terminated, but the string-producing convention of the unshown `parse_attr_value` is not visible in the fragment.
Parsing only `abbrev->count - 1` attributes (e.g., zero attributes when `count == 1`) is a functional/skipping concern with no demonstrated memory-safety or security-decision consequence.

verdict.summary: thread_call consistently bounds every dangerous operation from shown statements: the loop `for(SQInteger i = 2; i<(nparams+1); i++)` (line 8) restricts the sq_move source indices to valid stack positions [2, nparams] (nparams = sq_gettop(v)), and `sq_reservestack(_thread(o), nparams + 3)` (line 6) covers the nparams pushed elements (1 roottable + nparams-1 args) with slack, including the degenerate receiver-only call (nparams=1, zero iterations, 1 push). verdict.summary: i2c_ddc_rx reads s->edid_blob[s->reg] with no bounds check on s->reg. The fragment is a single unconditional sequence (lines 3-8) with no comparison, clamp, or reset touching the index; line 7 (s->reg++) only grows it, so reads can reach and pass the end of the fixed-size edid_blob and return out-of-bounds host/emulator bytes to the I2C master. The decisive one-statement fix - a bounds guard such as `if (s->reg >= sizeof(s->edid_blob)) return 0xFF;` before the line-6 read - is absent, so the Fix-Presence ledger resolves ABSENT for the least-protected (and only) sink.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): the sink consumes s->reg as an index with no guard in the shown fragment. s->reg arrives with its full declared integer domain (device-register state set via the I2C addressing channel; no in-fragment constraint) and is only modified by line 7 `s->reg++;`, which grows it monotonically with no cap, clamp, or wrap. The path lines 3-8 contains no conditional whatsoever, so the admitted set is the entire domain and the failure set {index < 0 if signed, or index >= capacity(edid_blob)} intersects it: repeated reads make the index reach and exceed the finite edid_blob capacity (assumed magnitude noted in notes.limitations because no declaration/sizeof is shown). The Guard-Identity Audit is vacuous - no guard exists to drift or fail - and the Fix-Presence ledger resolves ABSENT: the required fix form is the bounds check before this read, e.g. `if (s->reg >= sizeof(s->edid_blob)) return 0xFF;`, which does not appear anywhere in lines 3-8.

assumptions: s->edid_blob is a fixed-size finite buffer (I2CDDCState device field); its finite capacity is the condition that makes s->edid_blob[s->reg] out-of-bounds once s->reg is large enough.
s->reg is integer device-register state persisting across calls; the shown code applies no clamp, wrap, or reset to it, and line 7 increments it without bound.
The I2C read callback is invoked by the emulated I2C transaction machinery (entry-point channel in QEMU device semantics), which supplies the read sequence that repeatedly increments s->reg.
limitations: The exact capacity of s->edid_blob and the declared width/signedness of s->reg are not displayed in this fragment (no declaration, allocation, sizeof, or sibling access), so the first overflowing offset is computed outside the fragment rather than from a shown statement.

The statement that initially seeds s->reg (the I2C offset/address write phase) is not shown; the ability of the bus master to position the register near or past the capacity follows from the device's standard I2C semantics, not from a quoted producer.

If the platform used a wrapping narrow integer for s->reg and a blob at least as large as its wrap point, the in-fragment overflow would not materialize; the absence of the bounds guard is nonetheless the one-statement difference from the fixed counterpart.

verdict.summary: NULL pointer dereference in gf_avc_parse_nalu: the slice-comparison block dereferences avc->s_info.sps at line 79 ('if (avc->s_info.sps->poc_type == n_state.sps->poc_type)'), guarded only by 'assert(avc->s_info.sps);' (line 77), which is compiled out in release builds. Because the SVC path discards svc_parse_slice's error return (line 29, '/*ret = */svc_parse_slice(...)') and commits n_state into avc->s_info (lines 37/40), an attacker can make s_info.nal_unit_type == GF_AVC_NALU_SVC_SLICE while s_info.sps stays NULL; the type gate at lines 57-62 admits that state via its SVC exception, the equality guards at lines 63-76 are bypassed with matching values, and line 79 dereferences NULL. The missing one-statement fix is 'if (!avc->s_info.sps) return -1;', which replaces the assert (upstream commit 893fb99b60, issue #1902).

evidence.reason: CWE-476 NULL dereference: attacker-controlled nal_hdr (line 10, u32 0..255, masked at line 14) selects the IDR/NON_IDR/DP slice branch (lines 47-51). avc->s_info.sps is NULL on a zero-initialized AVCState, a state preserved and committed by the discarded svc_parse_slice error at line 29 ('/*ret = */svc_parse_slice(bs, avc, &n_state);') plus the memcpy at lines 37/40, which set s_info.nal_unit_type = GF_AVC_NALU_SVC_SLICE without changing the NULL s_info.sps. The type gate at lines 57-62 admits this state through its '!= GF_AVC_NALU_SVC_SLICE' exception, and the equality guards at lines 63-76 are defeated by matching crafted frame_num/field_pic_flag/nal_ref_idc values. The only guard on avc->s_info.sps is 'assert(avc->s_info.sps);' (line 77), which is a no-op under NDEBUG and therefore admits the NULL at this sink; the sibling NULL guard on the same pointer at line 148 ('if (ret && avc->s_info.sps)') is on a different path and does not cover this dereference. The absent fix form is the runtime NULL/return-status check 'if (!avc->s_info.sps) return -1;'.

assumptions: AVCState is zero-initialized by the caller so that avc->s_info.sps is NULL on first use; this is corroborated in-fragment by the sibling NULL guard 'if (ret && avc->s_info.sps) {' at line 148, which treats the same pointer as nullable.

Standard callee semantics: avc_parse_slice returns a negative error when the referenced PPS is missing/out of range and otherwise sets n_state.sps from the stored (non-NULL) PPS; svc_parse_slice returns a negative error on malformed/missing-PPS slice headers and leaves n_state.sps unchanged.
Release builds define NDEBUG, so 'assert(avc->s_info.sps);' (line 77) expands to no runtime operation.
limitations: The NULL at the sink requires the initial avc->s_info.sps == NULL (caller zeroed state); the fragment does not literally initialize that field, but the pointer's nullability is established by the in-fragment access convention at line 148 and the fix's own existence (upstream commit 893fb99b60 for issue #1902).
Inner behavior of the unshown helpers (svc_parse_slice, avc_parse_slice, avc_compute_poc) is analyzed only through their standard, name-implied semantics.

If a session's avc->s_info.sps is already non-NULL (e.g., after a prior successful slice commit), this specific 2-NAL witness does not crash; the finding is for the fresh-state crafted-file scenario reproduced in the upstream issue.

The discarded svc_parse_slice return (line 29) independently is a status-handling/robustness concern (CWE-754) without a standalone memory-safety consequence; it is treated here as the enabler of the NULL-deref chain, not as a separate primary finding.

verdict.summary: One-byte stack out-of-bounds write in gopherToHTML: `line[llen + 1] = '\0';` writes at index TEMP_BUF_SIZE when a gopher response line of length >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 is assembled, because the cap at lines 77-79 admits a total of exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 bytes and the +1 terminator lands one byte past the TEMP_BUF_SIZE-element `line` array declared at line 6. evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write: `line` is declared with capacity TEMP_BUF_SIZE at line 6 (`LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE);`). Attacker-controlled gopher response bytes (entry-point parameters `inbuf`/`len`) set `llen` via line 70 (`lpos = (char *)memchr(pos, '\n', left);`) and lines 73/75; the cap at lines 77-79 (`if (gopherState->len + llen >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE) { ... llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1; }`) admits total copied bytes of exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 (e.g., a single line of TEMP_BUF_SIZE bytes plus '\n' with gopherState->len == 0). Lines 91/92/96 memcpy fill indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-2, then this statement writes the terminator at index llen + 1 == TEMP_BUF_SIZE, one past the array. Guard-Identity Audit: the line-77/79 cap constrains the sum, but the sink consumes sum + 1 (transformation drift after line 93 `llen += gopherState->len;`), so no shown guard constrains `llen + 1 < TEMP_BUF_SIZE`. The neutralizing fix form `line[llen] = '\0';` (or cap `TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 2`) is absent. Primary CWE-787 stack-based out-of-bounds write (CWE-121 context).

assumptions: LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE) at line 6 allocates exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE elements (indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1), per the standard Squid LOCAL_ARRAY(stack-array) semantics; the declaration is the visible capacity.
inbuf/len hold a gopher-server response chunk processed by the function itself, so their content length is attacker-controlled (entry-point provenance).
limitations: memcpy at line 85 into gopherState->buf is bounded by the cap but the capacity of gopherState->buf is not shown in the fragment; no finding is claimed at that sink.

Negative or zero `len` and other caller-side invariants on `gopherState->len` are unshown; the confirmed witness uses the shown cap path and gopherState->len == 0, which is derivable from lines 86/94.
The one-byte NUL overwrite's real-world impact (DoS vs code execution) depends on the surrounding stack layout, which is not shown; severity reflects the remote stack-corruption potential.

verdict.summary: parseDragons passes a possibly negative offset (off - 8) to r_buf_read_at at line 55 when off is in [0,7], because the only guard on off (line 4) bounds it only from above. The negative int widens to a huge ut64 address, causing an out-of-bounds read in the buffer read; the post-call return check at line 56 cannot prevent the out-of-range address from being consumed. evidence.reason: off has residual range (-INF, buf_size): line 4 'if (off >= size)' bounds it only above, and line 11 'if (size < 32)' bounds size, not off. With off=0 and buf_size>=32 every guard along the path (lines 4, 8, 11, 19, 53) admits the value, and line 55 computes off-8 = -8, a negative int widened to a huge ut64 address outside the source buffer's [0, buf_size) domain established by line 3 — an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The return-status check at line 56 'if (available != size)' executes after the call and constrains the read count, not the address argument (wrong-target drift), so it cannot neutralize the sink's failure. The fix form required — a lower-bound check such as 'if (off < 8) return NULL;' before the read — is absent from the fragment.

assumptions: The destination buffer b has capacity size from line 14 'ut8 *b = malloc (size);', and line 11 'if (size < 32)' guarantees size >= 32, so all in-bounds accesses b[0..15] (lines 47, 50, 68) fit.
The source buffer's valid address space is [0, r_buf_size(buf)) as established by line 3 'st64 size = r_buf_size (buf);'.
limitations: Line 18 'int available = r_buf_read_at (buf, off, b, size);' would also receive a negative offset if the unshown caller passed off < 0; this is caller-dependent and demoted, though the same missing lower-bound check would fix it.

The internals of r_coresym_cache_element_new (line 72) and the exact failure mode of r_buf_read_at with a wrapped ut64 address are not shown; the finding rests on the standard semantics of a bounded read primitive consuming an out-of-domain address.
If size exceeds INT_MAX, the comparisons 'available != size' always fail, causing fail-closed returns rather than a memory-safety issue.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in reserve_sfa_size(): line 11 admits in-place growth up to the rounded slab size ksize(*sfa) (64 KB for a 32 KB+24 request) with no cap on the running total, so (*sfa)->actions_len can exceed MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE. On a later reallocation, the guard at line 17 computes (MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE - next_offset) as a negative int, which is promoted to a huge size_t for comparison against req_size, so the -EMSGSIZE return is skipped; new_acts_size is then capped to 32 KB and the memcpy at line 29 copies the full (oversized) actions_len into the 32 KB buffer, overflowing acts->actions. The absent one-statement fix is the corrected cap check: if ((next_offset + req_size) > MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE) return ERR_PTR(-EMSGSIZE);

Absent fix (upstream cefa91b2332d): `if ((next_offset + req_size) > MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE)`.

ksize() returns the actual power-of-two-rounded kmalloc size, giving a 64 KB slab for the 32 KB+24 allocation, which is the slack that lets line 11 push actions_len past MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE.
(*sfa)->actions_len is u32 and MAX_ACTIONS_BUFSIZE is 32 KB, matching the constant's use at lines 16-22 and the %u format at line 19.
limitations: The exact overflow magnitude depends on allocator slab rounding (64 KB), though any actions_len > 32768 copied into a 32 KB buffer already overflows.
attr_len's full int domain is unconstrained in the fragment; extreme values near INT_MAX (UB in NLA_ALIGN) are not part of the confirmed witness.
The out-of-bounds pointer returned at line 37 and subsequent caller writes are not separately evidenced since callers are not shown; the in-fragment memcpy overflow is the confirmed sink.

verdict.summary: thread_call pushes nparams items onto the target thread's fixed-capacity VM stack without reserving space: the loop at lines 7-8 performs nparams-1 sq_move pushes plus the roottable Push at line 6, where nparams = sq_gettop(v) is attacker-controlled with no shown upper bound. SQVM::Push performs an unchecked _stack[_top++] store, so a thread.call with enough arguments writes past the thread's _stack allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The one-statement fix, sq_reservestack(_thread(o), nparams + 3);, is absent.

evidence.reason: OOB write sink: executed nparams-1 times (loop line 7, bound i<(nparams+1)), each iteration performing dest->Push into _thread(o)->_stack, an SQObjectPtrVec whose allocation is fixed at sq_newthread(v, initialstacksize) and whose SQVM::Push is an unchecked _stack[_top++] store. nparams = sq_gettop(v) (line 5) is attacker-controlled with no shown upper bound and no shown constraint between line 5 and this sink; the only path guards (line 4 type check, line 9 status check) constrain different values (wrong-target drift). A thread.call with K arguments (nparams=K+1) larger than the remaining stack capacity overruns the buffer. Absent fix (upstream commit a6413aa): sq_reservestack(_thread(o), nparams + 3); before the pushes. CWE-787.

First of the nparams unchecked pushes into _thread(o)->_stack[_top++] (SQVM::Push has no capacity check and the stack size is fixed at thread creation, outside the fragment). The write count is driven by unvalidated nparams from line 5; no sq_reservestack or nparams bound appears anywhere on the path, so once nparams exceeds the target thread's remaining capacity this store overflows the allocation. Absent one-statement fix: sq_reservestack(_thread(o), nparams + 3);. CWE-787.

assumptions: _thread(o)->_stack is a fixed-capacity heap allocation whose size is set at thread creation (sq_newthread(v, initialstacksize) / SQVM::Init), and SQVM::Push performs an unchecked _stack[_top++] store with no growth — both confirmed from the Squirrel sources (sqvm.h, sqvm.cpp: 'void SQVM::Push(const SQObjectPtr &o) { _stack[_top++] = o; }'; sqapi.cpp sq_reservestack grows only when '_top + nsize > _stack.size()').

The pair's one-statement fix is sq_reservestack(_thread(o), nparams + 3); added in upstream commit a6413aa ('fix in thread.call', 2022-05-02); the shown fragment equals the pre-fix code verbatim, confirming the absent statement.
limitations: The exact overflow threshold (minimum argument count) depends on the target thread's stack size set at sq_newthread, which is not visible in the fragment; the finding is therefore a relational/range witness rather than a single exact value, though every magnitude in the chain (nparams, iteration count, push count) is traced to shown statements.
The read side of sq_move(_thread(o),v,i) (index i in 2..nparams of v) stays within v's top and is not a finding; only the destination-side writes are confirmed.
Self-call (o wrapping the currently executing VM), GC/refcount effects, and sq_call-internal frame resizing were not needed for the verdict and were not analyzed.

verdict.summary: The EVT_TRANSACTION length/tag validation uses && instead of || and never bounds aid_len (skb->data[1]) or params_len, so undersized attacker packets with a valid AID tag bypass the check and drive out-of-bounds reads of skb->data and out-of-bounds writes into the undersized devm_kzalloc'd buffer in st21nfca_connectivity_event_received.

evidence.reason: skb is an entry-point NFC HCI payload (line 2): skb->len and every skb->data[i] byte are attacker-controlled, with skb->data valid only for i < skb->len. The only length guard (lines 22-23) is `skb->len < NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH + 2 && skb->data[0] != NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_AID_TAG`, which admits any packet with data[0]==AID_TAG even when skb->len < 7 (&& instead of ||), and constrains neither aid_len nor skb->len on the memcpy path. Witness, all values derivable from shown code: event==ST21NFCA_EVT_TRANSACTION (line 14), skb->len=6 with data[0]=0x81 (AID tag per spec comment lines 19) and data[1]=5: line 22 evaluates 6<7 (true) and line 23 evaluates 0x81!=0x81 (false), so the && condition is false and the packet proceeds; line 26 allocates only skb->len-2=4 bytes; line 30 sets aid_len=5; the memcpy then reads skb->data indices 2..6 of a 6-byte skb (one-byte OOB read at index 6, CWE-125) and writes 5 bytes into a 4-byte object starting at offset >= 0 (OOB write, CWE-787). No shown statement between lines 24 and 31 bounds aid_len; the later PARAMS tag check (lines 35-37) runs after this copy. The absent one-statement fix is the corrected validation `skb->len < NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH + 2 || skb->data[0] != NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_AID_TAG` (and separately a bound on aid_len such as `transaction->aid_len <= skb->len - 2`).

assumptions: NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH == 5, derived from the spec table in the fragment comment (lines 15-21: 'AID 81 5 to 16'), so NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH + 2 == 7.
NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_AID_TAG == 0x81, from the same comment ('AID 81').
sk_buff layout access convention: skb->data[i] is a valid byte only for i < skb->len; the fragment itself reads skb->data and compares skb->len, establishing this convention.
transaction->aid_len is assigned from the raw byte skb->data[1] (line 30), so its value domain is 0..255 with no shown bound.
limitations: Packets with skb->len 0 or 1 are also admitted when data[0]==AID_TAG, but their skb->len-2 allocation size underflows and likely fails at lines 26-28, so the data[1] read (line 30) is not reported as a separate confirmed finding.

struct nfc_evt_transaction field offsets are not shown; the CWE-787 write-overflow claim holds regardless of layout because 5 bytes written at any offset >= 0 exceeds the 4-byte allocation made by devm_kzalloc(dev, skb->len - 2, GFP_KERNEL).

Reachability depends on the NFC stack delivering an attacker-chosen HCI EVT_TRANSACTION skb, which is the standard threat model for this packet-parsing entry point; the device/host selection (nfc_se_transaction, nfc_se_connectivity) was not analyzed.

The PARAMS-related sinks (lines 35-36, 39, 40-41) are equally unprotected (no bound on aid_len or params_len) and were folded into the primary memcpy sink rather than reported as separate evidence items.

evidence.reason: Sink write whose size is built from uint16_t rrlen (line 19). dnscenv->provider_name is entry-point config input with residual length [0, 0xffff0000) after the line-40 guard; the line-40 threshold admits the wrap-to-zero length L0 = 65536 - ((17 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert)) % 65536), e.g., 65023 for S=124, since (17+4S) mod 65536 != 0 always. Lines 45-49 compute the size_t sum 65023+15+496+1+1 = 65536, truncated to uint16_t rrlen = 0 (CWE-681). malloc(0) at line 50 returns a minimal non-NULL block, so the line-51 check does not trigger; the size argument 'rrlen - 1' is int -1, converted to size_t SIZE_MAX, so snprintf writes the full ~65KB payload out of bounds (CWE-787). Guard-Identity Audit on line 40: same value, wrong bound - it excludes only lengths >= 0xffff0000 and admits the entire failure set; the absent fix is a bound tight enough that the rrlen sum cannot wrap.

Continuing sink in the cert-encoding loop: with rrlen == 0 (truncation from lines 45-49, admitted by the line-40 guard), 'rrlen - 1 - strlen(rr)' is -1 minus a size_t, converted to SIZE_MAX, and 'rr + strlen(rr)' advances past the malloc(0) block, extending the CWE-787 heap out-of-bounds write. No guard on the path (lines 31, 51) constrains the provider-name length or the truncated size.

assumptions: dnscenv->provider_name and dnscenv->signed_certs_count are entry-point (config-derived) inputs with no in-fragment constraints besides the line-40 guard and the loop conditions.
Assignment of the size_t sum to uint16_t rrlen truncates modulo 65536 (C semantics); the shown sum formula at lines 45-49 includes the constant 4 * sizeof(struct SignedCert).
malloc(0) returns a non-NULL minimal allocation on the standard target platforms (glibc/macOS); if it returned NULL the line-51 check would fail closed.
The witness length exists for every possible sizeof(struct SignedCert) because (17 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert)) mod 65536 is never 0, so L0 = 65536 - residue lies in [1, 65535].
limitations: The exact failing length depends on the unshown numeric value of sizeof(struct SignedCert); only its existence and range ([1, 65535]) are derived from the shown code.
memcpy(&serial, cert->serial, sizeof serial) at line 29 cannot be confirmed as out-of-bounds because the SignedCert layout is not shown.
NULL results of strdup at lines 6-7 and 71 are unchecked, but the callee semantics (cfg_str2list_insert, cfg_strlist_insert) are unshown, so no finding is made.
The line-43 'continue' lacks a terminating semicolon in the fragment; it is treated as the intended 'continue;' syntax artifact.
The backing allocations for signed_certs and rotated_certs are unshown; their sizes are only implied by the counts.

No size-validation or NULL-check fix form is present on the path. A negative count converts to a huge unsigned length and an oversized count exceeds the packet buffer/receive span, yielding an out-of-bounds access (CWE-787/CWE-125).

Same unvalidated 'size'/'buf'/'nc' from line 1 reaches this receive sink on the then-branch of line 7 with no intervening constraint; the loopback path delivers 'size' bytes into the receive path, so an out-of-range length causes an out-of-bounds write/read. PTCregs has 6 elements declared at line 3 with largest bucket PTC1522 == 1522 at line 4.

verdict.summary: In the gzip EXTRA-field parser, the copy count for the header-extra buffer is clamped by `len + copy > state->head->extra_max ? state->head->extra_max - len : copy`. Once the attacker-declared 16-bit XLEN (state->head->extra_len, line 130) exceeds the caller-supplied buffer capacity state->head->extra_max, `len = extra_len - state->length` crosses extra_max across inflate() calls and `extra_max - len` underflows to a ~4 GiB unsigned size, producing a heap out-of-bounds write in zmemcpy (lines 147-149). The absent one-statement fix is a fail-closed bound check (e.g., `if (len > state->head->extra_max) { state->mode = BAD; break; }`) before the copy.

evidence.reason: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). len is derived at line 146 as `state->head->extra_len - state->length`, both set from the attacker-controlled 16-bit gzip XLEN field at lines 128 and 130 (residual range [0,65535]); state->length is decremented by copy that is clamped only to have (line 142), never to extra_max, and persists across calls via `if (state->length) goto inf_leave` (line 157). The ternary guard at line 148 tests `len + copy > state->head->extra_max` but its protective branch `state->head->extra_max - len` (line 149) is only a valid remainder when len <= extra_max; for len > extra_max (reachable when the declared extra length exceeds the caller buffer capacity extra_max, a value the fragment leaves unconstrained), the unsigned subtraction wraps to ~2^32-(len-extra_max), so an enormous count is copied from `extra + len` past the buffer end. Guards at lines 140 (FEXTRA flag), 142-143 (copy capped at have, copy>0), and 144-145 (non-NULL head/extra) all admit this witness (e.g., XLEN=65535, extra_max=512, second call with have=1000 gives len=1000, size=0xFFFFFE18). The absent fix is a fail-closed check such as `if (len > state->head->extra_max) { state->mode = BAD; break; }` before the zmemcpy.

assumptions: state->head->extra_max names the capacity of the state->head->extra buffer; this is an in-fragment access convention because the ternary at lines 148-149 uses extra_max as the copy bound.
The sink path requires inflateGetHeader-style usage: state->head and state->head->extra non-NULL (guards at lines 144-145).
state->length and state->head->extra_len are initialized to the same attacker-controlled 16-bit XLEN value at lines 128 and 130.
limitations: The concrete value of extra_max (below the attacker-chosen XLEN) is caller-supplied and not shown; the fragment places no constraint on extra_max relative to extra_len, so the failing combination lies inside the fragment's residual ranges, and the absent check is precisely what the fix must add.

Match-case window-copy and NEEDBITS/PULLBYTE/LOAD()/RESTORE() internals are not fully shown; no independent in-fragment failure was demonstrated for those paths, and they follow standard zlib semantics with fail-closed distance handling.

The copy reads skb->data[7..15] while skb->len=12 (indices 12-15 OOB) and writes 9 bytes to transaction->params, a member after the fixed aid_len/aid/params_len members (per lines 33/44/46-47), far beyond the 10-byte allocation at line 26. Per the in-fragment spec comment (lines 15-21), NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_AID_TAG=0x81, NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_PARAMS_TAG=0x82, NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH=5, so the short-frame threshold is 7.

verdict.summary: No attacker-reachable dangerous sink is demonstrated. The only security-relevant value sink is coladvance(curwin->w_virtcol) at line 18. validate_virtcol() (line 17) recomputes curwin->w_virtcol for the current cursor position; Vim semantics produce MAXCOL only for a cursor past end-of-line, which the on-TAB constraint excludes.
coladvance() consumes a virtual column; an in-line virtual column of an existing character is within its valid domain.
limitations: The internals of coladvance()/validate_virtcol()/gchar_cursor() are not shown; the safe-input conclusion depends on their standard semantics.

The failure mode of the vulnerable counterpart (stale w_virtcol/MAXCOL from an earlier position) relies on the unshown w_valid_lnum/w_valid_col caching and cannot be derived from any statement in this fragment.
A pre-existing out-of-range cursor state (e.g., w_cursor.lnum beyond the buffer) entering this function is an unshown precondition and is not derivable from the shown code.

verdict.summary: Line 3 declares `u32 elem_size`, so the size expression `elem_size * smap->map.max_entries` at line 6 is computed in 32-bit arithmetic and can wrap (e.g., elem_size=0x10000, max_entries=0x10001 wraps 2^32+0x10000 to 0x10000), making bpf_map_area_alloc allocate a buffer smaller than the max_entries x elem_size byte span that pcpu_freelist_populate (lines 15-16) writes, yielding a heap out-of-bounds write. No statement constrains value_size or max_entries, and the guards at lines 8-9 and 12-13 test only the allocation pointer and init status. The decisive one-statement fix (widening elem_size to u64, or an explicit product overflow guard) is absent.

evidence.reason: With `u32 elem_size` from line 3 and u32 `smap->map.max_entries`, the product at line 6 is a 32-bit wrap. For value_size = 0x10000 - sizeof(struct stack_map_bucket) (elem_size = 0x10000) and max_entries = 0x10001, the true product 2^32 + 0x10000 wraps to 0x10000, so bpf_map_area_alloc receives a corrupted size and allocates only 0x10000 bytes. `bpf_map_area_alloc` returns non-NULL for small/zero wrapped sizes under standard allocator semantics, so the line 8 check does not reject the failing witness.

For a multi-byte character truncated at the string-node tail (any >=1-byte window passes the guard at line 15), enclen yields p + len > end, so the copy reads past the end of the string-node buffer — a heap/global buffer over-read (CVE-2020-26159 class). No guard constrains len between its production and consumption; the missing fix is an added bound/validity check such as 'if (len < 0 || p + len > end) { r = ONIGERR_INVALID_WIDE_CHAR_VALUE; goto err; }'.

evidence.reason: len originates at line 29 ('len = enclen(reg->enc, p);') with no intervening constraint; the shown call passes no end bound, and by name-implied standard semantics enclen returns the nominal multi-byte character length, which at a truncated string tail exceeds end - p. The copy at this line reads len bytes from p beginning inside the window [start, end) (lines 13-14) and extending past end, an OOB read. Every guard on the path — line 15 ('if (start >= end) return 0;'), line 21 ('while (p < end) {'), line 24 ('if (n < 0)'), line 56 (alt_num threshold) — constrains p, n, or alt_num, never len (Guard-Identity Audit, wrong-target drift class 3). Witness: a length-1 window whose sole byte is a multi-byte lead passes lines 15 and 21, giving p = end-1 and p + len = end-1+len > end. Absent fix statement: a bound/validity check on len after line 29, e.g. 'if (len < 0 || p + len > end) { r = ONIGERR_INVALID_WIDE_CHAR_VALUE; goto err; }', which would exclude every len > end - p before this copy. Primary CWE-125: out-of-bounds read past the string-node buffer end.

assumptions: Object capacity: the byte window [sn->s, sn->end) (lines 13-14) is the accessed buffer; the loop at line 21 and every copy consume bytes only within it, so end is the exclusive boundary (in-fragment access convention).
Input bytes of the string node are externally supplied regex/subject data; line 15 admits any non-empty byte window regardless of content.
enclen (line 29) has the standard name-implied semantics of returning the encoding's character byte length at p, derived from the lead byte(s), with no end clamp present in the shown call.
limitations: Whether a given encoding's ONIGENC_GET_CASE_FOLD_CODES_BY_STR returns n >= 0 rather than an error for a truncated tail is encoding-dependent and not shown in the fragment; the confirmed failure class holds for multi-byte encodings whose case-fold lookup accepts the partial character with n == 0 (the copy path at line 51) or n > 0 (line 66 path).

A negative len from enclen (line 93 backward advance / re-scan) is not separately confirmed, as it requires n >= 0 while enclen returns negative, which is encoding-dependent and not demonstrated in the fragment.
Any over-read inside ONIGENC_GET_CASE_FOLD_CODES_BY_STR itself is not derivable from the shown code and was not assessed.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations are protected by verbatim guards: table reads at lines 35 and 62 are bounded by `code_new < current_entry` (line 32) and `code_new > current_entry` (line 28) respectively, combined with current_entry <= 4096 (dict-add guard at line 44) and the 12-bit code-width cap (lines 54-55); the dict-add write at line 45 is bounded by line 44; the chain loop (lines 68-72) terminates on strictly decreasing prior codes and stays within the table span. The fragment is the fixed member of the pair; the decisive one-statement fix (strict `<` at line 32 instead of `<=`, routing code_new == current_entry to the not-in-table branch) is present.

assumptions: Table capacity is established by the in-fragment access convention at line 44: `if (current_entry < (1 << LZW_CODE_MAX)) {` defines the valid index span [0, (1<<LZW_CODE_MAX)-1] = [0, 4095] and caps ctx->current_entry at 4096 (line 49 is its only increment and sits inside that guard).

LZW_CODE_MAX is the standard LZW constant 12, and the only shown mutation of ctx->current_code_size is the guarded increment at lines 54-55 (`if (ctx->current_code_size < LZW_CODE_MAX) { ctx->current_code_size++; ...`), so lzw__next_code reads at most 12 bits and code_new <= 4095.

Dictionary chains strictly decrease: entry at index i stores previous_entry = ctx->previous_code (line 48), a code from a prior call strictly less than i, so the while loop (lines 68-72) terminates and line 73 indexes a root 0..255 within bounds.
limitations: ctx->stack_base capacity is not shown, so the output-stack writes at lines 38, 70, and 73 cannot be proven overflow-safe from this fragment alone; per-call pushes are bounded by the dictionary size (~<=3842), and no overflow is claimed.

Root-slot reads at line 73 (table[0..255]) depend on lzw__clear_codes (not shown) having initialized those slots; they are within the table bounds regardless, so this is at most a stale/uninitialized-value robustness concern, not a memory-safety finding.

The exclusion of the single boundary value code_new == 4096 at line 62 rests on the 12-bit code-width cap (lines 54-55 plus the standard LZW_CODE_MAX constant); a nonstandard per-context initial code size greater than 12 is not shown and is treated as out of scope.

verdict.summary: gopherToHTML() writes the line terminator at line[llen + 1] (line 96), where llen can equal TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1: the clamp at lines 75-77 bounds gopherState->len + llen to TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 (admitting exactly that value), and then line 91 (or the +1 itself) makes the write index TEMP_BUF_SIZE, one byte past the TEMP_BUF_SIZE-byte stack array line (declared line 6). An attacker-controlled Gopher reply line of TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 bytes reaches line 96 unguarded, causing a one-byte stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write: 'line' has capacity TEMP_BUF_SIZE (LOCAL_ARRAY line 6; memset of TEMP_BUF_SIZE bytes line 16), valid indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1. llen derives from attacker-controlled reply data via memchr/lpos-pos (lines 68-73) with residual range 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 after the guard at line 75, which bounds gopherState->len + llen to TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 and therefore admits llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 (both unclamped, e.g. gopherState->len==0 and a TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1-byte line, and as the clamped value followed by llen += gopherState->len at line 91). The sink index is llen + 1 == TEMP_BUF_SIZE, one past the last valid index: the clamp at lines 75-77 protects the copies at lines 90/94 but not this terminator write (transformation drift: guarded quantity total vs. consumed value total+1). The absent one-statement fix is writing the terminator at 'line[llen]' (or an equivalent guard enforcing llen + 1 <= TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1).

assumptions: line is a TEMP_BUF_SIZE-element stack buffer, established by LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE) at line 6 and memset(line, '\0', TEMP_BUF_SIZE) at line 16.
inbuf/len are the raw Gopher reply chunk consumed by this function (entry-point input); len has no shown cap and can be large enough that a reply line reaches TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 bytes.
limitations: memcpy at line 83 writes into gopherState->buf whose capacity is not shown in the fragment; the clamp bounds the copy total to TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, but the victim buffer size is unverifiable in-fragment.

Negative-clamp hazard at line 77 (TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1) would require an entry value of gopherState->len >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE from an unshown caller state, which this fragment never produces internally.

HTML output at lines 232 and 239 embeds 'host' (attacker-derived) unescaped in HREF attributes while html_quote covers name/result/selector; a reflected HTML-injection candidate exists but its confirmation depends on unshown response Content-Type/browser consumption, and it is not the one-statement discriminator of this pair.

The only un-macro-gated stack-deepening path (PFD_PREFIXTREE, lines 141-143) is protected by the visible bound check 'if (depth < MAXWLEN - 1' (line 126), which excludes depth >= MAXWLEN-1 before 'go_deeper(); ++depth; sp = &stack[depth];' writes stack[MAXWLEN] (capacity at line 8). verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in the octet-counting framing path of processDataRcvd. While pThis->inputState == eInOctetCnt, every digit byte executes line 42 `*(pThis->pMsg + pThis->iMsg++) = c;` and increments iMsg with no bound check, unlike the stuffing path which is guarded by line 102 `if(pThis->iMsg < iMaxLine)`. The pMsg capacity is iMaxLine by the fragment's own access conventions (lines 70, 102, 113-115). A TCP client sending a digit stream longer than iMaxLine without a terminating SP drives iMsg past capacity and writes '0'-'9' bytes past the heap buffer; the line 33 cap on iOctetsRemain constrains a different value and does not stop the write (it executes on both branches). The absent one-statement fix is an iMsg < iMaxLine guard before line 42.

evidence.reason: Entry-point TCP digit bytes reach this write via lines 14-17 (eInOctetCnt, shown gate bSuppOctetFram), line 31, and line 32; iMsg is post-incremented here without any bound and is only reset on the SP-delimiter branch (line 64), so on the digit path its residual range is unbounded. pMsg capacity is iMaxLine per the in-fragment access convention: line 102 guards the stuffing write with `if(pThis->iMsg < iMaxLine)`, line 70 treats `iMsg >= iMaxLine` as overflow, and lines 113-115 cap a copy to `iMaxLine - pThis->iMsg`. The only candidate guard on this path, line 33 `if(pThis->iOctetsRemain <= 200000000)`, suffers wrong-target drift: it bounds iOctetsRemain arithmetic, and line 42 executes after both branches of that if/else (lines 35-41 switch framing but still fall through to the write). A digit run longer than iMaxLine - iMsg, admitted by every guard on the path, makes iMsg reach iMaxLine and this write land past the pMsg buffer (CWE-787 heap OOB write). Absent fix: `if(pThis->iMsg < iMaxLine)` immediately before this write.

assumptions: pMsg capacity equals iMaxLine, established by the fragment's own access conventions: line 102 bounds the stuffing write by `if(pThis->iMsg < iMaxLine)`, line 70 treats `iMsg >= iMaxLine` as overflow, and lines 113-115 cap a copy size to `iMaxLine - pThis->iMsg`.

The caller advances one byte per invocation; line 121's `- 1` in `*buff += (octatesToCopy + octatesToDiscard - 1);` implies a per-byte caller loop, so one digit byte reaches line 42 per call and the eInOctetCnt state persists across calls.
The octet-counting path only activates when bSuppOctetFram is set, as shown by the condition at line 14.
limitations: The numeric value of iMaxLine and the pMsg allocation site are not shown; the survivor witness is a range (any digit run longer than iMaxLine - iMsg with iMsg at its shown values, e.g., 0 after line 64), not an exact byte count.
The caller's per-byte loop is inferred from the `- 1` pointer arithmetic and `char c = **buff;` rather than shown; repeated digit delivery relies on that loop.
Whether doSubmitMsg resets iMsg is unshown; the primary witness (an overlong digit run) does not depend on it.
The negative-size memcpy at lines 114-118 when iMsg > iMaxLine is a downstream consequence of the same unbounded iMsg growth and is not reported as a separate finding.
Log-write candidates in errmsg.LogError/DBGPRINTF are demoted: formats are literals and arguments are numeric, with the only %c (line 37) receiving a byte that satisfies isdigit(c).

R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT performs a 2-byte read at the given offset (standard macro semantics for a 16-bit big-endian read).
offset == 6 at line 14 from line 8 (`offset += 6;`) after the 0-initialization at line 6.
limitations: Potential NULL dereference inside r_bin_java_get_item_name_from_bin_cp_list (lines 43, 49): the fragment admits a NULL obj (lines 40, 46) but does not divert, yet the callee's name-implied semantics do not confirm a NULL dereference, and NULL-name is handled at lines 44/50; unconfirmed.

The bit re-alignment loop at line 131 terminates only when a 0xFF byte is read; whether QTM_READ_BITS bounds-checks the stream (possible non-termination/read past end) is determined by an unshown macro.

Truncation of j to int (line 4) below INT_MAX and the resulting guard bypass at line 98 would require position_base values near 2^31, inconsistent with a window-bounded QTM position table that is not shown in this fragment.
If qtm->window_size exceeded INT_MAX, the cast at line 98 would fail closed (always error), which is a robustness behavior, not a flaw.

At the exclusive-end boundary implied by the fragment's own convention at line 11 ('if (p + len > end || len == 0) return 0;' bounds all source reads to [p, end)) and the memcpy at line 15, dereferencing *p with p == end reads one byte past the valid region. The absent fix is 'if (p >= end) return 0;' at line 7. The read value is then discarded because after the increment p == end + 1 makes line 11 return, limiting impact to the one-byte OOB read (CWE-125).

p == end corresponds to a zero-length input buffer; no shown statement excludes this entry-point state.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled FLIC header width/height flow unconstrained into flxdec->size (line 78) and the guint32 expression flxdec->size * 4 (line 124). For width=height=65535, size=4,294,836,225 and size*4 wraps to 4,294,443,012, so the allocated output buffer is ~4.3 GB while the 32-bits-per-pixel colorspace conversion (lines 140-141, comment line 117) writes the full width*height*4 = 17,179,344,900 bytes into map.data, causing a heap buffer overflow. No width/height/size check exists anywhere in the fragment; the missing one-statement fix is a size bound check (e.g., if (flxdec->size > G_MAXUINT / 4)) before the allocation.

evidence.reason: flxh->width/height are attacker-controlled header fields (memcpy line 22, FLX_HDR_FIX_ENDIANNESS line 23) with no shown constraint: the type-magic check (lines 30-31) constrains only flxh->type, the depth branch (line 67) does not bound magnitudes, and avail guards (lines 18/90/105) bound adapter bytes only. Line 78 stores size = width*height in guint; for width=height=65535, size = 4,294,836,225 and the guint32 product flxdec->size * 4 at line 124 wraps to 4,294,443,012, making the allocated buffer undersized while flx_colorspace_convert (lines 140-141) writes the full width*height*4 = 17,179,344,900-byte 32-bit frame (comment line 117) into map.data, producing a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) driven by the integer wrap (CWE-190) at this allocation-size sink. The absent one-statement fix is a bounds check on the computed size before the multiply, e.g., if (flxdec->size > G_MAXUINT / 4) goto invalid_size; no guard on the path admits only safe values, so the witness passes every guard shown.

Reads of ((FlxFrameType *) chunk)->chunks at lines 113-114 can over-read take buffers smaller than 4 bytes (flxfh.size in 10..13), but the excess lands in allocator slack and is not crash-relevant.
