u1 << 32 and q1 << 32 (lines 29, 36) are defined only for 64-bit mp_limb_t; for a hypothetical 32-bit-limb build the shifts are UB, but that is a build property not established by the fragment.

verdict.summary: Stack-based out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the CTO_None macro-expansion path of compileRule: the macro-argument copy at line 170 writes arg.length widechars into tmpFile.line (capacity MAXSTRING, established by the line 157 guard convention) without any check that linelen + arg.length <= MAXSTRING. A table defining a macro whose expansion prefix fills the line buffer and whose call supplies a sufficiently long argument token drives the index past MAXSTRING. The one-statement fix absent is a capacity guard (e.g. if (tmpFile.linelen + arg.length > MAXSTRING) { compileError(...); return 0; }) before the argument-copy loop.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled macro argument token (getToken at line 130) with arg.length >= 1 is copied into tmpFile.line, whose capacity is MAXSTRING widechars per the in-fragment access convention: guard line 157 '} else if (tmpFile.linelen >= MAXSTRING) {' paired with definition write line 164 admits indices 0..MAXSTRING-1. The definition-copy loop (lines 144-165) is admitted by guard line 157 up to linelen == MAXSTRING, then the substitution branch (line 166, subst < m->substitution_count) reaches the sink without any check on linelen + arg.length, so writes at index >= MAXSTRING occur whenever linelen + arg.length > MAXSTRING. Guard line 157 fails the Guard-Identity Audit (drift class 3/4: it constrains the definition-character write at line 164, not the value linelen+j consumed at line 170), and the loop bound at line 169 (j < arg.length) bounds iterations, not target indices. The absent fix is a capacity check (e.g., if (tmpFile.linelen + arg.length > MAXSTRING) { compileError(...); return 0; }) before line 169. Primary CWE-787: out-of-bounds stack write.

assumptions: tmpFile.line has capacity MAXSTRING widechars; the fragment's own guard at line 157 (tmpFile.linelen >= MAXSTRING) together with the write at line 164 establishes valid indices 0..MAXSTRING-1.
CharString-style token/definition buffers (token at line 3, arguments at line 127) are bounded by MAXSTRING, so a macro argument token of length up to MAXSTRING is derivable from the input line.

The substitution branch at line 166 is reachable because the fragment's own condition subst < m->substitution_count and the use of m->substitutions at lines 168/172 demonstrate macros with substitutions are consumed on this path; substitution-index values are produced by the unshown compileMacro.
limitations: Potential out-of-bounds read of arguments[] at line 168 (arguments[m->substitutions[2*subst+1]-1]) is not confirmed in-fragment: an invalid substitution index would require a malformed macro substitution list produced by the unshown compileMacro, so it is demoted.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in the fragment carries a verbatim protective statement that passes the Guard-Identity Audit: the argc>=8 gate (lines 11-12) bounds all argv[3..7] and arg_start∈{8,9} indexing, each argv_eol/argv read in the argc>8 block has its own strict argc guard, the host buffer is sized exactly (line 42: strlen(argv[4])+1+strlen(argv[5])+1) with a bounded snprintf (line 46) and a malloc-NULL check (line 44), the pos_attr/pos_realname dereferences are NULL-gated (lines 53, 60), and the printf sink uses a literal format string with NULL-escaped arguments (lines 83, 97-101). No sink has a residual derivable failure set.

Computing argv[x] + 1 on a hypothetical empty token would yield a pointer at the terminating NUL consumed later as %s; producing an empty token depends on the unshown message tokenizer, so it is not a confirmed reachable OOB read from the shown code.

verdict.summary: DecodePngV2 carries the complete protective bounds check verbatim: lines 18-20 verify width/height against int truncation and non-positive values, cap each dimension below 1LL<<27, and cap total_size below 1LL<<29. Every downstream sink (allocate_output shapes at lines 33/38, strides at lines 63/70/81, new uint16[height*width*decode.channels] at line 77) consumes only the same const width/height with no interleaved mutation, and the maximum admitted product 4*(2^29-1) = 2^31-4 fits in int, so no integer overflow or out-of-bounds write is derivable from shown statements.

assumptions: decode.channels is the per-pixel channel count produced by the unshown png::CommonInitDecode/libpng from the PNG color type; no shown statement admits a value outside 1-4, so products such as decode.channels * width * sizeof(uint16) remain below INT_MAX under the shown width/total_size caps.
allocate_output success is guaranteed by OP_REQUIRES_OK (lines 30-38), so output->flat<...>().data() is not a NULL dereference and buffer at line 77 comes from a throwing new.
Shapes {1,h,w,c}/{h,w,c} (lines 33/38) and strides c*w*elem (lines 63/70/81) are internally consistent: h rows of c*w*elem bytes exactly fill the h*w*c-element tensors/buffer.
limitations: An int overflow of the allocation count at line 77 or of the strides at lines 63/70/81 would require decode.channels >= 5 (or <= 0), a magnitude with no producer in the shown statements (PNG channel counts are 1-4 by the unshown format/libpng invariant); any such witness rests on an unshown environmental fact and is demoted, not a finding.

The decode-context cleanup (png::CommonFreeDecode / gtl::MakeCleanup) is absent from this extraction; error-abort paths (OP_REQUIRES at lines 6, 21-23, 47-55) would not free the decoder context here, a resource-lifecycle concern outside the shown statements with no in-fragment memory-safety consequence.

Constructor-level validation of the channels_ and dtype attributes is not part of the shown fragment; it is not needed for the verdict because the shown bounds block alone excludes every derivable failing value.

verdict.summary: The only sink with a fragment-established capacity is the stack buffer `buffer` (line 5) that backs `dire->name`. The guard at line 71 (`if(dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN)`) rejects exactly the failure set {dire->size >= 256} and admits 0..255; combined with the `+1`-enlarged buffer capacity (`SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1` name bytes), the maximum write (memcpy of dire->size+1 bytes plus the NUL at `dire->name[dire->size + 1]`, lines 76-78) stays in bounds (final index 256 <= capacity 257). The `dir->dirs` stores are covered by the growth-at-multiples realloc, and all other candidates (directory_table OOB reads, strcpy into unshown `dir_ent.name` capacity, unchecked `read_inode` NULL) lack an in-fragment capacity, producer, or type and are demoted to limitations. Decisive protective statement present.

assumptions: `dire->name` is the trailing name array of `struct squashfs_dir_entry`, so the name area of `buffer` (line 5: `sizeof(struct squashfs_dir_entry) + SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1`) has capacity `SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1` bytes; established by the shown allocation and the shown access pattern (memcpy to `dire->name` and termination at `dire->name[dire->size + 1]`).

`SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN` is 256 and `dire->size` is non-negative per the standard squashfs on-disk entry (8-bit size field), so the failure set for the line 76-78 write is `dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN`, and the guard at line 71 rejects exactly that set.
`SQUASHFS_SWAP_DIR_HEADER`/`SQUASHFS_SWAP_DIR_ENTRY` copy fixed sizes matching `sizeof(dirh)`/`sizeof(*dire)` into the stack objects.
limitations: Out-of-bounds reads from `directory_table + bytes` (lines 52, 66, 76) are not confirmable: the fragment never shows `directory_table`'s capacity or a bound relating `bytes` to it; `size` at line 49 derives from attacker-controlled `(*i)->data`.
`strcpy` at line 97 into `dir->dirs[dir->dir_count].name` is not confirmable: the capacity of `struct dir_ent.name` is not shown in the fragment.
Dereference of `*i` (lines 25-29, 32, 41, 48-49) after `read_inode` (line 17) is not a confirmed NULL dereference: no NULL-returning path of `read_inode` is demonstrated in the fragment.

A negative `dire->size` (which could make `dire->size + 1` wrap in the memcpy length) is not derivable from the shown code: the field's signedness is unshown and the standard on-disk format bounds it to 0..255.
The `corrupted:` path (lines 109-111) is truncated with no visible `return NULL;`; no security consequence is demonstrated from it.

verdict.summary: Both 2-byte reads (lines 30 and 35) are protected by the bounds check at lines 26-27, which admits only p+4 <= max and therefore keeps every byte read strictly inside [start, max). The guard tests the exact pointer p consumed by both memcpys with no intervening mutation, and it sits on every path before the sinks.

assumptions: The fragment consistently treats max as the exclusive end bound of the parse region (used in get_name_len, get_name, and the line 26 check), so reads admitted by p+4 <= max are in-bounds relative to that bound.

name_part_len and name_len are non-negative on successful return from get_name_len (line 11), following the standard semantics of a length output; a negative value is not producible from shown statements.

get_name (line 19) writes no more than the measured name_len bytes, so the name_len+4 allocation (line 15) covers the write; this is a name-implied helper contract, not relied on for any safety verdict.
limitations: Integer overflow in name_len+4 at line 15 requires name_len near INT_MAX, whose production depends on unshown get_name_len internals; not confirmable from the fragment.
Overflow inside get_name (line 19) would require a helper-contract violation that the fragment does not demonstrate.
Pointer-arithmetic overflow in start + name_part_len (line 23) is not realistically derivable from shown code.
The bounds check protects relative to the caller-supplied max; whether max itself encloses the real packet buffer is a caller invariant outside the fragment.

verdict.summary: GetDeviceForInput's only sink with a derivable failure set, tensor->flat<ResourceHandle>()(0) on an empty resource tensor, is guarded verbatim by the NumElements()==0 rejection at lines 15-17, which passes the Guard-Identity Audit (same tensor, same int64 count, no interleaved mutation or transformation; admitted set {NumElements()>=1} keeps index 0 in bounds). device->name() (line 7) and device->device_type() (line 27) are NULL-guarded on the exact dereference, and FindDeviceFromName's status is consumed by TF_RETURN_IF_ERROR before *result = input_device. The unresolved absl::get<Device*>(op.Device()) variant access at line 39 lacks a holds_alternative/get_if guard, but no shown statement derives a non-Device*-holding variant state and the failure would be a crash-only DoS, so it is demoted to a limitation rather than a confirmed sink.

assumptions: Tensor::NumElements() returns a non-negative int64 count and Tensor::flat<T>() exposes exactly NumElements() elements for the matching dtype, which the line 9 branch (tensor_handle->dtype == DT_RESOURCE) guarantees for flat<ResourceHandle>() (standard Tensor semantics).

TF_RETURN_IF_ERROR propagates non-OK statuses, so the line 14 and line 22-23 success paths guarantee a valid non-null Tensor and a populated input_device before line 18 / line 24 (standard macro semantics).
ctx.HostCPU() at line 3 returns a valid CPU device (framework contract; the fragment shows no NULL producer for cpu_device).

It is also a crash-only DoS with no security-relevant state change before termination, per class rules a limitation, not a finding.

The line 38 guard constrains the local device from tensor_handle->device() (drift class 3, wrong target) and therefore does not protect line 39; this is noted but does not constitute a confirmed finding because the line 39 failure state is not derivable from the fragment.
NULL possibility for tensor_handle->device() or ctx.HostCPU() is not established by any shown producer; even if it were, the line 7 and line 27 dereferences are guarded on the exact same value.

verdict.summary: parse_query() reads the DNS type and class fields at p = start + name_part_len (lines 26 and 31) without any check that p + 4 <= max, so an attacker-crafted DNS packet whose query name ends exactly at the end of the packet makes get_name_len/get_name succeed while p == max, causing an out-of-bounds heap read of up to 4 bytes past the packet buffer.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled DNS packet: name_part_len (line 10) is unconstrained by any shown statement, p = (start + name_part_len) is set at line 23, and the only guards (line 11, line 20) check status, not p vs max (wrong-target drift). A name that fills [start, max) yields p == max, admitted by every guard, and this 2-byte read at max is out of bounds against the packet region whose exclusive end is max per the fragment's own access convention (lines 10, 19, 35). The fixing statement the fragment lacks is a bounds check such as 'if (p + 4 > max) return ...;' before the memcpy. Primary CWE-125, out-of-bounds read.

Same unguarded path: after line 26 and p += 2 (line 28), p is max+2 when the query name ends at the packet end (p == max at line 23), so this read accesses max+2 and max+3, 4 bytes past the end of the attacker-controlled packet buffer, on a status-success path through the only guards (lines 11 and 20). The same absent one-statement fix (a p vs max bounds check after line 23) would neutralize it. Primary CWE-125, out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: max is the exclusive end of the DNS packet's readable region; this is the fragment's own access convention, shown by passing max as the scan bound to get_name_len (line 10) and get_name (line 19) and by computing the parsed length as (int)(p - start) (line 35).
An attacker can supply the DNS packet contents, making name_part_len (line 10) attacker-controlled with no shown cap.
limitations: The allocation size name_len+4 at line 15 is derived from attacker-controlled name_len with no shown bound; a huge name_len would be a resource-exhaustion concern, but no in-fragment statement produces a failing magnitude, so it is not a confirmed finding.
The write of get_name into q->name.ptr (capacity name_len+4, line 15) shows no in-fragment violation and is not reported.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every handshake-layer-produced cipher pointer is consumed only under its own in-fragment non-null guard (lines 18, 25, 28, 31, 35, 55, 67); clientParams is empty-checked before the dereference at line 53 (`if (!clientParams) {` at 48, fail-closed throw); handshakeReadHeaderCipher is NULL-checked by `CHECK(handshakeReadHeaderCipher);` at line 68 before the move at line 71. verdict.summary: Fragment is the patched counterpart of CVE-2022-23589 / TFSA-2022-052 (MulConvPushDown null-pointer dereference). It contains the decisive one-statement fix, quoted at lines 18-20: 'if (mul_left_child == nullptr || mul_right_child == nullptr) { return false; }', which excludes nullptr for both GetNode results on every path before any dereference (IsReallyConstant at lines 22-23, device() at 32-33, and all conv_node/const_node aliases). NumNonControlInputs(*node) == 2 (line 14) implies input(0) and input(1) are in-bounds entries of the node's input vector; no shown code mutates node inputs before lines 16-17.

The empty()/size() checks at lines 60, 70, 78 make mul_props[0], conv_props[0], input_props[1], and const_props[0] valid.

conv_node->attr().at("data_format") (line 83) throws if the attribute is absent; Conv2D/Conv3D op signatures guarantee the attribute, and the failure mode is fail-closed (no memory-safety impact).

verdict.summary: Integer overflow in the u64 product `elem_size * smap->map.max_entries` at line 7: with attacker-chosen map attributes `value_size` and `max_entries` near U32_MAX (unconstrained in the fragment), the allocation size passed to bpf_map_area_alloc wraps to roughly 8.6e9-1.3e11 bytes instead of ~1.8e19, so the map buffer is undersized relative to the elem_size*max_entries span that pcpu_freelist_populate writes. No guard bounds value_size, max_entries, or the product; the NULL and status checks guard other operations.

evidence.reason: Sink: the u64 multiplication feeds the allocation size (CWE-190). Phase 1 residual ranges: smap->map.value_size (line 4) and smap->map.max_entries (line 7) are unconstrained entry-point bpf() map attributes, full u32 domains [0,0xffffffff]. With value_size=0xffffffff, max_entries=0xffffffff, elem_size = sizeof(struct stack_map_bucket)+0xffffffff >= 2^32+3 (lines 3-4), and the product (2^32+3)(2^32-1) = 2^64 + 2^33 - 3 wraps to ~8.6e9 instead of ~1.8e19; the wrapped size is consumed by bpf_map_area_alloc. No guard on the path constrains value_size, max_entries, or the product: the u64 type (lines 3-4) only widens the arithmetic, and the NULL check (lines 9-10) and err check (lines 12-14) are wrong-target guards for this sink (they test different values). The wrapped allocation is then walked by pcpu_freelist_populate (lines 16-17) over the unwrapped span, writing out of bounds when the oversized allocation succeeds.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read (CWE-125) on the local vector `std::vector<int64_t> height_cum_seq;` (L35). Taint: `pooling_ratio_[1] = -1.0` from the op-attribute domain is admitted by the only guard, L19 `input_size[i] >= pooling_ratio_[i]` (1 >= -1.0 passes; the comparison bounds the ratio only from above, never excluding 0 or negatives). L30 `static_cast<int>(std::floor(input_size[i] / pooling_ratio_[i]))` yields -1; L31 `DCHECK_GT(output_size[i], 0);` is a debug-only assertion compiled out in NDEBUG, so the negative size reaches `GeneratePoolingSequence` (L39), which returns an empty vector. L94 `for (int64_t hs = 0; hs < height_cum_seq.size() - 1; ++hs)` then evaluates `0 - 1` in unsigned arithmetic, underflowing to SIZE_MAX, so hs=0 is admitted and `height_cum_seq[0]` (this line) reads one int64 past the vector's zero-capacity buffer; L98 `height_cum_seq[hs + 1]` overruns identically, and the garbage values reach `in_mat.col(in_offset)` / `out_mat.col(out_offset)` (L114-L115). Absent fix: a release-enforced `OP_REQUIRES(context, output_size[i] > 0, ...)` after L30 (or `pooling_ratio_[i] > 0` before it) — the DCHECK at L31 does not protect release builds and L19's admitted set contains the failing divisor.

Unprotected division/calculation (CWE-682). The only preceding guard, L19 `input_size[i] >= pooling_ratio_[i]`, admits pooling_ratio_[i] = 0.0 and all negatives (residual range (-inf, input_size[i]] from the unconstrained list<float> attribute). `pooling_ratio_[i] = 0.0` divides by zero (inf) and the out-of-range float-to-int cast is UB (typically INT_MIN); negative ratios yield negative output_size. L31 `DCHECK_GT(output_size[i], 0);` is compiled out under NDEBUG and provides no release protection, and no other statement constrains the divisor or result before the value is consumed by GeneratePoolingSequence (L39-L42), TensorShape (L48-L49), and the pooling loops (L94-L115). Absent fix: `OP_REQUIRES(context, output_size[i] > 0, ...)` or a `pooling_ratio_[i] > 0` validation.

assumptions: pooling_ratio_ is an op attribute of type list<float> whose full float domain (including 0.0 and negatives) is unconstrained except by the shown comparison at L19.
Tensor dimension sizes (input_size[i]) are non-negative; the fragment relies on that for the division/floor to behave as described for the ratio witness.

GeneratePoolingSequence's name-implied contract of emitting output_length+1 boundary values means that a non-positive output_length yields an empty or degenerate sequence consumed by the loops at L94/L102.
limitations: The internals of GeneratePoolingSequence are not shown; the empty-sequence behavior for output_length < 0 is taken from its name-implied semantics and the shown argument `output_size[1] = -1`.

Reachability of the loop OOB at L96 presumes the unshown allocate_output/TensorShape path (L46-L50) does not fail-closed on a negative dimension in release; if it does abort/error, the residual confirmed failure is the division/UB-cast at L30 (crash-only DoS), and the OOB read becomes unreachable.

If a shape function or op registration outside this fragment validated pooling_ratio values (e.g., requiring >= 1), the candidate would be neutralized; no such constraint is visible in the shown code.

verdict.summary: SparseCountSparseOutputShapeFn reads dimension index 1 of input(0) without validating the input's rank. A crafted model supplying a rank-0 or rank-1 indices tensor makes c->Dim return a null DimensionHandle, which is then dereferenced by c->Matrix(nvals, rank) and c->Vector(rank), causing a NULL pointer dereference during shape inference.

evidence.reason: rank comes from line 2 `auto rank = c->Dim(c->input(0), 1);` with no shown rank constraint on input(0). For an input(0) shape of rank 0 or rank 1, Dim's standard semantics return a null DimensionHandle for out-of-range dimension index 1; that null handle reaches this sink unchanged (no check or assignment between line 2 and line 4). c->Matrix(nvals, rank) then dereferences the null handle (CWE-476). The absent fix is a rank-2 validation of input(0) before line 2 (e.g., `if (c->Rank(c->input(0)) != 2) return errors::InvalidArgument(...)`), or a null/validity check on rank before this line; neither exists in the fragment.

The same null dimension handle produced at line 2 (when input(0) has rank < 2, which the fragment nowhere excludes) is consumed by c->Vector(rank), dereferencing a null DimensionHandle (CWE-476). No guard or validation statement exists on the path from line 2 to line 6; the fix form (rank-2 validation of input(0) before line 2, or a null check on rank) is absent.

assumptions: InferenceContext::Dim returns a null (invalid) DimensionHandle when the requested dimension index is out of range for the given shape, per standard TensorFlow semantics in the affected versions; unknown-rank shapes yield UnknownDim instead.
input(0)'s shape is entry-point supplied (the graph/tensor shape being validated), and the fragment imposes no constraint on its rank.
limitations: The exact crash location inside InferenceContext::Matrix/Vector is not shown in the fragment; the confirmation relies on the name-implied standard semantics that a null DimensionHandle is dereferenced during shape construction.

If a particular TensorFlow build's Dim returned UnknownDim rather than nullptr for out-of-range indices, the null dereference would not occur; no such protective contract is visible in the shown code, and a NOT-vulnerable verdict cannot rest on such a callee contract.

Behavior of session_state->GetNewId() and the TensorStore::AddTensor/TensorAndKey internals is not shown; no shown use of their results forms an index, size, or copy length, so no out-of-bounds or status flaw can be confirmed from the fragment alone.

A deref of `local` would only occur if `find_site_by_name` returned truthy while leaving `*site` NULL, a callee-contract violation not derivable from this fragment; demoted.

verdict.summary: Unary-minus constant folding on a zero-valued LiteralNumber (line 11-12) returns builder.getLiteralNumber(V) with V == -0.0 without the zero-sign equality check that every other zero-producing fold in this function applies (lines 21, 24 use builder.getLiteralNegativeZero()). Because getLiteralNumber key-canonicalizes -0.0 and +0.0 to the same literal, folding -(0) yields +0 instead of the JS-required -0, an observable constant-folding miscompile (CWE-682).

evidence.reason: Sink at line 12 consumes V = -literalNum->getValue() (line 11) for any LiteralNumber operand whose value is 0.0, a member of the full double domain the fragment leaves unconstrained. The only guard on the path is line 10's dyn_cast check (admitted set literalNum != nullptr), which constrains a different property and cannot exclude V == 0.0. For operand +0.0, IEEE negation yields V = -0.0, and the sink returns the canonical +0 literal (the fragment's own convention at lines 21 and 24 routes -0 results through builder.getLiteralNegativeZero(), which this path never calls). The absent one-statement fix is the equality check + sink substitution 'if (V == 0.0) return builder.getLiteralNegativeZero();'; without it, folded -(0) is +0 instead of JS -0, an incorrect-calculation constant-folding miscompile (CWE-682, severity low).

assumptions: The operand LiteralNumber value domain is the full IEEE double range because the fragment imposes no constraint on literalNum->getValue() (line 11), so 0.0 is a derivable member.
The in-fragment convention that -0 fold results are constructed via builder.getLiteralNegativeZero() (lines 21, 24) identifies line 12 as the least-protected zero-producing sink.

builder.getLiteralNumber(-0.0) returns the canonical +0 literal because literal numbers are get-or-created keyed by value (Module::getLiteralNumber -> literalNumbers_.getOrEmplace over OwningFoldingSet<LiteralNumber>, whose Profile is a cast to int64_t colliding for -0.0 and +0.0); the fragment itself shows no statement preventing this.
limitations: Null-dereference of operand at lines 8/30 is not confirmed: no NULL producer is shown in the fragment, so a NULL reaching the deref would depend on an unshown caller (CWE-476 demoted).
The -0 miscompile is a semantics/logic flaw with no memory-safety, injection, or crypto impact; severity assessed as low.
TypeofKind (lines 29-45) not folding BigInt/Symbol literals is a missed optimization, not a finding; its default:break (line 43) avoids any reachable abort.
For an operand that is already -0.0, a naive fix returning negative zero would itself diverge from JS (-(-0) is +0); the confirmed witness (operand +0.0 -> result required to be -0) is unaffected.

verdict.summary: The legacy (non-resource) path of GetSessionHandleOp writes a tstring into the scalar output via handle->flat<tstring>().setConstant(...) without any check that ctx->expected_output_dtype(0) is DT_STRING. The only dtype guard, line 9 (== DT_RESOURCE), protects the other branch and admits every non-resource dtype; a request for a smaller-element dtype (e.g., DT_INT32) allocates a 4-byte scalar at line 8, and the tstring write overflows the buffer (type-confused heap out-of-bounds write, CWE-787). The absent fix is an equality/require check that the output dtype is DT_STRING on this path.

evidence.reason: Sink S1: handle->flat<tstring>().setConstant(...) writes one tstring-sized object into the scalar output whose capacity is 1 element of ctx->expected_output_dtype(0), allocated at line 8 with TensorShape({}) (a scalar, 1 element). Phase 1 residual range for expected_output_dtype(0) on this path is DataType \ {DT_RESOURCE} because the branch at line 9 ('if (ctx->expected_output_dtype(0) == DT_RESOURCE)') admits only equality to the true branch and falls through on every other value. The Guard-Identity Audit for line 9 as a protector of this sink fails as wrong-target drift (class 3): it constrains the same variable but for the opposite branch, excluding only DT_RESOURCE and never establishing dtype == DT_STRING. Witness DT_INT32 (4-byte element, in the admitted complement set): line 9 evaluates false, line 16 enters else, line 18 reinterprets the 4-byte buffer via flat<tstring>() and setConstant writes sizeof(tstring) bytes past the end — heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) via type confusion. The absent fix form is a dtype identity check on this path, e.g. '} else if (ctx->expected_output_dtype(0) == DT_STRING) {' or an OP_REQUIRES(ctx, ctx->expected_output_dtype(0) == DT_STRING, ...) before the write; no such verbatim statement exists in the fragment.

assumptions: Capacity of the output tensor is 1 element of the allocated output dtype, from line 8 'ctx->allocate_output(0, TensorShape({}), &handle)' (scalar shape).
Standard name-implied semantics: Tensor::flat<T>() reinterprets the buffer as T elements without a runtime dtype identity check, and setConstant() writes one T-sized object per element.

The sibling write at line 15 ('handle->scalar<ResourceHandle>()() = resource_handle;') establishes the in-fragment convention that the write element type must match the allocated output dtype, which the line 18 write breaks for non-string dtypes.
limitations: The framework-produced value ctx->expected_output_dtype(0) is only visible through the shown branch; whether a specific real-world op registration could actually yield a non-resource, non-string dtype (e.g., DT_INT32) is not shown in the fragment, so that link rests on the absence of any shown invariant rather than a visible registration contract.
ctx->session_state()->GetNewId() returns an int64 whose range is unconstrained, but no shown consumer converts an out-of-range id into a security failure, so it is not a finding.
AddTensor and allocate_output return Status objects both consumed by OP_REQUIRES_OK (lines 5 and 8); no status-handling flaw is present.

verdict.summary: expand_case_fold_string writes the case-fold expansion of an attacker-influenced regex literal into the fixed-size stack buffer `buf[ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN]` (line 11) via ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD (lines 62-63), and the returned fold_len is used unchecked as the extent for the copies at lines 79 and 87. No shown statement bounds or status-checks fold_len against the buffer capacity before `foldp = buf;` (line 64) and the `foldp + fold_len` reads, so a fold output exceeding ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN (or a negative error length) causes a stack-buffer overflow / out-of-bounds read. The decisive one-statement fix — a bound check on fold_len (e.g., `if (fold_len > ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN) { r = ONIGERR_...; goto err; }`) after line 63 — is absent.

evidence.reason: Primary stack-buffer-overflow sink (CWE-787). `buf` capacity is fixed at the visible declaration `UChar buf[ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN];` (line 11). The fold bytes are written here for attacker-controlled pattern bytes (provenance: `start = sn->s; end = sn->end;`, lines 16-17, entry-point input reduced only by the non-empty check at line 18). `fold_len` (the callee's written byte count) is never bounded or status-checked before line 64 `foldp = buf;` and the uses at lines 79/87; the guards on the path — line 24 `while (p < end)`, lines 27-30 `if (n < 0)`, line 60 `if (n != 0)`, line 95 `alt_num > THRESHOLD...` — each fail the Guard-Identity Audit (wrong-target drift: they constrain p, n, alt_num, not fold_len). A case-fold output larger than ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN overflows the stack buffer with unvalidated bytes. Absent fix: an added bound/status check on fold_len after line 63 (e.g., `if (fold_len > ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN) { r = ONIGERR_...; goto err; }`).

Secondary out-of-bounds read sink (CWE-125) driven by the same unvalidated `fold_len`: `foldp` is `buf` (line 64) and `fold_len` is the unchecked return of ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD (lines 62-63), so `foldp + fold_len` and the copy extent exceed the line-11 buffer when the fold output is larger than ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN (or fold_len is a negative error converted to a huge size). No shown statement constrains fold_len between line 63 and this use; the identical absent one-statement fix (bound/status check on fold_len) applies. Line 79 `onig_node_new_str(foldp, foldp + fold_len);` carries the same over-read.

assumptions: The string node content `[sn->s, sn->end)` derives from the caller-provided regex pattern (entry-point input); oniguruma compiles patterns from untrusted sources.
`UChar buf[ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN];` (line 11) is the only object whose capacity bounds the fold write; its size is the macro-named maximum case-fold length.

`items` (line 10) is sized with the same constant that bounds `n` from ONIGENC_GET_CASE_FOLD_CODES_BY_STR (lines 25-26), so `n` stays within the array by contract; `alt_num` growth is capped by the line-95 break.
limitations: The exact failing magnitude (fold_len > ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN) depends on the encoding's case-fold output semantics, which the fragment does not show; the confirmed evidence is a sound relational/range witness with named capacity, not an exact single-value derivation.

S3 (out-of-bounds read past `end` via `len = enclen(...)` / `p += len` on a truncated final multibyte char at lines 32/132/67) is not confirmed: it requires pattern bytes invalid for the configured encoding, which upstream parsing normally rejects; no such producer is shown in the fragment.

NULL dereference from the node-allocation failures (lines 45-46, 79-80, etc.) is not a confirmed finding: every allocation result is NULL-checked on every path, and failing allocations of attacker-fixed small sizes is not a demonstrated NULL producer.

evidence.reason: run is the return of DecodeRun(length,m_lRunIndex[0]) at line 51, decoded from the untrusted bitstream gated at line 40, and the fragment contains no cap on run against the remaining line length. The absent fix is `if (run > length) run = length;` (or an equivalent while(run && length) fill condition). CWE-787 heap out-of-bounds write.

On the same overrun path, the run fill at line 58 drives length negative, so the guard at line 68 `if (length) {` evaluates true (negative is nonzero) and this run-interruption write stores one more element at index >= m_ulWidth[0] past the line->m_pData capacity (capacity from lines 30-31/138 convention). verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched member of the pair. The only derivable heap-underflow failure — a negative `dec` making `reslen += dec` under-count the backward fill (lines 68-69 vs 99/107/112/120/131) — is fully excluded by the verbatim guard `if (dec < 0) dec = 0;` (line 17), which passes the Guard-Identity Audit (same int value, no interleaved mutation, checked before every consumer). assumptions: `String(n, ReserveString)` provides `n` data bytes plus an internal NUL slot, so `snprintf(tmpbuf, 64, ...)` (line 23) into `String tmpstr(63, ReserveString)` (line 21) and `snprintf(tmpbuf, tmplen + 1, ...)` (line 33) into `String(tmplen, ReserveString)` (line 31) fit exactly, matching the retry condition `if (tmplen >= 64)` (line 29).

Standard `snprintf("%.*F", dec, d)` semantics with `dec >= 0` produce exactly `dec` fractional digits for finite `d`, so `declen == dec` (line 94) and the fractional/point/integral/separator accounting in `reslen` (lines 66-83) matches the fill byte-for-byte.
`int` is 32-bit and `String::size()` is 64-bit `size_t`; with `dec >= 0` and `d` finite, `integral <= 309`, so `reslen` cannot wrap for derived values.
limitations: If `thousand_sep.size()` exceeded ~21.7 MB (or `dec_point.size()` approached 2^31), the assignment `integral += ((integral-1)/3) * thousand_sep.size();` (line 63) or `reslen += dec_point.size();` (line 76) would truncate to `int` and the fill would write past `resbuf`; the checks at lines 58-60 and 72-74 only test 64-bit wrap and do not catch truncation. This is not a confirmed finding because no shown statement produces such a magnitude — it requires an unshown caller-supplied multi-MB string.

`declen > dec` (line 94) would under-count `reslen` and overflow the fill, but reaching it requires `%.*F` to emit more fractional digits than its precision argument, which violates the callee's standard semantics and is not derivable from the fragment.

An attacker-chosen precision near `dec = 2^30` would force ~1-2 GB allocations (lines 31/84) and is a potential memory-exhaustion/DoS, but it depends on unshown caller values and engine/OS limits, and the snprintf paths fail closed on `tmplen < 0` (lines 24/34).

verdict.summary: Every dangerous sink is governed by a verbatim, in-fragment protective statement: input_min/input_max per-channel reads are bounded by element-count checks (L16, L6/L12); ranges writes are bounded by L32+L56; the Eigen chip scans are in bounds because L22 and L25 force the transposed dim-0 size to equal depth; output writes are covered by checked scalar allocations (L84-L85). assumptions: OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK abort the kernel when the condition is false/on error, so statements after them execute only when the checked condition holds (standard TensorFlow macro semantics).

flat_inner_dims<qint32>() (L35) keeps the tensor's last dimension as the inner dim; with dims()==4 and dim_size(3)==depth the 2-D view is [outer, depth], and shuffle({1,0}) (L43) yields [depth, outer], so chip<0>(i) has dim-0 size exactly depth.
Tensors are dense and contiguous, so NumElements() equals the buffer element count (standard TensorFlow Tensor contract).
allocate_output(..., {}, ...) creates a rank-0 tensor with exactly one element.
qint32 is int32-backed; dtype mismatches are rejected by the framework before Compute.
limitations: std::abs(INT32_MIN) (L64) is UB for a qint32 value of INT32_MIN, and 1L << 31 (L68) is UB where long is 32-bit; these affect only computed float ranges and have no security-relevant consumer here.
L69 writes is_non_negative from multiple OpenMP threads without a reduction; a benign data race could produce an incorrect output_min value (correctness, not a security finding).

If input_min or input_max were rank-0 scalars, the guards' own dim_size(0) calls at L8/L12 would touch TensorShape internals outside this fragment's sink set; the loop-indexed reads remain bounded because depth equals the element count.

A very large attacker-supplied depth would allocate a proportionally large ranges vector (L32), but that size derives from tensors the framework already allocated, so no independent resource-exhaustion finding is demonstrated.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation carries its own protective statement, all quoted verbatim: dim_size(0) is guarded by 'if (input.dims() > 0)' (line 4); dims is confirmed 1-D via IsVector (line 15); the dims element count is pinned to the input rank by 'input_dims == dims.dim_size(0)' (line 20); the switch dispatch is bounded by 'input_dims <= 8' (line 25) with cases 0-8 all present (lines 39-47); and the output allocation status is checked by OP_REQUIRES_OK (line 30) before output reaches HandleReverseCase (line 35). assumptions: TensorShape::dims() returns a non-negative int rank, so after the line-25 upper bound (input_dims <= 8) the switch cases 0-8 at lines 39-47 cover every reachable input_dims value.

The >8 side is closed by the line-25 OP_REQUIRES; the <0 side is not derivable from the fragment because tensor ranks/dimension counts are non-negative, so this is a robustness/hardening concern, not a confirmed vulnerability.
Any downstream consumer of the output tensor after this kernel (and consequences of an unfilled output) is outside the fragment and was not analyzed.

verdict.summary: AutoParallel::Initialize indexes a graph node's repeated 'input' field with a fixed position from gradient_pos (2..9) without ever checking input_size(), so an attacker-supplied GraphDef containing an apply-gradients node (e.g. op "ApplyGradientDescent") with fewer inputs than the index causes an out-of-bounds read at line 67 and an out-of-bounds write at lines 70-71; additionally, dequeue_node is read uninitialized at line 88 when no train node is a dequeue op.

evidence.reason: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The index gradient_pos[apply_gradients_op] is a fixed constant from the shown map (line 50: "ApplyGradientDescent" -> 2, up to line 60: 8), while the capacity is the node's repeated 'input' field whose length is attacker-controlled via item.graph (line 5) with no shown minimum. The only path guard, the op-membership check at lines 41-43, constrains graph_.node(i).op() and not input_size() (Guard-Identity Audit drift class 3, wrong-target), so every node whose input count is <= index is admitted. A witness NodeDef{op:"ApplyGradientDescent", input:["a","b"]} passes line 41, enters apply_gradients_nodes_ at line 43, and at lines 70-71 mutable_input(2) dereferences the out-of-bounds repeated-field element and writes div_node->name() through it. Absent fix: an input-count guard, e.g. if (apply_gradients_node->input_size() <= gradient_pos[apply_gradients_op]) return Status(error::INVALID_ARGUMENT, ...); before the access.

Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) preceding the OOB write: input(gradient_pos[apply_gradients_op]) reads the repeated 'input' field at a fixed index (2..9 from lines 50-60) whose capacity is the attacker-controlled input_size() from item.graph (line 5). The op-membership guard at lines 41-43 checks only the op string, not the input count (wrong-target drift), so an apply-gradients node with fewer inputs than the index (e.g. op "ApplyGradientDescent" with input_size 2 and index 2) reaches this unchecked protobuf accessor. Absent fix: input_size() <= gradient_pos[apply_gradients_op] check before the access.

Uninitialized pointer use (CWE-457). dequeue_node is declared at line 79 (const NodeDef* dequeue_node;) without an initializer and assigned only inside the loop at line 82 when IsDequeueOp matches; train_nodes is the attacker-chosen transitive fanin of item.fetch (line 76), so the attacker supplies a graph with no dequeue op, the loop at lines 80-85 completes without assignment, and the uninitialized value is read at line 88 and dereferenced at lines 89-90. Absent fix: initialize at declaration, const NodeDef* dequeue_node = nullptr;.

assumptions: item and all its fields (item.graph, item.fetch, item.init_ops, item.MainVariables()) are entry-point inputs derived from an attacker-supplied GrapplerItem/GraphDef (line 5).
The capacity of the indexed repeated field is the node's input_size(), equal to the number of input entries the attacker places in the GraphDef; no shown statement establishes any minimum.
protobuf RepeatedPtrField operator[]/Mutable perform unchecked element access in release builds, per name-implied standard semantics.
The apply_gradients_ops set (lines 27-37) and the gradient_pos key set (lines 50-60) are textually identical, so the line 41 op guard does protect the map-key lookup at lines 62 and 67.
limitations: Log-injection candidate (node names/init strings streamed into LOG/VLOG at lines 16, 20, 24, 44, 89) is demoted: no shown evidence of a log backend that re-parses the stream, impact limited to log-line forgery.
AddNodeDivConst()/AddNodeDiv() results are dereferenced without NULL checks, but no NULL producer is demonstrated inside the fragment.
The concrete impact of the uninitialized dequeue_node read depends on the garbage value (benign null or crash on dereference); the uninitialized read itself is confirmed by shown control flow.

The exact kernel/target of the OOB write (AdjacencyList of the repeated field, then the string object) depends on protobuf internals, but the out-of-bounds element access is name-implied standard behavior.

verdict.summary: pgpPrtParams parses attacker-supplied PGP packet sequences and returns success (rc==0, exporting digp at line 33) without ever verifying that subkey packets carry a valid binding signature from the primary key. Every guard on the path (lines 10, 11, 14, 15, 22) admits a witness {PGPTAG_PUBLIC_KEY, PGPTAG_PUBLIC_SUBKEY}, so an attacker-controlled unbound subkey is accepted as trusted key material for downstream signature verification (CVE-2021-3521). evidence.reason: Sink is the success/accept decision that hands attacker-controlled key material to the caller. Input pkts is entry-point (line 1); its residual range after the shown guards is any sequence of decodable packets (line 11), the first filtered only on tag when pkttype is nonzero (line 15), all later packets — including PGPTAG_PUBLIC_SUBKEY — parsed into digp at line 22 with no verification. The witness {public-key packet, subkey packet} is admitted by line 10 (p < pend), line 11, line 14, line 15 (skipped after first iteration), and line 22 (upstream pgpPrtPkt returns 0 for subkey tags), then reaches line 30 with p == pend and digp != NULL, yielding rc==0 and *ret = digp at line 33. No statement in the fragment verifies a subkey binding signature (missing fix form: pgpVerifySelf / sigtype == PGPSIGTYPE_SUBKEY_BINDING / expect-ordering gate added in rpm commit bd36c5d for CVE-2021-3521). Result: improper verification of cryptographic signature, CWE-347; the unbound subkey is trusted by the caller's signature-verification machinery, allowing attacker-signed material to verify as authentic.

assumptions: pkts/pktlen denote an externally supplied PGP key/signature buffer whose parsed result (digp) is consumed by the caller as trusted key material for cryptographic signature verification.
The object being trusted is the packet buffer delimited by line 5: `const uint8_t *pend = pkts + pktlen;`.

verdict.summary: In php_wddx_pop_element, the result of php_base64_decode (line 32) is passed to ZVAL_STR (line 35) without any NULL check. An attacker-controlled <binary> element whose base64 text makes php_base64_decode return NULL (e.g., content "a=", where padding '=' occurs at i%4==1) produces an IS_STRING zval with a NULL string pointer, which is then dereferenced by zval_ptr_dtor on the ST_FIELD path (line 56), by Z_STRLEN in the class-name check (line 66), or at hash teardown after line 105/109, causing a NULL pointer dereference/DoS. The fixed counterpart adds `if (new_str) { ZVAL_STR(&ent1->data, new_str); } else { ZVAL_EMPTY_STRING(&ent1->data); }`.

evidence.reason: Line 35 consumes new_str, the unchecked return of php_base64_decode (lines 32-33), to build a string zval. new_str's NULL outcome is attacker-reachable: the <binary> element text is entry-point input with no shown length/format constraint (only the non-IS_UNDEF check at line 21), and php_base64_decode's standard semantics (PHP-7.0 ext/standard/base64.c, non-strict mode) return NULL when '=' occurs at i%4==1 (e.g., content "a="), confirmed by upstream regression bug #72750 whose fixed output is string(0) "". No statement between lines 32 and 35 tests new_str, so ZVAL_STR stores a NULL value pointer with type IS_STRING_EX; the NULL is dereferenced on the ST_FIELD-undef path at line 56 (zval_ptr_dtor -> Z_DELREF reads NULL->gc.refcount), at the class-name check line 66 (Z_STRLEN of a NULL zend_string), or at teardown of the hash populated at line 105/line 109. All guards on the path (line 10 top==0, line 21 IS_UNDEF, line 50 top>1, line 55 ST_FIELD) constrain stack indices or zval types, not new_str, so none pass the Guard-Identity Audit for this sink. The absent one-statement fix is the NULL/return-status check `if (new_str) { ZVAL_STR(&ent1->data, new_str); } else { ZVAL_EMPTY_STRING(&ent1->data); }`; primary CWE is CWE-476 (NULL pointer dereference).

assumptions: php_base64_decode (PHP-7.0, non-strict) returns NULL when a padding '=' appears at i%4==1 — confirmed by the shown call's callee semantics and by upstream bug #72750's regression test (fixed output string(0) "").
The stack's `top` counter bounds `elements[top-1]`; the in-fragment top guard (line 10) and `top > 1` check (line 50) make every wddx_stack_top/efree-of-entry use in-bounds.
ent1->varname is a NUL-terminated heap string assigned by the (unshown) push handler; strlen at line 105 is safe for valid deserialization flow.
limitations: Later upstream hardenings not present here (serialize/unserialize class guard, object_init_ex SUCCESS check, ZSTR_EMPTY_ALLOC fast-path for binary) are outside the one-statement pair difference and were not used as findings.
The __wakeup call (line 44) and potential HASH_OF on a property-less object were not confirmed as flaws from the fragment alone.
The EL_BINARY '='-padding input is the concrete degenerate witness; other NULL-producing inputs (e.g. a NUL byte break) are equivalent but unnecessary.

verdict.summary: EvalGatherNd validates only that indices are non-negative (lines 6-12) and never bounds them above against the params dimensions, so an attacker-controlled indices tensor containing any non-negative index that is at least as large as the corresponding params dimension passes every shown guard and reaches the GatherNd/GatherNdString sinks (lines 16-28), which by standard gather semantics use those values to index params, producing an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The absent one-statement fix is an upper-bound check comparing each index against the params dimension.

evidence.reason: Sink consumes the attacker-controlled indices buffer from line 4; the only guards on the path are line 7 'if (indices_values[i] < 0)' and line 12 'TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, indices_has_only_positive_elements);', whose admitted set is [0, IndicesT_MAX] — they constrain only the lower bound. A witness index v >= params_dim (e.g., INT32_MAX) satisfies line 7 (v < 0 false), keeps the flag true, passes line 12, and is forwarded unchanged to GatherNd, whose name-implied semantics index params at v, reading out of bounds. The Guard-Identity Audit fails for the magnitude hazard (wrong property: sign vs. upper bound), so the guard is insufficient; the absent fix form is an upper-bound/equality check of each index against params->dims before dispatch. Primary CWE-125 (OOB read).

Same failure set and path as the numeric GatherNd sink: the non-negative-but-unbounded index values passed through lines 6-12 reach GatherNdString, which uses them to index the params string tensor; any index >= the params dimension causes an out-of-bounds read. The shown negativity guard does not constrain the upper magnitude (Guard-Identity Audit: insufficient coverage), and the upper-bound check against params dims is absent. Primary CWE-125.

assumptions: indices tensor contents are attacker-controlled model input (provenance from GetTensorData<IndicesT>(indices), line 4).
GatherNd/GatherNdString follow their standard name-implied semantics: index into params using the supplied index values, requiring 0 <= v < params_dim.
Line 5 num_indices = indices->bytes / sizeof(IndicesT) bounds the in-fragment read loop, so the loop itself is safe (consumes at most indices->bytes bytes).
limitations: params' concrete dimensions/capacity are not declared in the fragment; the out-of-domain magnitude is established as a range (any v >= the runtime params dimension, up to IndicesT_MAX) rather than an exact absent dim.

The exact historical pairing (whether the negativity check is the pre-existing code) is not needed for the verdict; the ledger is decided by the least-protected sink, which lacks any upper-bound validation.
ReportError at lines 30-32 is a %s-with-char*-format call and is safe; it is not a finding.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in the per-channel range computation: `depth` is taken from `input_max.NumElements()` (line 6), but `input_min` is validated only via `input_min.dim_size(0) == depth` (line 8). An attacker-controlled `input_min` shaped `[depth, 0]` passes that check while `input_min.NumElements()` is 0, so the loop `for (int64_t i = 0; i < depth; ++i)` reads `input_min_data[i]` out of bounds at line 52. The missing fix is an element-count check such as `input_min.NumElements() == depth` instead of the first-dimension check; `input_max_data[i]` is protected because its check (line 12) forces its own element count to equal `depth`.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read (CWE-125). Taint: `input_min` shape is entry-point data whose only shown constraint is line 8 (`input_min.dim_size(0) == depth`), leaving shapes like `[depth, 0]` in its residual domain, so the buffer from line 16 (`input_min.flat<float>().data()`) holds `NumElements() == 0` floats. Depth at line 6 (`const size_t depth = input_max.NumElements();`) is attacker-controlled with no shown minimum (e.g., 5). The guard at line 8 fails the Guard-Identity Audit by wrong-target drift: it constrains the first-dimension size against `input_max`'s count, not the flat element count (NumElements) that the index `i` reaches. With `input_max` having 5 elements and `input_min` shaped `[5, 0]`, line 8 passes (5 == 5), line 42 (`for (int64_t i = 0; i < depth; ++i)`) executes i = 0..4, and line 52 reads `input_min_data[0..4]` from a 0-element buffer. The absent one-statement fix is an element-count check, e.g., `OP_REQUIRES(ctx, input_min.NumElements() == depth, ...)` replacing the line 8 `dim_size(0)` comparison. Note `input_max_data[i]` is not the vulnerable operand: line 12 plus line 6 force `input_max.NumElements() == depth`.

assumptions: Line 6: `depth = input_max.NumElements()` is attacker-controlled with no shown minimum or cap.
Line 16/17: standard TensorFlow `flat<T>().data()` is valid for exactly `NumElements()` elements of the respective tensor.
Zero-size dimensions (e.g., shape `[depth, 0]`) are valid TensorFlow tensor shapes; the fragment imposes no rank or positive-dimension constraint.
limitations: `transposed_input.chip<0>(i)` (lines 44, 46) may be OOB if `depth` exceeds `input`'s channel/column count, but `input`'s shape and therefore the chip target capacity are not shown in the fragment, so this is unconfirmable per the capacity rule.
`input_min.dim_size(0)` / `input_max.dim_size(0)` on rank-0 (scalar) tensors is undefined behavior in release builds with a nondeterministic outcome; not used as a witness.

`std::abs(min_per_channel)` at line 50 overflows in the signed `int32_t` domain when the value is INT32_MIN; the corrupted result only feeds float output math at line 54, with no memory/index/security-decision consumer, so it is a robustness concern.
`std::vector<float> ranges(depth)` (line 18) can be large, but it mirrors the already-existing `input_max` element count with equal float size (no amplification), so it is demoted.
Under the `_MSC_VER` OpenMP branch (line 36) the missing `reduction(max: out_min_max)` clause races on a float output only; no memory-safety or security sink is involved.

verdict.summary: No confirmable vulnerability in the shown fragment: every dangerous operation carries a verbatim protective statement or has an empty failure set. The upsampler fill is exactly bounded by `for(i = 0;i < m_ucCount;i++)` (line 18) against the `m_ucCount`-element allocation (line 15), excluding index `i >= m_ucCount`; both memsets match their allocations (lines 10-11 and 15-16, pointer sizes equal); the recursive call is NULL-guarded (lines 32-33). The only unresolved concerns - UBYTE counter non-termination at `m_ucCount >= 256`, unchecked `AllocMem`/`ComponentOf`/`TablesOf` NULL results, and `m_ucCount*8` overflow - have no producer of the failing value in the fragment and are demoted to limitations.

assumptions: Capacity of `m_ppUpsampler` is exactly `m_ucCount` elements per the allocation at line 15; capacity of `m_ppDecodingMCU` is `m_ucCount*8` elements per the allocation at line 10.
`UBYTE i` (line 5) is an unsigned 8-bit type, so the loop counter domain is 0..255.
`sizeof(class Upsampler *)` equals `sizeof(class UpsamplerBase *)` because both are object pointer types (line 15 vs line 16).
The memset extent expressions at lines 10-11 and 15-16 are evaluated at `size_t` precision from the same operands.
limitations: Non-termination of the loop at line 18 for `m_ucCount >= 256` is not a confirmed finding: `m_ucCount` is an unshown member with no shown producer of a value >= 256, and even then the UBYTE counter keeps every write index <= 255, inside the allocation.

Unchecked `AllocMem` returns (lines 10, 15) and unguarded `ComponentOf`/`TablesOf` dereferences (lines 19, 26) would be NULL-deref flaws only if a NULL producer were demonstrated in the fragment; none is shown (library-error contract only).
Possible integer overflow of `m_ucCount*8` at line 10 depends on an unshown `m_ucCount` type and magnitude.
Behavior of unshown callees (`BuildCommon`, `CreateUpsampler`, `ComponentOf`, `TablesOf`) is out of scope.

verdict.summary: TransposeShapeFn reads the attacker-controlled perm constant and, for a negative perm element (e.g. -1), the guard at line 51 only checks in_idx >= rank, so a negative in_idx reaches c->Dim(input, in_idx) at line 55 and indexes before the input shape's dimension array, causing an out-of-bounds read. The fix is to add the missing negative bound: if (in_idx < 0 || in_idx >= rank).

evidence.reason: in_idx originates at line 48 as data[i], where data = AsInt64<int32>(perm, rank) (line 43) preserves the signed values of the attacker-controlled perm constant tensor from line 4 (input_tensor(1)); the witness value -1 is in the residual range because no shown statement constrains the sign of perm elements. The guard at line 51 (if (in_idx >= rank)) admits all negative values (-1 >= rank is false), and no other guard on the path (lines 9, 23, 33, 35, 36) touches perm contents. The input shape's dimension array has capacity rank == 2, established by WithRank(input, rank, &input) at line 33, so index -1 is outside [0, rank-1]. c->Dim takes the index as an array subscript (standard name-implied semantics), so the read is out of bounds (CWE-125): index -1 with a 2-slot array, reached with in_idx = -1, perm = [-1, 0], input rank 2, all guards passed in order (line 51 admits the value). The absent fix is the negative bound in the guard: if (in_idx < 0 || in_idx >= rank).

assumptions: The perm constant tensor contents (line 4, input_tensor(1)) are attacker-controlled and may contain any int32/int64 value, including negatives; no shown validation filters them.
AsInt64<int32>(perm, rank) (line 43) returns exactly rank elements with int32 values widened to int64 without clamping, so a value of -1 in perm yields in_idx = -1 (line 48).
Lines 33 (WithRank(input, rank)) and 36 (WithValue(perm_elems, rank)) together establish that input's dimension array has exactly rank slots and that perm has exactly rank elements.
limitations: dims.resize(rank) at line 32 sizes an allocation from an unbounded attacker-derived rank (CWE-400-style DoS candidate); its exploitability depends on the magnitude accepted and unshown allocation-failure handling, so it is not asserted as the primary finding.

The loop counter at line 49 is int32_t while rank is int64_t; for rank > INT32_MAX the increment would overflow, but reaching such a rank requires the prior dims.resize to succeed (unshown environmental fact).

If the unshown c->Dim implementation internally bounds-checks its index, the negative in_idx would yield an unknown dimension instead of an OOB read; the verdict follows the standard array-subscript semantics of Dim and the actual TensorFlow fix, which added the negative check at the call site.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the protected counterpart: the instrument-index dereference (line 123) is guarded by the bounds check at line 120 (pat->data[i][2]<0 || pat->data[i][2]>=e->song.insLen), the row index i is guarded at lines 15-17, the volume divisor chanVolMax is clamped at line 70, and the volColors index is clamped at lines 159-160. verdict.summary: In gf_hinter_finalize, the GF_ESD* returned by gf_isom_get_esd(file, sceneT, 1) (L105) and gf_isom_get_esd(file, odT, 1) (L66) is dereferenced without a NULL check at L134-135/L98-99 (esd->OCRESID / esd->ESID) and passed to gf_list_add (L102/L137). assumptions: gf_isom_get_esd(file, trackID, 1) returns NULL when the track or its sample description 1 has no ESD; this NULL outcome is corroborated in-fragment by the guard 'if (!esd) continue;' at L144 for tracks of the same file.

Uninitialized build of slc on paths where the OD embedding block did not run (odT==0, sample count != 1, or embedding failed) is a CWE-457-style robustness concern with no shown security consumer.
Unchecked return of gf_odf_desc_write (L167) and NULL-return semantics of gf_isom_get_sample were not confirmed as reachable NULL producers.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in the APNG decoder: an attacker-supplied short fcTL chunk (chunk.size < 34) is parsed at lines 142-149 without any size check, reading png_get_uint_32/16 and byte fields at chunk.p+12..chunk.p+33 past the end of the chunk buffer; a second OOB source read occurs in memcpy(chunkIHDR.p + 8, chunk.p + 12, 8) at line 161 for chunk.size in [12,19]. The missing fix is a chunk.size >= 34 guard before parsing fcTL fields.

evidence.reason: chunk.size originates from the attacker-controlled PNG chunk length field via read_chunk(&r, &chunk) (line 64) and is never constrained in the fragment; the CHUNK access convention (chunk.p holds chunk.size bytes, cf. processing_data(png_ptr, info_ptr, chunk.p, chunk.size) at line 176 and the sibling guarded access chunkIHDR.size == 25 at line 39) fixes the buffer length at chunk.size. A complete fcTL chunk with total size 12 (length field 0) passes guards 65, 66 and the fcTL dispatch at 73-74 (hasInfo is false initially), then reaches this read: png_get_uint_32(chunk.p + 12) reads bytes 12..15 past the 12-byte buffer, and the parse continues through chunk.p[33] at line 149 (22 bytes OOB). The absent one-statement fix is a size guard such as 'if (chunk.size < 34) { delete[] chunk.p; break; }' before the field parse; guard at lines 153-155 runs after the reads and constrains w0/h0/x0/y0 values, not chunk buffer extent (wrong-target drift). Heap OOB read: CWE-125.

Deepest OOB access of the fcTL parse on the same path as line 142: for the admitted witness chunk (fcTL, chunk.size = 12, hasInfo = false, guards 65/66/73-74 passed), reading chunk.p[33] dereferences byte 33 of a 12-byte buffer, i.e. 22 bytes past the heap allocation. The guard at 153-155 is evaluated after this statement and audits w0/h0/x0/y0/dop/bop values, not chunk buffer length. Absent fix: the chunk.size >= 34 size check. CWE-125.

Second sink of the same missing-check class: reached when hasInfo is true (attacker supplies an IDAT first, line 174-176) and an fcTL chunk then arrives. The memcpy reads 8 bytes from chunk.p + 12..19; for a complete fcTL chunk with chunk.size in [12,19] this reads past the chunk.p allocation. No chunk.size validation exists on this path (the 153-155 guard constrains frame coordinates, not buffer extent), so the absent fix is the same size guard before fcTL parsing. CWE-125 heap OOB read.

assumptions: chunk.p points to a heap buffer of exactly chunk.size bytes: evidenced by the in-fragment access conventions processing_data(png_ptr, info_ptr, chunk.p, chunk.size) (lines 176, 192), processing_data(..., chunk.p + 4, chunk.size - 4) (line 183), and the sibling tooltip-style guarded access chunkIHDR.size == 25 before touching chunkIHDR.p + 8..15 (lines 39-41).
png_get_uint_32/png_get_uint_16 read 4/2 bytes at the given offset (standard PNG helper semantics).

A PNG chunk has total size 12 + length-field (4 length + 4 type + data + 4 CRC), so an attacker-controlled length of 0 yields a 12-byte chunk, matching the IHDR convention (size 25 for 13 data bytes).
limitations: Integer-overflow candidates at rowbytes = w * 4 / imagesize = h * rowbytes (lines 53-54), w0 * h0 (line 103), and the x0 + w0 addition in the guard (line 154) depend on the numeric value of cMaxPNGSize, which is not defined in the fragment; not confirmable from shown code.

fdAT 'chunk.size - 16' underflow (line 181) stores a huge value at chunk.p+4..7 that is never consumed as a length, and memcpy(chunk.p + 8, "IDAT", 4) stays in-bounds for the minimum 12-byte chunk; not a confirmed finding.
isAbc reads at chunk.p[4..7] (lines 187-188) stay within the minimum 12-byte chunk; no finding.

First-frame pixel-loop out-of-bounds (lines 114, 121-124) would require imagesize wrap, which requires cMaxPNGSize >= 2^30 (unshown); sub-frame indices are otherwise bounded by the line 153-155 guard.

verdict.summary: No dangerous sink with a demonstrated failing value exists in the shown fragment. All memory-touching work is inside the unshown helpers GatherNd<T, IndicesT> (lines 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15) and GatherNdString<IndicesT> (line 17), invoked with pointers but with no in-fragment capacity, index derivation, or guard, so OOB/NULL hypotheses are unconfirmable limitations (Phase 4 requires a visible capacity/producer). The only visible string sink, context->ReportError (lines 19-21), uses the compile-time literal format "Params type '%s' are not supported by gather_nd." with a fixed TfLiteTypeGetName argument, excluding format-string and log injection. The switch is fail-closed: every params->type not matched by lines 4-17 reaches default (line 18) and returns kTfLiteError (line 22).

assumptions: params->type (line 3, line 21) is a TfLiteType enum consumed only by the switch and by TfLiteTypeGetName, which maps enum values to fixed internal name strings.
The format string at line 20 is a compile-time literal and cannot be replaced by attacker-controlled bytes.
Helper failures are propagated by the direct returns at lines 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17.
limitations: Out-of-bounds read/write inside GatherNd<T, IndicesT> (lines 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15) and GatherNdString<IndicesT> (line 17) is not confirmable: the object capacities and index arithmetic that could exceed them are inside unshown callees; no shown statement establishes a capacity or a derivation that exceeds it.
