Whether attacker-supplied indices values can be processed unsafely depends on the unshown helper internals and the unshown Eval-side indices-type dispatch; this is a limitation under the Verifiability Rule, since the helper calls have no in-fragment guard claiming to protect them.
No loops, crypto, file/access, or authz operations appear in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The kernel indexes params_nested_splits_in[0] at line 12 protected only by a DCHECK_GT (line 11), which is compiled out in NDEBUG/release builds. An attacker-supplied empty params_nested_splits list (size 0, no shown minimum) reaches the index in release builds, causing a heap out-of-bounds read. The absent fix is a runtime OP_REQUIRES validating params_nested_splits_in.size() > 0 before the access.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read (CWE-125): params_nested_splits_in is filled from context->input_list at lines 4-5 with no shown minimum on its size, so N==0 remains in the residual range. The only guard on the path is line 11 'DCHECK_GT(params_nested_splits_in.size(), 0);', a debug-only assert compiled out in NDEBUG builds, which fails the Guard-Identity Audit (no runtime effect). With N==0, the index expression params_nested_splits_in[0] on line 12 reads out of bounds. The absent one-statement fix is a runtime input-validation check such as OP_REQUIRES(context, params_nested_splits_in.size() > 0, errors::InvalidArgument(...)) before line 12.

assumptions: SPLITS_TYPE is a signed integer type (TensorFlow convention: int32/int64), so dim_size(0)-1 can be -1 but does not wrap unsigned.
DCHECK_GT is a debug-only assert that is compiled out under NDEBUG in release builds (standard C++/TensorFlow semantics).
OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK abort the kernel on a false condition or failed status.
limitations: A num_params value of -1 (when params_nested_splits_in[0].dim_size(0) == 0) cannot be confirmed as harmful: its only shown consumer is ValidateIndices (line 13), which fail-closed rejects out-of-range indices by name-implied semantics.
Potential out-of-bounds or index faults inside the unshown helpers ValidateIndices, MakeSplits, WriteSplits, and WriteValues (lines 13, 24-26, 29, 30-32) cannot be confirmed from this fragment.

If the op registration truly enforces N >= 1 (as the comment on line 11 claims), the empty-list path would be unreachable at runtime; that invariant is not shown as code in the fragment and cannot be credited under the analysis rules.
If line 11 were replaced by a runtime OP_REQUIRES, the fragment would be safe with respect to the line-12 OOB read; that protective form is exactly the absent fix identified.

verdict.summary: php_wddx_pop_element stores the unchecked return value of php_base64_decode() into ent1->data (lines 33-36); on WDDX <binary> content containing a non-base64 character the decoder returns NULL, and the resulting IS_STRING zval with a NULL zend_string* is dereferenced in-fragment at line 67 (Z_STRLEN(ent1->data)) when the field is named php_class_name inside a struct, or at lines 102-103 (add_property_zval / Z_DELREF) when merged into an object. The NULL/return-status check on new_str that would neutralize the failure is absent.

evidence.reason: NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476). new_str from php_base64_decode (lines 33-34) may be NULL because the <binary> element text is attacker-controlled XML character data with no shown constraint (line 34 reads it via Z_STRVAL/Z_STRLEN); the fragment stores it unconditionally at line 36 (ZVAL_STR(&ent1->data, new_str)) with no NULL check, leaving ent1->data as IS_STRING with a NULL zend_string*. When the field carries varname equal to PHP_CLASS_NAME_VAR (line 66) inside a struct (ent2 ST_STRUCT/IS_ARRAY, lines 56/62/68), evaluation of this condition reaches Z_STRLEN(ent1->data) = ZSTR_LEN(Z_STR(...)) = (NULL)->len and crashes. Every guard on the path (lines 11-13 top!=0, 22 data not IS_UNDEF, 40 not IS_OBJECT, 51 top>1, 56 ent2 not ST_FIELD, 62 ent2 IS_ARRAY, 65 varname non-NULL, 66 strcmp==0) constrains only stack geometry, entry types, or the varname string - none tests new_str or the stored pointer, so the NULL reaches the sink unguarded. The absent one-statement fix is a NULL/return-status check on the php_base64_decode result (e.g., if (!new_str)) before line 36.

assumptions: php_base64_decode returns NULL when the input contains a character outside the base64 alphabet (name-implied PHP callee contract; the fragment stores the result unchecked at line 36).

In-fragment access convention (lines 34, 56, 65-68): a leaf/binary stack entry carries its raw element text as IS_STRING and may also carry a non-NULL varname when declared inside <var name=...>, and a struct parent entry has type ST_STRUCT with IS_ARRAY data.
The struct keeps the converted object after a php_class_name var (line 94 ZVAL_COPY_VALUE), making the line 98-103 object branch reachable for later siblings.
limitations: The empty-stack NULL-deref class (wddx_stack_top with top==0) resolves PRESENT: line 11-13 guards all three wddx_stack_top calls (lines 20, 53 with line 51-52, 122), passing the Guard-Identity Audit; it is not the missing fix.
strlen(ent1->varname) at line 106 relies on varname NUL-termination established on the unshown push side; not analyzed as a finding.

The line 102-103 deref alternative requires the parent struct to have been converted to an object first; it is secondary to the line 67 deref, which needs only the attacker-chosen varname php_class_name.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched member of the pair. Every dangerous operation carries a verbatim protective statement: the 2*hash_len allocation at line 22 sizes both buffer halves; the PBKDF2 comparison at line 48 is bounded to keylen (line 41) and targets the stored key tail, so key+keylen ends exactly at the allocation boundary; NULL outcomes of digest_alloc and calloc are fail-closed at lines 13-17 and 23-24; and all read/crypto/digest status returns are consumed at lines 35-36, 45-46, and 53-54. No over-read, over-write, NULL dereference, status flaw, or auth fail-open is derivable from the shown code.

assumptions: PBKDF2_SALT_LEN <= PBKDF2_LENGTH and both are positive build-time macros, so keylen = PBKDF2_LENGTH - PBKDF2_SALT_LEN >= 0 and the salt plus key tail fit within the 2*hash_len region (lines 39-41, 43-44, 48); these macros are not attacker-controlled and their ordering is an unshown build invariant.

digest_length(d) returns the positive digest length for the digest successfully allocated by digest_alloc(PASSWD_SUM) at line 12 (fail-closed at line 13), matching what digest_digest writes at line 51.
read_env_passwd/read_default_passwd write at most hash_len bytes into the provided buffer (name-implied contract); used only to confirm capacity sufficiency, not as a decisive protective statement.
crypto_memneq performs a constant-time comparison (name-implied); not credited as the decisive guard.
limitations: A failure requiring PBKDF2_SALT_LEN > PBKDF2_LENGTH (negative keylen converted to size_t) or PBKDF2_SALT_LEN == PBKDF2_LENGTH (zero-length compare admitting ret = 1) depends on unshown build-time macro values and is not derivable from the fragment, so it is demoted.
hash_len == 0 from digest_length(d) would require a zero-length digest object that no shown producer can create; not derivable from shown code.

The caller's interpretation of the return value (0 vs 1) is not shown; within the fragment, ret = 1 is set only on an exact constant-time match and all mismatch/failure paths return 0 or negative, so no fail-open auth decision is derivable.
An overfilling malicious read_env_passwd/read_default_passwd implementation is outside this fragment (the suspicious unshown helper would be the other member of the pair, not this code).

verdict.summary: In r_bin_ne_get_entrypoints, the moveable-entry branch indexes bin->segment_entries[segnum - 1] after only checking segnum > 0 (line 60). segnum is a raw attacker-controlled byte from the NE entry table, while the array's valid index space is 0..SegCount-1 (established by the sibling guard `bundle_type < bin->ne_header->SegCount` at line 64). A crafted NE file with a small SegCount and a moveable bundle carrying segnum > SegCount causes an out-of-bounds heap read at line 61.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds heap read: segnum is read from the attacker-controlled entry table at line 57 (`ut8 segnum = *(bin->entry_table + off);`) with no shown constraint, and line 61 dereferences segment_entries[segnum - 1]. The only guard, line 60 (`if (segnum > 0)`), admits segnum in [1,255], which includes every index above the array's valid span 0..SegCount-1 (established in-fragment by the sibling guarded access at lines 64-66, `bundle_type < bin->ne_header->SegCount`). A witnessed file with SegCount=1 and segnum=2 passes guards at lines 2, 10, 30, 34, 42, 51, 55, and 60, and reads segment_entries[1]. The absent one-statement fix is a bound check such as `segnum <= bin->ne_header->SegCount` before the index, matching the Fixed branch's guard; its absence is CWE-125 (OOB read).

assumptions: bin->segment_entries has valid indices 0..SegCount-1, established by the in-fragment access convention at lines 64-66 (bundle_type < bin->ne_header->SegCount) for the same array object.
NE header fields (SegCount, EntryTableLength, offsets) and entry-table bytes are attacker-controlled NE file content with no shown constraints.
limitations: Potential buffer-window mismatch for the inner ut16 reads at lines 57-59 (guard at line 42 is expressed over tableat while reads index bin->entry_table) cannot be confirmed because the identity entry_table == buffer + tableat is not shown in the fragment.
Integer overflow of `tableat + off` at lines 30/42 is not demonstrable from the shown types and is not reported.
r_list_get_n at line 22 with entry_cs - 1 == 0xFFFFFFFF is safe via standard in-range semantics plus the NULL ternary guard at line 23; not a finding.

verdict.summary: Use-after-free: freeaddrinfo(servinfo) at line 61 frees the addrinfo chain, but on the successful-bind path the dangling ptr->ai_addr is still dereferenced by getsockname at line 70 and by net_port_get/net_address_get at lines 77-78. The fixing one-statement change -- performing freeaddrinfo after the address has been consumed (or copying the sockaddr before the free) -- is absent.

evidence.reason: ptr->ai_addr is the address storage allocated by getaddrinfo (line 21) and freed by freeaddrinfo(servinfo) (line 61); the loop's bind-success path (line 54) breaks at line 58 and reaches line 70 with ptr non-NULL (line 63 admits it). getsockname writes the socket address into that freed buffer and reads/writes the freed ai_addrlen, a use-after-free (CWE-416). The absent fix statement is the relocation of freeaddrinfo(servinfo) to after the address reads (lines 70-78), which the fragment lacks.

Reads the same ptr->ai_addr that freeaddrinfo(servinfo) (line 61) freed after the addrinfo chain was allocated at line 21; reachable on the bind-success path via lines 58 and 63. The lifetime-ordering fix (free after this use) is absent, so this is a second use-after-free read (CWE-416).

Consumes the freed ptr->ai_addr (freed at line 61, allocated at line 21) on the bind-success path; sizeof(addr) only bounds the output buffer and does not fix the input's lifetime. The needed fix -- freeaddrinfo after the last address use -- is absent; use-after-free read, CWE-416.

assumptions: getaddrinfo at line 21 allocates the addrinfo chain and servinfo owns it; this is the object whose lifetime line 61 ends (standard getaddrinfo/freeaddrinfo semantics).
freeaddrinfo(servinfo) at line 61 frees every node of the chain, including the node ptr points to and its ai_addr/ai_addrlen storage.
A bind success (line 54) forces the break at line 58, so the path to lines 70, 77, 78 is the guaranteed success path, not an exceptional branch.
limitations: The snprintf return value (line 20) is unused, but the write is bounded by sizeof(strport) (capacity 8) and *port's declared unsigned-short domain, so no overflow is derivable.
Manifestation of the UAF (crash vs. silent heap corruption) depends on allocator state between line 61 and line 70, which is not shown.
close(fd) return values (lines 31, 85) are ignored; no security consequence is derivable within this fragment.
cfgaddr is passed to getaddrinfo and DPRINTF only; no injection sink exists with it in this fragment.

verdict.summary: All fivefold broadcast pointer advances exactly match the in-fragment flat-size invariants (input1 = y0*y1*y2*y4, input2 = y0*y2*y3*y4, output = y0*y1*y2*y3*y4): input2 is re-based each i1 iteration by 'input2_data_ptr = input2_data_reset;' (lines 51 and 80), input1 is advanced only once per i2 by 'input1_data_ptr += y4;' outside the y3 loop (line 60), and no failing value demonstrably reaches elementwise_f (lines 54-55) or scalar_broadcast_f (lines 82-83). The only in-fragment-derived degenerate candidate (output overwrite when y4 == 0 is admitted by the line-45 guard) cannot be confirmed because the output buffer capacity is never shown.

assumptions: broadcast_shape has at least 5 entries (the fragment itself indexes entries 0..4 at lines 40-44, an in-fragment access convention).

The pattern invariants stated in the fragment hold: input1.shape.FlatSize = y0*y1*y2*y4 and input2.shape.FlatSize = y0*y2*y3*y4 (lines 38-39), with y3 broadcast for input1 and y1 broadcast for input2.
elementwise_f/scalar_broadcast_f implement standard bounded elementwise semantics over exactly the passed count (a count of 0 performs no access).
The output write count y0*y1*y2*y3*y4 is the intended fully broadcast output; the output buffer is sized by the caller.
limitations: y4 == 0 (and negative y4) is admitted into the else branch by the line-45 guard 'if (y4 > 1)', and that branch writes y0*y1*y2*y3 elements whose pattern product would be 0; this is not confirmed as OOB because the output buffer capacity (output_shape.FlatSize() or an allocation) is never shown in the fragment, and a 0-size tensor reaching this kernel would require unshown caller/tensor-validation facts.
NULL input/output pointer dereference is not confirmable: no NULL producer is shown in the fragment; NULL from an unshown caller is an unshown-environment failure.
Very large (INT_MAX-scale) dimensions could make total writes large, but the backing buffer sizes are caller-side and never shown, so no capacity violation is derivable.
No status, authz, injection, crypto, file, or disclosure sink exists in the fragment, so no other finding was evaluated.

verdict.summary: In ccp_run_aes_gcm_cmd, the decrypt path computes ilen = aes->src_len - authsize with no check that src_len >= authsize; a zero/short ciphertext (zero-length input is explicitly contemplated at lines 50-51) wraps ilen to ~2^32, and that value is used as the DMA length for ccp_init_data(src/dst) and as the GCTR loop bound, causing an out-of-bounds DMA read/write. Independently, aes->iv_len is never validated, so dm_offset = CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES - aes->iv_len underflows when iv_len exceeds the ctx allocation, and the wrapped offset is used at ccp_set_dm_area(&ctx, ...). Both missing bound checks are the absent one-statement fixes.

evidence.reason: Unsigned underflow sink: aes->src_len (unsigned int, AEAD-request field) has no shown lower bound and line 50-51 explicitly contemplates input lengths of 0; aes->authsize is constrained to {4,8,12,13,14,15,16} by the switch at lines 34-45 (16 also via the line 33 default). On the decrypt branch (lines 59-63), src_len=0 with authsize=16 yields ilen=0xFFFFFFF0, which passes the guard `if (ilen > 0)` at line 144 (wrong-target/after-the-fact: it admits the wrapped value) and all earlier guards (lines 21, 24-27, 29, 34-44 constrain iv/key_len/key/authsize, never src_len - wrong-target drift). The wrapped value is consumed as the length argument of ccp_init_data(&src,...,ilen,...) and ccp_init_data(&dst,...,ilen,...) at lines 148-159 and as the GCTR loop bound `while (src.sg_wa.bytes_left)` at line 167, producing an out-of-bounds DMA read/write (CWE-787) caused by the underflow (CWE-191). The absent one-statement fix is a bound check `if (aes->src_len < authsize) return -EINVAL;` before the subtraction.

Second unsigned-underflow sink: aes->iv_len is never validated in the fragment (the 96-bit IV statement at lines 93-95 is an unenforced comment). When iv_len exceeds the ctx allocation size shown at lines 97-99 (ccp_init_dm_workarea(&ctx, cmd_q, CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES, ...)), dm_offset wraps to a near-2^32 value and is consumed at ccp_set_dm_area(&ctx, dm_offset, aes->iv, 0, aes->iv_len) (lines 104 and 197) with length iv_len, and by ccp_copy_to_sb/ccp_copy_from_sb on &ctx (lines 108-109, 190-191, 201-202), addressing outside the allocation for a DMA read and write (CWE-191 -> CWE-787). No shown guard constrains iv_len (lines 21-22/24-27/29-30 test iv/key_len/key only - wrong-target drift). The absent one-statement fix is a bound/equality check on aes->iv_len against CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES before this arithmetic.

assumptions: ctx allocation capacity is CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES (lines 97-99) and key DMA area is at least CCP_SB_BYTES (line 76-78), with key_len validated to {16,24,32} (lines 24-27).

final_wa capacity is AES_BLOCK_SIZE (16 bytes) per line 211, so final[0]/final[1] (lines 216-217) are in-bounds; authsize <= 16 keeps ccp_get_dm_area/ccp_set_dm_area on the tag path in-bounds (lines 242, 245, 249).
Decrypt is a supported path because the fragment branches on aes->action at lines 56 and 240.
The guard `if (nbytes)` at line 172 confines op.u.aes.size in line 174 to 7..119 (nbytes in 1..15), with no failure set.
limitations: Arrival of a decrypt request with src_len < authsize at this driver depends on the unshown crypto-API/AEAD wrapper (crypto_aead_decrypt may reject cryptlen < authsize); that check is not shown and is not credited, but it caps confidence below 0.91.
The exact DMA overrun mechanics of the oversized ilen depend on unshown ccp_init_data and CCP engine behavior interpreted by name-implied semantics.
For S2, the absence of any bounds check in ccp_set_dm_area's offset use is inferred from the name-implied 'set area' semantics, not from a shown callee body.
The 32-bit wrap of aes->aad_len * 8 and ilen * 8 in lines 216-217 (for lengths >= 2^29) is self-consistent within this driver and is treated as functional, not a confirmed security finding.
Non-termination of the GCTR loop in the underflow case was not separately confirmed and is subsumed by the OOB DMA finding.

verdict.summary: FractionalAvgPoolGrad-style backward op indexes the in_backprop Eigen map with in_index = (b*in_rows + in_r)*in_cols + in_c, where in_r and in_c originate from row_seq_tensor/col_seq_tensor values that are only length-checked (L38, L44), never value-checked. A sequence value of -1 (admitted by every shown guard) yields in_index = -5 into the 16-element double temp buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write (and read) at L109.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write (CWE-787) and OOB read (CWE-125) at the in_backprop sink. in_row_start = row_seq_tensor_flat(r) (L86) and in_col_start = col_seq_tensor_flat(c) (L91) are entry-point int64 values (inputs at L30-31) whose only constraints are the count checks row_seq_tensor.NumElements() > out_rows (L38) and col_seq_tensor.NumElements() > out_cols (L44) — counts, not values (wrong-target drift), so -1 is admitted. The end clamps in_row_end = std::min(in_row_end, in_max_row_index) (L89) and in_col_end = std::min(in_col_end, in_max_col_index) (L94) cap ends only and never constrain starts. Witness: orig_input_tensor_shape=[1,4,4,1] (passes L25-26) gives in_rows=in_cols=4 with a 16-double temp buffer (L62-71, matrix cols in_cols*in_rows*in_batch=16 at L76); out_backprop=[1,1,1,1]; row/col sequences [−1,0] pass L38/L44 (2 > 1); loops at L101/L102 execute once with in_r=in_c=−1, so in_index=(0*4−1)*4−1=−5 (L103) and coeffRef(0,−5) accesses 5 doubles before buffer start, written via in_backprop_ref += at L110-111. Absent fix: a value-range check such as OP_REQUIRES(context, in_row_start >= 0 && in_row_start < in_rows) with the symmetric column check, before the loop at L101.

assumptions: Temp buffer capacity of 16 doubles derived in-fragment from orig_input_tensor_shape values (L55-58), in_shape allocation (L62-71), and the map dimensions in_cols * in_rows * in_batch at L76.
Eigen Map::coeffRef performs unchecked raw-pointer addressing by its standard semantics.
limitations: out_backprop rank is never validated before dim_size(0..3) at L33-36; a rank < 4 tensor could read past TensorShape internals (framework-dependent, not counted).

out_depth is bounded only by the d-loop (L105) while the temp matrix has in_depth rows; a second attacker-reachable OOB path to the same L109 sink exists when out_depth > in_depth and no equality check is shown — same sink statement, so folded into the single evidence item.
Negative/zero num_elements_in_pooling_cell (L96-97) yields double division semantics without memory impact; not a finding.
Huge in_* dims could overflow the L76 product before allocation; allocation failure is handled fail-closed by OP_REQUIRES_OK at L69-71, so not counted.

verdict.summary: check_passwd() allocates a 2*hash_len buffer (line 22), splits it into passwd1_sum/passwd2_sum regions of exactly hash_len bytes (line 26), checks digest_alloc (line 13), calloc (line 23), and every security-relevant return status before use (lines 35, 45, 53), and all strncmp/KDF/digest accesses stay within the in-fragment capacity. No demonstrated failing value reaches any sink; the fragment is the fixed member with decisive protective statements present.

assumptions: Line 22 `calloc(hash_len * 2, ...)` establishes the full buffer capacity, so `passwd2_sum = passwd1_sum + hash_len` (line 26) yields a second region of exactly hash_len bytes; all later reads/writes (lines 39, 43-44, 48, 51, 56) are bounded by this in-fragment capacity.

The fragment's own layout convention (lines 39-41: key at passwd2_sum + PBKDF2_SALT_LEN, keylen = PBKDF2_LENGTH - PBKDF2_SALT_LEN) partitions a stored blob of PBKDF2_LENGTH = hash_len bytes into salt + key, keeping key accesses in-bounds.
digest_length(d) (line 19) and PBKDF2_LENGTH (line 10) are positive lengths per standard digest-API/config semantics, so hash_len == 0 is not derivable from shown code.
read_env_passwd/read_default_passwd (lines 29, 31) write at most len bytes per their name-implied standard semantics, and the fragment passes len equal to the region capacity.
limitations: Macro values (PBKDF2_LENGTH, PBKDF2_SALT_LEN, PBKDF2_COUNT) are not shown; a failing layout (e.g., keylen < 0) is not derivable from the fragment and would be contradicted by its own partition convention.
A hash_len == 0 scenario that would make strncmp(passwd1_sum, key, 0) always succeed is not producible from shown statements.

On a compare mismatch, the fragment returns the positive byte count from read_env_passwd/read_default_passwd rather than a 0/1 boolean; whether that is mis-handled depends on the unshown caller, so it is not a confirmed finding.
strncmp digest comparison (lines 48, 56) is non-constant-time, a theoretical timing side channel on password verification, but no exploit is demonstrated from shown code.
digest_alloc failure (NULL d) is only config/environment-driven and is in any case guarded at line 13.

verdict.summary: The parameter-swap block corrupts switched_params.input2_shift: line 15 assigns unswitched_params.input1_multiplier instead of unswitched_params.input1_shift, breaking the symmetric offset/multiplier/shift swap established by lines 10-14. When broadcast_category is anything other than kFirstInputBroadcastsFast (admitted by lines 17-19), params binds to switched_params (lines 21-22) and elementwise_f (lines 54-55) / scalar_broadcast_f (lines 82-83) consume a multiplier value in the shift slot, producing incorrect quantized arithmetic output (CWE-682). The one-statement fix, switched_params.input2_shift = unswitched_params.input1_shift;, is absent.

evidence.reason: Wrong-operand assignment (CWE-682): unswitched_params.input1_multiplier (entry-point quantization data, full domain, unconstrained) is written into the input2_shift slot, while lines 10-14 establish the swap must pair like fields (shift with shift, as line 12 pairs input1_shift with input2_shift). When use_unswitched is false — any broadcast_category other than kFirstInputBroadcastsFast admitted by lines 17-19 — params is bound to switched_params at line 22, so the corrupted input2_shift reaches elementwise_f (line 54) and scalar_broadcast_f (line 82), where the quantized scaling multiplies use a fixedpoint-multiplier magnitude in place of the shift exponent, corrupting output values for any model with input1_multiplier != input1_shift. No guard on the path constrains or corrects the value; the absent fix statement is switched_params.input2_shift = unswitched_params.input1_shift;.

assumptions: params.broadcast_shape has at least 5 entries (established by the fragment's unconditional reads at lines 40-44).

The loop extents follow the fragment's own flat-size model (lines 38-39: input1 = y0*y1*y2*y4, input2 = y0*y2*y3*y4, output = y0*y1*y2*y3*y4), making the loop accesses internally consistent given matching caller capacities.

elementwise_f/scalar_broadcast_f are standard TFLite quantized helpers that consume params.input2_multiplier and params.input2_shift as a fixedpoint multiplier/exponent decomposition (named-parameter semantics).

External cross-check: the fragment equals TensorFlow's post-CVE-2021-37688 fixed BinaryBroadcastFiveFold except for line 15; upstream (e.g. commit 15691e456c7dc9bd6be203b09765b063bf4a380c) has switched_params.input2_shift = unswitched_params.input1_shift;, confirming line 15 is the pair's single mutated statement.
limitations: NULL dereference at line 82 (*input1_data_ptr): the null-check guard at line 66 is present and passes the Guard-Identity Audit, but no NULL producer is demonstrated inside the fragment (pointers come from callers), so this class was not a confirmable finding.

Out-of-bounds reads/writes at lines 54-55 and 82-83 sized by y3/y4: buffer capacities are not established in the fragment (no allocation, sizeof, or declared sizes), so OOB claims are demoted to limitations.
The presence of the line-66 null check (the real CVE-2021-37688 fix) does not neutralize the line-15 defect; the verdict is decided by the least-protected sink.

verdict.summary: protocol_client_msg processes attacker-controlled VNC messages using only exact-equality length checks (len == 1 / len == 8 / len == 4), so short and length-mismatched messages reach unguarded sinks. CUT_TEXT: with len=9 and dlen=0x1000 (read_u32 at line 70), client_cut_text reads 4096 bytes from data+8 while only len-8=1 byte of the received span [0,len) is valid, an OOB read (CWE-125); with len in 2..7 even the length field read is OOB. SET_ENCODINGS: with len=5 and limit=1 the loop's memcpy writes data[4..7] beyond the received span (CWE-787). The decisive absent statements are `if (dlen > (len - 8)) return 20;` and `if (limit > (len - 4) / 4) return 4 + (limit * 4);` (plus the missing `if (len < N) return N;` minimum-length guards in every case).

evidence.reason: len is entry-point network size (size_t); guard at line 61 `if (len == 1)` excludes only len==1 and the block at lines 64-68 constrains dlen only on the len==8 branch, so residual len is {2..7} ∪ {9..} with dlen=read_u32(data,4) fully attacker-controlled. Witness len=9, dlen=0x1000 (bytes data[4..7]): guards L61 and L64 admit it, then client_cut_text reads 4096 bytes from data+8 while only len-8=1 byte of the received-message span [0,len) exists — OOB read, CWE-125; for len in 2..7 even read_u32(data,4) reads past the span. The absent fix is the value guard `if (dlen > (len - 8)) return 20;` (and, for short messages, `if (len < 8) return 8;`).

limit=read_u16(data,2) is an attacker-controlled 16-bit count; guards at lines 23-24 (`if (len == 1)`) admit len=5 and the len==4 block (lines 26-29) protects only the len==4 branch (wrong-branch coverage). Witness len=5, limit=1: loop `for (i = 0; i < limit; i++)` at line 33 runs i=0 and memcpy writes bytes data[4..7] while the received span is [0,5) — OOB write, CWE-787 (read_s32(data,4) at line 34 is likewise OOB). The absent fix is `if (limit > (len - 4) / 4) return 4 + (limit * 4);` bounding the count against the remaining message length.

assumptions: `data` is the received VNC message; only bytes [0, len) are valid — an access convention shown by the fragment's length-driven parsing and the frame-size returns `return 8 + dlen;` (line 67) and `return 4 + (limit * 4);` (line 29).
`len >= 1` on entry is established in-fragment by `vnc_read_when(vs, protocol_client_msg, 1);` (line 138).
read_u8/read_u16/read_u32/read_s32 are the standard fixed-offset field readers that index `data` at the shown offsets.
limitations: The network I/O layer that re-invokes this handler is not shown; per the no-caller-assumption rule, `len` is analyzed over the full residual domain admitted by the shown guards. If an unshown caller only ever delivered exactly a previously returned expected size, the short-len witnesses (len<8) might not be reachable — the dlen-vs-(len-8) mismatch class at line 70 and the unbounded limit loop at line 35 remain adversarial regardless of delivery granularity.
The physical allocation size of `data` is not shown; out-of-bounds is judged against the [0, len) received-message access convention rather than a visible malloc/new size.

The `8 + dlen` (line 67) and `4 + (limit * 4)` (line 29) return values can wrap at extreme attacker values; this class was not needed for the verdict and is left as an unconfirmed secondary hypothesis.
All printf calls use literal formats with data only as %d arguments; no format-string/command-injection sink exists in the fragment.

verdict.summary: SWTPM_NVRAM_CheckHeader validates the blob header against sizeof(bh), the size of the blobheader pointer (8 bytes on 64-bit), instead of sizeof(*bh), the size of the struct. A blob with length 8 (and totlen=8, min_version<=BLOB_HEADER_VERSION) passes every guard, after which the struct-field reads — most notably ntohs(bh->flags) at line 33 — read past the end of the 8-byte buffer, an out-of-bounds read. The absent one-statement fix is the struct-size bound 'if (length < sizeof(*bh))' at line 7.

verdict.summary: Stack buffer overflow in inbound_cap_ls: the attacker-controlled CAP LS capability list is split without limit and accumulated into a fixed 256-byte buffer via repeated strcat calls in an uncapped loop. Repeating a recognized capability (e.g. 'multi-prefix') more than ~18 times overflows buffer[256].

evidence.reason: buffer is declared as char buffer[256] (line 4), capacity indices 0..255. extensions_str is entry-point IRC server data split without a token cap by g_strsplit(extensions_str, " ", 0) (line 15), and iterated by the uncapped loop 'for (i=0; extensions[i]; i++)' (line 19). Each matching recognized extension appends a fixed literal to buffer; no guard bounds the loop count or checks remaining capacity. A CAP LS payload repeating 'multi-prefix' 19 times writes a 256-char string requiring a NUL at index 256, exceeding the 256-byte capacity (string length 9 + 19*13 = 256 after the 19th append), a stack buffer overflow (CWE-121/787). The absent one-statement fix is a bound/capacity check (e.g. capping loop iterations or requiring strlen(buffer) < sizeof(buffer) - max) before the strcat sinks.

assumptions: buffer has capacity 256 bytes as declared at line 4.
extensions_str is server-supplied (network) data; g_strsplit with max_tokens=0 splits without a token limit.
limitations: The appends use fixed string literals, so the attacker controls the number of appends (via repetition count) rather than the length of any single appended token; overflow therefore requires many repetitions of a recognized name.
No injection, NULL-deref, or crypto sink is present; the sole confirmed mechanism is the stack buffer overflow.

verdict.summary: In load_buffer, if get_prelink_info_range_from_mach0 returns NULL, the code jumps to the beach label while obj is still NULL (initialized at line 11, allocated only at line 18, after the jump), then dereferences it at `obj->cache_buf = NULL;` (line 67), causing a NULL pointer dereference on attacker-supplied Mach-O input.

evidence.reason: NULL dereference: obj is declared NULL at line 11 (`RKernelCacheObj *obj = NULL;`) and the only allocation, line 18 (`obj = R_NEW0 (RKernelCacheObj);`), executes after the `goto beach` at line 15. When `get_prelink_info_range_from_mach0` (line 13) returns NULL, line 14 (`if (!prelink_range)`) admits the NULL and line 15 jumps to `beach:` (line 65), reaching the store through NULL at line 67 with no check on obj on that path. The guard at line 19 is not on this path (it is evaluated after the jump), and the line 14 guard constrains prelink_range, not obj (wrong-target drift). The absent fix is a NULL-obj guard at the dereference (e.g., `if (obj) obj->cache_buf = NULL;`) or allocating obj before the prelink-range check; its absence makes a crafted file crash the loader (CWE-476, medium severity DoS).

assumptions: obj starts NULL via the visible declaration at line 11 and is assigned only at line 18, which is past the `goto beach` at line 15.
The NULL outcome of get_prelink_info_range_from_mach0 on malformed input is admitted by the fragment's own error branch at lines 14-15.
fbuf is non-NULL (result of r_buf_ref on the caller's buf), so line 66 is not a separate NULL issue.
limitations: rebase_info's unchecked NULL (line 10) is stored and boolean-tested only; it is never dereferenced in the fragment, so no finding is derived from it.
`bf->rbin->iob.io` (line 59) is framework-provided data with no shown NULL producer or in-fragment dereference before use, so an io NULL is not a confirmed finding.
Any out-of-bounds reading inside r_cf_value_dict_parse is delegated to a bounded parser call (lines 26-27) with no in-fragment derivation of an exceeding offset, so it is not a finding.

verdict.summary: pjstun_parse_msg performs out-of-bounds reads before its length guards execute. The attribute-header fields are dereferenced at line 42 ((*attr)->length) and line 51 ((*attr)->type) with only the loop condition `while (msg_len > 0 ...)` (line 36) as a pre-sink guard, which admits attacker-controlled msg_len values 1..3 while the object capacity from line 27/34 is exactly msg_len bytes after the 20-byte STUN header; the `if (msg_len < len)` check at line 45 runs after the reads (check-then-use drift) and cannot protect them. The STUN header fields at lines 11 and 26 are likewise read before any buf_len >= sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) validation. The absent fix statements are a minimum attribute-header length check on msg_len before dereferencing *attr (e.g., msg_len >= sizeof(pjstun_attr_hdr)) and an upfront buf_len >= sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) check before reading the header.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125): msg_len is attacker-controlled via line 26 (pj_ntohs of the 16-bit length field, residual range 0..65535). The line 27 equality check and line 34 fix the object capacity so exactly msg_len bytes exist from p_attr (buf_len == sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) + msg_len). The loop condition at line 36 (`while (msg_len > 0 ...)`) admits msg_len = 1, 2, 3, and the read of (*attr)->length at p_attr+2..3 then exceeds the msg_len-byte region by 1-2 bytes. The `if (msg_len < len)` guard at line 45 is evaluated only after this read (Guard-Identity Audit: check-then-use drift), so it protects nothing on this path. Absent fix: a minimum header-size check such as `if (msg_len < sizeof(pjstun_attr_hdr))` before dereferencing *attr.

OOB read (CWE-125): with the same attacker-controlled msg_len and the line 27/34-derived capacity of exactly msg_len bytes from p_attr, the loop condition at line 36 admits msg_len = 1, and this 2-byte read of (*attr)->type at p_attr+0..1 reads 1 byte beyond the object. The line 45 `if (msg_len < len)` check again executes after the read (check-then-use) and does not constrain it. Same absent fix: a minimum attribute-header length check on msg_len before reading the attribute fields.

OOB read (CWE-125): buf_len is an unconstrained entry-point parameter (network datagram length) with no shown minimum before this read of the 2-byte length field at buf+2..3; buf_len = 2 or 3 makes it read 1-2 bytes beyond the buffer. The only capacity check, `if (msg_len != buf_len - sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr))` at line 27, executes after this dereference (check-then-use drift), so it cannot protect it. Absent fix: an upfront `if (buf_len < sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr))` validation before reading the STUN header fields.

OOB read (CWE-125): with buf_len unconstrained (residual range 0..SIZE_MAX, no shown minimum) at this first dereference of the STUN header, buf_len = 0 or 1 admits this 2-byte read of msg->hdr->type at buf+0..1 past the end of the buffer. No guard precedes it; the line 27 length validation runs later. Absent fix: an upfront `if (buf_len < sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr))` check before the header-field reads.

assumptions: On the loop path the buffer capacity from p_attr is exactly msg_len bytes, derived in-fragment from line 27 (`if (msg_len != buf_len - sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr))`) and line 34 (`p_attr = (char*)buf + sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr);`).
msg->attr capacity equals PJ_ARRAY_SIZE(msg->attr) via line 6, and the loop bound at line 36 (`msg->attr_count < attr_max_cnt`) keeps the line 37 index in range.
pjstun_attr_hdr is a 4-byte header with the 2-byte length field at offset 2, consistent with the in-fragment arithmetic `len = pj_ntohs((*attr)->length) + sizeof(pjstun_attr_hdr)`.
limitations: The overread bytes are consumed only by the length-mismatch comparison (line 45, which returns an error for these sizes) and by a numeric warning log (line 55), so there is no attacker-visible disclosure and no memory write; impact is confined to a 1-3 byte OOB read, hence low severity.
NULL buf is not reported: no NULL producer is shown in the fragment; NULL can only originate from an unshown caller, which is outside the fragment's derivable evidence.
The top-of-function header overreads (lines 11/26) depend on the caller passing buf_len < 4, but buf_len is the unconstrained entry-point length and no shown statement excludes those values.

verdict.summary: do_i2c_md accepts an unbounded, attacker-controlled length (hextoul(argv[3], NULL), line 48). Assigning it to signed int nbytes (line 65) makes nbytes negative for length > INT_MAX; the one-sided cap at line 70 then passes that negative value as linebytes, which is used as the byte count of dm_i2c_read/i2c_read (lines 73/75) writing into the 16-byte stack buffer linebuf (line 67), producing an out-of-bounds write. No bound on length, nbytes, or linebytes excludes the negative range.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled argv[3] (line 48) yields uint length up to 0xFFFFFFFF; nbytes = length (line 65) makes it -1; line 70's one-sided cap (nbytes > DISP_LINE_LEN ? DISP_LINE_LEN : nbytes) admits -1; the read then transfers that negative count (huge when converted to an unsigned byte count) into the 16-byte stack buffer linebuf declared at line 67. Guards at lines 21/24/40/47/53 admit the witness 'i2c md <chip> 0 ffffffff', and the post-call ret check at line 77 cannot prevent the overflow during the call. Absent fix: a bound on length (e.g., if (length > 0x1000) return CMD_RET_USAGE;) or a lower clamp of linebytes. Primary CWE-787 out-of-bounds write.

evidence.snippet: ret = i2c_read(chip, addr, alen, linebuf, linebytes);
evidence.reason: Same failure in the non-DM build: linebytes derived from the unconstrained length can be negative (line 65/70) and is passed as the transfer count into the 16-byte linebuf (line 67), overrunning the buffer. No shown guard bounds length or linebytes on this path; the same absent bound/offset check applies. Primary CWE-787 out-of-bounds write.

assumptions: linebuf[DISP_LINE_LEN] (line 67) declares the on-stack buffer capacity consumed by the read (DISP_LINE_LEN elements, 16 in U-Boot).
dm_i2c_read/i2c_read follow standard read semantics: they transfer the supplied byte count into the caller's buffer; a negative int count converts to a huge unsigned transfer size.
limitations: If a particular I2C driver rejects a negative transfer count rather than converting it to a large unsigned count, the impact reduces to a robustness/DoS concern; the unguarded negative count reaching the read is nonetheless shown in-fragment.
Huge positive lengths (<= INT_MAX) cause unbounded loop iterations (resource exhaustion); not part of the primary finding.
The repeat path (i2c_dp_last_length, line 19) inherits the same unbounded provenance from a prior attacker command; not needed for the confirmed witness.

verdict.summary: ljpeg_start() reads a JPEG segment length into len = (data[2]<<8|data[3]) - 2 without any non-negative/bound check; a crafted marker (e.g., FF E1 00 00) yields len = -2, which converts to a huge size_t and makes fread(data, 1, len, ifp) consume the entire remaining attacker-controlled stream into the 65536-byte stack buffer uchar data[0x10000], causing a stack-based buffer overflow. The only pre-sink guard (line 15) checks tag, not len (wrong-target drift).

evidence.reason: len is derived at line 14 as (data[2]<<8|data[3]) - 2 from attacker-controlled stream bytes and retains residual range [-2, 65533] because the only prior guard, line 15 if (tag <= 0xff00) return 0;, constrains tag, not len (Guard-Identity Audit drift class 3, wrong target). Witness: marker bytes FF E1 00 00 yield tag=0xffe1 (passes line 15) and len=-2, which converts to a huge size_t; fread then writes all remaining attacker-supplied stream bytes into the stack array uchar data[0x10000] (capacity 65536, line 4), overflowing it once the stream holds more than 65532 further bytes. The absent one-statement fix is a lower-bound check on len before line 16, e.g., 'if (len < 0) return 0;' (or an upper/lower size bound), which does not appear anywhere in the fragment. Primary CWE-121: stack-based buffer overflow via unbounded write over a visible buffer size.

assumptions: uchar data[0x10000] has capacity 65536 bytes (line 4), establishing the object capacity that the unbounded fread write exceeds.

ifp is the attacker-controlled JPEG input stream (entry-point data); fread standard semantics apply: negative int len converts to a huge size_t and the call reads up to the request count or EOF into the destination buffer.
limitations: The concrete overflow magnitude (>65532 remaining stream bytes) is attacker-supplied file content rather than a constant fixed by shown code; it is part of the same entry-point input, so the witness is not demoted, but the magnitude is not a shown constant.

Unchecked fread status at lines 9/12 permits uninitialized/stale bytes to drive parsing (data[1] != 0xd8 gate) and can cause non-termination of the do-while loop at EOF with tag != 0xffda (DoS); no memory-safety impact confirmable from shown code alone.
Stale unbounded-but-in-bounds reads of data[] in the 0xffc3/0xffda cases (data[7], data[1+data[0]*2], data[3+data[0]*2]) are robustness concerns without a confirmed security consumer.
jh->huff / jh->free array capacities and make_decoder_ref internals are not shown, so indexing at lines 30 and 42-45 cannot be confirmed as out-of-bounds.
calloc failure at line 47 is handled by merror (abort) and the allocation size is bounded to ~1.57 MB by wide <= 65535 and the line 41 clrs <= 6 check.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only memory sink with a capacity visible in the fragment is the S3M pattern unpacker writing into 'pattern' (allocated 64*32*5 bytes at line 249), and every such write is bounded: 'row' is capped by the verbatim guard 'if (row >= 64)' with 'break' (lines 310-315) and 'chn' is masked to 0..31 by 'pi&31' (line 320), so the maximum write index is 63*160+31*5+4 = 10239 within the 10240-byte buffer. Reads of 'orders' and 'packed' are bounded by their shown allocations/counts, and array-index loops match their shown allocation sizes. Sinks on 'header->ord', 'smp[]', 'instr[]', and 'phead[]' have no capacity derivable from the shown fragment, so no out-of-bounds failure can be confirmed for them.

assumptions: 'orders' capacity equals header->ordnum (allocated at line 26 and read/indexed with the same count at lines 75-78).
'pattern' capacity is 64*32*5 = 10240 bytes (line 249); its 5-byte cell writes at lines 331-341 stay within it given row<=63 and chn<=31.
'packed' capacity is size+5 (line 285) and only 'size' bytes are read (line 296).
insParaPtrs/patParaPtrs/samplePtrs are allocated with header->insnum/header->patnum and only indexed within loops bounded by those counts.
'safeRead' is assumed to advance 'index' and return defaults at the end of 'packed', consistent with its name and the 'while (index<size)' condition.
limitations: Potential overflow of 'header->ord[j++]' (line 83) is not confirmable: the fragment shows no capacity for 'header->ord' (no declaration, allocation, or access convention), so an out-of-range index cannot be derived from shown code.

Potential overflow of 'smp[s]' (lines 139-182, 380-396), 'instr[i]' (lines 194, 202, 233), and 'phead[i]' (line 359) is not confirmable: capacities are outside the fragment and no access convention is shown.

If 'f.read(orders,1,header->ordnum)' (line 75) returns short, some 'orders' bytes may be uninitialized when read at line 80; no security-relevant consumer of that data is shown, so disclosure is unconfirmed.
Non-termination or misbehavior of the unpacker loop (lines 301-344) would require an unshown 'safeRead' flaw and is out of the fragment's evidence.
Pointer/sample/pattern arrays referenced through 'module' are assumed non-NULL due to the checks at lines 12-13.

verdict.summary: In mobi_decode_infl's delete branch, the unguarded pos-- at line 41 can drive pos to -1 (two consecutive deletes with dir '<' collapse the used size to 0), and the guard at line 45 only checks l < 0 and the top of d + l, so pos == -1 is admitted; the compare decoded[pos] at line 49 then performs a heap out-of-bounds read one byte before the decoded buffer (CWE-125), with a conditional out-of-bounds write via memmove at line 53.

evidence.reason: pos is attacker-rule-controlled on the delete path: with *decoded_size == 1 and rule bytes {0x03, 0x41, 0x41}, lines 9-11 set mod='d', dir='<' and keep pos=1 (line 12 not triggered since olddir==dir); two consecutive delete data bytes decrement pos to 0 then to -1 (line 41). l = *decoded_size - pos = 0 - (-1) = 1 (line 44), so the guard at line 45 ('if (l < 0 || d + l > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX)') admits the value: l < 0 is false and d + l telescopes to decoded + size, which is not > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX — wrong-target drift, since it constrains l and the upper end of d+l but never pos >= 0. The access convention decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX (line 45) bounds the buffer to indices 0..SIZEMAX-1, so decoded[pos] with pos == -1 is a heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The absent one-statement fix is a pos < 0 bound check on the delete path (e.g., extending line 45 to 'if (pos < 0 || l < 0 || ...)' or guarding the pos-- at line 41).

assumptions: decoded's capacity is INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX bytes, established by the in-fragment access convention decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX (lines 32, 45), giving valid indices 0..INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX-1.
*decoded_size is an entry-point input with no shown minimum, so values like 1 (and 0, reachable via the shown (*decoded_size)-- at line 54) are in the residual range.
rule is NUL-terminated, as the loop while ((c = *rule++)) at line 7 assumes.
limitations: The out-of-bounds write at line 53 (memmove(d, s, (size_t) l) with d = decoded - 1) is environment-dependent: it executes only if the unshown preceding byte decoded[-1] equals c at line 49; the guaranteed violation is the OOB read at line 49 (CWE-125).
A rule stream missing its NUL terminator would overrun rule's buffer, but rule's capacity is not shown in this fragment, so it cannot be confirmed as a finding.

Insert and position-setting sinks are protected: line 22 ('if (pos < 0 || pos > *decoded_size)') and line 32 ('if (l < 0 || d + l > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX)') keep those paths in bounds, but neither constrains the delete path's pos >= 0.

verdict.summary: getaddrinfo's failure status at line 23 is only checked with `if (ret < 0)` (line 24), which admits every non-negative error code (e.g., positive EAI/WSA codes on Windows). On such an admitted failure, `servinfo` (declared at line 4, never initialized) is consumed uninitialized by the for-loop at line 30 and by `freeaddrinfo(servinfo)` at line 63, causing undefined behavior/crash (CWE-754 primary, CWE-457 secondary). The absent one-statement fix is a complete status check (`if (ret != 0)` or `if (ret == 0)` inversion) at line 24.

evidence.snippet: for (ptr = servinfo, fd = -1; ptr != NULL; ptr = ptr->ai_next)
evidence.reason: Sink consuming uninitialized `servinfo`. `ret = getaddrinfo(...)` (line 23) can fail with a non-negative EAI/WSA error; guard line 24 `if (ret < 0)` admits all ret >= 0, so `servinfo` (declared line 4, never initialized) is read by the loop condition and dereferenced in the body. Guard-Identity Audit: same variable, same type/precision, no interleaved mutation, but the guard covers only the negative portion of the failure set — the complete fix `if (ret != 0)` is ABSENT. Uninitialized-pointer dereference → crash/DoS (CWE-754 primary, CWE-457 secondary).

Second sink consuming the same uninitialized `servinfo` after a non-negative `getaddrinfo` failure admitted by guard line 24 (`if (ret < 0)`). `servinfo` is declared at line 4 with no initialization and is passed to `freeaddrinfo` without any status assurance on this path; the absent fix is the complete return-status check (`if (ret != 0)`) at line 24. Consuming uninitialized freed-list pointer → undefined behavior/crash (CWE-754/CWE-457).

assumptions: `cfgaddr` and `*port` derive from caller/config data (entry-point-derived), governing whether `getaddrinfo` can fail.
`servinfo` (line 4) is not initialized or assigned between declaration and its consumption at lines 30/63 on the failure path.
limitations: The trigger requires a platform where `getaddrinfo` error codes are non-negative (e.g., Windows); on POSIX systems with negative EAI codes the line 24 check covers the failure set.
If the successful-return contract of `getaddrinfo` (non-NULL list) is assumed, the success path itself shows no memory-safety flaw.
Log-content influence via `cfgaddr` (potential CWE-117) is demoted: control characters in config data are not demonstrated by shown code, and the config is operator-controlled.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched member: the NJS_ERROR branch carries the return-status guard `if (njs_is_memory_error(vm, &vm->retval)) { return NJS_ERROR; }` (lines 67-69), which excludes an out-of-memory interpreter failure from reaching the `failed:` sink (the `ctx->capability->reject` call at line 80 and `njs_async_context_free(vm, ctx)` at line 83), preventing the OOM-routed use-after-free. No other sink has a failing value demonstrable from the shown statements; NULL-deref and out-of-bounds candidates lack in-fragment producers or capacities.

The memory-error state is a real interpreter outcome because the fragment itself distinguishes it via `njs_is_memory_error(vm, &vm->retval)` at line 67.
limitations: The precise use-after-free mechanism inside `njs_async_context_free` / the OOM reject path is not visible in the fragment; the verdict rests on the in-fragment guard excluding the dangerous state from the sink.
The NJS_AGAIN path (lines 63-64) leaves the old `ctx` alive, a possible leak with no demonstrated security consequence.

The scope write at line 37 (`*njs_scope_value(vm, ctx->index) = *value;`) has no shown capacity for the async scope or derivation of an out-of-range `ctx->index`; NULL-deref of `ctx`/`ctx->await`/`ctx->capability` has no in-fragment NULL producer.

verdict.summary: in_backprop_tensor_temp_mat.coeffRef(d, in_index) (line 121) writes into a buffer of in_depth*in_cols*in_rows*in_batch doubles (lines 86-88), but d is bounded only by out_depth (line 117) and in_index only by pooling-sequence starts that are never range-validated (lines 98, 103) and by batch/rows/cols that are never checked against in_batch/in_rows/in_cols. Attacker-supplied shapes or sequence values admitted by every shown guard produce an out-of-bounds heap write (e.g., in_depth=1 with out_depth=4, or row_seq element -1).

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write (CWE-787). The sink matrix capacity is in_depth*in_cols*in_rows*in_batch doubles, fixed by the Map over in_backprop_tensor_temp (lines 86-88, allocated from in_shape at lines 81-83). The row index d is admitted in the full range [0, out_depth) by line 117, and out_depth (line 36) is attacker-supplied with NO shown relation to in_depth (line 58); with orig_input_tensor_shape=[1,1,1,1] and out_backprop=(1,1,1,4), every guard passes (line 26, lines 38/44 for sequences [0,1]/[0,1], lines 59-70, end-clamps at 101/106) yet coeffRef(d=1..3, in_index=0) writes elements 1..3 of a 1-element buffer. Independently, in_index=(b*in_rows+in_r)*in_cols+in_c comes from unclamped starts row_seq_tensor_flat(r) / col_seq_tensor_flat(c) (lines 98, 103): an admitted sequence element of -1 yields in_index=-1 (line 115). Absent fix: a dimension-consistency/range check, e.g., OP_REQUIRES(context, out_depth == in_depth && out_batch == in_batch && out_rows <= in_rows && out_cols <= in_cols, ...), or clamping of in_row_start/in_col_start to [0, in_rows-1]/[0, in_cols-1]; none such statement exists in the fragment.

assumptions: Capacity of the write target is fixed by the visible allocation and Map: in_backprop_tensor_temp has in_depth*in_cols*in_rows*in_batch doubles (lines 81-88).
Tensor dim_size values are non-negative (TF Tensor invariant), so out_batch/out_rows/out_cols/out_depth >= 0.
Pooling sequences, output shape, and input shape are op inputs (context->input(0..3)) and therefore entry-point-controlled; the fragment imposes no value constraints on them.
limitations: Negative in_shape dims (only != 0 is checked at lines 59-70) are not pursued; TensorShape/allocator behavior may fail closed.
Integer wrap in b*in_rows*in_cols for astronomically large attacker dims was not analyzed as a separate trigger.
The in_r/in_c loops with an end below the start produce empty bodies (no underflow), so only the negative-start and out-dim>in-dim derivations are confirmed.

verdict.summary: ComparisonQuantized validates only input1->type at line 3 before casting both tensor buffers to the template element type. input2->type is never checked, so an attacker-supplied tensor of any other type (e.g., kTfLiteFloat32, kTfLiteInt16, or the opposite-signed 8-bit type) reaches GetTensorData<input_dtype>(input2) at lines 26 and 31. The absent one-statement fix is a type guard on input2 (e.g., input1->type == input2->type or input2 membership in the guard at line 3); without it the reference kernels index input2's buffer with a mismatched element stride, a type confusion enabling mis-sized/out-of-range element reads (CWE-125) and wrong comparison results.

evidence.reason: Sink casts the entry-point tensor input2's raw buffer to input_dtype elements. Phase 1: input2->type has no shown constraint; line 3 constrains only input1->type, which is Guard-Identity Audit drift class 3 (wrong target: the guard tests a different field than the sink consumes), so the residual range of input2->type is the full TfLiteType domain. Phase 4 witness: input2->type = kTfLiteFloat32 (or kTfLiteInt16 / opposite-signed 8-bit type), admitted by line 3 (tests input1) and by both outcomes of the line 23 requires_broadcast branch, reaches the cast on the broadcast path. The reference kernel then indexes input2's allocation (element_count x sizeof(actual_type)) with the element stride of input_dtype, enabling mis-sized element reads (CWE-125) and wrong values. The absent one-statement fix is a type-equality/membership check on input2, e.g. if (input1->type != input2->type) return; before the cast.

Same unprotected sink on the non-broadcast path (requires_broadcast == false, line 23 else branch). input2->type remains unconstrained to the sink: the line 3 guard tests only input1->type (wrong-target drift), and no statement between it and line 31 checks input2's type. The witness input2->type = kTfLiteFloat32 is admitted on this path and reaches the mis-typed cast, which passes the reference kernel a mismatched element stride over input2's buffer (CWE-125 / type confusion). The absent fix is the same one-statement input2 type check (e.g., input1->type == input2->type).

assumptions: input_dtype is instantiated from the input1 quantized type (1-byte uint8_t/int8_t), as implied by the guard at line 3 admitting only kTfLiteUInt8 and kTfLiteInt8.
TfLiteTensor data buffers are allocated as element_count * sizeof(element_type) bytes and GetTensorData returns the raw buffer pointer (standard TFLite library semantics).
The unshown reference_ops kernels index the passed data arrays by shape-derived element counts (name-implied standard semantics).
limitations: With input_dtype fixed to a 1-byte type, pure byte-width arithmetic keeps reads inside input2's allocation when input2's actual element width is 1 byte or larger; the strongest out-of-bounds manifestation of this type-confusion family occurs in the sibling unquantized/float instantiations sharing the same unguarded dispatch, whose dispatch code is not shown.

verdict.summary: RaggedGather-style Compute computes `num_params = params_nested_splits_in[0].dim_size(0) - 1` (line 18) guarded only by the rank check `params_nested_splits_in[0].dims() > 0` (line 16). That guard admits an empty rank-1 split tensor (shape [0]), so `dim_size(0) == 0` is attacker-derivable and yields `num_params == -1`, an out-of-domain negative parameter count consumed at line 19 by `ValidateIndices(indices_in, num_params)` as the bounds parameter for index validation. The absent one-statement fix is a positivity/emptiness check such as `params_nested_splits_in[0].dim_size(0) > 0` (or `num_params >= 0`) before the subtraction.

evidence.reason: params_nested_splits_in[0] is an attacker-controlled entry-point tensor (lines 5-6). Its dimension is constrained only by line 16's rank check `params_nested_splits_in[0].dims() > 0`, which admits a rank-1 tensor of shape [0]; nothing in the fragment excludes dim_size(0) == 0, so line 18's `- 1` underflows to num_params == -1. Line 19 then consumes num_params == -1 as the exclusive bounds parameter of `ValidateIndices(indices_in, num_params)`, corrupting the index-validation decision (a security-relevant comparison/bound) with a negative count outside the valid parameter domain. Line 16 fails the Guard-Identity Audit (drift class 2: it constrains RANK, while the sink consumes a SIZE-derived arithmetic value). The absent fix form is a bound check `dim_size(0) > 0` (or `num_params >= 0`); primary CWE-682 (incorrect calculation producing an out-of-domain negative count consumed by a security-relevant bound check).

assumptions: SPLITS_TYPE is a signed integer type (int32/int64 as used by TensorFlow), so 0 - 1 yields the representable value -1 rather than a wraparound.
The op's tensor inputs (params_nested_splits, indices, params_dense_values) are supplied by the caller/attacker through the framework's registered op inputs.
context->input(params_nested_splits_in.size()) and .size() + 1 (lines 12, 14) are within the node's declared input count once input_list succeeds; no shown arithmetic can exceed it.
limitations: The memory-safety outcome of num_params == -1 inside ValidateIndices is not visible: under a strict two-sided bounds implementation all indices are rejected (fail-closed, op error); under a lax one-sided bounds check negative indices could propagate into MakeSplits. This helper body is not shown, so the OOB-read form of the consequence is not a confirmed finding.

The classic RaggedGather OOB (params_nested_splits claiming more values than params_dense_values_in.dim_size(0), reaching a slice past capacity in the unshown WriteValues) is not demonstrable from the shown fragment and is out of scope for the verdict.

verdict.summary: pjstun_parse_msg stores each parsed attribute into msg->attr[msg->attr_count] with no cap on msg->attr_count: a 16-bit STUN length field lets an attacker pack up to ~16K minimal (4-byte) attributes, writing past the fixed msg->attr member array (missing guard: 'if (msg->attr_count >= PJSTUN_MAX_ATTR) return ...;'). Separately, the attribute header is dereferenced at line 41 before the 'if (msg_len < len)' check, so a message whose length field leaves only 1-3 trailing bytes causes a 1-3 byte out-of-bounds read.

evidence.reason: The write target is &msg->attr[msg->attr_count] (line 36); the loop is driven by the attacker-controlled 16-bit msg_len (line 25) with a minimum consumption of 4 bytes per iteration (lines 41-42), so msg->attr_count (line 61) reaches up to 16383. No statement in the fragment caps msg->attr_count; line 44 ('if (msg_len < len)') constrains len, not the count, and lines 51-52 only log. For msg_len = 68 (buf_len = 88) with 17 zero-length attributes, lines 26 and 35 admit the path (68 == 88-20; 68 > 0) and line 40 writes msg->attr[16], past a fixed capacity N < 16384 of the msg->attr member array (access convention: the fragment's only access is msg->attr[msg->attr_count]). The absent one-statement fix is a count guard, e.g., 'if (msg->attr_count >= PJSTUN_MAX_ATTR) return PJLIB_UTIL_ESTUNTOOMANYATTR;', before line 36/40. Confirmed CWE-787 out-of-bounds write.

The dereference (*attr)->length reads bytes p_attr+2..+3, requiring at least 4 valid bytes, but the loop condition 'while (msg_len > 0)' (line 35) admits msg_len = 1..3 bytes remaining (msg_len is the attacker-controlled 16-bit length field, line 25, pinned to buf_len - 20 by the equality at line 26). With msg_len = 2 and buf_len = 22, lines 26 and 35 admit the path and this statement reads 2 bytes past the end of buf; the only length guard 'if (msg_len < len)' (line 44) is evaluated after this deref and cannot protect it (control-point order failure). The absent fix is a minimum-length requirement before the deref, e.g., 'if (msg_len < sizeof(pjstun_attr_hdr)) return PJLIB_UTIL_ESTUNINATTRLEN;'. Confirmed CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: msg->attr is a fixed-size array member of pjstun_msg indexed by msg->attr_count; the integer capacity constant (PJSTUN_MAX_ATTR) is not displayed in the fragment, so the S2 witness relies on the convention that the member array is much smaller than the 16383-count index space the fragment itself derives.

Each loop iteration consumes at least 4 bytes because len >= sizeof(pjstun_attr_hdr) = 4 after rounding at lines 41-42, bounding the loop to at most 16383 iterations for the 16-bit msg_len; this is the shown numeric derivation for the unbounded msg->attr index.
pjstun_attr_hdr is laid out as two 16-bit fields (type at offset 0, length at offset 2) so (*attr)->length reads offsets 2-3.
limitations: The header reads at lines 10 and 25 occur before any buf_len >= sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) check; a buf_len < 4 input would over-read there, but this is demoted because producing it requires an unshown caller to pass a sub-header buffer, whereas S1 is reachable from a normal 22-byte datagram within the fragment's own logic.

The precise overflow magnitude and adjacent-object corruption for S2 depend on the unshown size of msg->attr (PJSTUN_MAX_ATTR) and the location of msg (stack vs heap) in unshown callers; the count-cap guard is absent regardless.

The 1-3 byte OOB read at line 41 is transient (the function returns ESTUNINATTRLEN afterward); its security impact is limited to a small memory disclosure/crash window unless the read lands on unmapped memory.

limitations: Line 50 admits negative in_idx in [-(rank-1), -1] (e.g., attacker perm value -1); whether c->Dim misbehaves on negative indices is an unshown callee property, so no OOB is confirmed from the fragment alone.

The case of perm != nullptr with perm_elems not value-known (in which WithValue at line 35 binds rather than verifies) requires an unshown TensorFlow shape-state inconsistency; it is not derivable from the shown code.

An attacker-chosen huge rank could exhaust memory at dims.resize(rank) (line 32) or overflow the int32 loop counters at lines 48/57, but only after an environmental allocation failure; treated as a limitation, not a confirmed finding.

verdict.summary: ReadMATImage computes ldblk as (k * MATLAB_HDR.SizeX) in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic without any magnitude check; a large file-supplied SizeX (e.g., 0x20000000 for miDOUBLE at line 230, or 0x80000001 for miINT16 at line 196) wraps ldblk to 0 or 2, under-sizing the BImgBuff allocation at line 270 so that CalcMinMax at line 278 (and ImportQuantumPixels at lines 304/314) read SizeX pixels from a near-zero-byte heap buffer, causing an out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125) via the integer overflow (CWE-190). The only dimension guard (lines 243-244) excludes only zero dimensions and does not bound SizeX.

evidence.reason: CWE-190: MATLAB_HDR.SizeX is attacker-controlled with residual range [0, 2^32) from line 119 (ReadBlobXXXLong returns unsigned int) and is never magnitude-checked. Here 8 * SizeX is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic: SizeX=0x20000000 wraps to 0. The wrapped ldblk is then used at line 270 to size BImgBuff (AcquireQuantumMemory(ldblk,sizeof(double)), capacity 8*ldblk = 0 bytes) and at line 278 CalcMinMax is passed SizeX=0x20000000, SizeY=1 with that zero-capacity buffer. The only guard on the path, lines 243-244 'if (image->columns == 0 || image->rows == 0) goto MATLAB_KO;', admits SizeX=0x20000000 (columns != 0) and constrains only the zero dimension, not the magnitude consumed by the sink; the absent fix is a bound/overflow check on SizeX (or on ldblk) before the allocation.

evidence.reason: CWE-125: with the wrapped ldblk=0 from line 230, BImgBuff (allocated at line 270) has ~0 bytes while CalcMinMax is called with x=MATLAB_HDR.SizeX=0x20000000 and y=1; its name-implied semantics scan the x-by-y element matrix stored in data (BImgBuff), reading out of bounds from the undersized heap buffer. Reachability is admitted by every shown guard (StructureClass whitelist lines 143-154, CellType switch lines 219-230, zero-dimension guard lines 243-244), with the sole fragile link that SetImageExtent at line 265 must succeed for the path to proceed; the decisive absent fix is a magnitude guard on SizeX/ldblk before line 270.

assumptions: MATLAB_HDR.SizeX/SizeY receive unsigned 32-bit values from ReadBlobXXXLong (declared 'unsigned int (*ReadBlobXXXLong)(Image *image)' at line 25), so k * SizeX is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and wraps modulo 2^32.

ImportQuantumPixels at lines 304/314 consumes the row only if quantum_info->number_pixels is set, which is not shown in this fragment; the CalcMinMax path at line 278 does not depend on that and carries the primary finding.
