verdict.summary: fastrpc_dma_buf_attach is the fixed counterpart. Every dangerous operation is protected by a verbatim guard: the kzalloc NULL check (`if (!a)`, line 9) excludes `{NULL}` before `&a->sgt` is used at line 12; the dma_get_sgtable return check (`if (ret < 0)`, line 14) frees `a` and returns (`kfree(a); return -EINVAL;`, lines 16-17) so a failed sgt and a freed `a` never reach any later use; and `attachment->priv = a;` (line 22) is placed after the error block so the failure path cannot leave a dangling priv. `INIT_LIST_HEAD(&a->node);` (line 21) precedes `list_add` (line 25), and the only format string is a literal. No failing value derivable from the shown code reaches any sink.

assumptions: Standard semantics of dma_get_sgtable: returns 0 on success and a negative errno on failure, making `ret < 0` (line 14) the correct failure test.

The dma-buf framework supplies non-NULL `dmabuf` and `dmabuf->priv` (`buffer`) when invoking this attach callback; that invariant is not visible in the fragment and is used only to avoid manufacturing a NULL finding, never to justify a shown sink.
The caller of the (failed) attach path kzallocs `attachment`, so `attachment->priv` is NULL unless line 22 has executed.
limitations: NULL dereference of `dmabuf` or `buffer` (`dmabuf->priv`) is not demonstrable: no NULL producer is shown in the fragment, so it is demoted rather than reported.

Use-after-free potential involving consumers of `attachment->priv` or `buffer->attachments` outside this function (e.g., fastrpc_dma_buf_detach, not shown) cannot be confirmed from this fragment and is out of scope.
Internal failures of dma_get_sgtable (e.g., sg-table allocation failure inside the helper) are neutralized by the shown `ret < 0` path and are not a separate concern.

verdict.summary: One-byte out-of-bounds read in _gnutls_server_select_suite: the first SCSV scan loop `for (i = 0; i < datalen; i += 2)` (line 13) reads `data[i + 1]` (lines 17 and 30) on every iteration, but the even-length guard `if (datalen % 2 != 0)` (line 78) executes only after that loop and returns at line 80, protecting only the later loops. An attacker sending an odd-length cipher-suite list whose last byte equals the SCSV major byte (e.g., datalen=1, data[0]=0x56) triggers the read of `data[datalen]`, one byte past the shown datalen-byte access range.

evidence.reason: CWE-125 one-byte over-read. The loop `for (i = 0; i < datalen; i += 2)` (line 13) fixes the valid index space of `data` to 0..datalen-1. `datalen` is entry-point input (line 2) with no shown parity or minimum constraint before this loop. With the degenerate witness datalen=1, i=0 admitted by line 13, and `data[0] == GNUTLS_FALLBACK_SCSV_MAJOR` (attacker-chosen last byte 0x56) satisfying line 29, line 30 evaluates `data[i + 1]` = `data[datalen]`, one byte past the shown range. The only even-length guard, `if (datalen % 2 != 0)` (line 78) with return at line 80, is evaluated after this loop — guard-after-use ordering drift (Guard-Identity Audit class 1) — so it constrains nothing on this path. Absent fix: a `datalen % 2 != 0` rejection or `i + 1 < datalen` bound placed before line 13.

CWE-125 same unguarded one-byte over-read in the same loop (line 13) as evidence item 1, reachable when `session->internals.priorities.sr != SR_DISABLED` (line 15) and `data[datalen-1] == 0x00` with odd datalen, reading `data[datalen]`. The parity guard at line 78 runs after the sink and cannot protect it; the fix absent here is the same pre-loop even-length/bound check.

assumptions: `data` is treated by the shown loop at line 13 (`i < datalen`) as a datalen-byte buffer with valid indices 0..datalen-1; no caller-side padding or extra capacity is assumed.
`datalen` and the bytes of `data` are attacker-controlled ClientHello cipher-suite data; the fragment shows no constraint bounding or capping them before line 13.
limitations: A possible odd-`cipher_suites_size` over-read of `cipher_suites[i + 1]` in the memcpy calls at lines 105-108 and 131-134 cannot be confirmed: `cipher_suites_size` is assigned from the unshown helper `_gnutls_remove_unwanted_ciphersuites` (line 61, set at line 72), and an odd output is not derivable from shown semantics.
Internal reads inside `server_find_pk_algos_in_ciphersuites` (line 43) are not visible in the fragment, so no in-fragment failure can be confirmed there.

The renegotiation-SCSV read (line 17) additionally depends on `session->internals.priorities.sr != SR_DISABLED`, a session field not shown; the fallback-SCSV read (line 30) exhibits the identical failure without that dependency.
Wrap-around non-termination of the line 13 loop would require datalen == UINT_MAX (~4 GiB), which is not concretely producible from shown code; not treated as a finding.

verdict.summary: The fiber_switch fragment contains dangerous operations (an argument copy into the fiber stack and callinfo/proc dereferences), but every identified sink either carries a verbatim protective statement or has no failing value derivable from the shown code. The copy loop (lines 38-40) is bounded by b/e derived from len and is covered by the fragment's own capacity statement mrb_stack_extend(mrb, len+2) at line 35, which exceeds the len+1 slots actually consumed (receiver at stbase[0], args at stbase[1..len]); the proc dereference at line 45 is guarded by the fail-closed NULL check if (!c->ci->proc) at lines 32-34 on the only path. No OOB, NULL, or integer failure can be demonstrated in-fragment: the fiber stack capacity and CI-array capacity are never shown numerically, and no NULL producer is demonstrated, so those candidates are limitations rather than findings.

assumptions: Line 28 fiber_switch_context(mrb, c) switches mrb->c to c, so the line 35 mrb_stack_extend(mrb, len+2) capacity request targets the fiber context c whose stack the copy loop writes.

For a MRB_FIBER_CREATED fiber, c->ci == c->cibase (single entry frame; the 'pop dummy callinfo' comment at line 42 refers to the vmexec dummy above it), so the line 32 check on c->ci->proc guards the line 45 dereference of c->cibase->proc.
Line 35's mrb_stack_extend(mrb, len+2) is the fragment's only stack-sizing statement and reserves room covering stbase[0..len+1] (receiver, len+1... including receiver+args and the optional block).
limitations: Copy loop OOB (potential CWE-787): no numeric fiber-stack capacity appears in the fragment (c->stend is never referenced, no allocation constant shown), so the failure magnitude is an assumed quantity; Phase-4 OOB rule (a) is unsatisfied.

NULL deref of c->cibase->proc / c->ci->proc (potential CWE-476): no in-fragment NULL producer is demonstrated; the line 32 check is fail-closed, and the ci-vs-cibase identity is a state-machine invariant not literally shown.
Line 50 c->ci[1].stack[0] = value: CI-array capacity at c->ci+1 is not shown, so no failing index is derivable.
Line 56 mrb_vm_exec(mrb, c->ci->proc, c->ci->pc) after a possible c->ci-- at line 42: no NULL/uninitialized CI value is derivable from shown statements.
Line 35 len+2 integer overflow would require len near MRB_INT_MAX, a magnitude not producible from the shown code.
Line 35's exact capacity guarantee is implemented in an unshown callee; per the Verifiability Rule this caps (rather than inflates) confidence in the safe verdict.

verdict.summary: r_bin_ne_get_entrypoints performs out-of-bounds reads from bin->entry_table: the line 30 capacity check is consumed before 'off++' at line 37, so the bundle_type read at line 38 can dereference one byte past the buffer when a nonzero bundle_length occupies the last buffer byte; and the moveable branch's r_read_le16 at line 62 reads bytes off0+4..off0+5 although the line 42 check guarantees only through off0+4, while the intervening 'off > EntryTableLength' check at line 59 binds the table length, not the buffer capacity. Both sinks lack a buffer-capacity re-check after the increments (CWE-125, heap OOB read on attacker-controlled files).

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125). The only capacity guard on this path, `if (tableat + off >= r_buf_size (bin->buf)) { break; }` (line 30), is evaluated before `off++` (line 37) and admits equality `tableat + off == r_buf_size(bin->buf) - 1`; after the increment the dereference reaches absolute position `r_buf_size(bin->buf)`, one byte past the buffer, when the last table byte holds a nonzero bundle_length (line 34 does not break). Guard-Identity Audit: drift class 1 (check-then-use) — `off` is modified between the check and the use, and no statement between line 37 and line 38 re-bounds it (line 29 constrains the table length, not the buffer). Absent fix: a capacity re-check after the increment, e.g. `if (tableat + off >= r_buf_size (bin->buf)) break;`, before this read.

OOB read (CWE-125). At the for-body top `if (tableat + off + 4 >= r_buf_size (bin->buf)) { break; }` (line 42) with `off = A` guarantees only positions `A..A+4`; after `off++` (line 50), `off += 2` (line 56), and `off++` (line 58), the 2-byte read covers `A+4..A+5`, and when `tableat + A + 4 == r_buf_size(bin->buf) - 1` the high byte reads position `r_buf_size(bin->buf)` — OOB. The intervening `if (off > bin->ne_header->EntryTableLength) { break; }` (line 59) constrains `off` against the table length, not the buffer capacity (drift class 3, wrong target), and uses `>` so the boundary still falls through. Absent fix: a buffer-capacity check at the read point, e.g. `if (tableat + off + 2 >= r_buf_size (bin->buf)) break;`, before this read.

assumptions: bin->entry_table maps into bin->buf at absolute offset tableat = bin->header_offset + bin->ne_header->EntryTableOffset; the fragment's own access convention (lines 30 and 42, checked against r_buf_size(bin->buf)) establishes the valid span entry_table + k iff tableat + k < r_buf_size(bin->buf).

NE header fields (EntryTableOffset, EntryTableLength, SegCount, csEntryPoint, ipEntryPoint), bin->header_offset, bin->alignment, bin->segment_entries, and r_buf_size(bin->buf) are derived from the attacker-supplied file; no shown statement imposes a fixed relationship between EntryTableOffset/EntryTableLength and the buffer size beyond the shown checks.
limitations: The failing witnesses place the entry-table boundary byte exactly at the last buffer byte (guard-edge equality); this is attacker-controllable via file length and header fields, but the boundary-equality reliance keeps confidence in the 0.65-0.79 band.
r_list_get_n (segments, entry_cs - 1) at line 22 is not counted as a sink: the callee's internal bounds behavior is unshown, and the fragment NULL-checks the result before use (`s? s->paddr: 0`).

The segment_entries reads at lines 64 and 72-73 are guarded by the shown in-range checks (lines 63 and 71) and are not findings; the fixed-branch delta read at line 70 lies inside the span guaranteed by line 42.

verdict.summary: The only path/OS sink, open(name, ...) at lines 38-39, carries the sink-substitution fix O_NOFOLLOW verbatim at line 39, excluding final-component symlink following on every path, and the only fd sink, ioctl(myfd, ...) at lines 52-58/63-69/78-84, is protected by the check `if (myfd < 0)` at line 42. The remaining operations (literal-format archive_set_error, conditional close) have no derivable failure set, so no dangerous sink resolves ABSENT.

assumptions: O_NOFOLLOW at line 39 (`    O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW);`) excludes names whose final path component is a symlink for the open at lines 38-39; open failure yields myfd<0 and returns at lines 42-43.
The check at line 42 (`	if (myfd < 0)`) precedes and constrains every later use of myfd, and myfd is never reassigned between that check and the ioctl consumers at lines 52, 63, and 78.
FS_*/EXT2_* flag constants used at lines 14-28 fit a 32-bit int, so the unsigned-long-to-int assignment at line 62 does not truncate in practice.
limitations: A symlink in an intermediate path component (other than the final component) is not excluded by O_NOFOLLOW; exploiting it requires an on-disk directory layout never shown in the fragment, so the bypass is demoted rather than treated as a finding.
__archive_ensure_cloexec_flag(myfd) at line 40 may receive -1 if open() failed, but no dangerous effect is shown in-fragment (fcntl(-1,...) fails harmlessly).

The extraction-path semantics of name (e.g., path traversal) are the function's intended contract; no in-fragment construction or sanitization is shown, and no failing value within the fragment was demonstrated.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The attacker-controlled SetEncodings count is protected by `if (limit > 0)` (line 28), which excludes the degenerate limit==0 re-negotiation loop (CWE-835/400), and the cut-text payload length is capped by `if (dlen > (1 << 20))` (line 66), excluding all dlen > 1 MiB including values that would wrap `8 + dlen` (CWE-400/190). The fixed-offset reads and the SetEncodings loop are safe for every `len` value the fragment itself can derive (1, 4, 8, 20, 2, 6, 10, 12, 4+4*limit, 8+dlen); partial/coalesced intermediate lengths and the unshown buffer capacity would be needed to demonstrate any out-of-range access, so those candidates are demoted to limitations.

assumptions: The fragment's length-request protocol (returning full message sizes 4, 20, 10, 8, 6, 2, 12, 4+4*limit, 8+dlen) is honored by the unshown caller, so re-invocations carry the complete message (`len == required`), making the SetEncodings loop span [4, 4+4*limit) and the cut-text span [8, 8+dlen) in-bounds.
The conditional `if (len == 1) return N;` pattern establishes the fragment's convention that only the first `len` bytes of `data` are valid message bytes.
limitations: Fixed-offset reads on intermediate lengths (len in [2, N-1] for pixel format, framebuffer, key, pointer, ext-key, audio, and the `limit = read_u16(data, 2)` else-branch at line 31) are not in-fragment derivable - they require the unshown caller to invoke the handler with a partially coalesced first chunk; no object capacity for `data` is shown, so no OOB is confirmed.

The SetEncodings loop (lines 33-38) has no direct in-fragment guard tying `limit` to `len`; its safety rests on the line 29 negotiation plus line 28's `limit > 0` guard. A direct `if (len < 4 + (limit * 4)) return 4 + (limit * 4);` bound is ABSENT as text, but no failing witness is derivable from shown code (buffer capacity unshown; no derivable partial `len`), so this is a limitation, not a finding.

A cut-text message arriving in one shot with `len > 8` would skip the `if (len == 8)` block and could reach `client_cut_text` (line 77) with an unvalidated `dlen`; exploiting this requires unshown TCP-coalescing behavior and an unshown buffer capacity, so it is demoted.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in r_bin_java_bootstrap_methods_attr_new: R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT (buffer, offset) at line 9 reads two bytes at offset 6 with no check that offset+2 <= sz. An attacker-controlled attribute length sz in 0..7 reaches the read with attr non-NULL, reading past buffer[0, sz). The loop guard at lines 14-16 evaluates after the read and does not protect it.

evidence.reason: Sink reads buffer[offset] and buffer[offset+1] with offset fixed at 6 by line 6 ('offset += 6;'). sz is an entry-point (file-data) ut64 with no shown minimum, residual range 0..7. Witness: sz = 7, attr non-NULL (line 7 branch admits it), so the read hits index 7 while buffer capacity is [0, sz) (sz parameter plus line 17 using 'sz - offset' as remaining length). Guard-Identity Audit: line 14 'if (offset >= sz)' is evaluated after the read (order drift) and line 7 constrains attr, not sz (wrong-target drift); neither excludes the witness. Absent fix: a pre-read bounds check such as 'if (offset + 2 > sz)' before line 9. Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: buffer capacity is [0, sz), from the sz parameter and the access convention at line 17 ('sz - offset' passed as remaining length).
R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT reads two consecutive bytes at the given offset (standard macro semantics).
The attr != NULL branch at line 7 is the normal parsing path; no NULL-producing input is shown and none is needed for the OOB read witness.
limitations: Line 17's call to r_bin_java_bootstrap_method_new is guarded only by 'offset < sz'; whether one remaining byte suffices depends on unshown callee internals, so no out-of-bounds claim is made inside the callee.
r_list_append at line 20 on a possibly NULL r_list_newf result is an OOM-only concern, not attacker-controlled.
If an unshown contract of r_bin_java_default_attr_new guaranteed sz >= 8 and attr non-NULL, the line 9 witness would be demoted; no such contract is visible in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The decisive protective statement is present verbatim: lines 32-34 `if (!c->ci->proc) { mrb_raise(mrb, E_FIBER_ERROR, "double resume (current)"); }` exclude a NULL entry proc on every path into the MRB_FIBER_CREATED block before the proc dereferences at lines 52 and 63, and the stack-copy sinks are bounded by the shown guards/caps: `if (len >= 15)` (line 38), `mrb_stack_extend(mrb, 3)` (line 39), `len = 15` (line 41), and `mrb_stack_extend(mrb, len+2)` (line 44) covering the copy span stbase[1..len]. No NULL producer, out-of-bounds index, or negative length is derivable from the shown statements, so no confirmed failure reaches any sink.

assumptions: `mrb_stack_extend(mrb, room)` extends the current fiber stack to provide `room` usable slots (slots 0..room-1 are valid after the call), which makes `c->stbase[1]` (slot 1 of 3, line 39) and `c->stbase[1..len]` within `len+2` slots (line 44) in bounds.

For a created fiber, `c->ci` and `c->cibase` belong to the same fiber context `c` returned by `fiber_check(mrb, self)` (line 3), and the `c->ci--` pop at line 36 (comment `/* pop dummy callinfo */`) adjusts the pointer within that same callinfo array, so the guard at lines 32-34 constrains the entry proc that lines 51-52 and 63 consume.
`len` (mrb_int, line 1) is an argument-vector count whose shown producers (`mrb_ary_new_from_values(mrb, len, a)` and the assignment `c->cibase->n = len`) never generate a negative value.
limitations: A NULL-proc (double-resume) failure for `MRB_PROC_ENV(c->cibase->proc)->stack[0]` (line 52) or `mrb_vm_exec(mrb, c->ci->proc, c->ci->pc)` (line 63) requires a NULL producer (the dummy callinfo being NULLed) that is never shown in the fragment; absent that producer the candidate is not independently confirmable, and the shown guard at lines 32-34 excludes it on the only shown entry path.
`len < 0` reaching `mrb_stack_extend(mrb, len+2)` (line 44) / `c->cibase->n = len` (line 51) is admitted by the `else` branch, but no shown statement can derive a negative length, so it is demoted.

`c->ci[1].stack[0] = value;` (line 57) writes one callinfo entry past `c->ci`; its safety depends on the callinfo-array layout established in the unshown fiber initialization, so no capacity or access convention confirms or refutes an out-of-bounds write here.
The runtime behavior of the unshown helpers (`fiber_switch_context`, `fiber_result`, `mrb_vm_exec`) is not audited beyond the standard semantics of their shown arguments.

verdict.summary: SWTPM_NVRAM_CheckHeader bounds the blob length against sizeof(bh), the size of the blobheader* pointer (8 bytes), instead of sizeof(*bh)/sizeof(blobheader) (12 bytes). A blob whose declared length is 8-11 bytes passes the line 8 guard and the header field reads at lines 23/32/40 (bh->min_version, bh->hdrsize, bh->version) read past the buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) whose bytes can reach the log output at lines 25-28 or crash the process. The absent one-statement fix is using sizeof(*bh) (or sizeof(blobheader)) in the line 8 length check.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read at the first field whose byte extent exceeds a pointer-sized buffer. `length` is entry-point input with residual range [8, UINT32_MAX] because the only guard, line 8 `if (length < sizeof(bh)) {`, tests against sizeof(bh) = sizeof(blobheader *) = 8 (64-bit ABI) rather than sizeof(blobheader) = 12 (the operand the fragment itself uses at lines 33 and 36). Witness length = 8 passes line 8 (< admits equality) and line 15 (attacker sets totlen so ntohl(bh->totlen) == length), then line 23 dereferences bh->min_version at offset 8, one byte past the 8-byte buffer. Guard-Identity Audit: wrong-target drift - the guard constrains length against the pointer variable's size, not the struct size consumed by the reads, so the admitted set [8, 11] intersects the sink's failure set. Absent fix: change line 8 to `if (length < sizeof(*bh)) {` (or sizeof(blobheader)).

Same CWE-125 overread: with the same length = 8 witness admitted by line 8 (sizeof(bh) = pointer size) and line 15, bh->hdrsize is read at offsets 10-11, past the 8-byte buffer. The subsequent line 33 check `if (hdrsize != sizeof(blobheader)) {` only gates the line 41 offset write and comes after the vulnerable read, so it does not protect this sink. Absent fix: the line 8 guard must use sizeof(*bh)/sizeof(blobheader) so lengths 8-11 are rejected before any header-field dereference.

assumptions: blobheader spans 12 bytes (SWTPM layout: totlen uint32_t, flags uint32_t, min_version uint8_t, version uint8_t, hdrsize uint16_t); the fragment establishes the struct-size bound by its own sizeof(blobheader) uses at lines 33 and 36 and by the five member accesses.
sizeof(bh) at line 8 is the size of the blobheader* pointer (8 bytes on a 64-bit ABI); the verdict holds on any ABI where the pointer is smaller than the struct.
length and data come from external blob storage; the fragment's own checks treat length as the buffer extent, so no caller-side size invariant is assumed.
limitations: The exact overread byte count depends on the unshown blobheader layout; the adversarial witness is the range [8, 11] rather than a single displayed numeric capacity.
On a hypothetical 32-bit ABI the pointer-size bound is 4 and the overread begins even earlier; this does not change the verdict.
Disclosure of overread bytes into the log writes (lines 25-28) is treated as impact of CWE-125, not a separate finding.

verdict.summary: In the UTF-8 reverse-string branch, p = njs_string_offset(string_prop.start, end, from) (line 103) and the backward walk are performed with from/to never constrained against the string length (lines 74-75): when from is out of [0, length-1] or from - to + 1 exceeds length, njs_utf8_prev(p) (line 109) and njs_utf8_next(p, end) (line 104) dereference at/behind string_prop.start/end, causing a heap out-of-bounds read (and, for negative from, the documented NULL dereference in njs_string_offset). The index-validity/range guard that upstream added ('verify that from index is valid', e.g. 'if (i > to)' around the offset computation) is absent.

evidence.snippet:
p = njs_string_offset(string_prop.start, end, from);
            p = njs_utf8_next(p, end);
evidence.reason: from/to are assigned from args->from/args->to (lines 14-15) and no statement in the fragment constrains them against the string bounds established at lines 74-75 (length; end = string_prop.start + string_prop.size) or against 0. For from >= length the offset helper returns end and pre-fix njs_utf8_next reads *end (1-byte over-read); for from < 0 an invalid index reaches njs_string_offset (NULL dereference documented by upstream fix eafe4c7a); and with from - to + 1 > length the loop at line 108 runs past the first character so njs_utf8_prev(p) (line 109) walks below string_prop.start, over-reading heap bytes consumed by njs_string_new (line 112). No guard on any path constrains this value: line 77 checks length==size (wrong-target), line 62 checks object (wrong-target), lines 84/108 bound i only by the unconstrained to. The absent one-statement fix is the index-validity/range guard (upstream 'if (i > to)' before computing p, and/or a start-bounded njs_utf8_prev). Primary CWE-125 heap out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: String byte bounds are [string_prop.start, end) with end = string_prop.start + string_prop.size (line 75), and valid character indices are [0, length) with length from line 74; this is also the fragment's own index-to-pointer convention via line 103.
The pre-fix helper semantics are those visible at the same revision: njs_utf8_prev(p) does 'p--; c = *p;' with no lower bound, and njs_utf8_next reads *p before any end test.
args->from/args->to have no shown call site, so their residual range is the full int64 domain; consequences are evaluated only for arithmetic demonstrable inside the fragment.
limitations: The exact failing from/to values are caller-provided (e.g., upstream's regression test Array.prototype.lastIndexOf.call('Ф','Ф',-1/-2)); the fragment itself shows the unconstrained parameter space and the unbounded loop derivation, but not a literal failing constant.

The same missing bound affects the ASCII branch (p = string_prop.start + from, line 80, read at line 86); it is the same root cause but upstream fixed only the UTF-8 branch and short strings may be stored inline, so it is not reported as a separate finding.

The NULL-dereference variant from a negative from occurs inside njs_string_offset, whose internals are not shown in this fragment; it is corroborated only by the upstream fix message and is therefore noted here rather than as a second CWE.
The array fast path (guarded by from < array->length at lines 27-28) and the object path (guards at lines 144/147) are separate, protected sinks and are not part of the vulnerable finding.

verdict.summary: Every in-fragment memory-write sink carries a verbatim remaining-capacity guard: the m= segment (lines 12-26) is covered by the line 9 length check with 36 bytes of margin (worst-case segment overhead ~15 bytes), the fmt writes are covered per-iteration by line 28 (admits end-p >= slen+1, consumes exactly slen+1), and the CRLF write is covered by line 37 (admits end-p >= 2, consumes exactly 2). Helper calls pass the exact remaining length and check the printed < 0 status. No demonstrated failing value reaches any sink.

assumptions: Buffer capacity is len, established in-fragment at line 4: char *end = buf+len;
pj_utoa of a pj_uint16_t port/port_count writes at most 5 digits; even a 32-bit magnitude (<=10 digits) stays within the 36-byte margin of the line 9 check.
fmt[i].slen, media.slen, transport.slen are counted string lengths; each fmt write is separately bounded at line 28.

print_connection_info/print_bandw/print_attr follow standard print-helper semantics (write no more than the passed length, return written count or negative on failure); the fragment supplies exactly end-p and checks printed < 0.
limitations: Internal bounds of the unshown helpers (conn/bandw/attr) are not verifiable in this fragment; the fragment's protective contribution is the bounded length argument plus the printed < 0 status check at lines 47/56/65.
The (int)(end-p) cast at line 46 could truncate only if len > INT_MAX (~2 GiB), an unshown environmental condition; demoted.
Wrap of media.slen+transport.slen+12+24 at line 9 would require the two lengths to sum near SIZE_MAX, a magnitude no shown statement can produce; demoted.
The signed/unsigned comparison at line 28 (end-p > slen) misbehaves only if p > end, which is unreachable from the shown code because every prior advance is guarded.

verdict.summary: Buffer overflow in print_media_desc: the length gate at line 9 reserves only a fixed +12+24 bytes beyond media/transport lengths, but the format loop (lines 27-31) writes one space plus fmt[i].slen bytes per format with no remaining-space check. An SDP media line with enough formats/long enough format tokens (e.g., fmt_count=8 with fmt[i].slen=3 at the minimum admitted len=46) overruns the len-byte output buffer (end = buf+len, line 4), a heap/stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled SDP format entries supply fmt[i].slen with no shown cap; the only prior guard, line 9, admits any len >= media.slen+transport.slen+36 but its constant +24 does not scale with fmt_count + sum(fmt[i].slen), so the Guard-Identity Audit fails (drift class 3: insufficient/wrong-target bound). Capacity end = buf+len is established at line 4; for media.slen=4, transport.slen=6, port=10, fmt_count=8, each fmt[i].slen=3, len=46 (admitted by line 9), the loop needs 32 bytes while only 28 remain, so this copy writes past end: out-of-bounds write, CWE-787. Missing fix statement: a check bounding fmt_count + sum(fmt[i].slen) (or an in-loop 'remaining < 1 + fmt[i].slen' guard) before this copy.

Same unprotected format-loop path as line 29: one byte is written per fmt_count iteration, and fmt_count is attacker-controlled with no cap in the fragment. The line-9 size gate reserves a fixed 24 bytes for all formats while this loop emits fmt_count bytes of spaces, so with the same witness (fmt_count=8, len=46, 28 bytes remaining) this write also lands past buf+len before the memcpy at line 29: out-of-bounds write, CWE-787. Missing fix statement: the same aggregate or per-iteration bounds check.

assumptions: pj_size_t is unsigned; the buffer capacity for the writes is len bytes, established in-fragment by 'char *end = buf+len;' at line 4.
The media description fields (fmt_count, fmt[i].slen, media/transport slen) originate from externally supplied SDP parsed by PJSIP; no shown statement constrains fmt_count or any fmt[i].slen.
pj_utoa writes decimal digits without an in-fragment bound; the +12 margin is only sufficient for typical small SDP port values.
limitations: The exact number of fmt entries the SDP parser can store (fmt array capacity) and any per-token length cap are not visible in this fragment; the witness uses fmt_count=8 with slen=3 each, and the overflow also holds for a range of smaller counts with longer tokens.

print_connection_info / print_bandw / print_attr are assumed to honor their remaining-length argument and return -1 on overflow (callee internals not shown); negative returns are checked on every path, so no failure is confirmed there.
The overflow magnitude depends on attacker-chosen format entries; the finding is a range (any fmt list whose fmt_count + sum(fmt[i].slen) exceeds the remaining budget), not a single fixed byte count.

The inner-loop offset consumed by p[x] is bx * nBw + x, the exact expression tested at line 20.

A negative y0 = (r + h - bh) % maxY and consequent negative index would require negative r, h, or bh values from an unshown call site; no shown statement produces them.
Integer overflow in (y0 + y) * bpl or bx * lprn->nBw requires unshown magnitudes and is not demonstrable from the fragment.
A division-by-zero at line 11 would require maxY == 0, which no shown statement produces.

OOB index writes and the error-path read indices_flat(bad_i) (lines 53, 71) are bounded by the functors' standard check-index-before-write and return-convention semantics, with no in-fragment derivation admitting an out-of-range value. No sink with a real failure set lacks its protective statement.

assumptions: params->flat_outer_dims<T>() (line 43) yields params->dim_size(0) rows, and line 29 bounds params->dim_size(0) to the Index range.
N_big = indices.NumElements() (line 20) is a non-negative int64 element count; line 22 caps it so the cast at line 27 is exact and N is non-negative.

TensorShapeUtils::StartsWith (line 58) makes num_updates a multiple of N when N > 0, so updates.shaped<T, 2>({N, num_updates / N}) (line 63) never exceeds the updates buffer (or has zero extent -> functor no-op).
Scalar branch: IsScalar(updates.shape()) (line 44) precedes updates.scalar<T>() (line 45).
limitations: Write-side bounds checking inside ScatterScalarFunctor/ScatterFunctor is not shown; params_flat write safety relies on the functors' standard semantics (validate the index before writing, return the first invalid position i in [0, N) and stop). The error-path read indices_flat(bad_i) (lines 53, 71) is in-bounds only under the functor return convention (-1 on success, i in [0, N) on first invalid index); a hypothetical callee returning >= N would overrun, but that is beyond standard semantics.

The ValidateInput guard is CPU-only; a GPU instantiation with op==DIV and a zero update is not guarded, but no concrete crash or memory-safety failure is demonstrated for that path in the fragment.

verdict.summary: cvtchar's parse reads are bounded by the string's NUL terminator under the fragment's own convention, with explicit guards for both trailing-escape cases ('\' -> case '\0' with len=1 at L17-L19; '^' -> c=='\0' with len=1 at L42-L43) and a self-terminating digit loop (L26). The caller's use of the returned len is not shown; the in-fragment invariant (len never advances the parse past the terminator) holds for all shown inputs.

verdict.summary: One-byte out-of-bounds read in _gnutls_server_select_suite: the first loop (L13, i < datalen, step 2) reads data[i+1] at L17/L30 before the datalen-parity check (L78) is reached, so an attacker-supplied odd datalen (e.g. 1) admits i = datalen-1 and reads data[datalen], one byte past the datalen-byte cipher-suite buffer. The fix (parity check before the first loop, or an i+1 < datalen bound) is absent at the required control point; the existing check at L78 protects only the later selection loops.

evidence.reason: Sink reads data[i+1] where i is the loop counter of `for (i = 0; i < datalen; i += 2)` (L13). datalen is the attacker-controlled ClientHello cipher-suite length (entry-point, unsigned int, 0..UINT_MAX); the fragment imposes no parity constraint before this loop, and data's capacity is datalen bytes per the loop-bound convention (L13/L92/L123) and the L74-77 comment. Witness: datalen=1, data[0]=0x56 (GNUTLS_FALLBACK_SCSV_MAJOR) passes L13 (i=0<1) and L29 (data[0]==MAJOR), forcing evaluation of data[1] -- one byte past the 1-byte buffer. The only parity guard, L78 `if (datalen % 2 != 0)`, executes after this loop (use-then-check, drift class 1), and the L13 bound constrains i, not i+1 (identity drift). The absent one-statement fix is an early parity rejection (or `i + 1 < datalen`) before L13, which would exclude odd datalen from this path entirely. Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read (adjacent-byte disclosure / DoS).

Same OOB read mechanism as L30 within the same unguarded first loop: with odd datalen, the last admitted i (loop bound L13 `i < datalen`) is datalen-1, so data[i+1] indexes data[datalen], one byte past the datalen-byte buffer. The && chain at L15-17 requires `session->internals.priorities.sr != SR_DISABLED` and `data[i] == GNUTLS_RENEGO_PROTECTION_REQUEST_MAJOR`; both are content/config filters, not bounds checks, and the parity guard at L78-81 runs only after the loop, so it cannot protect this read (drift class 1). Primary CWE-125; the precondition on the session's sr setting is noted but not required for the L30 path above.

assumptions: data points to exactly datalen bytes of the peer cipher-suite list; established in-fragment by the loop bounds `i < datalen`/`j < datalen` (L13, L92, L123) and the comment at L74-77 ('Data length should be zero mod 2 ... every ciphersuite is 2 bytes').
cipher_suites (L7) has MAX_CIPHERSUITE_SIZE bytes and cipher_suites_size <= sizeof(cipher_suites) via L48-50, so 2-byte reads at the last inner-loop index stay inside the array.
GNUTLS_FALLBACK_SCSV_MAJOR / MINOR and GNUTLS_RENEGO_PROTECTION_REQUEST_MAJOR/MINOR are byte constants an attacker can place in the list.
limitations: Impact is limited to a 1-2 byte over-read (info disclosure / crash); exploitability depends on the unshown heap layout behind data, so severity is medium, not high or critical.
The L17 read additionally requires `session->internals.priorities.sr != SR_DISABLED` (session config not shown); the L30 fallback-SCSV path is the config-independent primary witness.

server_find_pk_algos_in_ciphersuites (L43) receives data/datalen before the parity check and would face the same odd-length hazard, but its internals are unshown, so no independent sink is confirmed there.
The parity check at L78-81 is present but misplaced; it correctly protects only the later selection loops (L92-L146), which are resolved PRESENT.

verdict.summary: Heap-based buffer overflow in readconf_main: suffix pointers derived from an unvalidated config-file-list element of residual length up to big_buffer_size-1 are written with unbounded sprintf calls (lines 25, 30, 41) with no remaining-capacity check, overflowing big_buffer.

evidence.reason: suffix = filename + Ustrlen(filename) (line 16) points into big_buffer at an offset whose residual range is [0, big_buffer_size-1]: the producer string_nextinlist(&list, &sep, big_buffer, big_buffer_size) (lines 10-11) stores list elements into big_buffer of size big_buffer_size with no shown minimum or cap below it, and config_main_filelist (line 6) is entry-point data with no shown validation. This sprintf writes up to 279 bytes (1+20+1+256+1) with no remaining-space guard, so an element of length >= big_buffer_size-278, admitted by every guard on the path (uname>=0 at 22 and config_file==NULL at 27/39 constrain other values), overflows big_buffer — heap OOB write, CWE-787 (CWE-122). The absent fix is a length/remaining-capacity check or a bounded snprintf before the write.

Same unprotected suffix write as line 25, reached via the config_file == NULL path (line 27): writes up to 258 bytes at suffix, failing when Ustrlen(filename) >= big_buffer_size-257, a member of the producer's shown output range (lines 10-11), with no guard on the length; %.256s caps only the nodename field (wrong-target drift), not the write position. Heap OOB write CWE-787/CWE-122; absent fix is the same length/remaining-space guard or bounded snprintf.

Same unprotected suffix write (euid-only variant) reached whenever CONFIGURE_FILE_USE_EUID is compiled and config_file == NULL (line 39): writes up to 22 bytes, failing when Ustrlen(filename) >= big_buffer_size-21; the length is unconstrained in the fragment (producer range from lines 10-11), and no guard on the path checks remaining buffer space. Heap OOB write CWE-787/CWE-122; the absent fix is a length/capacity guard or bounded snprintf.

assumptions: big_buffer has capacity big_buffer_size, established by the in-fragment access convention: string_nextinlist(&list,&sep,big_buffer,big_buffer_size) at lines 10-11 and again at line 255, with filename pointing into big_buffer.
string_nextinlist copies each list element into the provided buffer, truncating at the given bufsize, so element lengths up to big_buffer_size-1 are producible (name- and bufsize-implied semantics).
config_main_filelist is entry-point-supplied (CONFIGURE_FILE / -C) and receives no validation anywhere in the fragment.
limitations: The exact failing magnitude (element length >= big_buffer_size-278) is not produced inside the fragment; it depends on the external contents of config_main_filelist. It is entry-point data with no shown validation, so the finding stands as a range witness rather than an exact value.

NULL dereference of expand_string(host_number_string) at line 391 (Ustrtol(s,&end,0) with no NULL check) is demoted: expand_string's NULL-on-error is a library contract and the fragment shows no in-fragment value that admits NULL for this call.
A negative host_number passes the n > LOCALHOST_MAX check (line 396) and is stored (line 400), but no security-relevant consumer is shown; robustness only.
Log injection via CR/LF in config_main_filelist was not confirmed; no newline producer is shown.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation carries a shown protective statement. Frame descriptor reads are guarded by two `gif_bytes < 12` checks (lines 43, 61); colour-table reads by `gif_bytes < (int)(3 * colour_table_size)` (line 111); trailing image-data reads by `gif_bytes < 1`/`< 2` (lines 144, 171); and the frame-write sink is bounded by `(offset_x + width > gif->width) || (offset_y + height > gif->height)` (lines 92-93). Not vulnerable.

offset_x, offset_y, width, height are each in [0, 65535] because they are built from two unsigned octets at lines 84-87; therefore offset_x + width <= 131070 cannot wrap a 32-bit unsigned int at line 92.
colour_table_size <= 256 from the 3-bit size field documented in the descriptor comment (lines 73-78), matching a 256-entry table; table allocation itself is not shown.

Frame index `gif->frames[frame].display` (line 19) is read before the frame-range check (line 24); an out-of-range frame requires an unshown caller.
Colour-table entry capacity (local/global, >= 256) and the bitmap_get_buffer buffer size are established outside the fragment; no in-fragment failure producer is shown.
`return GIF_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY` at lines 159 and 236 skips the buffer_position restore (lines 332-333); robustness/state-leak only.

`int last_undisposed_frame = frame - 2` (line 213) relies on implementation-defined unsigned-to-int conversion for frame == 1; standard two's-complement yields -1 and the clear path, so no derivable failure.

verdict.summary: vidtv_s302m_encoder_init NULL-checks every allocation before use: `if (!e) return NULL;` (lines 8-9) guards all `e` dereferences, `if (!e->encoder_buf) goto out_kfree_e;` (lines 17-18) guards encoder_buf use/free, `if (!ctx) goto out_kfree_buf;` (lines 32-33) guards `ctx` dereference, and `if (args.head)` (line 51) guards the head-list walk and append. Decisive protective statement present; fragment is NOT vulnerable.

kfree(NULL) is a guaranteed no-op under standard kernel allocation semantics, which makes the error-path frees at lines 63 and 66 safe for NULL values.

Any NULL dereference on e->name would occur only in unshown caller code, so per in-fragment evidence this is a robustness/status-handling gap, not a confirmed CWE-476 finding.
Non-termination of the loop at line 52 would require a cycle in the args.head list, which can only be produced by an unshown caller; demoted.
Consistency between args.src_buf and args.src_buf_sz (lines 25-26) is caller-established; any misuse of that buffer would occur in the unshown encode path.

verdict.summary: XM pattern-decode loop reads a heap buffer of size patdata using an unbounded byte counter pc. With patdata=1, rows=1, channum=1 and a non-packed cell byte 0x00, memcpy(slot, buffer+pc, 5) at line 342 reads 4 bytes past the 1-byte allocation (heap out-of-bounds read, CWE-125). The only guards on the path (L288 patdata nonzero, L292 buffer non-NULL, L302/L303 loop bounds) do not constrain pc relative to phead[y].patdata, so the fragment lacks the decisive one-statement bound check.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read: buffer is allocated as new mp_ubyte[phead[y].patdata] (L289) with patdata attacker-controlled (f.readWords L265/L272, full 0..65535 domain, no shown minimum). pc starts at 0 (L301) and is incremented per cell (L311/L343); the loops at L302/L303 run rows*channum cells where rows (L264/L271) and channum (L49) are also uncapped file values, and the minimum per-cell consumption is 1 byte, so pc reaches/exceeds patdata. Witness patdata=1, rows=1, channum=1, byte 0x00: guards L288 (if (phead[y].patdata)), L292 (if (buffer == NULL)), L302 (r<phead[y].rows), L303 (c<header->channum), L308 (if ((buffer[pc]&128)) == false) all admit the path, then memcpy reads buffer[0..4] from a 1-byte allocation. No bound check on pc against phead[y].patdata exists on any path (absent fix: e.g., 'if (pc + 5 > phead[y].patdata) break;'), so the failure set {pc reaches patdata..patdata+4} is fully admitted — CWE-125.

Same unbounded pc over the L289 allocation: in the packed-flag path, pc advances to patdata or beyond when rows*channum exceeds patdata (minimum 1 byte consumed per cell at L311), and buffer[pc] is dereferenced past the 1-byte buffer with no intervening check constraining pc. Guards on the path (L288 nonzero patdata, L292 non-NULL buffer, L302/L303 loop bounds) fail the Guard-Identity Audit (wrong-target drift — they constrain patdata/buffer/loop count, not pc). CWE-125.

assumptions: Code block line numbers were taken from the fragment as displayed; L342 is the memcpy(slot,buffer+pc,5) statement and L289 is the new mp_ubyte[phead[y].patdata] allocation.
Minimum per-cell consumption of 1 byte in the packed-flag path comes from L308/L311 (read pc, pc++); in the uncompressed path the consumption is 5 bytes (L342/L343).
f.read(buffer,1,phead[y].patdata) at L297 fills exactly patdata bytes; the loop cells then consume at least 1 byte each, so patdata=1 with rows*channum=1 is the degenerate boundary of the read space.
limitations: f.read(insData,1,instr[y].size-33) at L107/L461: the L104/L455 guard bounds only the upper side (size-33 <= 230); a negative size-33 would bypass it, but the signedness of TXMInstrument::size is not shown in the fragment, so the failure cannot be confirmed.
smpReloc[nbu[sc]] at L229/L232/L596/L599: nbu bytes are unvalidated 0..255, but the numeric value of MP_MAXINSSAMPS is not shown, so OOB-read reachability depends on an unshown macro.
header->hdrsize-=4 underflow (L36) and f.read(hdrBuff,...) (L45): depends on the unshown type of TXMHeader::hdrsize and is a DoS-type concern.
patternData writes L373-L379: in-bounds only if the L278 multiplication rows*channum*6 does not overflow; the types of rows/channum are not shown.
phead[y] indexing under L258/L302 and smp[g+s] writes: capacities of module->phead and module->smp are not shown; the L629/L677 checks bound only s, not g+s.
allocateSongMessage(len+1) (L779) with len=0xFFFFFFFF wrapping to 0 and f.read(module->message,1,len) (L783): capacity and clamping behavior of the callee are not shown.
Stereo-mix reads sample[i+samplen] at L708/L724: depends on the allocation inside unshown loadModuleSample.
VERBOSE printf with %s on possibly non-NUL-terminated headers is compile-time-optional and was not evaluated as a finding.

verdict.summary: njs_await_fulfilled() diverts any Error-typed awaited settlement value to the failed: label via `if (njs_is_error(value)) { goto failed; }` (lines 13-15), invoking the promise-reject sink with that value (lines 71-72) and freeing the async context (line 74). The await continuation (lines 34-39) and any enclosing catch/finally are skipped, so exceptions thrown by an awaited function escape uncaught and reject the async function's promise at the wrong control point. The upstream fix (commit c62a9fb9) removes exactly this check; it is absent here.

evidence.reason: `value` is the awaited promise settlement value from `value = njs_arg(args, nargs, 1);` (line 12); Error instances are in its domain, as proven by the fragment's own check `if (njs_is_error(value)) {` (line 13), which admits exactly Error-typed values and executes `goto failed;` (line 14) — it is the enabler, not a protector, and no subsequent guard constrains `value` before this sink. The reject call consumes `value` and is followed by `njs_async_context_free(vm, ctx);` (line 74), freeing the async context while the coroutine is still suspended, so the continuation at lines 34-39 and the enclosing catch/finally are bypassed: an improper check of an exceptional condition that lets the exception escape uncaught (CWE-703). The absent one-statement fix is the removal of lines 13-15 (`if (njs_is_error(value)) { goto failed; }`), which upstream applied in commit c62a9fb9.

assumptions: `njs_arg(args, nargs, 1)` returns a valid pointer to the awaited promise settlement value (a JS value; `njs_is_error` at line 13 demonstrates Error instances occur in its domain).
`njs_vmcode_interpreter(vm, ctx->pc, ctx->capability, ctx)` (line 39) resumes the suspended coroutine from `ctx->pc`, and `ctx->capability` is the promise capability of the async function invocation.
Per standard njs semantics, `NJS_OK`/`NJS_AGAIN`/`NJS_ERROR` discriminate interpreter completion, and the reject path at lines 71-74 settles and frees the async context.
limitations: The impact is a control-flow/error-handling defect (CWE-703), not a confirmed memory-corruption: no out-of-bounds, NULL-deref, or use-after-free is provable from the shown statements alone.
`async_frame = ctx->await; async = &async_frame->native;` (lines 17-18) has no shown NULL producer for `ctx->await`; a NULL check absence there is not independently confirmable.
`*njs_scope_value(vm, ctx->index) = *value;` (line 34) has no visible capacity for `ctx->index`; not confirmable as out-of-bounds.
The memory-error early return at lines 58-60 leaks the async context, but this is a robustness concern present in the fixed upstream code as well.

Producing an Error-typed args[1] relies on the engine's await machinery (e.g., `await fn()` where `fn()` rejects with `new Error(...)`, or a promise fulfilled with an Error instance); the fragment's own `njs_is_error(value)` check on the argument demonstrates this value is in scope.

verdict.summary: The fragment carries the decisive protective statements: line 9 `if (offset + 8 > sz)` bounds the 2-byte num_bootstrap_methods read at line 13 (admits sz >= 14, excluding the failure set {sz < 14}), and lines 18-19 `if (offset >= sz) { break; }` gate every call to r_bin_java_bootstrap_method_new at line 21 (admits offset < sz, excluding {offset >= sz} including the degenerate offset == sz). Both guards pass the Guard-Identity Audit (same ut64 offset/sz, no interleaved mutation between check and use), so no out-of-bounds read or size underflow is derivable from the shown code. No other sink has an attacker-reachable failure set.

assumptions: buffer is treated as an sz-byte readable region, as implied by the API pairing of buffer with sz in r_bin_java_default_attr_new (line 5) and the byte arithmetic at line 21.
num_bootstrap_methods is a u2 (0..65535) read at line 13, bounding the loop counter domain.
r_bin_java_bootstrap_method_new is a parser that consumes at most the size argument it is passed; the fragment always passes a valid in-bounds pointer and a non-underflowed size (sz - offset >= 1).
limitations: r_list_append at line 24 would dereference NULL only if r_list_newf (line 15) failed via heap exhaustion of a small attacker-fixed structure; allocation failure is not attacker-reachable per the NULL-producer rule.

Primary CWE-125, heap out-of-bounds read.

verdict.summary: Every fd-consuming sink (ioctl GETFLAGS at lines 51-57, ioctl SETFLAGS at lines 62-68 and 77-83, close at line 93) is protected by the verbatim guard `if (myfd < 0) return (ARCHIVE_OK);` (lines 41-42), which excludes all negative fd values (including -1 and INT_MIN) on every path before use. __archive_ensure_cloexec_flag is a fcntl-style helper whose standard behavior on an invalid fd is a graceful, ignored EBADF error with no dereference or memory write.

Linux file-flag constants (FS_IMMUTABLE_FL / FS_APPEND_FL / FS_JOURNAL_DATA_FL / EXT2_* variants) are small values, so the unsigned long -> int conversion at line 61 does not wrap for values produced by the shown flag constants.
The caller that supplies `name`, `fd`, `set`, and `clear` performs its own path sanitization and fd ownership management; the fragment does not show those callers.

`__archive_ensure_cloexec_flag(myfd)` (line 39) is invoked before the line 41-42 guard when `open` fails (myfd == -1); this is treated as harmless because the helper only performs fcntl-style calls that error out on invalid fds, but the guard does not precede this specific call.

The EPERM subset retry (lines 74-76) can return ARCHIVE_OK while leaving immutable/append flags unset; this is a robustness/semantics nuance with no demonstrated security-mechanism consequence.

verdict.summary: ga_concat_shorten_esc is the protected member of the pair. Every read is confined by visible guards: line 10 rejects NULL str before any dereference, line 16 (for (p = str; *p != NUL; ++p)) ensures mb_ptr2char_adv(&s) at line 20 is only reached on a non-NUL in-bounds byte, and line 22 (while (*s != NUL && c == mb_ptr2char(s))) gates the mb_ptr2char(s) read with a short-circuit bound on the exact same pointer s, so s never reaches or passes the NUL terminator. mb_ptr2char_adv / mb_ptr2char follow standard Vim semantics: a non-NUL byte yields clen >= 1, s advances to the next character start or the NUL terminator, and reads never pass the NUL of a truncated multibyte sequence.

Equal character values have equal byte lengths in Vim's encodings (canonical UTF-8 has unique encodings; DBCS 1-byte and 2-byte values never collide), so s += clen at line 25 stays on character boundaries.
ga_concat and ga_concat_esc append into a growing garray and escape special characters; gap is implicitly non-NULL (no NULL producer shown at this call site).

verdict.summary: In sctp_make_strreset_req, stream_len, outlen and inlen are __u16. evidence.reason: Heap OOB write: stream_num (entry-point-derived __u16, domain 0..65535, no shown bound) = 65535 truncates at line 6 (__u16 stream_len = stream_num * sizeof(__u16)) to stream_len=65534, and line 12 (outlen = (sizeof(outreq) + stream_len) * out) truncates 65550 to outlen=14, so line 15 (retval = sctp_make_reconf(asoc, outlen + inlen)) allocates a 14-byte chunk. Guards line 16 (!retval), line 19 (if (outlen), admits 14) and line 28 (if (stream_len), admits 65534) all pass, then this sink copies 65534 bytes into a ≤14-byte buffer. assumptions: stream_num is caller-supplied request data with no shown validation; its full __u16 domain 0..65535 is analyzed (line 3).

verdict.summary: lprn_is_black computes y0 = (r + h - bh) % maxY at line 11 with unconstrained signed int parameters r, h and no shown minimum on nBh/BlockLine. Under C's truncating modulo a negative dividend (e.g., r = h = 0, bh = nBh >= 1) yields a negative y0 unless the dividend is an exact multiple of maxY. No guard between lines 11 and 13 constrains y0, so the negative offset (y0 + y) * bpl + bx * nBw indexes lprn->ImageBuf at line 13 and is dereferenced at line 15, producing a heap out-of-bounds read before the buffer (CWE-125). The decisive one-statement fix — a non-negative clamp such as 'if (y0 < 0) y0 += maxY;' after the modulo — is absent.

evidence.reason: y0 is produced at line 11 as '(r + h - bh) % maxY' from unconstrained signed int parameters r, h (no shown validation; full declared domain). With a negative dividend and maxY >= 2, C's truncating modulo yields y0 < 0 (e.g., r = h = 0, bh = lprn->nBh >= 1, 0 < bh < maxY gives y0 = -bh). There is no statement between line 11 and this line that constrains y0: the loop conditions at lines 12 and 14 test y and x, respectively (Guard-Identity Audit: wrong-target drift, class 3), so the negative y0 reaches the index expression. With bpl > 0 (bytes per scan line) and bx = 0 the byte offset (y0 + 0) * bpl is negative, forming a pointer before the lprn->ImageBuf object (valid index space starts at 0 per the fragment's own access convention at lines 13/15), and the dereference at line 15 reads out of bounds (CWE-125). The absent fix form is a non-negative clamp of y0 (e.g., 'if (y0 < 0) y0 += maxY;') after line 11.

At the first outer iteration (y = 0, admitted by line 12) and first inner iteration (x = 0, admitted by line 14), p points to lprn->ImageBuf minus a positive multiple of bpl because y0 < 0 (derivation in the primary evidence: negative dividend at line 11 with no intervening clamp or bounds check). The read p[x] therefore dereferences memory before the start of the ImageBuf allocation — a heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). No NULL, bounds, or sign guard protects p before this dereference; the absent one-statement fix is the y0 >= 0 clamp after line 11.

assumptions: lprn->ImageBuf is the heap byte array indexed by the fragment's own access convention at lines 13 and 15; its valid index space starts at 0, so any negative byte offset is out of bounds.
gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line(pdev) returns a positive scan-line byte length (standard device-API semantics), so a negative y0 scaled by bpl yields a negative byte offset.
Reachability requires bh = lprn->nBh >= 1 and nBw >= 1 so the loops at lines 12 and 14 execute; no shown statement enforces or excludes these values.
limitations: The witness is a sound relational/range witness, not a single pinned value: a concrete negative y0 additionally requires maxY = (lprn->BlockLine / lprn->nBh) * lprn->nBh >= 2 (e.g., BlockLine >= 2 * nBh) so a nonzero negative remainder exists; the values of BlockLine and nBh are not shown, so that magnitude is assumed.

The values of r, h, bx are caller-supplied and no call site is shown; the fragment itself imposes no constraint, so the failing values (e.g., r = h = 0; bx = 0) are admitted by the shown code, but the caller premise is outside the fragment.
An out-of-bounds read past the end of ImageBuf (positive-offset violation) cannot be confirmed because the buffer's allocation size is not shown.

If nBh == 0, line 9 divides by zero and line 11 modulos by maxY == 0 (undefined behavior, crash-only), but no shown producer of nBh == 0 exists, so it is recorded as a robustness limitation rather than a confirmed finding.

res->ContribRow has exactly line_length elements, per the shown allocation at line 17: gdMalloc(line_length * sizeof(ContributionType)).
