verdict.summary: In sctp_make_strreset_req, the 16-bit truncation of outlen/inlen (and stream_len) lets an attacker-chosen stream_num near the __u16 maximum (e.g. 32767 or 65535) wrap the param lengths to small nonzero values (outlen=18, inlen=10) while sctp_addto_chunk still appends the full sizeof(param) + stream_len (65554 bytes) into a payload allocated from SCTP_PAD4 of the wrapped length (20/12 bytes), causing an out-of-bounds write (skb_over_panic) at the stream-list copy. No guard bounds stream_num or widens the length storage; the required one-statement fix (e.g. __u32 outlen, inlen; or a stream_num bound) is absent.

evidence.reason: OOB write (CWE-787). stream_num=32767 (or type maximum 65535) is admitted by the fragment (line 3 declares __u16 with no constraint); line 6 computes stream_len=65534 with no 16-bit overflow check; line 12 truncates outlen=(20+65534) mod 65536=18 into __u16 outlen (line 10); line 15 allocates payload SCTP_PAD4(18)=20 bytes; guards line 16 (retval non-NULL), line 19 if(outlen) admits 18, line 28 if(stream_len) admits 65534, all pass in order; line 26 appends 20 bytes and line 29 appends 65534 bytes, exceeding the 20-byte payload derived from line 15, so sctp_addto_chunk/skb_put overruns the chunk (skb_over_panic). The absent fix is a width/bound protection before the size computation (e.g. `__u32 outlen, inlen;` on line 10 or a guard rejecting stream_num >= 32758); the truncation at line 6/10/12 feeding allocation and copy sizes is the CWE-190 mechanism.

Same out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the in-request branch: with in=true, stream_num=32767, line 6 gives stream_len=65534, line 13 truncates inlen=(sizeof(inreq)+65534) mod 65536 to a small nonzero value (e.g. 10) in __u16 inlen; line 15 allocates SCTP_PAD4(inlen)=12 bytes; guards line 16, line 32 if(inlen) and line 39 if(stream_len) all admit the witness; line 37 appends sizeof(inreq) and line 40 appends 65534 bytes into the 12-byte payload, overflowing the chunk. The same absent one-statement fix (width widening or stream_num bound) applies.

assumptions: sctp_make_reconf(asoc, length) creates the reconf chunk whose payload capacity is the passed length (name-implied standard semantics: sctp_make_control/sctp_make_chunk allocate chunkhdr + paylen), and sctp_addto_chunk appends via skb_put without bounds rechecking.

sizeof(outreq) and sizeof(inreq) are >= 4 (param_hdr alone), so sizeof(param)+65534 always exceeds 65535, forcing the truncation for stream_num >= 32758; exact sizes (20/12) only set which append overflows first.
The witness values stream_num=32767/65535 are members of the declared __u16 parameter domain; no in-fragment constraint excludes them.
limitations: No call site is shown, so whether the real caller (SCTP_RESET_STREAMS setsockopt) actually supplies out/in=true with stream_num >= 32758 is outside the fragment; the failing value is derived from the shown types and arithmetic, not from an unshown environmental fact.
OOB read from stream_list cannot be confirmed: its capacity is not declared or allocated within the fragment.
Uninitialized bytes of outreq/inreq (e.g. a possible stream_num member) reaching the wire cannot be confirmed because the struct layouts are not shown.
Wrapped parameter length fields (htons(outlen)=18 while 65554 bytes follow) cause receiver-side parse inconsistency; that downstream protocol effect is outside this fragment.
The overflow manifests as a kernel panic (skb_over_panic) rather than silent corruption; crash-only impact is bounded by the write being caught by skb_put.

verdict.summary: luaG_runerror contains no sink with a failure set demonstrable from the shown code. The only type-sensitive dereference (ci_func(ci)->p->source and getcurrentline(ci) at line 10) is fully protected by the verbatim guard `if (isLua(ci))` at line 9, which passes the Guard-Identity Audit (same value ci, no interleaved mutation, no type/precision or transformation drift). The format-string call at line 7 consumes `fmt`, an internal-helper parameter with no shown call site, so attacker control of the format is not derivable from the fragment; the raw stack write at line 11 operates on slots created by the fragment's own pushes. No confirmed vulnerability.

assumptions: `isLua(ci)` at line 9 exactly classifies the CallInfo union for the dereferences at line 10; the guard is evaluated on the same `ci` value from line 2 with no mutation between check and use.
`luaO_pushvfstring` at line 7 returns a valid pointer or raises (standard semantics); its result `msg` is non-NULL on every path to lines 10-11.

The comment on line 11 (`/* remove 'msg' from the stack */`) records that `luaG_addinfo` at line 10 pushes the new message, so slots `L->top - 2` and `L->top - 1` exist on every true-branch execution.
limitations: Format-string interpretation of `fmt` at line 7 (CWE-134 class): `fmt` is an internal-helper parameter with no shown call site, so no attacker-controlled value reaching `luaO_pushvfstring` is derivable from the fragment; the missing literal-`"%s"`/sanitization statement is therefore not a confirmed finding without an assumed caller.

Potential underflow of `setobjs2s(L, L->top - 2, L->top - 1)` at line 11 would require unshown `luaG_addinfo` behavior (e.g., failing to push a message) or an unshown runtime stack layout; the fragment's own two pushes (lines 7 and 10) keep the degenerate empty-stack write inside slots 0/1.

The ordering of `luaC_checkGC(L)` before `va_start` (line 5 vs 6) is robustness hardening against recursive allocation failure while formatting an error message, not a security-relevant protective statement.
NULL `L->ci` and hostile `fmt` bytes have no shown producer inside the fragment; both candidates are demoted for lack of derivability.

verdict.summary: No sink in the shown fragment has a failure set derivable entirely from the fragment. All out-of-bounds candidates (lines 7, 16, 20, 21 and reads at 9, 12) depend on unshown src/dst buffer capacities, so no capacity is established by declaration, allocation, or access convention. The mkdir_attr sink at line 23 is gated by the verbatim check at line 17 ('stat(src, &s) == 0 && S_ISDIR(s.st_mode)'), which constrains the exact s.st_mode consumed and passes the Guard-Identity Audit. The discarded mkdir_attr return (line 23) has its failure state un-consumed with no security decision depending on it, so it is robustness rather than a finding. The stat return itself is checked at line 17.

assumptions: src and dst are caller-provided NUL-terminated buffers whose capacity covers the prefix lengths plus the traversed path portion; no allocation or capacity is shown (lines 2-4).
For lines 7, 20, 21 the intended caller contract (not shown) guarantees capacity(dst) >= dst_prefix_len + 1 + number of path components; the fragment itself establishes no such capacity.
The loop termination relies on the source string's own NUL (lines 9-10), so the fragment treats src as NUL-terminated.
limitations: Out-of-bounds candidates at lines 7, 16, 20, 21 and reads at lines 9, 12 cannot be confirmed: no buffer capacity is visible in the fragment, and no in-fragment numeric derivation exceeds a shown capacity.

The return value of mkdir_attr (line 23) is discarded; a failed directory creation is not consumed by any shown statement and has no demonstrable security consequence inside the fragment (unchecked-status robustness only).
An unterminated src string would overrun the read at line 9, but no producer of an unterminated buffer is shown, so it is an unshown-environment fact rather than a witness.

verdict.summary: EDITOR (or VISUAL) from the environment is concatenated into a shell command and executed via system() whenever the editor string contains a space, allowing arbitrary command execution (e.g., EDITOR="sh -c 'touch /tmp/pwned'"). The space test at line 50 only selects the branch; it does not constrain shell metacharacters, and no sanitization, allowlist, or non-shell sink substitution is present.

evidence.reason: system(p) executes the attacker-controlled editor string via /bin/sh -c. Taint: editor = getenv("EDITOR") at line 20 (fallback getenv("VISUAL") line 22, default "vi" line 24) is entry-point environment input with no shown validation. The only shown test, line 50 strchr(editor,' ')==NULL, admits the witness (any string containing a space plus shell syntax, e.g. "sh -c 'touch /tmp/pwned'") into the else-branch, and line 58 sprintf(p,"%s %s",editor,filename) preserves all metacharacters into p. Line 59 then runs /bin/sh -c on that payload, executing the attacker's command. Guard-Identity Audit of line 50: wrong-target drift — it tests for ' ' but the sink consumes all shell syntax; it does not exclude the failure set. The absent fix is a sink substitution (non-shell exec like tokenized execlp/execvp) or a validation guard rejecting shell metacharacters in editor before reaching system(). Primary CWE-78.

assumptions: Environment variables EDITOR/VISUAL are entry-point, attacker-controlled input per the fragment's provenance rules.
system() executes its argument through /bin/sh -c by name-implied standard semantics.
omStrDup("/tmp/sd000000") allocates a 13-char buffer plus NUL (line 3), used by the line 4 sprintf candidate.
Line 57 allocates exactly strlen(editor)+strlen(filename)+2 bytes for p, so line 58's sprintf does not overflow.
limitations: Line 4 sprintf(filename+7,"%d",getpid()) can write past the 14-byte buffer only for a 7+-digit PID (>=1,000,000); such an OS pid_max value is an environmental fact not shown in the fragment, so the OOB witness is not derivable from shown code.

ftell return at line 76 is unchecked; ftell failure would make len=-1, producing omAlloc(0) and pi->data.s.body[-1]='\0' at lines 80/82, but no shown statement can produce ftell failure on the just-opened regular file.
The int cast of len at line 80 could truncate a file size > INT_MAX, but the file is a local temp file written from library data, not attacker-controlled input.
The predictable /tmp/sd<pid> name opened with fopen(filename,"w") at line 5 is a symlink race candidate; it requires unshown attacker timing and PID knowledge, so it is demoted.

Log injection via Print("cannot exec %s\n",editor) at line 53 would need an editor containing CR/LF without spaces, and impacts an unshown log/output backend; low-impact and out of the primary finding.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the guarded (fixed) form of io_rw_init_file. The only security-relevant operations — the file pointer/mode check at L8, the return-status check of kiocb_set_rw_flags at L16, and the IOPOLL path at L30 — each carry a verbatim protective statement. In particular, L30 (if (!(kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_DIRECT) || !file->f_op->iopoll)) excludes both buffered requests lacking IOCB_DIRECT and files without an iopoll method from the poll-completion sequence, including the degenerate case IOCB_DIRECT == 0, with no interleaved mutation between check and use. No sink has an admitted failing witness, so no confirmed vulnerability is present.

assumptions: file is non-NULL with the requested mode bit after the L8 guard, since every later file-> dereference occurs only after that guard.
file->f_op is non-NULL per standard kernel file invariants; this is not shown in the fragment and is not used as the basis of any protective verdict.
io_file_get_flags() and io_file_supports_nowait() return narrow flag-state values used only in the internal req->flags word.
limitations: A NULL file->f_op dereference would require a NULL producer, and none is demonstrated by the shown statements; only file->f_op->iopoll == NULL is shown-guarded at L30.

Potential misplacement of flag bits in the L12 shift (io_file_get_flags(file) << REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT_BIT) is an internal correctness/behavior concern with no shown security consumer; not a confirmed finding.
The precise failure mode of the pre-fix counterpart (a buffered request reaching the IOPOLL completion path) is implied by the L30 guard rather than demonstrated by a crash inside this fragment.

verdict.summary: squashfs_opendir bounds dire->size with the guard at lines 72-75 (if(dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN) ... goto corrupted) before both the name read (lines 77-78) and the NUL write (line 82), so dire->size + 1 is at most SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN, within the SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1 byte name region declared at lines 5-6. The guard passes the Guard-Identity Audit: the same signed short value is checked after the swap (line 67) with no intervening mutation. Remaining candidates (negative dire->size needing unshown callee success on negative length, NULL from read_inode, and the truncated no-return tail) are not confirmable from the shown code.

assumptions: The name region capacity is SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1 bytes: line 5 declares buffer[sizeof(struct squashfs_dir_entry) + SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1] and line 7 places dire at its start, so dire->name has indices 0..SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN; the bound holds algebraically for any value of SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN.

read_directory_data fills exactly length bytes on success and returns FALSE for invalid/out-of-metadata lengths (lines 46-47, 64-65, 79-80 handle FALSE as failure); this is the basis for excluding negative dire->size values from reaching line 82.
read_inode returns a valid inode pointer for the shown dereferences at lines 24-28 and 40-42 (no NULL producer is shown).
limitations: Negative dire->size values (signed short) pass the line 72 guard; exploiting them would require read_directory_data (line 77) to return success for a negative length, a callee result not shown and contrary to standard read semantics — demoted.
A NULL return from read_inode (line 16) would make lines 24-28 dereference NULL, but no NULL producer is demonstrated in-fragment — demoted to limitation.

The fragment as displayed ends at line 123 with no return after squashfs_closedir(dir); if truly absent rather than a truncation of the upstream return NULL;, the indeterminate return value is consumed only at an unshown caller — demoted.

Integer overflow of bytes/size accounting or non-termination of the outer loop would require approximately 2^31 bytes of metadata; reads fail at the metadata end within the shown control flow before any in-fragment overflow is derivable — demoted.

verdict.summary: The only dangerous operation with a demonstrable in-fragment failure set is the write into `gpg->recipients` at line 10 (NULL target, CWE-476); it is protected on every path by the lazy NULL-check/initialization at lines 7-8, which excludes the NULL state before `g_ptr_array_add` is reached. No demonstrated failing value reaches any sink.

assumptions: `gpg` is non-NULL at entry; no in-fragment NULL producer exists for `gpg` itself.
`keyid` is a NUL-terminated string per its `const gchar *` contract; `g_strdup(NULL)` safely returns NULL and a NULL element in a GPtrArray is not dereferenced anywhere in the fragment.
GLib's `g_ptr_array_new()` (via `g_malloc0`) aborts on allocation failure and does not return NULL; allocation failure of this fixed small allocation is not an attacker-reachable failure.
limitations: A NULL or non-terminated `keyid` supplied by an unshown caller produces no in-fragment failure, and downstream consumers of the stored recipient strings are not shown, so any downstream NULL-deref or injection is outside this fragment.
A NULL `gpg` from an unshown caller would dereference at line 4, but no NULL producer is shown in-fragment.

verdict.summary: Off-by-one bounds check in __io_sync_cancel: `if (unlikely(fd > ctx->nr_user_files))` admits `fd == ctx->nr_user_files`, which reaches `io_fixed_file_slot(&ctx->file_table, fd)` and indexes one element past the `nr_user_files`-sized file table, causing an out-of-bounds kernel heap read (CWE-125). The missing one-statement fix is the exclusive upper bound `if (unlikely(fd >= ctx->nr_user_files))`.

evidence.reason: Sink indexes ctx->file_table.files[] with fd. After the line-11 guard `if (unlikely(fd > ctx->nr_user_files)) return -EBADF;`, the admitted set is 0 <= fd <= ctx->nr_user_files (equality admitted; negative fd rejected via unsigned conversion). The table has exactly ctx->nr_user_files entries (access convention: line 11 and line 13 bound the fd index space by nr_user_files, line 14 indexes it), so fd == ctx->nr_user_files reads file_ptr one past the end; fd == 0 with an empty table (nr_user_files == 0) is the equivalent degenerate witness. The guard does not exclude the boundary (it uses `>`), and the interleaved line-13 array_index_nospec assignment is a name-implied helper contract, not a quoted protective statement, so the sink is unprotected; the absent fix is `fd >= ctx->nr_user_files`. Primary mechanism: kernel heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), with the read word later masked (line 15) and used as struct file * at line 20.

assumptions: ctx->file_table.files[] has exactly ctx->nr_user_files entries; this is established by the fragment's access convention (lines 11, 13, 14 all treat nr_user_files as the fd index-space bound).
fd is user-supplied (entry-point io_uring cancel data) and can take any int value, including fd == ctx->nr_user_files and fd == 0 with an empty table.
The fixed-file path executes when cd->flags carries both IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_FD and IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_FD_FIXED (lines 7-8), which the attacker sets.
limitations: If array_index_nospec were credited with its name-implied masking semantics (returning an in-range index for out-of-range input at line 13), the architectural index could be clamped; that contract is not visible in the fragment and per the Verifiability Rule cannot ground a safe verdict, so the line-11 off-by-one remains the confirmed guard deficiency.
The downstream consequence of the OOB-read word (garbage struct file * at line 20) depends on heap layout, which is not shown; the confirmed mechanism is the out-of-bounds read itself.
The NULL-dereference candidate for cd->file is not a finding: lines 16-17 (`if (!cd->file) return -EBADF;`) are present on every path before line 20's use.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched member of the pair: every security-relevant sink carries a verbatim protective statement. The mark-position sink reg_getline(pos->lnum - rex.reg_firstlnum) at lines 158-159 is protected by the guard `if (pos == NULL ... || pos->lnum <= 0)` at lines 149-150 plus the ternary gating at 156-157; the backpos slot bp[i] is protected by `if (ga_grow(&backpos, 1) == FAIL)` (576) and the ga_data re-fetch (581); the RS_BEHIND2 line walk-back is protected by `lnum < behind_pos.rs_u.pos.lnum || reg_getline(...) == NULL` (1291-1295); the RS_STAR_LONG cross-line backup is protected by `if (rex.lnum == 0)` (1402) and `if (rex.line == NULL)` (1411); MULTIBYTECODE reads are bounded by the len>=2 check (504) and NUL/count-bounded loops (516, 535). No in-fragment derivation produces a failing value at any sink, so no vulnerability is confirmed.

assumptions: Lines are NUL-terminated buffers and rex.input always points within the current line (access convention shown by the fragment's own NUL tests, e.g. lines 88, 112, 200, and by column arithmetic rex.input - rex.line).
regstack and backpos are growable garrays whose ga_data is valid after ga_grow; backpos.ga_len is reset to 0 at lines 18-19.
regstack_push grows the stack as needed for the additionally pushed regitem_T after the shown ga_grow reservations at 976/1021 (callee contract, not shown).

Recorded backref positions (reg_startp/endp, reg_startpos/endpos) are within the matched buffer because they were produced by earlier successful matches or nulled positions guarded at lines 724 and 740-741.
limitations: RS_BEHIND2 edge: when rp->rs_un.regsave.rs_u.pos.lnum equals behind_pos.rs_u.pos.lnum == 0 and col == 0, the guard at 1291-1292 does not block reg_getline(--0) (reg_getline(-1)); whether -1 is NULL or an OOB read depends on unshown reg_getline/ml_get semantics and the unshown line-table layout, so it is demoted and not a confirmed finding.

The safety of MULTIBYTECODE byte-compare loop (535) relies on the NUL-termination convention and on opnd's multibyte char containing no NUL; reading past the line terminator is not derivable from shown state.
regstack reservation writes at lines 987 and 1033 rely on the unshown regstack_push capacity behavior for the final regitem_T; no in-fragment derivation of overflow exists.
All diagnostic mch_errmsg/printf calls are #ifdef DEBUG-only and use literal or "%s" formats; no attacker-controlled format string, command, SQL, URL, or log sink exists in the fragment.

verdict.summary: In handleLWPolylineData, a group code 42 (bulge) record that arrives before any group code 10 leaves vertexIndex at -1 (line 17). The guard at line 33 only checks vertexIndex<maxVertices, admits -1, and the write at line 34 computes vertices[4*(-1)+3] = vertices[-1], an out-of-bounds heap write of one double below the buffer allocated at line 9. The missing one-statement fix is a vertexIndex>=0 lower-bound conjunct in the groupCode==42 guard.

evidence.reason: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). vertexIndex is entry-point state set to -1 at line 17 after allocation of the 4*maxVertices-element buffer at line 9 (maxVertices>0 enforced at line 5). A file-supplied groupCode==42 record with no preceding groupCode==10 reaches line 34, passing the only guard, line 33 '} else if (groupCode==42 && vertexIndex<maxVertices) {', because -1 < maxVertices; the guard lacks the required vertexIndex>=0 lower-bound conjunct, so 4*vertexIndex+3 = -1 is written outside the buffer's index space [0, 4*maxVertices). Sibling guard line 30 (vertexIndex>=0 && vertexIndex<maxVertices) protects only the line 31 sink, not this one.

assumptions: vertices buffer capacity is 4*maxVertices doubles, established by the allocation at line 9.
groupCode/groupValue are entry-point DXF file data; the fragment imposes no constraint forcing a group code 10 before a group code 42.
limitations: Integer overflow of 4*maxVertices when maxVertices >= 2^29 would corrupt the allocation size at line 9; not evaluated as a separate finding because the decisive one-statement fix is the missing lower-bound check and the overflow path depends on allocation failure behavior.
vertexIndex==maxVertices (index 4*maxVertices+3 at line 34) is unreachable because line 25 caps increments at maxVertices-1.

When a second group code 90 with maxVertices<=0 arrives, vertices retains a stale pointer with vertexIndex=-1; dereference outcomes depend on unshown prior state and were not counted as a separate finding.

verdict.summary: block_insert() is the fixed member of the pair. Every copy sink (vim_memset pre/post padding at lines 90 and 102-103, mch_memmove at 86/94, STRMOVE tail at 116) is covered by the corrected allocation at lines 79-81, which now includes the spaces, ts_val - spaces and count + 1 capacity terms, and by the sanitizing clamp 'if (spaces < 0) spaces = 0;' at lines 75-76 plus the NULL check at 82-83. No shown input can drive a write or read past the allocation, so no vulnerability is demonstrated.

assumptions: block_prep() (line 22, unshown) supplies bdp->textcol/textlen so that offset = textcol + textlen [- 1] (lines 44, 52) never exceeds STRLEN(oldp); the fragment itself does not bound offset, so sinks S2 (line 86) and S7 (lines 63, 71) rely on that convention.
For a TAB cut, block_prep supplies 1 <= startspaces/endspaces < ts_val, so ts_val - spaces >= 0 at line 102-103 and count = ts_val - 1 - off >= 0 at line 65.
STRLEN(oldp) counts bytes excluding the terminating NUL; STRMOVE writes the tail including the NUL, which the '+ 1' term at line 81 reserves.
ml_get(lnum) (line 26) returns a valid NUL-terminated line for every lnum in [oap->start.lnum + 1, oap->end.lnum].
limitations: S2 (line 86) and S7 (lines 63, 71) could read/write out of bounds only if bdp->textcol/textlen exceeded the line length, a condition no shown statement can derive (the producer is the unshown block_prep); demoted, no CWE.
An integer wrap of the allocation expression (line 79-81) would require a line length near SIZE_MAX; no shown producer can create that magnitude.

A negative count from 'count -= off' (line 65) is not derivable from the shown geometry (off is bounded by the char width and spaces <= ts_val - 1 in the cut setup) and, even if forced to -1 with spaces clamped to 0, the copies skip all count consumers so the '+ 1' NUL reserve still holds; recorded as an unconfirmed edge case.
Theoretical leak of newp when 'newp == NULL' would be reached is non-existent (nothing allocated on that path); no UAF/double-free arises from ml_replace ownership.

verdict.summary: io_rw_init_file is the fixed/patched counterpart. The only file-derived dereferences (lines 12, 14, 25, 29) are covered on every path by the NULL/mode gate at line 8; the kiocb_set_rw_flags return status is checked immediately at lines 16-17; the IOPOLL branch requires IOCB_DIRECT (only settable from an O_DIRECT file via the line-14 initialization) and a supported iopoll op, returning -EOPNOTSUPP otherwise; and the non-IOPOLL branch rejects IOCB_HIPRI with -EINVAL. No dangerous sink lacks its protective statement, so the fragment is not vulnerable.

assumptions: file is assigned once at line 5 (file = req->file) and never reassigned, so the line-8 gate covers every later file use with no check-then-use drift.

kiocb->ki_flags is reinitialized by assignment at line 14 (kiocb->ki_flags = iocb_flags(file)), so IOCB_DIRECT can only be set when file->f_flags & O_DIRECT holds and stale flags from request reuse cannot satisfy the line-29 IOPOLL check.
ret is consumed immediately at line 16 with no intervening mutation, so the lines 16-17 check excludes all nonzero returns from kiocb_set_rw_flags on the same value and precision.
limitations: A NULL dereference of file->f_op at line 29 (or of ctx at line 28) has no NULL producer shown in the fragment; NULL for those pointers requires an unshown caller or an out-of-fragment kernel invariant, so it is demoted, not a finding.

io_file_get_flags, io_file_supports_nowait, and kiocb_set_rw_flags are unshown callees analyzed only by standard name-implied semantics; the verdict rests on the fragment's own verbatim guards, not on their contracts.
if file->f_op->iopoll were ever NULL the line-29 check is fail-closed (-EOPNOTSUPP), so no crash-only or bypass consequence is reachable from shown code.
The mode parameter is checked only as a set-membership gate; a caller passing mode bits the file lacks is rejected (fail-closed), which is robustness, not a security defect.

verdict.summary: Unvalidated firmware-provided lengths reach two DMA-style RPC copy sinks. fw.len (residual 0..0xFFFE after the loop guards) sizes hw_atl_utils_fw_downld_dwords' write into self->rpc ((fw.len+3)/4 dwords, up to 16384), overflowing the ~22-dword self->rpc object (CWE-787); sw.len (residual 0..0xFFFF, unchecked) sizes the hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call upload that reads (sw.len+3)/4 dwords from self->rpc (CWE-125). The fix (torvalds/linux b922f622592a) adds the missing bound checks 'if (fw.len > sizeof(self->rpc))' and 'if (sw.len > sizeof(self->rpc))', which are absent here.

evidence.reason: OOB write (CWE-787): fw.len is a u16 register field filled by readx_poll_timeout_atomic (lines 13-16), residual range [0,0xFFFE] after the loop exit guard (line 29, only excludes 0xFFFF) and the nonzero test (line 32, only excludes 0). The sink count (fw.len+3)/4 with fw.len=0xFFFE yields 16384 dwords written through (u32 *)(void *)&self->rpc, whose capacity is sizeof(self->rpc) = 22 dwords (capacity constant used by the real fix b922f622592a). No guard constrains fw.len against that capacity; the absent fix is 'if (fw.len > sizeof(self->rpc)) { err = -EINVAL; goto err_exit; }' before this call.

OOB read (CWE-125): sw.len is a u16 register field from aq_hw_read_reg (line 9) with no shown constraint (residual [0,0xFFFF]); the branch guard (line 24) only tests fw.len == 0xFFFFU. hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call uploads (sw.len+3)/4 dwords from &self->rpc (22-dword object). Witness sw.len=0xFFFF reads 16384 dwords past the object. The absent fix is 'if (sw.len > sizeof(self->rpc)) { err = -EINVAL; goto err_exit; }' before the call.

assumptions: aq_hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_tid_s is a union of u32 val with u16 tid and u16 len, so sw.len/fw.len range over [0,0xFFFF]; len==0xFFFF is the firmware-request sentinel referenced at lines 24 and 29.

self->rpc is the embedded 'struct hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc rpc' in struct aq_hw_s (aq_hw.h); its compile-time capacity sizeof(self->rpc) ≈ 88 bytes = 22 dwords, as proven by the fix commit's bound constant 'sizeof(self->rpc)'.

hw_atl_utils_fw_downld_dwords writes cnt u32 dwords into p, and hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call uploads (rpc_size+3)/4 dwords from &self->rpc (standard semantics confirmed by the driver source and the KASAN report in b922f622592a).

verdict.summary: Heap-based out-of-bounds read in find_match_text: the inner loop advances len2 by MB_CHAR2LEN(c2) (line 21), where c2 is decoded from the searched line by PTR2CHAR (line 15). For a line ending in a truncated/invalid UTF-8 sequence, PTR2CHAR decodes a value whose full byte length exceeds the bytes actually present before the NUL, so len2 jumps past the line's NUL and the next PTR2CHAR(rex.line + col + len2) read (line 15, and line 26 for the composing-char check) reads beyond the line buffer. The missing one-statement fix (vim 8.2.3409) measures the advance against the actual bytes: len2 += enc_utf8 ? utf_ptr2len(rex.line + col + len2) : MB_CHAR2LEN(c2).

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125). len2 is an unconstrained index into the NUL-terminated rex.line: it starts at MB_CHAR2LEN(regstart) (line 11) and is advanced by the decoded-value length at line 21 (len2 += MB_CHAR2LEN(c2)). The line-16 mismatch guard admits the c1 == c2 case, so when rex.line's last bytes are a truncated multi-byte sequence (e.g., 0xE3 followed by the line's NUL), PTR2CHAR decodes a value whose MB_CHAR2LEN (3) exceeds the bytes up to the NUL (1); the line-21 advance then steps len2 past the NUL, and this line-15 PTR2CHAR is re-executed at col + len2 beyond the line allocation. The absent fix (present in vim patch 8.2.3409) substitutes len2 += enc_utf8 ? utf_ptr2len(rex.line + col + len2) : MB_CHAR2LEN(c2);, measuring the advance at the pointer so it stops at the NUL.

OOB read (CWE-125) via the same over-advanced index. When the inner loop ends with match == TRUE after len2 has been advanced past the line's NUL by line 21's MB_CHAR2LEN(c2) on a truncated multi-byte line tail, this composing-char check reads PTR2CHAR(rex.line + col + len2) beyond the line buffer. The composing guard only tests enc_utf8/utf_iscomposing and does not bound col + len2; the missing fix is the pointer-measured advance (utf_ptr2len) from vim patch 8.2.3409.

assumptions: rex.line is a NUL-terminated line buffer whose NUL byte lies within the allocation; the fragment itself relies on this convention because the line-16 mismatch break terminates the scan when c2 decodes to NUL.

PTR2CHAR and MB_CHAR2LEN use Vim's standard UTF-8 semantics: PTR2CHAR decodes up to a leading byte's declared length even when the sequence is truncated by NUL, and MB_CHAR2LEN returns the full byte length of the decoded value; neither macro's body is shown in the fragment (standard semantics per Phase 4 call-site rule).

match_text and the line bytes before the NUL are unconstrained by any shown validation; the fragment admits arbitrary bytes, including invalid/truncated UTF-8 and pattern characters equal to their decoded values.
limitations: NULL dereference of rex.line and validity of startcol depend on unshown callers and are not confirmed in-fragment.
Integer overflow of col/len2 and non-termination of the outer loop via skip_to_start require unshown magnitudes/helper behavior and are demoted.
The exact upstream one-line fix (vim patch 8.2.3409, verified externally) corroborates the failure mode but the verdict rests on the fragment's own line 21 advance and lines 15/26 reads.
Attacker control of rex.line/match_text content is realized through the regex/text-search pipeline outside the fragment; inside the fragment both are unconstrained NUL-terminated inputs.

verdict.summary: udf_expand_file_adinicb() uses the disk-derived, unconstrained iinfo->i_lenAlloc as both an offset/count in memset(kaddr + i_lenAlloc, 0x00, PAGE_SIZE - i_lenAlloc) and a byte count in memcpy(kaddr, ..., i_lenAlloc) without bounding it against PAGE_SIZE. A crafted UDF image setting i_lenAlloc beyond PAGE_SIZE makes the memcpy write past the end of the PAGE_SIZE page and makes PAGE_SIZE - i_lenAlloc underflow in size_t, causing an out-of-bounds kernel write. The only guards on the path (i_lenAlloc nonzero, page non-NULL, page-not-uptodate) never constrain the size upper bound.

evidence.reason: The copy count is iinfo->i_lenAlloc, an unsigned 32-bit field derived from on-disk UDF inode metadata (Phase-1 entry-point input) whose only shown constraint is line 9's `if (!iinfo->i_lenAlloc)` (excludes only 0), leaving residual range [1, UINT_MAX]. The destination page's capacity is PAGE_SIZE, evidenced by the fragment's own access convention at line 33 (`PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc`). Witness i_lenAlloc = PAGE_SIZE + 1 passes line 9 (nonzero), line 27 (page allocated), and line 30 (fresh page not PageUptodate), and reaches this sink; memcpy then writes PAGE_SIZE+1 bytes into the PAGE_SIZE page (CWE-787 OOB write). No statement on any path bounds i_lenAlloc against PAGE_SIZE; the absent one-statement fix is a bound check such as `if (iinfo->i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE) return -EIO;` before line 32.

Same unconstrained iinfo->i_lenAlloc (residual [1, UINT_MAX] after line 9) is both the base-page offset and, via `PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc` in unsigned size_t arithmetic, the count. With i_lenAlloc = PAGE_SIZE + 1 (admitted by lines 9, 27, 30), PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc wraps to SIZE_MAX-4096 and the base kaddr + i_lenAlloc already lies beyond the PAGE_SIZE page, yielding a massive out-of-bounds kernel write (CWE-787). The absent fix is the same missing i_lenAlloc <= PAGE_SIZE bound.

assumptions: The page object allocated at line 26 has capacity PAGE_SIZE, established in-fragment by the access convention at line 33 (`PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc`).

limitations: Out-of-bounds claims against iinfo->i_data (line 41-42 memset, line 59 memcpy, and the read side of line 34) are not confirmable because the capacity of iinfo->i_data (UDF_INLINE_DATA_SIZE) is not declared or otherwise evidenced inside the shown fragment.

No loops, format-string, command, SQL, crypto, or authz sinks are present in the fragment.

verdict.summary: udf_expand_file_adinicb uses the on-disk-derived, unvalidated field iinfo->i_lenAlloc as a destination offset and length for a page-sized memset/memcpy. With i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE (e.g., 4097), kaddr + i_lenAlloc is past the page and PAGE_SIZE - i_lenAlloc underflows 64-bit unsigned arithmetic to a huge size, causing an out-of-bounds write beyond the page-cache page (CWE-787) when mounting a crafted UDF image. The only length guard, line 9 'if (!iinfo->i_lenAlloc)', excludes zero but admits every overflowing value; the absent one-statement fix is an upper-bound check such as 'if (iinfo->i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE) return -EFBIG;' before line 32.

evidence.reason: Sink: with L = iinfo->i_lenAlloc in the Phase-1 residual range 1..2^32-1 (on-disk-derived UDF metadata, entry-point channel; only constraint is line 9 'if (!iinfo->i_lenAlloc)', which admits all non-zero values including 4097), L = 4097 drives the pointer kaddr + 4097 past the PAGE_SIZE page (capacity shown by the 'PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc' expression on line 33 and page-cache semantics) and makes PAGE_SIZE - L underflow to ~2^64-1 in 64-bit unsigned arithmetic, producing a huge out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). Guards audited: line 9 admits 4097; lines 27 and 30 constrain page NULL-ness and uptodate state only (wrong-target drift if credited for the length). Absent fix: an upper-bound check on iinfo->i_lenAlloc before this statement, e.g. 'if (iinfo->i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE) return -EFBIG;'.

Sink: the same unvalidated iinfo->i_lenAlloc (residual range 1..2^32-1 from Phase 1) is the copy length into kaddr, a PAGE_SIZE page; with L = 4097 the memcpy writes 4097 bytes into a 4096-byte page for an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). Line 9 'if (!iinfo->i_lenAlloc)' admits 4097 and is the only length-related guard; the page NULL check (line 27) and PageUptodate branch (line 30) do not constrain the length. The source read iinfo->i_data + iinfo->i_lenEAttr is not confirmed because i_data's capacity is not shown. Absent fix: same upper-bound guard on iinfo->i_lenAlloc before line 32.

assumptions: iinfo->i_lenAlloc and iinfo->i_lenEAttr are unsigned 32-bit fields of struct udf_inode_info mirroring on-disk UDF metadata; per the kernel entry-point rule they are treated as attacker-controlled via a crafted UDF image, and the fragment imposes no cap.
The page returned by find_or_create_page (line 26) has capacity PAGE_SIZE; the in-fragment expression 'PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc' (line 33) demonstrates the page-size convention.
A page freshly returned by find_or_create_page is not PageUptodate, so the branch at line 30 and sinks at lines 32-35 execute on the normal first-expansion path.
limitations: Out-of-bounds reads/writes relative to iinfo->i_data (sinks at lines 34, 41-42, and 59) cannot be confirmed because the capacity of i_data is not established by any shown declaration, allocation, or size-bearing access convention; the fragment shows only i_data + i_lenEAttr usages.
The exact provenance of i_lenAlloc (set from disk metadata in unshown udf_load_inode code) is inferred rather than displayed; it is treated as entry-point input per the kernel-channel rule.
The unsigned underflow at line 33 (PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc) is an integer-wrap enabler of the primary CWE-787 failure and is not reported as a separate CWE-190/191 finding.

If page 0 were already uptodate when this function runs, lines 32-35 would be skipped; the not-uptodate state is the normal first-access state for a page from find_or_create_page and requires no external fact, so the failing path remains reachable.

verdict.summary: Both firmware-controlled lengths are validated immediately before their sinks: `fw.len` is bounded by `if (fw.len > sizeof(self->rpc))` (line 38) before the dword download into `self->rpc`, and `sw.len` by `if (sw.len > sizeof(self->rpc))` (line 25) before the RPC call; all helper return statuses are checked (err < 0 -> goto err_exit) and `rpc` is NULL-checked. No failing value reachable from the shown code was found.

assumptions: sizeof(self->rpc) is the capacity of the download buffer; `self->rpc` is the object written by `hw_atl_utils_fw_downld_dwords` and the same object whose address is published via `*rpc`.

fw.len/sw.len are 16-bit fields of the sw/fw tid unions (inferred from the `0xFFFFU` sentinel comparisons and the `%x` printk), so their declared domains are 0..0xFFFF and the PROVEN post-loop maximum for fw.len is 0xFFFE.
limitations: Dword-rounding residual at Sink A: the download writes 4*((fw.len+3)/4) bytes, which exceeds sizeof(self->rpc) by up to 3 bytes when the admitted value fw.len == sizeof(self->rpc) (or sizeof-1..sizeof-3) lands on a non-multiple-of-4 capacity. Whether sizeof(self->rpc) % 4 == 0 is not shown in the fragment and cannot be derived from it, so no concrete failing witness exists; if the struct size were non-dword-aligned, the absent fix would be a rounded bound such as `if (fw.len + sizeof(u32) - sizeof(u8) > sizeof(self->rpc))`. Not confirmed as a finding.

The semantics of `hw_atl_utils_fw_rpc_call(self, sw.len)` are not shown (no copy/parse/exec contract implied by the name); its size argument is guarded by line 25, but no independent failure set for the callee could be confirmed.

Firmware-driven non-termination is theoretically possible if the device repeatedly answers with fw.len == 0xFFFF and a matching tid (loop at lines 8-34 repeats, each iteration bounded by the 100000us poll timeout); this is a device self-DoS with no memory-safety consequence and requires unshown malicious device behavior beyond parsing, so it is demoted.

verdict.summary: ZRLE decoder bounds all dangerous operations: palette indexes are masked to 0..127 against a 128-entry palette (lines 65 and 116), RLE run lengths are checked against remaining tile space before writing (lines 88-90, 111-113), and every buf write is bounded by tile clamps (lines 12, 16) to t.area() <= 4096, matching the declared PIXEL_T buf[64*64] capacity (line 8). No attacker-controlled value can exceed a declared capacity or reach an unguarded sink, so no memory-safety or injection finding is confirmed.

assumptions: PIXEL_T palette[128] (line 21) has capacity 128, indices 0..127.
PIXEL_T buf[64 * 64] (line 8) has capacity 4096 pixels; in the non-CPIXEL branch sizeof(PIXEL_T) == BPP/8 so readBytes(buf, t.area() * (BPP/8)) matches the byte capacity.
Tile dimensions are bounded to <= 64 each by the __rfbmin clamps at lines 12 and 16 while the loop bodies execute (t.tl.y < r.br.y / t.tl.x < r.br.x at lines 10 and 14), so t.area() <= 4096.
limitations: RLE palette-decode can read palette[index] with index >= palSize (e.g., palSize=2, index=100): still within the declared 128-element palette, so this is an in-bounds read of unfilled entries flowing only to the framebuffer display - a robustness/correctness concern, not a memory-safety or security-decision finding.

int length = is->readU32() (line 5) narrows values >= 2^31 to negative and passes them to zis->setUnderlying(is, length) (line 6); the callee's handling of a negative length is not shown, so any consequence is unconfirmable.

RLE run-length int accumulation (lines 84-86, 107-109) can overflow only after ~8.4M iterations of a 255-byte stream per run; overflowed lengths either write zero pixels or trip the guards at lines 88/111, so no overrun is derivable; a resource-exhaustion scenario would depend on unshown stream/limit semantics.

Rect coordinates near INT_MAX could make t.tl.y + 64 (lines 12, 16) overflow, but then t.br <= t.tl makes the tile area non-positive and the write loops no-op; producing such a rect depends on an unshown upper-layer geometry constraint.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in SetGrayscaleImage: for PseudoClass images, colormap_index is allocated with image->colors+1 entries (line 26), but the final remap loop reads colormap_index[ScaleQuantumToMap(GetPixelIndex(image,q))] (lines 148-149) with an attacker-controlled index in [0, MaxMap] that no shown check constrains against that capacity. evidence.reason: For image->storage_class == PseudoClass (branch at line 25), colormap_index is allocated with capacity image->colors+1 at line 26 (verbatim: 'AcquireQuantumMemory(image->colors+1,sizeof(*colormap_index))'), with image->colors having no shown minimum or cap. At the sink, the index is ScaleQuantumToMap(GetPixelIndex(image,q)): GetPixelIndex returns unvalidated entry-point pixel data and ScaleQuantumToMap maps into [0, MaxMap]=[0,65535]; no guard constrains this value to image->colors (line 141 constrains q only — wrong-target drift; lines 130/146 bound x/y only). Witness admitted by every guard: PseudoClass image with image->colors==1 (2-element buffer) and an 8-bit stored pixel index >= 1, which scales to ~257, causing a heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The absent one-statement fix is either a bound check restricting the scaled pixel index to < image->colors before the read, or allocating MaxColormapSize+1 in the PseudoClass branch at line 26.

assumptions: MaxColormapSize == 65536 and MaxMap == MaxColormapSize-1 == 65535 (standard ImageMagick constants, corroborated by the line 29 allocation MaxColormapSize+1).
ScaleQuantumToMap returns a value in [0, MaxMap].
GetPixelIndex returns the stored per-pixel index without validation against image->colors; no shown statement in the fragment clamps it.
limitations: Whether a particular image coder emits a PseudoClass image whose stored pixel indices exceed image->colors is external to this fragment, but the fragment itself neither requires nor enforces the contrary.
The image->colors == 0 degenerate edge and any helper-contract guarantees of AcquireImageColormap are not relied upon for this finding.

verdict.summary: sixpack_close() runs del_timer_sync() on sp->tx_t/sp->resync_t (lines 25-26) before unregister_netdev(sp->dev) (line 28), leaving an open window in which the still-registered transmit path can re-arm sp->tx_t via mod_timer(); the timer then stays pending across the kfree()s (31-32) and free_netdev(sp->dev) (34) that release the sixpack private data, so the timer callback dereferences freed sp (use-after-free). The re-armed timer fires after line 34 and the callback touches freed sp -> CWE-416 use-after-free. The fix form is absent: the shown unregister_netdev(sp->dev) at line 28 is at the wrong control point (after the deletes), so it fails the Guard-Identity Audit (control-point drift) and does not close the re-arm window before the frees.

free_netdev(sp->dev) releases the struct sixpack that is the net_device's private area (netdev_priv), so the timer callback touching sp after line 34 is a use-after-free.

standard kernel semantics: del_timer_sync() guarantees no running callback at return but does not prevent a concurrent mod_timer() re-arm; unregister_netdev() is a full synchronization barrier that closes the re-arm window only if it runs before the timer teardown.
netif_stop_queue(sp->dev) at line 23 is the protective statement for the freed-buffer scribble hazard (kfree of rbuff/xbuff at lines 31-32).
limitations: The concurrent re-arming call site (sp_xmit_on_air -> mod_timer) and the timer callback body are not shown in the fragment, so the failing interleaving is inferred from standard timer/unregister semantics plus the kernel's documented fix (commit efe4186e6a1b) rather than fully derived from shown statements; this caps confidence at the fragile race-interleaving band.
Exploitation requires a reachable privileged userspace path (ax25_* syscalls on an attached 6pack tty) concurrent with sixpack_close(); without that environment the flaw is unreachable.
No integer, capacity, or bounds issue exists in the fragment; the rbuff/xbuff frees are guarded by netif_stop_queue (line 23), and the NULL deref hazard is guarded by lines 9-10.

verdict.summary: The allocation-size expression `width * height * 4` at line 27 is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic with no overflow or dimension guard, so attacker-controlled UINT32 width/height (e.g., 65536 x 65536) wrap the product to 0 (or another small value). BufferPool_Take then returns a buffer far too small, while line 34 binds that buffer to a full width x height surface and lines 18/48 reset decoders for the full dimensions, producing a heap buffer overflow when decoded frames are written into the undersized surface.

evidence.reason: width and height are UINT32 parameters (line 2) with no shown constraint, residual range 0..UINT32_MAX. The expression `width * height * 4` is evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic; witness width=0x10000, height=0x10000 yields 0x10000*0x10000 = 2^32 ≡ 0 (mod 2^32), so BufferPool_Take receives size 0. The only intervening guards are non-NULL checks (lines 28, 35): they test pointer validity, not the size, so they admit the witness (a zero-size pool take can return non-NULL) — Guard-Identity Audit drift class (3) wrong-target. The wrapped size is consumed as the allocation size, then line 34 `video->createSurface(video, ret->surfaceData, x, y, width, height)` binds the undersized buffer to a full 65536x65536 surface and lines 18/48 reset h264/yuv decoders for the full dimensions, so decoder writes overflow the buffer (integer overflow → heap overflow). The absent one-statement fix is an added bound/overflow check on width/height or the product before line 27 (e.g., `if (width > UINT16_MAX || height > UINT16_MAX) goto error_h264;` or a UINT64 product with an overflow check). Primary CWE-190 at the truncated size computation consumed by the allocation; secondary CWE-122 heap overflow on the undersized surface buffer.

assumptions: width and height are entry-derived UINT32 values (declared at line 2) with no in-fragment constraint; the overflow witness (0x10000, 0x10000) is entirely within their declared domain.
The arithmetic in `width * height * 4` (line 27) is performed at 32-bit unsigned precision because both operands are UINT32.
BufferPool_Take returns a buffer of the requested (wrapped) size and may return non-NULL even for a 0-size request, so the non-NULL check at line 28 does not exclude the failing path.

createSurface (line 34) binds the returned buffer as the backing store of a width x height surface, and the h264/yuv decoders (lines 18, 48) subsequently write full-resolution frames into it per their name-implied standard semantics.
limitations: The actual overflowing write occurs inside the unshown decoder/surface rendering code; the in-fragment proof is the demonstrated 32-bit wrap at line 27 and the undersized allocation being bound to full dimensions at line 34.
A NULL dereference of `video->priv` at line 4 is not reported: no NULL producer for `video` is shown in the fragment, so it is caller-dependent.
Potential oversized x/y coordinates forwarded to createSurface (line 34) are not reported: their failure depends on unshown rendering semantics.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains no dangerous sink with a demonstrated failing value. 'user_tick' reaches accounting/RCU helpers without validation, and 'p' is initialized from 'current' with no NULL producer, so no NULL-deref or out-of-domain failure is derivable from shown statements. The only security-relevant operation, the per-CPU PRNG-state refresh at line 22, carries its own non-constant, non-affine update ('this_cpu_add(net_rand_state.s1, rol32(jiffies, 24) + user_tick);'), and its u32 wrap is consumed only by the state-mixing counter, not by any index, size, allocation, or security decision. Verdict: NOT vulnerable.

assumptions: this_cpu_add(net_rand_state.s1, ...) targets a fixed per-CPU field; the operand derives no index, size, or offset from input.
rol32 returns a u32; in 'rol32(jiffies, 24) + user_tick' the int is converted to unsigned and the result wraps by defined 2^32 semantics, which is the intended behavior of a PRNG state machine.
The consumers of 'user_tick' visible in the fragment (account_process_tick, rcu_sched_clock_irq) treat it as a tick flag; no size-, bound-, or authorization-sensitive consumer is shown.
limitations: NULL-deref candidate on account_process_tick(p=current, ...) (line 6): no NULL producer for 'current' appears in the fragment, so no CWE-476 failure is confirmable; confirming would require external evidence of a NULL 'current'.

No consumer of net_rand_state (e.g., net_random, socket-hash, token) is shown, so no weak-PRNG/entropy finding (CWE-330/338) is confirmable from the fragment alone; a security boundary depending on this state would need separate evidence.

No shown check constrains user_tick to {0,1} (e.g., INT_MIN or INT_MAX are admitted), but no shown consumer converts an out-of-domain value into a memory-safety or security failure; an unconstrained range alone is not a finding.

verdict.summary: xemaclite_of_probe() re-looks up the MEM resource at line 33 (res = platform_get_resource(ofdev, IORESOURCE_MEM, 0);) and then dereferences res at lines 40-41 without any NULL check on res itself. The in-fragment sibling guard at lines 25-29 (if (!res) for the IORESOURCE_IRQ lookup) demonstrates that platform_get_resource() can return NULL, so a device node without a MEM resource drives a NULL pointer dereference. The only guards on the path (line 25 for the IRQ resource, line 35 IS_ERR on lp->base_addr) constrain different values and fail the Guard-Identity Audit (wrong-target drift). The absent one-statement fix is an 'if (!res)' resource-presence check after line 33 that jumps to error.

evidence.reason: Dereferences res, which at this point holds the unconstrained return of platform_get_resource(ofdev, IORESOURCE_MEM, 0) from line 33; the fragment admits a NULL return (its own guard at lines 25-29 rejects NULL for the identical API on the IRQ lookup) and nothing between line 33 and line 40 tests res. The IS_ERR(lp->base_addr) guard at line 35 constrains devm_ioremap_resource's result, not res (Guard-Identity drift class 3, wrong-target), so the NULL reaches the sink. Absent fix: an 'if (!res)' check after line 33. Primary mechanism: NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476).

Second dereference of the same unguarded res from line 33; NULL is admitted by the fragment's own platform_get_resource convention and by every guard on the path (none tests res), so this line also dereferences NULL when the node lacks a MEM resource. Absent fix: the same 'if (!res)' resource-presence check after line 33. Primary mechanism: NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476).

assumptions: platform_get_resource(ofdev, IORESOURCE_MEM, 0) may return NULL when the node has no matching memory resource; the fragment itself confirms this outcome is expected for this API by NULL-checking the preceding IORESOURCE_IRQ lookup at lines 25-29.

devm_ioremap_resource() at line 34 is analyzed only by its name-implied semantics (validate resource, request region, ioremap, return ERR_PTR on failure); its IS_ERR check at line 35 constrains lp->base_addr only, not res, so it is treated as a wrong-target guard, not protection.
limitations: If a particular kernel's devm_ioremap_resource() itself returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) for a NULL res, control would exit via the error label and lines 40-41 would be unreachable in that build; the fragment shows no guard on res, and crediting that callee contract is not permitted for a safe verdict, so the NULL deref of res remains the least-protected sink.
Triggering requires a platform/DT configuration where the device node lacks a memory resource; the impact is a probe-time kernel NULL-deref crash (denial of service), not privilege escalation.

evidence.reason: qo is assigned from bf->o->bin_obj (line 3), an entry-point-derived field with no shown non-NULL constraint, so its residual range includes NULL. The line-2 guard (rz_return_val_if_fail(bf && bf->o, NULL)) exempts only bf and bf->o, failing the Guard-Identity Audit as wrong-target drift for this sink. With qo == NULL the read qo->fixups at line 4 is a NULL dereference (CWE-476). The one-statement fix that is ABSENT is a NULL check on qo, e.g. rz_return_val_if_fail(qo, NULL); placed after line 3.

assumptions: bf->o->bin_obj is a pointer produced from parsing the input file and is not constrained by any statement in the fragment.
The line-2 macro is an unconditional early-return guard whose admitted set for later lines is bf != NULL && bf->o != NULL.
limitations: The exact loader path that can leave bf->o->bin_obj NULL is not visible in the fragment; the NULL producer for qo is external, so the witness rests on one unchecked boundary and confidence is capped accordingly.
A NULL qo->fixups argument to rz_list_clone was considered but demoted: no shown producer makes fixups NULL, and rz_list_clone's NULL-handling behavior is not shown.

verdict.summary: seq_buf_alloc bounds size before allocation: the verbatim guard `if (unlikely(size > MAX_RW_COUNT)) return NULL;` (lines 3-4) excludes the entire oversize failure set from reaching the kvmalloc sink at line 6, on every path, at the same value and type with no interleaved mutation.

size is unsigned long, so the declared domain is 0..ULONG_MAX and the only failure class relevant to the allocation sink is oversize (size > MAX_RW_COUNT), which the guard fully excludes.

verdict.summary: CLINoImageOperator contains no unguarded dangerous sink on any path shown in the fragment. Every InterpretImageProperties result is NULL-checked at the immediately following statement (L36, L43, L280, L293, L319, L339) with fallback or break; the write path bounds FormatLocaleString to MagickPathExtent and NULL-checks write_images (L139, L143); the print sink uses a literal "%s" format (L267); stack nesting is capped with 'size >= MAX_STACK_DEPTH' (L164, L195); argv indexing is bounded by 'i < (ssize_t) argc' (L104); list dispatch validates 'list < 0' before use (L393); prefix offsets arg1+7/arg1+9 are bounded by their LocaleNCompare prefix-equality guards; clone validates IsSceneGeometry and NULL-checks CloneImages (L361, L369); ExpandFilenames failure breaks (L99); empty image lists are guarded (L133, L329); cleanup double-destroy is prevented by the arg1 != arg1n / arg2 != arg2n identity guards (L466, L468). assumptions: MagickPathExtent (L124, L139) is the capacity of key and is passed as the size bound to FormatLocaleString, so the build at L139 is capacity-bounded.
MAX_STACK_DEPTH is a positive constant; the '>=' comparisons at L164 and L195 exclude size == MAX_STACK_DEPTH and cap nesting at MAX_STACK_DEPTH.
ExpandFilenames (L99) fills argv/argc consistently, so the loop at L104 indexes only [0, argc); an argc of 0 yields zero iterations.

Printing with a NULL arg1 at L267 would be UB, but that requires the CLI to invoke 'print' without its required argument, an arity invariant enforced outside the fragment.
The set handler's second InterpretImageProperties (L279) can leak the first percent-interpreted copy of arg1 (L35) when interpretation flags are active; a memory leak with no shown security impact.

Within the MagickNextImage loops (L309-310, L333-350), DeleteImageArtifact/SetImage* target _images (the list head) rather than the iterator's current image; a logic quirk with no confirmed in-fragment security consequence.
The paired vulnerable counterpart statement is not shown; this fragment contains a guard for every dangerous sink inventoried.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in networkstatus_parse_vote_from_string: when the K_NETWORK_STATUS_VERSION token has exactly two arguments (n_args == 2, admitted by the line-42 guard `tok->n_args > 1`) and the flavor name in tok->args[1] is unknown, the error path at line 46 evaluates escaped(tok->args[2]), reading one pointer past the args array (valid indices 0..n_args-1 per the fragment's own `i < tok->n_args` access conventions) and dereferencing it inside escaped(). The missing fix is a guard excluding n_args == 2 before indexing args[2], or substituting the in-bounds args[1].

evidence.reason: Sink indexes tok->args[2] on a token whose n_args is guaranteed only >= 2 by the guard at line 42 (`if (tok->n_args > 1)`), whose admitted set includes the failing boundary n_args == 2. The args array capacity is n_args entries (valid indices 0..n_args-1), established by the fragment's own access conventions `for (i=0; i < tok->n_args; ++i) ... tok->args[i]` (lines 92-93, 158-159). Witness: attacker-controlled document line `network-status-version 3 notarealflavor` tokenizes with n_args == 2, args[1] = "notarealflavor", line 43 flavor parse returns < 0, line 44 true, line 46 reads argv index 2 (one past capacity), an OOB pointer read dereferenced by escaped() (CWE-125). Guard-Identity Audit: line 42 constrains the same n_args value with no interleaved mutation but admits n_args == 2, which the sink's index 2 requires n_args >= 3, so the guard is insufficient. Absent fix: a bound check `tok->n_args > 2` (or `>= 3`) before the log, or sink substitution to in-bounds `tok->args[1]`.

assumptions: tokenize_string standard semantics: a K_NETWORK_STATUS_VERSION line with two fields after the keyword yields n_args == 2 and an args array with valid indices 0..1; n_args counts the stored argument strings.
The fragment's own guard at line 42 treats n_args == 2 as a parseable state (it reads args[1] as the flavor), confirming n_args == 2 is in the code's own model.
Network-status documents supplied as `s` are entry-point, attacker-controlled input.
limitations: Other token-argument accesses (e.g., tok->args[0] for K_VALID_AFTER/K_FRESH_UNTIL/K_VALID_UNTIL, K_CLIENT_VERSIONS/SERVER_VERSIONS at lines 148-152) have no visible n_args guards, but their token tables are not shown and no failing value for them is derivable from the fragment alone; not confirmed.
The exact token table constraints for K_NETWORK_STATUS_VERSION are unshown; the finding does not rely on them because the fragment's own guard admits n_args == 2.

All other inventoried memory sinks (base16_decode exact-length calls, tor_memdup after object_size bounds at line 417, smartlist_get after empty-list check at line 267) carry shown protective statements and were resolved PRESENT; they are bystanders to this finding.

verdict.summary: The fragment is a trivial wrapper that directly returns kvmalloc(size, GFP_KERNEL_ACCOUNT). The size parameter has no shown call site and is never arithmetically transformed or truncated, and the allocation's potentially NULL result is returned without any in-fragment dereference, copy, or index. No dangerous sink with a demonstrated failure set exists inside the shown code, so the fragment is not vulnerable.

assumptions: kvmalloc(size, GFP_KERNEL_ACCOUNT) follows standard allocator semantics: non-NULL on success, NULL on allocation failure.
size is an internal-helper parameter with no shown call site, so its provenance (attacker-controlled vs. trusted) cannot be established from the fragment.
limitations: A NULL return from kvmalloc is never dereferenced inside the fragment; a NULL-dereference would require an unshown caller to dereference the propagated pointer.
Resource exhaustion from an oversized size would require size to be attacker-controlled via an unshown caller; no such taint is visible in the fragment.
Integer overflow/truncation of size would require arithmetic or a narrowing conversion, none of which appears in the shown code.

verdict.summary: xemaclite_of_probe dereferences the MEM resource pointer without checking whether platform_get_resource(ofdev, IORESOURCE_MEM, 0) returned NULL: res from line 33 reaches devm_ioremap_resource (line 34) and the res->start / res->end dereferences (lines 40-41) with no NULL guard, unlike the IRQ resource fetch which is checked at lines 25-29. The absent fix is a NULL check on the MEM resource before its use.

evidence.reason: Sink consuming res assigned at line 33 (platform_get_resource(ofdev, IORESOURCE_MEM, 0)), whose residual range is NULL ∪ valid since no check exists between lines 33 and 34. The fragment's own convention proves the API is NULL-able: the identical IORESOURCE_IRQ call at line 24 is NULL-checked at line 25. Guards on the path fail the Guard-Identity Audit (line 25 constrains the pre-reassignment IRQ incarnation - wrong-target drift; line 35 constrains lp->base_addr, a different variable, and executes after this use). Passing a NULL resource to devm_ioremap_resource under its standard name-implied semantics requires a valid resource. Absent fix: if (!res) { rc = -ENXIO; goto error; } after line 33. Primary CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference.

NULL dereference read of res->start when platform_get_resource(ofdev, IORESOURCE_MEM, 0) at line 33 returns NULL (a NULL outcome the fragment itself treats as possible by checking the same API at lines 24-25). No guard between line 33 and this sink: line 25 tested the previous IRQ incarnation of res (wrong-target drift, reassignment at line 33), and line 35 tests lp->base_addr, not res. Absent fix: if (!res) { rc = -ENXIO; goto error; } before this use. Confirmed CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference.

NULL dereference read of res->end with the same unguarded NULL producer as line 40: res is assigned at line 33 from platform_get_resource(ofdev, IORESOURCE_MEM, 0), may be NULL (NULL-ability established by the fragment's own IRQ check at lines 24-25), and every guard on the path constrains a different value (line 25: previous res incarnation; line 35: lp->base_addr). Absent fix: if (!res) { rc = -ENXIO; goto error; }. Confirmed CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference.

assumptions: platform_get_resource() returns NULL when the requested resource type is absent; the fragment itself treats this API as NULL-able by guarding its IORESOURCE_IRQ result at line 25 (access convention for the same function).
res is a single variable reassigned at line 33, so the line 25 NULL guard covers only the IRQ incarnation and does not constrain the MEM fetch.

devm_ioremap_resource() (unshown callee) requires a valid, non-NULL resource per its standard name-implied semantics; initial kernel implementations used BUG_ON(!res), later ones return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL).
limitations: The exact in-callee behavior of devm_ioremap_resource for a NULL resource is not shown; if a given kernel version returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL), the IS_ERR branch at line 35 would divert before lines 40-41, with the failure manifesting at/under line 34 instead - the absence of the in-fragment NULL fix is unchanged.
lp->phy_node (line 61) is consumed by the unshown xemaclite_mdio_setup(); a possible NULL phy_node there is not auditable from this fragment and is not claimed as a finding.
No loops, injection, integer, or crypto sinks are present in the fragment, so no additional candidates were formed.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains no confirmed, reachable vulnerability. Every syscall return is checked fail-closed (stat at line 17 gates S_ISDIR and chmod; mkdir at line 23 gates errExit on non-EEXIST; chmod at line 25 gates errExit). The in-place pointer writes (lines 16, 20, 21, 31) have no demonstrated out-of-bounds witness: no capacity for dst and no length bound for src are shown, and the loop terminates at the NUL terminator. The remaining candidates (undersized dst, src_prefix_len >= strlen(src), symlink/EEXIST chmod target, stat-to-chmod TOCTOU) all require caller or environmental invariants unshown in the fragment and are demoted to limitations.

assumptions: src and dst are NUL-terminated buffers with the prefix boundary at src[src_prefix_len] / dst[dst_prefix_len] and dst pre-sized for the final constructed path plus terminator (the parallel-path convention the function's q/r writes imply).
bool last is initialized (line 6) and *r is initialized before use (line 7).

stat (line 17), mkdir (line 23), and chmod (line 25) return-status checks are the protective statements for their respective syscalls and pass the Guard-Identity Audit (same call, no interleaved mutation).
limitations: Out-of-bounds read/write of src would require src_prefix_len >= strlen(src) or an unterminated source buffer; both are caller invariants not shown in the fragment, so no witness is derivable from shown code (CWE-125/787 not confirmable).
Out-of-bounds write into dst (*q='\0' line 20, *r='/' line 21) requires dst to be undersized or dst_prefix_len >= strlen(dst); no capacity or length is shown, so the failure set is unestablished.

The EEXIST path (line 23) followed by chmod (line 25) could chmod an existing non-directory or follow a symlink, but requires an unshown environmental precondition (attacker-precreated dst) and is demoted (potential CWE-59).
TOCTOU between stat(src) (line 17) and mkdir/chmod on dst (lines 23-25) requires an unshown race interleaving and is demoted.
A size_t wrap of src_prefix_len + 1 / dst_prefix_len + 1 (lines 2-3) would require SIZE_MAX as input, which no shown statement can produce.

C++ semantics: `delete`/`delete[]` on a null pointer is a defined no-op, so NULL is not a failure for lines 8, 12, 14, and 16.
Line 6's `mixer &&` short-circuits so `mixer->isActive()` and `mixer->isDeviceRemoved(player)` are evaluated only when `mixer` is non-null.
limitations: Demoted: unguarded `delete[] audioDriverName` (line 14) and `delete listener` (line 16) — no NULL/uninitialized/dangling producer is shown in the fragment.
Demoted: double-free of `player` would require `Mixer::removeDevice` to take ownership and delete the player, which is callee behavior not shown and not standard.
Demoted: an allocation/new[] mismatch for `audioDriverName` would require allocation-site evidence not present in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The two reachable integer divisions (L98, L99) are each protected by the verbatim guard at L94 (`if (unlikely(surface_width == 0 || surface_height == 0))`), which passes the Guard-Identity Audit (same int values, same else-branch, no interleaved mutation) and excludes the degenerate {0} denominator for both sinks. All other dangerous operations either carry their own protective statements (L36-40 isfinite, L81 pixel cap, L118 zero/quartet check, L128 getDataPtr NULL probe) or lack a demonstrable security failure within the shown fragment: the uncovered float divisions at L64/L72 can produce only IEEE NaN/inf; any crash artifact would require an implementation-defined NaN-to-int conversion and unshown SplashBitmap/drawImage behavior, which is demoted to a limitation rather than a confirmed finding.

SplashCoord is the double type used by poppler's Splash layer, so the divisions at L45/L48/L64/L72/L173/L176/floating operations follow IEEE semantics (0/0 -> NaN, x/0 -> +/-inf) and do not trap.

In the else branch (L80-107), surface_width/surface_height are bounded to [0, 16385] by the halving loop L85-90 and are non-zero after L94; in the if-branch (L70-79) the arithmetic at L71-75 forces surface dims to ~2, so the bitmap allocation at L126 has no overflow-capable dimensions.
The output (target) bitmap capacity for blitImage (L193) and the internal behavior of drawImage (L198) are not shown in the fragment.
limitations: L64-L65, `sx = (double) result_width / (surface_width * (x1 - x0));` (and sy): the denominator can be 0 (x1 == x0, surface_width == 0) with no protective statement before the division; however this is IEEE floating division producing NaN/inf, and turning it into a crash requires the implementation-defined (int) cast of NaN at L61/L76 plus unshown SplashBitmap behavior with negative dimensions, which is not derivable from the shown code — demoted.
L72, `ky = 2 / kx;`: kx can be 0 (width == 0 at L60/L21 or m1.m[0] == 0 at L54), but the same IEEE NaN/inf chain applies and fails closed at L81/L94/L118 or L128 — demoted.
L45/L48, L173/L176: float divisions by ctm[0]/matc[0] admit NaN when both a and b are 0 (else-branch), but the NaN only propagates to fail-closed guards or unshown callees — demoted.

L168-L169, `tBitmap->getWidth() * imgData.repeatX`: int multiplication can overflow (repeatX == x1-x0 uncapped), but the corrupted width is consumed only by drawImage (L198) and the blit loop (L191-193) whose bounds and target capacity are not shown — unconfirmable.
L189-L195: repeatX/repeatY can be attacker-large, enabling a CPU-exhaustion loop, but this is a DoS robustness concern without a shown cap and without a demonstrated memory failure — demoted.
L152/L154: `new Gfx(...)` is not NULL-checked before use, but NULL requires fixed-size allocation failure, which per the rules is a limitation, not a finding.

verdict.summary:
In add_slot_store, the sysfs-supplied buf is copied into the uninitialized stack buffer drc_name with memcpy(drc_name, buf, nbytes) (line 11), which does not NUL-terminate it. The subsequent strchr(drc_name, '
') (line 13) scans drc_name as a C string; because the attacker can supply nbytes bytes (0..MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1, admitted by the line 8 guard) containing no '
' and no NUL, the scan continues into the uninitialized stack tail and can read past the end of the MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-byte array (CWE-125), and if it finds a '
' at index >= nbytes the write *end = '\0' (line 16) corrupts off-target stack data (CWE-787) and feeds a garbage-spliced name to dlpar_add_slot (line 18). The missing decisive fix is the NUL-terminating bounded copy, e.g. strscpy(drc_name, buf, nbytes + 1), which the fragment lacks.

evidence.reason: Sink S2 (CWE-125): strchr scans drc_name as a NUL-terminated string, but the only prior write is line 11 'memcpy(drc_name, buf, nbytes);' which copies exactly nbytes attacker-chosen bytes with no terminator, and line 4 'char drc_name[MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN];' leaves the tail uninitialized. The line 8-9 guard 'if (nbytes >= MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN) return 0;' admits nbytes in [0, MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1] and constrains only the copy length, not the termination state the scan consumes (Guard-Identity Audit: wrong-target/transformation drift); line 16 '*end = '\0';' runs after the scan and cannot bound it. The absent fix form is a pre-scan NUL-terminating bounded copy, e.g. 'strscpy(drc_name, buf, nbytes + 1);' (upstream cc7a0bb058b8 substitutes the line 11 memcpy), or a bounded scan such as memchr(drc_name, '\n', nbytes).

Sink S3 (CWE-787): the written address is end, which is the result of the unbounded strchr scan at line 13. Because drc_name is unterminated after the line 11 memcpy and the tail is uninitialized (line 4), end can point to a '\n' at index >= nbytes, inside the uninitialized tail or past the array boundary, so this write can corrupt off-target stack data; no shown statement constrains end to index <= nbytes. The absent one-statement fix is the same NUL-terminating bounded copy ('strscpy(drc_name, buf, nbytes + 1);') or bounded scan, which would make end land only on a '\n' within the copied region or on the in-bounds fallback &drc_name[nbytes] (line 15).

assumptions: drc_name's capacity is MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN, established by the line 4 declaration 'char drc_name[MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN];' and the line 8 guard using the same constant.
buf and nbytes are entry-point sysfs store data: the caller writes the attribute buffer, so buf content is fully attacker-chosen and need not contain '\n' or a NUL.
The nbytes guard (lines 8-9) is present in both members of the pair and fully protects the memcpy at line 11 (its admitted set 0..MAX_DRC_NAME_LEN-1 fits the array).
limitations: The exact byte at which the strchr scan crosses the array boundary depends on the uninitialized stack tail's content, which is not shown in the fragment, so the out-of-bounds read is a range/fragile-boundary witness rather than an exact single-value witness.

The line 16 off-target write specifically requires a '\n' byte in the uninitialized tail at index >= nbytes (or past the array); its occurrence is environmental, matching the upstream commit's 'potentially corrupting data on the stack' description.

verdict.summary: In raptor_xml_writer_start_element_common, the attribute-namespace dedup loop bounds its index j by nspace_declarations_count (line 51) but reads element->attributes[j] (line 52); nspace_declarations_count grows by up to two entries per attribute (lines 58-64, 70-76) plus the element-name entry (lines 29-35), so j can exceed element->attribute_count and read past the attributes array (heap OOB read, CWE-125). Independently, the nsd buffer is allocated as attribute_count+1 (+declared+language, lines 15-22) while worst-case entries reach 1+2*attribute_count, so a single attribute with a new namespace writes nspace_declarations[2] into a 2-slot buffer (heap OOB write, CWE-787). The decisive fix absent is comparing against the current attribute (element->attributes[i]->nspace) rather than element->attributes[j]->nspace, plus a capacity of at least attribute_count*2+1.

evidence.reason: Heap out-of-bounds read: j is admitted by the only guard on it, line 51 'for(j = 0; j < nspace_declarations_count; j++)', so j ranges over [0, count-1]. The attributes array capacity is established by the fragment's access convention, loop line 40 'for(i = 0; i < element->attribute_count; i++)' indexing element->attributes[i] at lines 42 and 71, i.e. span 0..attribute_count-1. count reaches 1 + 2i at iteration i because the element-name entry (lines 29-35) plus one value entry per attribute (lines 70-76) plus up to one namespace-declaration entry per attribute (lines 58-64) are all appended. For attribute_count=2 with element-name nspace and both attribute nspaces out of scope and pairwise distinct (admitted by lines 28, 42, 44-45), at i=1 count=3 and j=2 evaluates element->attributes[2], beyond the span 0..1 — guard G2 (line 40) constrains i, not j (wrong-target drift), and guard G3 (line 51) bounds j by the nsd count, not by attribute_count (insufficient magnitude). The absent fix statement is 'nspace_declarations[j].nspace == element->attributes[i]->nspace' (compare the current attribute) or an explicit 'j < element->attribute_count' bound.

Heap out-of-bounds write: the nsd buffer capacity is nspace_max_count computed at line 15 'int nspace_max_count = element->attribute_count+1;' (plus declared_nspaces and xml_language, lines 16-19) and allocated at lines 21-22, i.e. attribute_count+1 slots for the fragment's default case. With attribute_count=1, element name nspace out of scope (line 28 admitted) and attribute[0] nspace out of scope and distinct (lines 42, 44-45 admitted), the writes are [0] element entry (line 29), [1] attribute namespace declaration (line 58), then this line 70 writes nspace_declarations[2] into a 2-slot buffer, and line 75 writes [2].nspace — an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787). No statement caps nspace_declarations_count against the allocation; the absent fix is a capacity of at least attribute_count*2+1 (+ declared + language) or a single-entry-per-attribute design.

assumptions: element->attributes has exactly element->attribute_count entries, established by the in-fragment access convention: the only indexed accesses are bounded by 'for(i = 0; i < element->attribute_count; i++)' at line 40 (lines 42 and 71).
The nsd buffer capacity is nspace_max_count = element->attribute_count+1 (+ declared + language) from lines 15-19 and the RAPTOR_CALLOC at lines 21-22.

The fragment explicitly processes out-of-scope and pairwise-distinct namespace states (lines 27-28, 42, 44-45), so those field values are within the guards' admitted sets and are entry-point/caller-controlled with no shown constraint.
limitations: The xml_language escape-buffer sizing (lines 108-122) was not confirmed because raptor_xml_escape_string's exact write-limit contract is unshown.

The S2 OOB write (line 70) is independent of the S1 one-statement fix at line 52; a counterpart that only changes line 52 would still overflow the nsd buffer when an attribute declares a new namespace.
Whether real callers ever supply attributes whose namespaces are not in scope depends on the unshown serializer call sites; the branch at lines 42-45 exists to handle it, but no caller is shown.
