verdict.summary: In smtp_command_parse_parameters, the limit passed to uni_utf8_get_char_n is (size_t)(p - parser->end). Inside the loop line 13 guarantees p < parser->end, so this pointer difference is negative and casts to ~SIZE_MAX, defeating the callee's max-length guard. An SMTP client can end the command with a partial multi-byte UTF-8 sequence (e.g. a trailing 0xC3 lead byte at p = end-1), causing uni_utf8_get_char_n to read up to 3 bytes past parser->end and, when the bogus character is accepted, advancing p past the end so i_strdup_until (line 67) copies beyond the received data. The one-statement fix — passing (size_t)(parser->end - p) — is absent.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125) enabled by a signed-to-unsigned conversion (CWE-195): the loop head at line 13 (`while (p < parser->end)`) admits p = parser->end - 1 and guarantees p - parser->end < 0, so the cast (size_t)(p - parser->end) yields ~SIZE_MAX. uni_utf8_get_char_n's second argument is the max length its standard semantics must observe before reading a multi-byte character; with the huge value its length check never fires, so an attacker-supplied trailing partial UTF-8 sequence (e.g. *p == 0xC3 at the last byte, remaining == 1) makes the callee read bytes at parser->end and beyond — outside the [cur, end) span established by the fragment's own loop convention. The error checks at lines 22/24 run only after that read (check-then-use drift), and a positive nch then advances p past parser->end at line 33, feeding i_strdup_until(parser->cur, mp) at line 67 with mp past the received data. The absent one-statement fix is the correct remaining-length argument (size_t)(parser->end - p).

assumptions: parser->end is the exclusive end of the available received command data; the readable index space [parser->cur, parser->end) is established by the loop bound at line 13 and the offset bookkeeping at lines 43/69.
uni_utf8_get_char_n's second parameter is a max length that its standard semantics bound reads to; a negative ptrdiff_t cast to size_t therefore defeats that bound.
The SMTP input buffer content and length are entry-point (network) data; the fragment imposes no minimum length and no constraint on the final byte's value.
limitations: The allocation size of the buffer backing [parser->cur, parser->end) is not shown; if it always had >=3 bytes of slack beyond parser->end the read could stay inside the allocation, but it would still read and consume bytes beyond the received command and drive the line 67 copy past the parsed span.
The source of uni_utf8_get_char_n is not shown; its bounded-read behavior is taken from its name/argument semantics per the call-site confirmation rule.

Actual disclosure or crash depends on buffer layout and heap state beyond the fragment; the confirmed mechanism is the out-of-bounds read relative to the fragment's own span convention, which may extend past the allocation depending on unshown layout.

verdict.summary: In smtp_command_parse_parameters(), the decode call at lines 19-20 passes (size_t)(p - parser->end) as the max length to uni_utf8_get_char_n(). The loop condition on line 12 guarantees p < parser->end while the loop runs, so p - parser->end is negative and the cast wraps to a SIZE_MAX-range length. A multi-byte UTF-8 lead byte within 1-3 bytes of the buffer end then makes the decoder read continuation bytes past parser->end (up to 3 bytes out of bounds). The nch<0 check (line 22) and the max_size check (line 33) run after the read and never bound the length argument; the required fix is the remaining-length expression (size_t)(parser->end - p).

evidence.reason: The taint is the SMTP receive buffer [parser->cur, parser->end) with parser->end exclusive (loop bound line 12 and p == parser->end line 42). Inside the loop p < parser->end always holds, so the max_len argument (size_t)(p - parser->end) on line 19 is a negative ptrdiff_t that wraps to SIZE_MAX-range; the object access convention bounds p to parser->end, and a multi-byte UTF-8 lead byte at p = parser->end - 1 (e.g. 0xC3, attacker-chosen wire data, admitted by line 12) makes uni_utf8_get_char_n read continuation bytes at parser->end and beyond before returning. The nch<0 check on line 22 fires only after the overread, and the max_size check on line 33 runs after the loop and constrains total size, not the decode length (wrong control point / wrong quantity), so neither is a decisive protective statement. The absent one-statement fix is a correct remaining-length argument, (size_t)(parser->end - p), yielding CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: Buffer capacity is [parser->cur, parser->end) with parser->end as the exclusive one-past-end pointer, established by the fragment's own access convention: loop bound `while (p < parser->end)` (line 12) and `if (p == parser->end)` (line 42).

uni_utf8_get_char_n(p, max_len, &ch) follows its standard semantics: it reads the continuation bytes of a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence and uses max_len only to detect truncation, so a SIZE_MAX-range max_len removes the truncation bound.
limitations: The overread is at most 3 bytes past parser->end; whether it crosses an unmapped page (crash) or leaks adjacent heap contents depends on allocation layout, so concrete impact is bounded but environment-dependent.

If a complete multi-byte character happens to decode entirely beyond parser->end, p (and thus mp on line 52) could advance past parser->end, extending i_strdup_until (line 65) past the buffer; this is a secondary consequence of the same defect and is subsumed by the primary CWE-125 sink.
The raw-byte AUTH path (line 17) is not affected; only the non-auth_response UTF-8 command-parameter path carries the vulnerable decode.

verdict.summary: ha_maria::drop_table discards the return status of maria_delete_table_files() at line 5, so a failed deletion of the table files is still reported as a successful drop to the SQL-layer caller (the function returns void). The absent one-statement fix is a return-status check/propagation such as 'return maria_delete_table_files(name, 1, MY_WME);'.

evidence.reason: The return status of the unconditional file-deletion call at line 5 is the Phase 1 residual range: unconstrained, never tested, never used. Every path leads to this call (lines 3-4 do not condition it), and the only statement touching its result is the '(void)' cast which discards the failure set (non-zero return). The sole conditional, line 3's 'DBUG_ASSERT(!file || file->s->temporary);', constrains only the open-handler state, not the deletion status (Guard-Identity Audit drift class 3, wrong-target), so it does not protect this sink. With the function declared void (line 1), a failed file deletion is reported as a successful table drop to the SQL-layer caller, leaving orphaned table data files (unchecked return value of a security-relevant file operation, CWE-754). The absent fix statement is a return-status check/propagation of maria_delete_table_files, e.g. 'return maria_delete_table_files(name, 1, MY_WME);'.

assumptions: maria_delete_table_files returns an error status when the file deletion fails, per its name-implied semantics and the MY_WME (write-message-on-error) flag at line 5.
The enclosing function's void return is consumed by the SQL-layer DROP-TABLE path as a success indication (caller-derived; no call site is shown in the fragment).
limitations: A concrete non-zero return from maria_delete_table_files requires an I/O, permission, or OS-level failure not shown in the fragment — an unchecked environment failure, hence the 0.74 confidence band.
No path-traversal/injection claim is made for 'name': its provenance is an unshown caller and the callee's path construction is not shown inside the fragment.
The discarded ha_close() status at line 4 is the same flaw pattern but has no demonstrated security consequence consumed within the fragment, so it is not reported as a separate finding.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in do_cmdline(): on the :while/:for jump-back path, 'current_line' is restored from cstack.cs_line[cs_idx] (line 446), which may hold a value >= lines_ga.ga_len because cmd_loop_cookie.current_line can be incremented past the stored lines when a function is defined inside the loop (lines 381-383) and current_line_before is captured unconditionally (line 332). The breakpoint block then reads ((wcmd_T *)lines_ga.ga_data)[current_line].lnum-1 (line 458) guarded only by 'breakpoint != NULL', with no upper-bound check of current_line against ga_len. The upstream fix (one statement) adds '&& lines_ga.ga_len > current_line' to that guard.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read of the lines_ga array of wcmd_T (capacity ga_len elements; allocated at line 73 via ga_init2 and grown at line 327). The index current_line is restored from cstack.cs_line[cstack.cs_idx] at line 446, a value that the shown code can set >= lines_ga.ga_len: line 383 assigns current_line from cmd_loop_cookie.current_line, which per the in-fragment comment (lines 381-382) 'may have been incremented when defining a function' beyond the lines stored in lines_ga; line 326-327 stores a line only when current_line == lines_ga.ga_len, while line 332 copies current_line to current_line_before unconditionally and line 477 persists it into cs_line[cs_idx]. The guards on this path (lines 439-444: cs_idx >= 0, CSF_WHILE/CSF_FOR and CSF_ACTIVE flags, cs_line[cs_idx] >= 0) constrain only the cstack entry and the lower bound of the index (drift class 3 / lower-bound-only), and line 453 'if (breakpoint != NULL)' is a NULL check on a pointer, not a bound on current_line. No statement on this path checks current_line < lines_ga.ga_len; the loop-top guard at line 177 protects the reads at lines 220-221, not this jump-back read (wrong control point). The absent one-statement fix is the upper-bound check 'lines_ga.ga_len > current_line' (added upstream), and the primary CWE is CWE-125 (heap out-of-bounds read feeding dbg_find_breakpoint()).

assumptions: lines_ga holds ga_len valid wcmd_T elements; the valid index domain is [0, ga_len-1] (ga_init2 line 73, store_loop_line growth line 327).
current_line is non-negative on entry and by every shown producer (initialized 0 at line 18; cs_line values filtered by >= 0 at line 443).
breakpoint != NULL implies fname != NULL: both are set together at lines 84-95.
limitations: The precise interleaving inside get_loop_line()/do_one_cmd() that increments cmd_loop_cookie.current_line past lines_ga.ga_len is not shown; its existence is documented by the fragment's own comment at lines 381-382.

The failing read requires an active debugging session (breakpoint set on a sourced file or executed function, lines 86-94) plus a function definition inside a :for/:while loop; this is a normal Vim feature combination, not a default-configuration input.

Sinks S1 (lines 220-221) and S2 (line 496) are protected by verbatim guards (lines 177 and 493) and are not findings; STRMOVE at line 406 copies within the same buffer (next_cmdline points into cmdline_copy) with no derivable failing value.

verdict.summary: simplestring_addn accepts a signed int add_len and never constrains its sign: the only length guard, `if(add_len)` (line 19), admits every negative value. A negative add_len converts to an enormous size_t in `memcpy(target->str + target->len, source, add_len)` (line 20), producing heap out-of-bounds read/write; the growth check at line 6 is skipped for negative lengths on maintained states, and line 22/23 subsequently write at a negative index. The absent one-statement fix is a sign check on add_len before any use.

evidence.reason: add_len is a signed int (declared on line 1) with residual range including all negative values: guard `if(add_len)` at line 19 admits every nonzero int, and the growth guard at line 6 (`if(target->len + add_len + 1 > target->size)`) is false on the witness path (e.g., add_len=-1, len=0 gives `0 > size`), so no realloc runs. At the memcpy sink the int converts to size_t, so add_len=-1 becomes SIZE_MAX: an out-of-bounds read of `source` and out-of-bounds write beyond `target->str` (CWE-787 primary, CWE-125 secondary). No shown statement constrains add_len >= 0; the absent fix is a sign check such as `if(add_len < 0) return;`.

With a negative add_len admitted by `if(add_len)` (line 19), line 22 (`target->len += add_len;`) underflows len; on the normal maintained state len==0, the write at line 23 targets index -1, an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787). The guards at lines 6 and 18 do not constrain the sign of add_len or the resulting len; the absent fix is the same sign validation on add_len before lines 22-23.

assumptions: add_len's value is supplied by a caller (no shown call site); the analysis uses the declared int domain and the admitted set of the shown `if(add_len)` guard.
memcpy converts the int length argument to size_t (standard C semantics), so any negative int becomes a huge size_t.
target->len starts at or below target->size-1 on maintained states per the fragment's own growth invariant (`target->len + add_len + 1 > target->size` forces capacity >= len+add_len+1).
limitations: The concrete negative magnitude (e.g., -1) is assumed to come from the caller; it is not derived by a shown statement inside the fragment, which caps confidence at the 0.5-0.64 band.
Integer overflow of `target->len + add_len + 1` or `target->size * 2` at lines 6/8/9 requires caller-supplied magnitudes not shown in the fragment.

Division by zero at line 12 (`newsize % incr` with incr==0) is not confirmable: the fragment pairs `target->size = 0` only with `target->str == NULL` (line 15), and a `size==0`/`str!=NULL` state would require an unshown manual struct state or an unshown `init_str` allocation-failure contract.
Realloc-failure handling is present (lines 13/15/18 set str to the return value, so a failed realloc yields str==NULL and the copy is skipped); no OOB finding is based on realloc failure.

verdict.summary: LZWDecodeCompat carries the decisive protective statement for its least-protected sink: `if(codep->length == 0) { ... return (0); }` guards every code>=256 string-copy path against a zero-length code-table entry, whose NULL next pointer would otherwise cause a one-byte backward heap write (`*--tp = codep->value` at op-1). The restart-block writes are bounded by the `if (residue > occ)` branch (write counts occ/residue within [op, op+occ)); table entry creation is bounded by the free_entp and free_entp->next range checks; `dec_codetab + code` stays in bounds because nbits is capped at BITS_MAX (code <= 4095 < CSIZE); and all single-byte writes require occ > 0 via the while loop. The remaining backward-write hypotheses (negative residue, zero-length caller request) require state or caller inputs not derivable from the shown code, so no failing value reaches any sink.

assumptions: sp->dec_restart and sp->dec_codep are modified only at lines 37, 58, 149 and 153; the fragment establishes that dec_codep->length > dec_restart at every restart entry (set only when codep->length > occ, and incremented only while residue > occ), so residue = codep->length - sp->dec_restart is >= 1 on line 29.

Code value domain: NextCode reads exactly nbits bits and nbits is capped at BITS_MAX by `if (++nbits > BITS_MAX) nbits = BITS_MAX;`, so code stays in [0, 4095], below CSIZE = 4096, keeping `sp->dec_codetab + code` in bounds.

Code-table chains are strictly decreasing in index (new entry links to an older oldcodep), so the chain walks in the restart block, the partial-copy block, and the full-copy loop terminate without cycles or premature NULL.
limitations: A zero-byte decode request (occ == 0) arriving while sp->dec_restart is set would make the do-while write loop at lines 42-45 perform an unbounded backward write (write-before-buffer). This requires the unshown caller to pass occ0 == 0, so it is demoted from a finding under the derivability rule.

A negative residue (sp->dec_restart > sp->dec_codep->length) would turn the partial-restart branch into a backward `op += residue` and a non-terminating write loop, but the shown state transitions at lines 142/153/37 maintain the opposite invariant; a violation would require state corruption outside the fragment.

NULL dereference in the restart skip walk (lines 38-40) would require a code-table chain shorter than its declared length, which the fragment's own table construction (line 120) does not produce; it is not derivable from shown statements.

verdict.summary: In hfsplus_find_cat, the catalog thread record's unicode name length (tmp.thread.nodeName.length), read from the on-disk record at line 9, is never bounded before hfsplus_cat_build_key_uni copies 2*length bytes out of the stack object tmp on lines 19-20. A crafted HFS+ image with length=0xFFFF passes the type/err guards (they constrain tmp.type and the read status, not the length) and causes an out-of-bounds read past the tmp buffer.

evidence.reason: Sink at lines 19-20 consumes tmp.thread.nodeName, a member of the stack union tmp whose capacity is sizeof(hfsplus_cat_entry) (line 4, line 9). nodeName.length is an on-disk u16 read from the catalog record at line 9 and is unconstrained by any shown statement (residual range 0..0xFFFF). The callee's name-implied semantics copy 2*length bytes from nodeName.unicode into the search key; with length=0xFFFF the copy reads ~131070 bytes from a few-hundred-byte stack object, an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Guards on the path fail the Guard-Identity Audit: line 10 constrains only hfs_brec_read's status (err==0 passes for attacker data), and lines 14-17 constrain only tmp.type (wrong-target drift), both admitting the witness. The absent one-statement fix is a bound check such as 'if (be16_to_cpu(tmp.thread.nodeName.length) > HFSPLUS_MAX_NAME) return -EIO;' before the call.

assumptions: tmp is a stack object of size sizeof(hfsplus_cat_entry), shown by its declaration at line 4 and the read bound at line 9.
hfs_brec_read(fd, rec, rec_len) caps the copy into rec at the named rec_len (bounded-read semantics), so line 9 itself does not overflow tmp.
hfsplus_cat_build_key_uni copies the length-prefixed unicode name (2*length bytes) into the key, per its name-implied key-builder semantics.
Catalog record contents, including nodeName.length and type, are attacker-controlled filesystem-image data (entry-point input).
limitations: The destination fd->search_key capacity is not shown in the fragment, so the corresponding out-of-bounds write side (CWE-787) of the copy is not independently confirmable and is not reported as a primary CWE.

The exact minimum overflowing length depends on the hfsplus_cat_thread struct layout, which is not shown; the witness length=0xFFFF is far beyond any plausible threshold, so the claim does not depend on the exact offset.
A secondary uninitialized-value variant (record shorter than the thread struct leaving length uninitialized) is possible but not needed for the confirmed overflow.

verdict.summary: The zip-slip path-selection sink is protected by an explicit containment check (`targetFile.isAChildOf (targetDirectory)` at line 16, with fail-closed return at line 17) that constrains the exact value consumed by createDirectory, createSymbolicLink, and FileOutputStream. Extraction through symlinked ancestors is additionally blocked by the hasSymbolicPart guard at line 36 (when followSymlinks == FollowSymlinks::no), the input stream is NULL-checked at line 24 before dereference, and every security-relevant return status is checked. No dangerous sink with a derivable failing value lacks its protective statement.

assumptions: isAChildOf is given its standard meaning: true only for paths that lie inside targetDirectory, so absolute and '..'-escaping entry paths are excluded.
hasSymbolicPart (targetDirectory, parent) detects any symlink component in the parent chain, blocking writes through previously extracted links under ordered per-entry processing.
All decisive guards were evaluated at the control point where targetFile is used, with no intervening assignment to targetFile (lines 14 -> 16 -> 20/27/32/36/39/47/52/57/60-62).
limitations: entries.getUnchecked (index) / createStreamForEntry (index) could be an out-of-bounds access, but the fragment shows no capacity for `entries` and no in-fragment access convention to derive one, so no OOB failure is confirmable from shown code.

The symlink target originalFilePath (line 44) is attacker-chosen, but creating a link does not write through it; later traversal is guarded by hasSymbolicPart at line 36, so no arbitrary-write escape is derivable within the fragment.

A TOCTOU window between hasSymbolicPart (line 36) and opening the output stream would require a concurrent external actor modifying targetDirectory, which is outside the fragment and therefore demoted.
followSymlinks == FollowSymlinks::yes deliberately permits traversal through symlinks per the parameter's semantics; that path is a caller-selected mode, not a missing guard.

verdict.summary: The fragment passes sizeof(err_str) (44 bytes, including the terminating NUL of the 43-character string declared at line 7) as the payload length to sctp_sf_abort_violation at lines 9-10, so the ABORT error cause is constructed with an off-by-one length that includes the NUL byte; the one-statement fix 'sizeof(err_str) - 1' is absent.

evidence.snippet:
return sctp_sf_abort_violation(ep, asoc, arg, commands, err_str,
					sizeof(err_str));
evidence.reason: SINK-1 consumes (err_str, sizeof(err_str)): err_str is the 44-byte array at line 7 (43 visible characters plus the implicit NUL), so sizeof(err_str) = 44 passes paylen = 44 on the single unconditional path with no guard between line 7 and the sink. The absent fix form is 'sizeof(err_str) - 1' (or strlen(err_str)), which would bound paylen to the 43 content bytes; without it the protocol-violation error cause is built with the incorrect length value — the off-by-one the pair's one-statement fix removes — primary CWE-805.

assumptions: The static array err_str at line 7 holds the literal's 43 characters plus an implicit NUL, so sizeof(err_str) = 44 (size_t) — the fragment's shown capacity and the exact paylen delivered at line 10.
The callee sctp_sf_abort_violation consumes the (payload, paylen) pair to construct/transmit the ABORT error cause (name-implied standard semantics used for call-site confirmation).
limitations: No out-of-bounds access is demonstrable against a shown local capacity: the 44-byte source array and a callee allocation sized for 4 + 44 both admit 44 bytes; the confirmed failure is the off-by-one length value itself at the packet-construction sink.

The downstream byte-exact consequence (the stray NUL in the transmitted cause / cause-length mismatch) lives inside the unshown callee and cannot be quoted from this fragment; the verdict rests on the callee's name-implied semantics plus the absent one-statement fix.

verdict.summary: ha_maria::drop_table performs a destructive file deletion with no runtime protective statement: name, an entry-point parameter whose full domain is unconstrained by the fragment, flows directly into maria_delete_table_files(name, 1, MY_WME) at line 5; the only gate on the path, DBUG_ASSERT(file->s->temporary) at line 3, is a debug-only diagnostic compiled out in production builds and does not constrain the name consumed by the sink, so the temporary-table precondition is unenforced at runtime (missing authorization gate, CWE-862).

evidence.reason: The sink deletes on-disk files for the table named by `name`. `name` is an entry-point parameter (Phase 1 provenance (a)) with no shown constraint, so its residual range is the full string domain, and it reaches the sink directly as the call argument on line 5 through an unconditional sequence (lines 3-5, no branch, no loop). The only guard on the path, line 3 `DBUG_ASSERT(file->s->temporary);`, fails the Guard-Identity Audit: it is a debug-only diagnostic that is compiled out under NDEBUG (no runtime constraint on any path), it constrains the different value `file->s->temporary` rather than the `name` the sink consumes (wrong-target drift), and per the class rules a diagnostic assert is not creditable as a protective statement. Fix-Presence resolution for this sink is ABSENT: the fragment lacks the one-statement runtime guard (e.g., `if (!file->s->temporary) return;` before the deletion, or input validation on `name`), so the destructive file-deletion operation has no covering protective statement at runtime — missing authorization gate, CWE-862.

assumptions: maria_delete_table_files(name, 1, MY_WME) deletes the on-disk files corresponding to the table named by `name` (name-implied standard semantics).
DBUG_ASSERT is a diagnostic macro that is evaluated and aborts only in debug builds and is compiled out in production (NDEBUG) builds.
limitations: A concrete failing invocation (a non-temporary `file->s`, or a `name` with path-destructive content) cannot be derived from statements inside the fragment; it requires an unshown caller violating the temporary-table contract or unshown SQL-layer table-name validation, which caps confidence in the low band.
The discarded return of `ha_close()` at line 4 is a status-handling candidate (CWE-754), but a failing close is not producible from the shown code — demoted.
A NULL dereference of `file->s` at line 3 has no NULL producer shown in the fragment — demoted.
Path traversal (CWE-22) via `name` into `maria_delete_table_files` is unconfirmed because the callee's path construction and the SQL-layer name rules are outside the fragment.

verdict.summary: In the ASCII read path of GmfOpenMesh, fscanf(msh->hdl, "%s", str) at lines 127 and 140 reads an unbounded whitespace-delimited token from the attacker-controlled mesh file into the fixed-size stack buffer char str[GmfStrSiz] declared at line 5. A crafted token at least as long as the buffer causes a stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121). No width-limited format or token-length check exists; the only added bound, line 39, protects the strcpy of FilNam (line 42), not these %s conversions.

evidence.reason: File tokens (entry-point data, read from the file opened at line 122) have an unconstrained length; %s writes the full token plus NUL into char str[GmfStrSiz] (capacity declared at line 5). Any token >= GmfStrSiz bytes overflows the stack buffer. Guards on the path fail the Guard-Identity Audit: line 122 checks msh->hdl, not the token (wrong-target drift), and the line 128 loop condition is evaluated after the write (check-after-use). The absent one-statement fix is a width-limited conversion (e.g., fscanf(msh->hdl, "%255s", str)). Mechanism: stack-based buffer overflow via unbounded %s copy (CWE-121).

Identical second unbounded %s sink into char str[GmfStrSiz] (line 5). File tokens are attacker-controlled and unbounded; a token >= GmfStrSiz bytes written before the line 141 condition (check-after-use) overflows the stack buffer. The line 39 length guard constrains FilNam for the line 42 strcpy only, not this token (wrong-target drift). The absent fix is a width-limited conversion format at this sink. Mechanism: stack-based buffer overflow via unbounded %s copy (CWE-121).

assumptions: GmfStrSiz is a positive compile-time constant and is the capacity of str per the declaration at line 5.
msh->FilNam provides at least GmfStrSiz bytes of storage, as implied by the line 39 bound check (strlen + 7 margin) preceding the line 42 strcpy.
The ASCII read path is taken when msh->typ has Asc (extensions ".mesh"/".sol" set by lines 53-58) and mod == GmfRead (line 63).
limitations: The numeric value of GmfStrSiz is not shown; the failing witness is a relational range (any token >= array length), not an exact byte count, though the overflow is certain for any positive value.
NULL-safety of the varargs-derived PtrVer/PtrDim (lines 152-153) depends on the unshown caller and is not assessed as a finding.
Internal helpers (safe_fread, ScaWrd, safe_fscanf, ScaKwdTab, GetPos) and the full GmfMshSct layout are not shown; their behavior was not relied on for the verified sinks.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed member of the pair. The dangerous path (a scan that can find a 'free' zero bit at a block index >= size in the last partial u32, causing u32 wrap in `size - start` at line 76 and bitmap writes past its end at lines 98/120) is neutralized by the verbatim guard `if (start >= size) {` at line 71, which excludes start >= size (including the degenerate boundary start == size and U32_MAX) on every path to the allocation writes. The guard passes the Guard-Identity Audit: start is the same u32 value, computed at line 70 and consumed unmodified at line 76. Other sinks (in-page reads bounded by the end-pointer arithmetic at lines 22-25/60-63/108 and `curr < end` at lines 41/90; dprint with literal formats) have no derivable failure set.

assumptions: A mapped page holds PAGE_CACHE_BITS bits, so `end = pptr + PAGE_CACHE_BITS / 32` (lines 23, 61, 108) and `end = pptr + ((size + 31) & (PAGE_CACHE_BITS - 1)) / 32` (lines 25, 63) keep every `curr < end` access inside the mapped page.
`len = *max` with `if (!len) return size;` (lines 10-12) guarantees len >= 1 past line 12.
The allocation is capped by `len = min(size - start, len);` (line 76), which is only reachable when `start < size` due to the guard at line 71.
limitations: `read_mapping_page` results (lines 17, 57, 104) are passed to `kmap(page)` (lines 18, 59, 106) without an `if (IS_ERR(page))` check; the fix form is absent, but producing an error pointer requires an unshown environment (a bitmap file shorter than ceil(size / PAGE_CACHE_BITS) pages), so per the NULL/error-producer rule it is a limitation, not a confirmed finding.

`mask = 1 << 31;` at line 45 is signed shift UB that yields a multi-bit mask, over-marking bits inside an already-valid word and skewing `*max`; it cannot derive an out-of-page index or an index >= size, so it is a robustness concern.
`(size + 31)` at lines 25/63 wraps for size within 31 of U32_MAX, shrinking `end` (fail-closed spurious 'bitmap full'), never widening it; robustness only.
`HFSPLUS_SB(sb).free_blocks -= *max;` (line 124) could underflow on inconsistent on-disk free-block counts; state is maintained outside the fragment.

verdict.summary: composite_setup carries a decisive protective statement for every provable dangerous sink. w_length (attacker-controlled u16) is clamped at line 14-24 to USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ on every path (OUT with w_length > BUFSIZ exits at line 22; IN is reassigned to BUFSIZ at line 20), then every length-fed operation is independently bounded: memcpy device descriptor (line 71) by 'value = min(w_length, (u16) sizeof cdev->desc);' (line 70); the OTG memcpy (line 127) by 'value = min_t(int, w_length, otg_desc_len);' (line 126) giving value <= 5; the OS-descriptor memset (line 287) by 'w_length = min_t(u16, w_length, USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ);' (line 286); and every cdev->config->interface[intf] index (lines 165/194/230/253/358) is guarded by 'intf >= MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES' (lines 163/192/228/251/356). All guards pass the Guard-Identity Audit (same value, same u16/int type, no interleaved mutation, no transformation drift). Remaining candidates (empty cdev->configs list producing a bogus OTG config from list_first_entry; OS-desc 'interface' reaching count_ext_prop/len_ext_prop/fill_ext_prop without a shown bounds check; NULL os_desc_req) depend on unshown helper internals or driver/environment state and cannot be confirmed from the fragment.

assumptions: req->buf capacity >= USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ, established by the fragment's own access convention: every attack-controlled length written into req->buf is clamped to USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ (lines 14-24) and each per-descriptor copy is min-bounded (lines 70, 78-79, 89, 95, 101, 126, 156, 202).

cdev->os_desc_req->buf capacity >= USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ, established by the fragment clamping w_length to exactly that constant (line 286) immediately before memset(buf, 0, w_length) (line 287).
cdev->config->interface[] has MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES slots, established by the fragment guarding every index with 'intf >= MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES' before each access (lines 163, 192, 228, 251, 356).
otg_desc_len is sizeof(struct usb_otg_descriptor) (3 bytes) or sizeof(struct usb_otg20_descriptor) (5 bytes), so min_t(int, w_length, otg_desc_len) (line 126) yields value <= 5.
limitations: OTG branch (lines 109-127): if cdev->configs were empty, list_first_entry (line 112-114) returns a non-NULL bogus pointer that 'if (!config) goto done;' (line 115) cannot exclude, and config->descriptors[0] (line 127) could fault; the empty list is not derivable from any shown statement (configs are driver-populated at bind time), so this is demoted.

OS-descriptor interface index (lines 309-320): interface = w_value & 0xFF spans 0-255 with no shown bound before count_ext_prop/len_ext_prop/fill_ext_prop; whether those helpers index os_desc_cfg->interfaces out of bounds depends on unshown helper internals with no standard name-implied semantics, so no OOB can be confirmed at the call site.

NULL dereference of cdev->os_desc_req (lines 281-284) is not confirmable: the gate checks cdev->use_os_string && cdev->os_desc_config (line 273) and the request allocation/buffer setup happens outside the fragment.

Internal bounds of unshown helpers (get_string, config_desc, bos_desc, set_config, fill_ext_compat/fill_ext_prop, composite_ep0_queue) are not audited; only their shown return-value handling (checks and min clamps at lines 88-89, 94-95, 101, 300-303, 317-322) is within scope.

verdict.summary: In php_wddx_pop_element, when a value element is popped, the enclosing stack entry ent2 is dereferenced at line 74 (Z_TYPE_P(ent2->data)) with only the ST_FIELD-specific null guard at line 68. A crafted WDDX packet that nests a value element inside another no-text value element (e.g. <string><string>x</string></string>) leaves an outer entry with data == NULL on the stack; it becomes ent2, passes every guard (lines 12, 23, 63, 68), and line 74 dereferences a NULL zval pointer, crashing wddx_deserialize (remote denial of service).

evidence.reason: ent2->data is dereferenced at line 74 for every ent2->type. NULL-data stack entries are an admitted state inside the fragment itself: line 23 (if (!ent1->data)) and line 68 (if (ent2->type == ST_FIELD && ent2->data == NULL)) both treat data == NULL as reachable. The only guard for ent2, line 68, constrains NULL data exclusively to ST_FIELD entries (guard-identity drift class: wrong-target/subset), so a value-type entry (from a nested no-text <string> or <null> parent, produced by ordinary attacker-controlled XML nesting) with data == NULL passes lines 12, 23, and 63-68 and reaches line 74, dereferencing a NULL zval*. The absent fix statement is a type-independent NULL check on ent2->data before the dereference (e.g. extending line 68 to if (ent2->data == NULL)). verdict.summary: On the USB_DT_DEVICE_QUALIFIER path, composite_setup() computes value = min_t(int, w_length, sizeof(struct usb_qualifier_descriptor)) (lines 74-76) and falls through to check_value, which queues req->buf (lines 403-407) even though no shown statement populates req->buf with the qualifier on this path (device_qual() fills the unshown cdev->qualifier, and the copy is absent). A malicious host's GET_DESCRIPTOR(DEVICE_QUALIFIER) request therefore receives up to 10 bytes of stale/uninitialized ep0-buffer contents — kernel memory disclosure. The one-statement fix — an initialization copying the qualifier into the response, e.g. memcpy(req->buf, &cdev->qualifier, value) — is ABSENT.

evidence.reason: ctrl->bRequest, ctrl->wValue and ctrl->wLength are entry-point attacker-controlled fields (lines 7-10; full u16 domains, w_length residually 0..USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ after the line 14-24 clamp). With bRequest=GET_DESCRIPTOR, bRequestType=USB_DIR_IN and w_value>>8==USB_DT_DEVICE_QUALIFIER (lines 43-46, 70), passing the line 71-72 dual-speed/non-SuperSpeed guard, device_qual(cdev) (line 74) fills the unshown cdev->qualifier and value is set to min_t(w_length, sizeof qualifier) (lines 75-76). value >= 0 then reaches check_value (lines 403-407) where req->length = value and composite_ep0_queue(cdev, req, GFP_ATOMIC) transmits req->buf, yet no shown statement on this path writes req->buf (only line 30 req->length = 0 precedes; the copy from cdev->qualifier is missing). The fix form — an initialization copying the qualifier into the response buffer (memcpy(req->buf, &cdev->qualifier, value)) — is ABSENT, so up to 10 bytes of stale/uninitialized ep0-buffer contents are disclosed to the untrusted host: primary CWE-200 information exposure.

verdict.summary: cq_size (int parameter, line 1) is consumed by roundup_pow_of_two() and ilog2() (lines 15-16, 46) with no validation anywhere in the fragment. A zero or negative value — a member of cq_size's full declared int domain, which the fragment never constrains — makes roundup_pow_of_two() compute 1UL << fls_long(n - 1) with n-1 wrapped to ULONG_MAX (a 64-bit shift by 64, undefined behavior) and feeds ilog2() a 0/negative size whose -1 result is stored into the log_cq_size field, producing an uncontrolled CQ/WQ size (up to 32768 entries) from a zero-size request. The missing one-statement fix is an input validation bounding cq_size to positive values before line 15, e.g. 'if (cq_size <= 0) return -EINVAL;'. Every other dangerous sink (wq-create return, kvzalloc NULL, vector2eqn return, create_cq return, loop index, PAS fill capacity) carries a verbatim protective statement, so this is the least-protected sink.

evidence.reason: cq_size is declared int (line 1) with the full signed domain; the fragment contains no constraint on it before this statement. For cq_size <= 0, roundup_pow_of_two() evaluates 1UL << fls_long((unsigned long)cq_size - 1): for 0 it is 1UL << fls_long(ULONG_MAX) = 1UL << 64 (shift-by-width UB after the n-1 wraparound), and for negatives the signed-to-unsigned conversion reaches the same ≥64 shift. The corrupted value is then consumed as log_cq_size at lines 16 and 46 via ilog2(cq_size) (ilog2(0) == -1), which sizes the WQ allocation made inside mlx5_cqwq_create (line 21) and the hardware CQ, producing an uncontrolled size (up to 32768 WQEs) from a 0-size request. No guard, bound, equality check, or sanitization of cq_size exists on any path (guards at lines 23, 34, 40, 59 constrain other values); the demanded fix form — input validation such as 'if (cq_size <= 0) return -EINVAL;' before line 15 — is absent. Primary CWE-190 (integer wrap feeding an allocation/configuration consumer).

assumptions: roundup_pow_of_two() for non-constant arguments expands to __roundup_pow_of_two(n) = 1UL << fls_long(n - 1), so n <= 0 produces a shift count of 64 (UB) after wrapping; ilog2(0) is -1 for runtime values.

MLX5_SET masks log_cq_size into a 4-bit field, so a -1/huge log value materializes as field 15 (WQ size 32768) rather than a plain overflow; both the temp_cqc (line 16) and cqc (line 46) uses are affected identically.

The WQ/PAS capacities used to clear other sinks are visible in the fragment: the loop bound at line 26 indexes the same wq object sized via temp_cqc at line 21, and the inlen formula at lines 31-32 allocates exactly sizeof(u64) * npages bytes beyond the fixed create_cq_in header, matching the npages PAS entries written at line 54.

Guards evaluated and passed for their own sinks: lines 23-24 (mlx5_cqwq_create return), lines 34-37 (kvzalloc NULL), lines 40-43 (mlx5_vector2eqn return plus kvfree), lines 59-60 (mlx5_core_create_cq return with unconditional kvfree at line 57).

The exact post-UB values (1 vs 0) and the resulting WQ size depend on architecture shift behavior and on mlx5_cqwq_create internals, which are not shown; the confirmed defect is the unguarded shift-by-width UB and loss of size control, not a specific corruption magnitude.
Potential NULL dereference of fdev->conn_res.uar (line 48) and conn/fdev (lines 3-4) is not reported: no in-fragment NULL producer exists.

The ilog2/roundup failure does not produce a demonstrated out-of-bounds access inside this fragment; impact is limited to undefined arithmetic and an inconsistent, attacker-influenced CQ size, hence severity low.

verdict.summary: In cp_create, the attacker-controlled OPT_MAXRLVLS value (line 166) is only upper-bounded at line 167 (if(tccp->maxrlvls > JPC_MAXRLVLS)), which admits negative values such as -1. The loop at line 286 uses the mixed signed/unsigned comparison rlvlno < tccp->maxrlvls, so a negative maxrlvls converts to a huge unsigned bound and the writes at lines 287-288 run past the JPC_MAXRLVLS-entry prcwidthexpns/prcheightexpns arrays, producing a heap out-of-bounds write. The lower-bound check at line 380 (if (cp->tccp.maxrlvls < 1)) executes only after the write loop and protects nothing.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write (CWE-787). tccp->maxrlvls is attacker-controlled via line 166 (atoi of the options value); after the line 167 guard `if(tccp->maxrlvls > JPC_MAXRLVLS)` the admitted set still includes -1. Line 286 `for (rlvlno = 0; rlvlno < tccp->maxrlvls; ++rlvlno)` compares uint_fast16_t rlvlno with signed maxrlvls, so -1 converts to a huge unsigned bound and rlvlno advances past the JPC_MAXRLVLS-entry prcwidthexpns array implied by the line 167 bound, writing this value out of bounds. The only relevant lower-bound fix form, `if (cp->tccp.maxrlvls < 1)` at line 380, is evaluated after the loop and is a guard-after-use (control-point drift), so it is ABSENT as a protector; the absent fix is a maxrlvls < 1 check before line 286.

Same heap OOB write class (CWE-787) for the sibling array: the same loop bound (line 286) driven by the negative, line-167-admitted maxrlvls = -1 indexes prcheightexpns beyond its JPC_MAXRLVLS entries; the line 380 lower-bound check postdates the loop and does not protect this sink.

assumptions: tccp->maxrlvls is a signed integer type: it stores the atoi result (line 166) and participates in > JPC_MAXRLVLS (line 167) and < 1 (line 380) comparisons.
tccp->prcwidthexpns[] and tccp->prcheightexpns[] each hold JPC_MAXRLVLS entries, implied by the fragment's own upper-bound guard name at line 167.
optstr (the encoder options string) is attacker-supplied entry-point data parsed at lines 102-106 and converted with atoi at line 166.
limitations: The exact negative-maxrlvls trip count depends on the platform width of uint_fast16_t versus int: on glibc/Linux (unsigned long) and MSVC (unsigned int) the loop becomes an unbounded/heap-corrupting run, while on platforms where uint_fast16_t is narrower than int the comparison -1 < 0 makes the loop a no-op; this platform dependence is the fragile boundary of the witness.
Integer-overflow arithmetic (lines 59-60, 238, 246, 248-249, 317-321) has no in-fragment security-relevant consumer; downstream tile processing is outside the fragment.
The ilyrrates copy loop (lines 329-331) and the post-allocation layer-count check (line 374) depend on the unshown jpc_atoaf count/allocation contract and are not confirmed from the fragment.

Log writes of attacker option values (lines 147-148, 202-203, 209-210, 218-219) use literal %s formats, so format-string injection is substituted away; CR/LF log-injection is possible but the log target and security context are not shown, so it is demoted.

Each guard constrains the same value at the same type with no interleaved mutation, and admits only in-bounds values including the degenerate boundaries.

assumptions: dec->pclr is non-NULL whenever dec->cmap is non-NULL, enforced in-fragment at lines 218-222 (cmap is destroyed if pclr is absent) before lines 247 and 267 dereference dec->pclr.
dec->numchans equals dec->cmap->data.cmap.numchans when cmap is present (line 233), so the CMAP check loop (line 238) and the palette loop (line 269) index exactly the same ents span.
dec->chantocmptlut has exactly dec->numchans entries allocated at lines 255-256.

pclrd->lutdata is laid out as numlutents*numchans entries and pclrd->bpc as numchans entries per the standard pclr-box layout; with the pcol guard this keeps the maximal line 276 index at numlutents*numchans-1.
IHDR presence (lines 128-131), COLR presence (lines 192-195), and component count > 0 (lines 141-144) are enforced before those objects are used.

Possible OOB read of dec->cdef->data.cdef.ents[i] at lines 309/313-317 if dec->numchans exceeds the CDEF box's declared channel count; the ents capacity is unshown, so it is demoted.

Line 268 (cdefd = &dec->cdef->data.cdef;) can compute a member address through a NULL dec->cdef when no CDEF box is present, but no load occurs and the value is consumed only inside #if 0, so no crash is derivable.
lutents (line 274) is dereferenced at line 276 without a NULL check; a NULL result requires actual OS allocation failure, an environment-dependent condition not demonstrated in the fragment.

verdict.summary: ReadCINImage performs an unbounded heap write into the quantum pixel buffer: cin.image.channel[0].bits_per_pixel is read raw from the file (line 136), stored as image->depth (line 344), and used to compute the per-row length (line 378) for ReadBlobStream(image,length,pixels,&count) (line 394). With no upper-bound validation on bits_per_pixel (absent fix: a check such as 'if (cin.image.channel[0].bits_per_pixel > 32) ThrowReaderException(...)'), a crafted CIN with depth=64, columns=4 yields length=96 bytes written into a 32-bit-quantum pixel extent of 48-64 bytes, a per-row heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The only path guard, the blob-size check at line 352, constrains file size, not depth/length vs capacity.

evidence.reason: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): length is derived from attacker-controlled bits_per_pixel (line 136, residual 0..255, unvalidated) via image->depth (line 344) and GetBytesPerRow(image->columns,3,image->depth,MagickTrue) (line 378), yielding columns*3*((depth+7)>>3), i.e. 96 bytes for columns=4, depth=64; the pixels buffer extent is columns*(32/8)*channels = 48..64 bytes per the shown 32-bit quantum setup (SetQuantumQuantum(quantum_info,32), line 375; SetQuantumPack(quantum_info,MagickFalse), line 376; SetQuantumPad(image,quantum_info,0), line 384). The only guard on the path, the blob-size check at line 352, admits the witness (4*1024/8=512 <= blobsize) and does not constrain length vs capacity (wrong-target drift). The absent one-statement fix is an upper-bound validation of bits_per_pixel/depth before the length computation (e.g., 'if (cin.image.channel[0].bits_per_pixel > 32) ThrowReaderException(CorruptImageError,"ImproperImageHeader");').

assumptions: GetBytesPerRow(columns,channels,depth,pad) computes columns*channels*((depth+7)>>3) rounded up to 32 bytes (standard ImageMagick callee semantics).

The quantum pixel buffer extent is columns*(quantum/8)*number_channels with quantum=32 per the shown SetQuantumQuantum(quantum_info,32) and SetQuantumPack(quantum_info,MagickFalse), with number_channels 3 (RGBQuantum) or 4 default; the overflow margin (96 vs 48-64) holds for both.
The channel table has 8 entries, derived from the shown loop bound 'for (i=0; i < 8; i++)' at line 130.
limitations: The exact allocation size of the GetQuantumPixels(quantum_info) buffer is not literally declared in the fragment; its extent is inferred from the shown 32-bit quantum configuration and the standard extent formula (convention-strength capacity), limiting confidence.

Demoted: serial-string NUL handling (memset line 248) causes no OOB because CopyMagickString caps reads at sizeof(serial); user_length path is guarded (lines 333, 337); all format strings are literals (no injection sink); no crypto/SSRF/authz sinks are present.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every dangerous sink with a failure set derivable from the shown code carries a decisive verbatim protective statement: the pixel_info buffer is sized to at least scanline_size (line 599, with scanline_size <= 0 excluded at 592), samples_per_pixel is capped at MaxPixelChannels (177), bits_per_sample validated at 171-172, rows_per_strip clamped at 567-568, strip/tile buffers sized by extent formulas at 729 and 824 that dominate TIFFStripSize/TIFFTileSize consumers, tile and generic paths guarded by HeapOverflowSanityCheck at 822 and 918 with exact-size allocation at 920-921, and all cache/queue pointers NULL-checked before use. Remaining concerns (pad/extra_samples inflation, zero tile-size non-termination, YCCK path) are demoted because their failing values depend on unshown libtiff/callee behavior.

assumptions: MaxColormapSize equals 65536 and MaxTextExtent is a fixed constant (macro values defined outside the fragment); the palette guard at lines 415-416 then admits bits_per_sample <= 16, so colors = GetQuantumRange(bits)+1 equals the TIFF colormap array size 2^bits indexed by the loops at 455 and 462.
libtiff's TIFFTAG_EXTRASAMPLES field contract provides a sample_info array of exactly extra_samples entries, so the loop at 538 with bound i < extra_samples reads in-bounds.

TIFFScanlineSize/TIFFVStripSize/TIFFStripSize/TIFFTileSize are the standard libtiff per-row/strip/tile byte counts matching the corresponding reads (TIFFReadEncodedStrip at 769-770, TIFFReadTile at 868-869, TIFFReadRGBAImage at 925-926) whose sizes are passed as their buffer-size arguments.
limitations: ReadYCCKMethod is never assigned to method within the shown fragment, so the TIFFReadPixels call at 675 and its pixel walk are not confirmed reachable here; even if reachable, line 599 sizes pixel_info to at least scanline_size (x4 bytes).

A crafted ExtraSamples count far exceeding samples_per_pixel could inflate the quantum pad at lines 625-646 and, if libtiff accepts such a count and ImportQuantumPixels consumes pad per source row, cause an over-read of the strip/tile buffers; this depends on unshown libtiff validation and callee semantics, so it is demoted.
A zero TIFFTAG_TILELENGTH/TILEWIDTH would make the tile loops at 848/859 fail to advance; whether libtiff admits tile size 0 is not shown in the fragment, so non-termination is not confirmed.

Unchecked returns of TIFFGetEXIFProperties/TIFFGetGPSProperties/TIFFGetProfiles-family calls, and HeapOverflowSanityCheck checking a single factor rather than the full product, are hardening/robustness observations with no confirmed in-fragment security consequence.

verdict.summary: The KDC's tgs_build_reply dereferences the request-body sname pointer (`s = b->sname;` line 55) with no presence/NULL check on the default (non-enc_tkt_in_skey) path. A TGS-REQ whose optional sname field is absent yields s == NULL, and `*s` is dereferenced at line 140, crashing krb5kdc (remote denial of service).

evidence.reason: NULL pointer dereference of `*s`: `s` is assigned the unvalidated, attacker-controlled entry-point field `s = b->sname;` (line 55) and is dereferenced at this sink on the default path where `enc_tkt_in_skey` is unset (the U2U replacement `s = &adtkt.cname;` at line 136 protects only that branch). No shown constraint bounds `b->sname` to non-NULL, and no guard on `s` exists between lines 55 and 140; guards on other values (lines 75-76, 749-753) are wrong-target relative to this sink, and the ret-check at lines 143/146 follows the deref rather than preceding it. A TGS request with the optional sname absent admits s == NULL to this deref, crashing the KDC (CWE-476, DoS). The absent one-statement fix is a presence/NULL validation of the request sname before the dereference (e.g., `if (s == NULL) { ret = KRB5KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN; goto out; }`).

assumptions: b->additional_tickets->val has capacity len (its ASN.1 decoded count) — guards at lines 75-76 and 749-751 exclude NULL/empty before val[0] indexing.
b->etype.val has capacity b->etype.len; loop bound line 302 and fail-closed check line 305 keep indices < len at sinks 303/314.

On fetch success (ret == 0), output pointers (client, s4u2self_impersonated_client, server) are set by the callee; ret-checks gate each subsequent deref (presence of ret-check is the protective statement credited).
tgt->cname / adtkt.cname are non-NULL by ticket-decrypt semantics for the U2U path's s reassignment.
The KDC-REQ-BODY sname field is optional per protocol (RFC 4120), so an absent field decodes to NULL b->sname; the fragment shows no constraint or validation to the contrary.
limitations: Unchecked krb5_make_principal return at lines 232-233 and 250-251 would leave sp NULL into krb5_unparse_name (lines 236/254); the NULL producer is allocator/name-parse failure of a fixed-size name, which the NULL-deref rule demotes to a limitation (no in-fragment producer).

If the actual ASN.1 decoder upstream enforces sname presence, the S1 witness (absent sname) would not reach the fragment; this is the fragile external link reflected in the confidence.

Log writes of principal names and from-address strings (lines 153-159 etc.) could carry control characters; no sanitization is shown, but this is treated as robustness, not the decisive pair difference.
